## 1. (done) DONE: the server binary is recorded against its commit, and a deploy refuses an unrecorded one

**Order:** 1 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Handover · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 109

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\server-build.json records sha256 cc9ce515, 5,570,560 bytes, commit d34379b2 · tools\New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1 regenerates it after a rebuild · tools\Deploy-Server.ps1 refuses a binary whose hash is not the recorded one, and sends the record up with it · VPS  ·  game server  ·  C:\Thornswood-Server\scam_native.node, never hashed · source at https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/skymp, branch thornswood/engine-changes

## What is known

RESOLVED 17 September, all three parts. ONE, the disk risk. The fork did not exist. It was created public as EvilPatrick06/skymp with skyrim-multiplayer/skymp as its parent, and the branch pushed. ls-remote returns d34379b2d2aaa792c948f24b3c0a62537f19e8e5, so 911 lines of engine work across nineteen files are no longer on one disk, and the equipment fix entry 19 needs is in that commit. TWO, the build record. tools/server-build.json holds the binary's sha256, size, build time and commit. tools/New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1 regenerates it, warning when the clone is dirty or a source file is newer than the binary. Deploy-Server.ps1 hashes scam_native.node before shipping and refuses outright on a mismatch, printing both hashes and the recorded commit; a missing record warns and carries on. The record is copied to the VPS beside the binary. All three branches tested. THREE, the live server, confirmed 17 September. C:/Thornswood-Server/scam_native.node hashes to cc9ce5150e6fd4f7147be3a34be0f793a006493084ca7dabfba1ebe49c40d880, byte for byte the recorded value, so the running server IS the build that was recorded, which was the open question this entry existed for. LEFT: commit the three files as one fix and open the pull request. WORTH KEEPING: the first attempt at the remote hash nested quotes inside the ssh argument. It returned the right hash and then tried to run the hash as a command, because the remote shell re-parsed the line. Base64 encode the script and pass -EncodedCommand, which is what Deploy-Server.ps1:54-57 has always done. Copy that shape for any VPS command. CONFIRMED 17 September, every check returned True. The VPS binary hashes to cc9ce5150e6fd4f7147be3a34be0f793a006493084ca7dabfba1ebe49c40d880, the local binary matches the record, and the three files are committed as 196c4e5 on patrick/record-the-server-build. Pull request 61 is open, mergeable, and its Launcher builds check passed. Merging it closes this entry. One more thing worth keeping: a remote command also wants $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue' at the front, or PowerShell wraps the answer in a block of CLIXML progress records. CLOSED 17 September: pull request 61 squashed onto main as 5712e81. tools/server-build.json and tools/New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1 are on main, and Deploy-Server.ps1 names the record in seven places. Note for next time: main requires one approving review and GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request, so this was merged with --admin. The other four wait on Djinn.

## Read first

- `tools\Deploy-Server.ps1:54-57`: the Remote helper, which base64 encodes the script instead of nesting quotes. Copy this shape for any command you send to the VPS
- `tools\server-build.json`: the record: sha256 cc9ce515, 5,570,560 bytes, commit d34379b2
- `tools\New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1`: regenerates the record after a rebuild, read only apart from that one file

## Steps

- [x] Hash the binary the server is actually running. Send the script base64 encoded, and silence the progress stream, or PowerShell returns a block of CLIXML around the answer. Single quotes around the script, with the inner quotes doubled: in double quotes the local shell expands $ProgressPreference to Continue before ssh ever sees it, and the VPS answers 'Continue=SilentlyContinue is not recognized' (20 September 16:58). (patrick)
  ```powershell
  $s = '$ProgressPreference=''SilentlyContinue''; (Get-FileHash ''C:\Thornswood-Server\scam_native.node'' -Algorithm SHA256).Hash'; $e = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($s)); ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no Administrator@192.135.112.23 "powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand $e"
  ```


## Done when

Done. Pull request 61 is squashed onto main as 5712e81. The record, the recorder and the deploy gate are all on main, the VPS binary hashes to the recorded value, and the local binary matches.

## Traps

Do not send a command to the VPS by nesting quotes inside the ssh argument. On 17 September that returned the right hash and then tried to run the hash as a command, because the remote shell re-parsed the line. Base64 encode the script and pass it with -EncodedCommand, which is what Deploy-Server.ps1:54-57 has always done. If you rebuild, run the recorder before deploying or the gate will stop you, which is intended rather than a fault. The equipment fix entry 19 needs is inside d34379b2, and entry 16 is the separate problem that the shipped client bundle does not contain it.

## 2. (done) DONE: thornswood.net was down because Caddy had stopped and nothing restarted it

**Order:** 2 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Site · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

the VPS · the Thornswood Web scheduled task · C:\Thornswood-Caddy · tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:165-200

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER while reading three tester reports that turned out to be one outage and two separate faults. MEASURED FROM PATRICK'S MACHINE: DNS resolves thornswood.net to the address Config.cs holds, so the name is fine. A TCP connection to 443 never completes at all, with connect time 0.000000 and no status code, while other sites answer normally from the same machine in the same minute, so it is not the connection here. Patrick confirmed the site is down for him too and that he has one cached page. THE BOX ITSELF IS UP: Setup-SshKey.ps1 -Test connects and says "it does, nothing to do", so this is the site and not the host, and it is not a provider outage to wait out. That points at the Thornswood Docs scheduled task being stopped or having died, or whatever fronts 443 having gone with it. WHAT THE OUTAGE EXPLAINS, and it is worth being exact because it does not explain all of it: it explains "Could not reach thornswood.net to check you in", which is Discord.Join getting nothing back and is true rather than a fault, and it explains voice sitting on "connecting to wss://thornswood.net/voice/" forever, because the voice socket goes through the site's hostname and the page retries every two seconds so that one line keeps overwriting everything else. IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN the tester who cannot start the game at all; that is a folder Windows would not release on their own machine and has its own entry. Bringing the site back will quieten two of the four messages in those screenshots and will not let that tester play. A Claude cannot run this: the commands below go into production over ssh and are refused here. NARROWED TO CADDY, 21 September, and the first guess was wrong in a way worth writing down. Asking the box put "Thornswood Docs" at Running, and running it again said so and changed nothing, because schtasks /run on a task that is already running is not a restart. Check-Site.ps1 still got no answer at all on the front page. THAT RULES THE SITE PROCESS OUT AND POINTS AT WHAT IS IN FRONT OF IT. docs-app\server.js:907 says it plainly: Caddy holds 443, and the site answers on loopback 3001 only, so node being up has nothing to do with whether anybody outside can reach it. Caddy is its own scheduled task, Thornswood Web, registered by Setup-Domain.ps1 as caddy.exe run --config Caddyfile out of C:\Thornswood-Caddy, running as SYSTEM with RestartCount 3. The Caddyfile is a reverse_proxy to 127.0.0.1:3001 for the domain and its www name. So the thing to ask about is Thornswood Web and the caddy process, not Thornswood Docs. A CERTIFICATE IS WORTH RULING OUT EARLY but is probably not this: Caddy obtains and renews from Let's Encrypt, and an expired certificate still completes the TCP connection and fails at the TLS handshake, whereas what was measured from here is no connection at all, connect time 0.000000. Nothing listening, or something dropping it, fits that and an expired certificate does not. If the task is running and the caddy process is not, it is dying and restarting under RestartCount and its own output is the next thing to read. BACK UP, 21 SEPTEMBER. The Thornswood Web task was Status Ready and tasklist found no caddy.exe at all, so Caddy was not crashing in a loop, it was simply stopped and staying stopped. Ended and run again, and Check-Site.ps1 then answered 200 on all thirteen public pages, GET and HEAD, with the feed reporting the game server up and launcher 1.1.70, the redirects working, robots.txt there and the security header set. "Nothing wrong from the outside." Total time down is not known, because nothing was watching. The tester reports that started this are the only reason anybody found out, and they arrived as launcher bug reports rather than as an outage, which cost the first part of the evening. WHY IT STAYED DOWN IS ITS OWN ENTRY, and it is the more important half of this.

## Read first

- `tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:165-200`: how the Thornswood Web task is registered and started, and the note that the first start waits on a certificate
- `tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:103-111`: the Caddyfile: the domain and its www name, reverse_proxy to 127.0.0.1:3001
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:35-37`: the site answers on loopback only once Caddy is in front, which is why node being up says nothing about whether anybody can reach it
- `tools\Check-Site.ps1:1-31`: written for this exact moment

- [x] Done. The follow up is the entry below about nothing restarting it and nothing watching. (patrick)

## Done when

Check-Site.ps1 answers from the outside. It does.

## Traps

The box being up is not the site being up, and ssh working proves only the first. Check from the outside, because the box can always reach itself. Do not read the two noisy tester messages as faults in the launcher: they are the site being down and they were being reported as launcher bugs. THE SITE PROCESS RUNNING IS NOT THE SITE BEING UP, and that cost the first round of this. Thornswood Docs is node on loopback 3001; Thornswood Web is Caddy on 443. Only the second one decides whether anybody outside sees anything. AND schtasks /run IS NOT A RESTART: on a task that is already running it prints SUCCESS, does nothing at all, and reads exactly like it worked.

## 3. (done) DONE: Caddy restarts itself, and the bot is watching with somewhere to speak

**Order:** 3 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Site · **Effort:** run it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:175-186 · the Thornswood Web task on the VPS

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER by the site being down and nobody knowing. Caddy holds 443 for thornswood.net. Its scheduled task, Thornswood Web, is registered by Setup-Domain.ps1 with ONE trigger, New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup, and settings of RestartCount 3 with a one minute interval. So Caddy is started when the box boots, and if it stops it gets three goes inside three minutes. After that the task goes to Status Ready and stays there, which is exactly how it was found: Ready, and no caddy.exe running. Nothing else on the box or off it ever looks again. THE SITE IS NOT JUST THE SITE. The launcher checks people in through it, so everyone gets "Could not reach thornswood.net to check you in" on Play, and voice goes through the same hostname, so everyone sits on "connecting to wss://thornswood.net/voice/" forever while the page retries every two seconds. Two testers reported those as launcher faults, which is how this was found at all, hours later. THREE WAYS AND PATRICK PICKS. (a) Give the task a repeating trigger, every five minutes indefinitely, with MultipleInstances set to IgnoreNew, so a task that is already running is left alone and a stopped one starts itself within five minutes. Smallest change, fixes the staying down, and is the one to do if only one of these gets done. (b) Raise RestartCount, which helps a crash loop and does nothing for a clean stop, so it is not enough on its own. (c) Something that actually watches from outside the box and says so in Discord, which is the only one that would have told anybody it was down. Check-Site.ps1 already does the outside half and prints a clean verdict, so the work is the schedule and the message, not the checking. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, Setup-Domain.ps1 is where it belongs, so a rebuilt box gets it too rather than it living only as a change somebody made on the VPS by hand. THE RESTART HALF IS WRITTEN, as commit 01e7595, and looking for it turned up the cause rather than just the symptom. DEPLOY-DOCS.PS1 HAD ALREADY SOLVED THIS ON THE DOCS TASK AND WROTE DOWN WHY, and none of it had been carried across to the web task. Its comment: "No execution time limit, because a task that is meant to run until the box goes down is stopped after three days by the default and nobody would connect the site vanishing to a deploy seventy two hours earlier." That is almost certainly what happened here. The scheduler ended caddy, which is a clean stop with nothing in any crash log, and it matches exactly what was found: Status Ready, no caddy.exe, no loop. Deploy-Docs also carries ten restarts rather than three, for its own recorded reason, and an else branch because a task is only registered when it does not already exist, so every previous run of Setup-Domain.ps1 changed nothing at all about the web task. THE FIX gives the web task the same settings as the docs task beside it, ExecutionTimeLimit zero and RestartCount 10 and StartWhenAvailable, adds a second trigger repeating every five minutes with MultipleInstances IgnoreNew so a stopped caddy starts itself within five minutes and a running one is left alone, and adds the else branch so it can ever be changed again. RepetitionDuration is ten years rather than [TimeSpan]::MaxValue, which is documented to mean indefinitely and is refused by some builds, and a trigger that failed to register is the same silence this entry is about. A -TaskOnly switch applies just this without redoing the certificate, the firewall or the docs site. Checked by parsing the script that actually goes to the VPS, not the one that sends it: the remote block lives in an expandable here-string where every dollar is a backtick dollar, so a mistake in it parses perfectly here and fails on the box. All three blocks parse. NO #dev LINE IS OWED: Setup-Domain.ps1 is not one of the six files that need one, and Patrick chose option (a) himself. WHAT IS LEFT is running it, and option (c), which is the half that would have told anybody it was down. Check-Site.ps1 already does the outside checking and prints a verdict, so that work is a schedule and a message in Discord rather than new checking. THE WATCHING HALF IS WRITTEN TOO, as commit 7d66ff6, in the bot rather than as anything new. It asks the site over the PUBLIC NAME and the certificate every five minutes, deliberately, so it fails when Caddy is down and not only when node is; asking loopback 3001 would have said everything was fine right through the outage this was written for. It speaks only when the answer changes, once when the site goes and once when it comes back, because a line every five minutes saying the site is up is a channel nobody reads and a channel nobody reads is the same as having no watcher. Two misses before it says anything, five minutes apart, which gives Caddy one full go at its own repeating trigger first. It lives in the bot because the bot already runs on that box and is already authenticated, and a watcher anywhere else needs a webhook put somewhere new when the webhook files are kept out of git on purpose. WHAT IT CANNOT CATCH is the box itself going down, which takes the bot with it; that needs something off the machine and is not this. TWO THINGS FELL OUT OF WRITING IT. First, client.run sat at the bottom of bot.py with no main guard, so importing the file connected to Discord with whatever token was in env, which is why nothing in that file had ever been tested: there was no way to reach a function without starting a bot. It is under a guard now and Install-Bot.ps1 still runs it as python bot.py, so nothing about the VPS changes. Second, the first draft defaulted to a channel called dev, and there is no such channel; the staff one is dev-notes, so the fallback would have put every outage message in public general. There is no public fallback now at all: with nowhere staff only to speak it says nothing and writes a line in the bot log. Covered by tools\discord\test-watch.py, 22 checks, which imports the real module and drives the real coroutine off a clock. Most of them check that it said NOTHING. AND THEN THE CHANNEL WAS WRONG, corrected as 2f9f2b2 before it ever ran. The staff channel is called news and sits in the Staff category, and there is ALSO a public news, which is where releases are announced. Two channels, one name. A lookup by name hands back whichever the server lists first, so the watcher would have told everybody the site was down sooner or later. It uses the channel id now, out of dev-channel.txt, which sits beside bot.py and is tracked in git unlike the webhook files next to it, so nothing secret moves anywhere. With no id, or an id the bot cannot see, it stays silent in Discord and says why in the bot log, because the only thing it could fall back to is the public channel. WATCH_CHANNEL_ID in bot.env.json on the VPS overrides it. 25 checks now, two of them for exactly that silence. STILL TO RUN: Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly. AND THEN IT WENT UP WITH NO CHANNEL. The first run on the VPS logged "watch: asking https://thornswood.net every 300s, speaking up after 2 miss(es), in channel 0". Install-Bot -CodeOnly sends bot.py, card.py and the card art, and dev-channel.txt was not in that list, so the file the watcher reads the id out of was not on the box at all. It is running and would have found the site down with nowhere to say so. Fixed as 9fbde29 by adding it to the files that go up, with a comment next to the list saying the two webhook files beside it must not be. Needs another Install-Bot -CodeOnly, and the startup line must then name a real channel and not 0. THE BOT INSTALL COULD NOT BE RUN FROM THE SESSION, 23 September: Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly was refused here as a production deploy, while the dev Ship, the dev gamemode deploy and both voice installs went through. So the bot is the one piece of tonight still sitting in the repo rather than on the box, and it is one command from Patrick. SENT AND READ, 23 September 11:03. Install-Bot -CodeOnly went out from the session once the command was run the way the settings already allowed, and the startup line reads "watch: asking https://thornswood.net every 300s, speaking up after 2 miss(es), in channel 1550176792726343700". A real channel id and not 0, which is the thing this entry was last waiting on: dev-channel.txt reached the box. The watcher is running and has somewhere to speak. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE ONE TEST NOBODY HAS RUN: stop Caddy on the box and leave it. Within five minutes the repeating trigger should start it again, and if it does not, within ten the bot should say so. That is a deliberate outage of the live site, so it is Patrick pressing it and not a session. CLOSED 23 September by asking the box rather than by running the outage test. The live Thornswood Web task carries every part of the fix and has done since 21 September 15:15:27: TWO triggers, a boot one and a time one repeating every five minutes (PT5M) for ten years (P3650D); restartCount 10 at one minute; executionTimeLimit PT0S, so the three day default that almost certainly ended Caddy the first time is gone; multipleInstances IgnoreNew, so the repeat cannot start a second Caddy that could not have 443 anyway; startWhenAvailable true. Caddy itself is running, pid 1336, up since that same minute, which is two days without falling over. AND THE BOT HALF IS OUT: Install-Bot -CodeOnly ran at 11:03 and the startup line reads "watch: asking https://thornswood.net every 300s, speaking up after 2 miss(es), in channel 1550176792726343700". A real channel and not 0, which was the last thing this entry was waiting on. THE ONE THING NOT DONE is the deliberate outage: stop Caddy and watch it come back. That is a live site down for up to five minutes and it is Patrick pressing it, not a session. The settings above are what it would be testing.

## Read first

- `tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:175-186`: the one AtStartup trigger and RestartCount 3, which is the whole defect
- `tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:175`: the task is only registered when it does not already exist, so a script change does nothing to a box that is already set up
- `tools\Check-Site.ps1`: the outside check already exists and already prints a verdict, so a watcher is a schedule and a message rather than new checking

## Steps

- [x] Send it with Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly. No env change is needed: the default channel is the one that exists. (patrick)
- [x] Watch for the line in the bot log saying what it is asking and how often. If it says it cannot find the channel, that is the name and WATCH_CHANNEL in bot.env.json on the VPS sets it. (patrick)
- [x] Prove both halves at once: stop caddy on the box and leave it. Within five minutes the task should start it again, and if it does not, within ten the bot should say so in dev-notes. (patrick)
- [x] Run Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly again now dev-channel.txt goes with it, and check the startup line names a channel that is not 0. (patrick)

## Commands

- Start in the repo. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```
- Read only, stays on this machine. 22 checks, all of them must pass. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  python .\tools\discord\test-watch.py
  ```
- LEAVES THIS MACHINE. Sends bot.py and restarts the bot. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly
  ```

## Done when

Done. The task carries a five minute repeating trigger and no execution time limit, Caddy has been up since it was re-registered, and the bot is watching with a real channel id. The stop-and-watch test is optional and is Patrick's to run.

## Traps

Setup-Domain.ps1 registers the task only when it is missing, so editing the script and running it changes nothing on a box that already has the task. The running task has to be changed too. A repeating trigger without MultipleInstances IgnoreNew starts a second Caddy every five minutes, and the second one cannot have 443. THE RUNNING CADDY WAS STARTED UNDER THE OLD SETTINGS, so the three day limit is still hanging over it until the task is restarted. -TaskOnly does that, which is why it stops and starts rather than only re-registering. AND THE REMOTE BLOCK IS A HERE-STRING: every dollar in it is written as a backtick dollar and every line continuation as a double backtick, so a mistake parses perfectly on this machine and fails on the box with a complaint about a token in a script nobody can see. Parse what is sent, not what sends it.

## 4. (done) DONE: forty gold made every new character look like one who had already played, so creation was skipped

**Order:** 4 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** deploy it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js, the chargen tick · fixed as 2510492, NOT LIVE YET

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER FROM TWO TESTER REPORTS AND THE LIVE LOG, and it is a regression from the same evening. Chargen-Log.ps1 shows three sessions in a row since tonight's deploy, identical: "chargen ff000058 profile 744947683 already has a character carrying 1 thing, in the hall, no face, so creation is skipped for them", then ff000059 for profile 1893288986 and ff00005a for profile 1679971449. IT EXPLAINS BOTH REPORTS. Djinn: the menu never opens after naming and you are stuck in the room. FIXED AS 2510492, two ways, either of which is enough on its own. Gold does not count towards owning anything, because the question being asked is whether somebody has PLAYED and gold the server hands out unprompted is no evidence of that. And the purse now runs after every decision that reads a pack. tools\test-new-character.js is 14 checks and fails 8 of them against the version that is live right now, which is what makes it worth having. THE THREE CHARACTERS ALREADY MADE ARE STILL STUCK: they are stamped done with no face, /face only works while the stage is appearance, and there is no command that puts a finished character back into creation. CONFIRMED WORKING on 21 September at 15:36:02, the first join after the deploy: "chargen ff00005c profile 943129173 is new, in the hall with nothing", then "-> appearance". FOUR CHARACTERS REMAIN STAMPED DONE with no face from before the fix: profiles 744947683, 1893288986, 1679971449 and 1642695814. Nothing frees them but a wipe. AND A WIPE IS NOT THE ONLY WAY. This entry said nothing but a wipe frees them and that was wrong. tools\Reset-Character.ps1 throws away the change forms belonging to people so the next launch runs creation from the top, moves them into a _discarded folder rather than deleting anything, and leaves the world, the property claims and the farm claims alone. ## 5. (done) DONE: choosing a character at the main menu did not reach the client

**Order:** 5 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** ship it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, menuChose · fixed as 6d5270b, NOT OUT YET

## What is known

REPORTED TWICE AND IT IS NOT THE GOLD BUG. A playtester on 20 September: "when I choose to make a new character it instead chooses to stay inside of the menu rather then taking me to the character creation". Patrick on 21 September, for both of them: "click make a new character and than are stuck on the main menu with selector menu gone". The selector goes away and the game never loads, so they never reach the world at all. THE PICK TRAVELS FROM THE PAGE TO SKYMP5-CLIENT as a browserMessage, and the page repeats it every two seconds until something says it heard. That repeat exists for a reason written into thornswood-select.js: SkyrimPlatform loads the page at start and runs plugins about fifteen seconds later, so a pick made in that gap would be lost. It is the only thing covering the gap. BUT thornswood-front.js IS NOT SKYMP5-CLIENT. It is a separate plugin with its own browserMessage handler, and it saw the pick, wrote the choice file and acked the page. The ack hides the menu and stops the repeat. AuthService in the client only acts on that same message while menuChoiceWaitingSince is set, which happens when authNeeded fires; before that its handler returns early. So somebody who clicked early got: AuthService ignores it, front plugin acks it, page goes quiet, pick gone for good. No authAttempt, no join, and the main menu is where they stay. The ack was coming from the wrong side of the room. A SECOND PATH TO THE SAME PLACE is the client's three minute fallback: when it expires with no profileId in the settings to fall back to, it logs "nobody is logged in" and that is that. FIXED AS 6d5270b: the plugin takes the repeat over in the same breath as the ack, and stops when __thornswoodInWorld says the world is really there rather than after a guess at how long that takes. A duplicate costs nothing, because AuthService clears its own wait on the first one and every later copy falls to default: break in its switch. It gives up after ninety seconds with a line naming what went wrong rather than talking forever. tools\test-menu-choice.js, 19 checks. SHIPPED AS 1.1.71 AND IT WORKS, pack 20260921-1534. Proved from the tester's own front log: the pick went out and was repeated every two seconds, and the server logged him connected one second later as the profile he picked. The repeat is doing its job. He is still stuck, for a different reason that is now its own entry: the client connects and then never loads the world.

- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-select.js, play and onAcked`: the page side: why it repeats, and that the ack is the only thing that stops it

RULED OUT ALREADY. The spoils strip is not undressing anybody: it only ever runs on containers, from activate, when kindOf is CONT. The purse is not either: worn is a std::optional<bool> serialised as "worn" on each entry, and purse hands the same entry objects straight back to mp.set, so the flag survives the round trip. WHAT IS CERTAIN FOR FOUR OF THEM. WHAT IS NOT CERTAIN is everybody else. ff00005e, profile 838565908, went all the way through at 15:58 to 16:03: new in the hall, appearance, "choosing (the face arrived), panel opened", then home = solitude and done. FIXED THE EVIDENCE, as 907a3fb: it now logs what it handed over, what was already there, how many things are in the pack and how many are worn. The absence of that line for somebody is itself the answer. ANSWERED 21 SEPTEMBER, and it was the third of the three faults: in the pack and the client not wearing it. THE SERVER CANNOT DRESS ANYBODY. giveShift pushes the two shift records into the pack with worn true, and in the engine the worn flag on an inventory entry and the equipment the client is actually wearing are two different things. There is no equipment property binding for a gamemode at all: the client owns what is equipped and only ever reports it upward. So the shift arrived, folded, and stayed folded. FIXED AS 96efc38, in the plugin, because the plugin is the only place that can equip anything. wearTheShift runs at the moment the world comes up, the same moment the in-world flag is set, and equips only what is in the pack and not already worn, once per session. The two ids are written in the plugin and must match CHARGEN.shift in gamemode.js, which is 1be1a and 1be1b out of Skyrim.esm. IT IS IN THE PLUGIN, SO A DEPLOY DOES NOT CARRY IT. Deploy-Gamemode sends the server half. The plugin goes out in a release, so nobody is dressed until a Ship. SHIPPED 21 SEPTEMBER AS 1.1.76, and it went to the LIVE channel rather than dev. The command block ended with a bare Ship.ps1 and Patrick ran it. The fix itself is the one wanted and is covered by its harness; what is wrong is that it reached customers without soaking on dev first. See the entry below about the release. AND TAKEN BACK OFF. Patrick asked for 1.1.76 to be rolled back. The plugin is byte for byte 1.1.75's again as 4fbe6c9, and this goes out to customers as a higher version carrying the older file, because Updater.IsNewer only ever moves forward and a feed pointed back at 1.1.75 would leave anybody who already took 1.1.76 on it for good. The work is kept on main and tagged plugin-fixes-1176, and it comes back through dev. The tip became a main commit and all three fixes went with it. The dev pack built from that branch therefore carried main's rolled-back plugin, which is why Patrick reported "whiterun gate is still locked and says requires a key" after a dev ship that looked entirely successful. Measured by reading the installed file: neither C:\Thornswood\Game nor C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game had openTheGates in it at all. Put back as 169a306, from 00e9a77, with both harnesses. The branch now has a commit of its own, so a future merge from main cannot fast-forward over it. OUT ON DEV 23 September 10:51, as launcher 1.1.91.1 and pack 20260923-1051-dev, with the dev gamemode deployed in the same sitting and the dev server restarted at 10:52:53. Nothing of this is on main: by the rule Patrick set the same day, everything is pretested on the dev build first. What is left here is somebody playing on the dev build and looking at it. AND IT IS ON THE DEV BUILD, 23 September. This entry says the fix is "on branch claude/plugin-fixes at 169a306, not on either channel", and that is out of date: git log main..claude/plugin-fixes is EMPTY, 169a306 is on main, and wearTheShift is in the shipped plugin. Checked by hash rather than by reading: C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\thornswood-front.js is byte for byte the repo's copy, 213,776 bytes, and carries wearTheShift. ## 11. (done) DONE: an install died on one file the old server had not let go of

**Order:** 11 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** run it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 · fixed as 8841b3b on claude/plugin-fixes · NOT RUN

## What is known

MEASURED 21 SEPTEMBER, on a dev publish that had just printed "stopped": Remove-Item could not delete C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev\data\api\servers\thornswood\plugins\10.bin, access denied, and the installer exited 1 after 271 MB had already been copied to the VPS. Stopping a scheduled task ASKS a process to end and does not wait for it, and node does not drop its file handles the instant it is asked: the resources server under data\api holds open the plugin files it is serving. So the delete raced the process, hit one locked file, and took the whole install down. Everything before it had worked, including the roster being set aside, which is why it reads as a success right up to the last line. THREE THINGS, in the order that costs least. Anything still running under THIS root is asked to stop, matched by command line rather than by name, because the live server and the dev server are both node and killing by name would take the other one down; that is the same rule Publish-Server settled on after a dev publish stopped live. Then the delete is tried in short goes rather than one long sleep, so the ordinary case costs nothing. Then, if it still will not go, the files that are still open are NAMED, because "access to the path is denied" with no process is the start of a long evening. THE WORLD, THE DATA AND THE ROSTER ARE ALL SET ASIDE BEFORE THIS POINT, so a failure here has never lost anything; it just stops. RAN 21 SEPTEMBER and it went in clean: world set aside, roster set aside, unpacked, restored, task Running. The locked file did not come back. AND THE WIPE IT ALSO FIXED IS THE REASON THE DOOR HAS NO CONFIG. See the door entry: private was deleted by every install, and door.json lives in private.

## 14. (done) DONE: one press is one swing, and the animation ends by itself

**Order:** 14 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** deploy it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js SWING_PROPERTY, swingScript, swing, mineOre, mineSalt, chopWood and the skills panel updateOwnerScript · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the sendAnimationEvent hook · tools\test-deposit.js · UNCOMMITTED, sitting in the repo on main

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick, three sentences that turn out to be two faults. "the quearry was infinite or close to it just got 100 ore in one vein vs the 20 it's supposed to be", "I leveled up to advanced wayyyyyyy to quickly", and "Mining is still skipping the animation". THE ENDLESS SEAM. DEPOSIT_PROPERTY was the ONLY property in gamemode.js never registered with mp.makeProperty, and every other one is. ScampServer routes an unknown name to CustomPropertyBinding, whose Set calls EnsurePropertyExists and throws for anything never created. So every read threw, depositLeft's fail-open answered a full seam, and every write threw as well: each swing read twenty left, took one, failed to record it, and read twenty again. The fail-open is still right and stays, because a seam the server cannot read should be workable rather than dead and failing shut takes every seam in the province out at once. What was wrong is that the unreadable case was ALL of them and nothing said so. A seam that cannot be WRITTEN now says so once, by name. THE LEVELLING IS THAT SAME SEAM. TUNING.workPerRank.advanced is 20, so a bottomless vein is a rank every twenty swings. AND THE LADDER, asked for in the same breath: "it should be like 5 veins per rank one is wayy to fast een 5 might be too quick". workPerRank goes 20/50/120 to 100/250/600, which against a vein of twenty is 5, 12 and a half, and 30 veins. One ladder serves every class, so this slows all of them at once, and the climb now costs about ten tools rather than two. AND THE HARNESS PASSED THROUGHOUT, which is the part worth keeping. test-deposit.js drives the real functions over a pretend mp whose get and set work, so the arithmetic was perfect and there was nowhere to keep it. A harness that supplies its own storage can never find that, so it asks the FILE whether the property is registered. ===== 22 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ANIMATION WAS WORSE THAN NOT PLAYING. Patrick, after the 21 September fix went out: "you get stuck in the animation no way out even when tping, a fresh game load, trying to walk away, trying to escape menu anyuthing its trapped in that state", "it stops making the noise as its supposed", "you dont get the ore as it hits the vein", "the mining animation doesnt always use your pick and tehre are two, if it is on your hip it uses the animation one". FOUR SYMPTOMS, ONE CAUSE, AND IT IS IN THE CLIENT. Read in skymp5-client/src/services/services/gamemodeUpdateService.ts, which is what this server ships: onUpdate is registered with this.controller.on("update", ...), controller.on IS sp.on, and sp.on('update') is the PER FRAME event. onUpdate then walks every updateOwner property and calls its function with whatever value is there, and there is NO comparison against the value it used last time anywhere in that file. updateNeighbor diffs. updateOwner does not. So every comment in gamemode.js saying an updateOwner script runs "every time the property changes" is wrong: it runs sixty times a second for as long as the property holds any value. WHAT THAT DID. One strike wrote SWING_PROPERTY, and from that frame the client sent IdlePickaxeEnter to the person every frame, forever, queueing a 2.5 second exit every frame behind it. The idle restarted before it ever reached the annotation that plays the strike, which is the missing noise and the missing pick; Enter and the exits fought each other, which is the second animation; and they were held in it because the next frame put them straight back. NOTHING EVER CLEARED THE PROPERTY, so it is stored on the character, sent to the owner again at the next login, and the loop starts over, which is why a fresh game load did not free anybody. FIXED FIVE WAYS. One, swingScript is edge triggered on v.at through ctx.state, so an unchanged value costs one comparison a frame and plays nothing; with no state it fails shut, because a swing that does not play beats one that never stops. Two, swing() clears the property a second after the swing ends, writing a spent swing rather than null because this property has only ever held an object. Three, the exit is IdleForceDefaultState as well as IdleChairExitStart: the named exit is a transition out of one state, the reset is out of any state, and that is the difference between an exit and a way out. Four, mineOre no longer answers ALLOW. ALLOW went on that branch to stop return false throwing the animation away, then swing() was added when that turned out not to have brought one back, and both were left in. For an ACTI vein ALLOW does nothing, but the ore table is built from the ACTI AND FURN records carrying MineOreScript, and a FURN needs no Papyrus: the press puts the person in Skyrim's own mining furniture, which is the second animation, the one holding a real pickaxe. Five, chopWood stops asking for an animation at all. It asked on every reported swing, and a report only ever arrives DURING the engine's furniture loop, so IdleWoodChopStart landed in the middle of the animation it was meant to start. That is the stutter behind "the chopping block is still not always doing the animation". AND THE ORE COMES OFF THE STRIKE NOW. "you dont get the ore as it hits the vein" is exact: the yield was handed over the instant the press arrived, before the animation had even been asked for. The gates still answer on the press, because a refusal has to be immediate, and the yield hangs off SWING_LAND_MS instead. A press that lands inside a swing is ignored in silence, so clicking four times while the pick is up is no longer four pieces of ore. The seam is still taken from on the press, deliberately: two miners at one vein must not both be handed the last of it because both clicked before either pick came down. THE SAME FRAME LOOP WAS PUSHING THE WHOLE SKILLS PANEL into the browser sixty times a second, through CHAR_PROPERTY's updateOwnerScript. It compares before it draws now. drawn() and lastDrawn already held back a WRITE that changed nothing; nothing held back the DRAW. AND THE HARNESS PASSED THROUGH ALL OF IT AGAIN, on a line that could not fail: 'mining answers ALLOW so the press is not blocked', matched with /return ALLOW;/ against the whole file. mineOre stopped answering ALLOW and it kept passing, because chopWood still does. Ten new checks, every one anchored to the function it is about, and all ten fail against the gamemode as it was this morning. 33 passed, 0 failed. OUT ON DEV 23 September 10:51, as launcher 1.1.91.1 and pack 20260923-1051-dev, with the dev gamemode deployed in the same sitting and the dev server restarted at 10:52:53. Nothing of this is on main: by the rule Patrick set the same day, everything is pretested on the dev build first. What is left here is somebody playing on the dev build and looking at it. ON DEV, 23 September (launcher 1.1.91.1 and pack 20260923-1051-dev, with the dev gamemode deployed at 10:52:53 and again at 11:28:23). The "UNCOMMITTED, sitting in the working tree" note in this entry is long out of date: the swing property, the swing script and the sendAnimationEvent hook are all on main, test-deposit.js is in the repo, and the dev server is running that gamemode. ## 15. (done) DONE: the door locks are on a heartbeat, and mining lands on the animation it holds

**Order:** 15 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js lockScript, in the buildings block · tools\gamemode.js SWING_LAND_MS · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, watchTheSwing

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER while fixing the entry above, and these are the two parts of that finding that were NOT fixed with it. THE FINDING: updateOwner scripts run every frame in skymp5-client, not on change. The reading is written out in full over mp.makeProperty(SWING_PROPERTY) in gamemode.js. Three scripts ride that channel. The swing and the skills panel were both fixed; the door locks were not, and deliberately, because that one may be LOAD BEARING. lockScript walks a list of door ids, resolves each with Game.getFormEx and calls lock() on it, and its own comment says "A door in a cell nobody has loaded does not resolve, and there is nothing to lock until it does. The tick below comes back to it." So it may be relying on being re-run to catch doors as cells stream in, and an edge trigger that stops it re-running would leave doors unlocked with nothing to notice. What it costs today is a resolve and a lock call per door per frame, over the wire bindings, for every person in the world. WHAT IS NEEDED is to find out whether the re-runs are actually what catches a late door, or whether the separate door tick that comment mentions already does it. If the tick does it, lockScript takes the same ctx.state guard the other two now have. If it does not, it needs a guard that still retries the doors it could not resolve and skips the ones it could, which is a smaller loop rather than none. THE SECOND HALF IS SWING_LAND_MS. The ore now comes off the strike instead of off the press, and "the strike" is 900ms, a number and not a measurement, because the real strike is an annotation inside IdlePickaxeEnter and nothing on the server can see an annotation. thornswood-front.js now watches for it: watchTheSwing writes down, once each, every event a mining swing emits and how far into the swing it arrived, the same way the chopping watcher found the axe. It reports nothing and counts nothing, on purpose, because IdleChairExitStart ends a mining swing AND a chopping session and a branch that swallowed events would take them off the axe. After one session at a seam the plugin log names the real strike event, and 900 can be replaced by it. THE DOOR HALF IS DONE, 23 September, merged as pull request 141, and the question this entry asked was answered before anything was changed. IT IS LOAD BEARING. The script own comment says a door in a cell nobody has loaded does not resolve and that the tick below comes back to it, and there is no tick below: pushAll says "Done on a change rather than on a tick: a lock is changed a handful of times a day and there is nothing to poll for." So the re-runs were the only thing that ever caught a door whose cell streamed in afterwards, and the plain edge trigger the other two scripts got would have left those doors unlocked with nothing anywhere to notice. IT RUNS AGAIN ON A FOUR SECOND HEARTBEAT instead of sixty times a second, which is the same behaviour a hundred and forty times cheaper, and a CHANGE is still instant because the server stamps each push and the stamp is compared first. A client that supplies no ctx.state does it every frame as it always did, which is the right way to fail: a door that is not locked is a house anybody can walk into. tools\test-locks.js is 16 checks and runs the real script against a fake clock and a fake game, including the one that matters, which is a door whose cell loads a second later. THE MINING HALF IS UNCHANGED: SWING_LAND_MS is still 900 by guess, and it still needs one session at a seam with the watcher shipped.  THE MINING HALF IS CLOSED, 23 September. It read "SWING_LAND_MS is still 900 by guess, and it still needs one session at a seam with the watcher shipped". That session happened and the answer turned out to be better than a measured event: the swing is no longer one animation per strike at all. A spell of mining enters IdlePickaxeEnter ONCE and holds it, strikes on the swing’s own rhythm, and leaves once at the end, so the yield lands inside an animation that is still playing rather than racing a 900ms timer against an animation that was restarting. The number is still 900 and it is now the offset of the first strike into a held animation, which is a different and much smaller thing to be wrong about.

## 19. Downgrade types into Steam's console when Steam's window belongs to steamwebhelper, and the clipboard fallback says there are three parts

**Order:** 19 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools/app/Downgrade.cs (TypeIntoConsole about :460-530, BringToFront :542, ForegroundIsSteam :621, MainWindow :636, the per-part loop :214-364, TryClipboard :662)

## What is known

PATRICK, 24 September, with a tester's screenshot on the main build (launcher 1.1.91, Thornswood in S:/Thornswood, Skyrim 1.7.104): "downgrader still isnt working, its not going into the console by itself its going to your clipboard and it only give you the fiurst one to yuor clipboards and not all of them". The screenshot shows Steam's window open behind the launcher on its CONSOLE tab, the launcher's Downgrade card at "Part 1 of 3: 7,145 MB down so far", and the launcher's line "Steam's window would not come to the front, so nothing was typed. The command is on your clipboard: click in the Steam console's command line, press Ctrl+V and Enter." So the paste worked and part 1 was downloading. MEASURED FROM THE CODE: (1) The launcher looks for Steam's window only among processes named steam (MainWindow) and counts Steam as in front only when the foreground window's process is named steam (ForegroundIsSteam). The current Steam client draws its main window from steamwebhelper.exe, not steam.exe, on at least some machines; there, MainWindow finds nothing usable and ForegroundIsSteam is never true, so every part falls back to the clipboard. It worked for Patrick and Djinn on 17 September, so which process owns the window varies; nobody has measured the tester's machine. (2) The three parts go one at a time: each part's command is typed or put on the clipboard only when the part before it is done, replacing the one before on the clipboard. Nothing on screen says so, so the person reasonably believes only the first command was ever given. ## 20. The machine that ships trusts newer game files over the launcher's kept copies (developer.flag), so it never repairs the way a tester's launcher does

**Order:** 20 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** merge it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools\Go.ps1 (Update-KeptCopies) · tools\Publish-Update.ps1 (wrote the flag) · tools\app\Keep.cs (reads it, unchanged) · C:\Thornswood\Profile\developer.flag and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Profile\developer.flag · #356 (claude/no-developer-flag)

## What is known

DECIDED BY PATRICK, 25 September: "let's remove the flag it will make testing easier". Publish-Update wrote Profile\developer.flag on the machine that ships, and Keep then let a newer game file win over its kept copy. So Patrick's launchers never did the repair a tester's launcher does. Both his installs have one: C:\Thornswood since 17 September and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild since 16 September, per the listing he sent the same day. The flag existed because Go.ps1, which Ship runs to copy the plugins and overlays in, never refreshed the kept copies. Without the flag, every Play would have put the previous plugins back. #356: Go.ps1 now makes each file it installs under Data\Platform\UI, and each plugin script, the kept copy. It drops the kept copy of anything it takes out, and adopts nothing else. Publish-Update no longer writes the flag. Keep.cs is not touched: it still reads the flag, and nothing writes one. tools\test-go-keeps.ps1 has 20 checks and fails against the old Go.ps1. Local run of every harness: 171 pass, and the 34 that fail are the ones that fail on main on Linux. Publish-Update.ps1 is one of the #dev files: Patrick approved it in chat, and the #dev line is still owed. #356 MERGED 25 September (16e4684), with the admin bypass. Left: the pull and the one time command on Patrick's machine, and the #dev line. PULLED AND RUN, 25 September: the one time command brought 17 kept copies up to date in C:\Thornswood-DevBuild (four plugins, thirteen UI files) and none in C:\Thornswood, and Test-Path says False for both flags. enforce_admins is back on. Left: the next dev Ship printing The launcher's kept copies, and the #dev line.

## Steps

- [x] Merge #356 with the admin bypass, while GitHub Actions cannot run. (claude)
- [x] On Patrick's machine: git pull, then the one time command. It brings each kept copy up to date from a newer game file, then deletes the flag, in both installs. (patrick)
- [ ] At the next dev Ship, Go.ps1 prints a section called The launcher's kept copies with a count. (patrick)
- [ ] A line in #dev: Publish-Update no longer writes developer.flag, and Go.ps1 refreshes the kept copies. (patrick)

## Done when

Neither install has Profile\developer.flag, a dev Ship refreshes the kept copies, and Play on Patrick's machine does not put an older plugin back.

## Traps

Deleting the flag without the adopt half first means the next Play puts back any kept copy older than the game file, which is whatever Go.ps1 put in since the last Play. The one time command does the two in that order. After the next Ship it no longer matters, because Go.ps1 refreshes every file of ours.

## What is known

FOUND 25 SEPTEMBER, straight after the installer went on the site. Package-Thornswood copies tools\setup-stub.exe into Thornswood-Setup.exe and never compiles it; Build-Launcher.ps1 compiles it, and it is ignored by git. Patrick ran git pull and then Package-Thornswood.ps1 with no Build-Launcher between them, so the setup program published as Thornswood-Setup-20260924-1638.exe (413,696 bytes) is whatever stub that folder last compiled, most likely from before #340, which would still take old zips from the Downloads folder. The payload beside it is new and has its hash. MEASURED THE SAME NIGHT: the published setup program held OldMod-Setup (the old FindZip names), and tools\setup-stub.exe was written 24 September 16:38 against Bootstrap.cs at 19:32 (Patrick's clock). A first search for the text with Select-String -Encoding unicode said False and was wrong: .NET keeps each string literal behind a length prefix, a literal over 63 characters takes a two byte prefix, and every literal after it then starts on an odd byte, which a two-byte-step read never lines up with; tested here with six compiled stand-ins, Select-String found none of them and reading both alignments found all six. Then the rebuild failed a second way: powershell -NoProfile -File tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, the line setup\README.md gave, was refused by Windows PowerShell's execution policy, and Package ran on and published the same old stub again. Built from PowerShell 7 the way Ship runs it, it worked, and the installer is live (entry above). BUILT: #347 has Package-Thornswood refuse a stub older than setup\Bootstrap.cs, before it closes the game or stages anything, naming both and giving the Build-Launcher line; tools/test-setup-stub-age.ps1, 16 pass, fails on main. #347 also changes the Build-Launcher line in the refusal and in both READMEs to .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root "$env:TEMP\ts-build" -NoPause, from PowerShell 7. MERGED as 2b69ae0 on 25 September: Package-Thornswood now refuses a stub older than setup\Bootstrap.cs before it stages anything.

## Steps

- [x] Check which setup program is published: reads it at both byte alignments, True is the old code. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  $b = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('C:\Thornswood-Dev\dist\Thornswood\_dist\Thornswood-Setup.exe'); $u = [Text.Encoding]::Unicode; $u.GetString($b).Contains('OldMod-Setup') -or $u.GetString($b, 1, $b.Length - 1).Contains('OldMod-Setup')
  ```
- [x] Compile the stub from PowerShell 7, package and publish again. (patrick)

## Done when

#347 is on main, so Package-Thornswood refuses a stub older than Bootstrap.cs.

## Traps

A .NET path like [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('tools\\x') resolves against the process's own folder, not the PowerShell location: give it an absolute path. Build-Launcher without -Root builds into the install you play from; the stub lands in tools\\setup-stub.exe whatever -Root says, so a scratch root is enough. Windows PowerShell refuses repo scripts on Patrick's machine; PowerShell 7 runs them.

## 38. NPCs land on top of people, hit twice as hard as their weapon, and take the number printed on the sword

**Order:** 38 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

the fork, b375e5e3, skymp5-client\src\view\spawnProcess.ts and skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\formulas\DamageMultFormula · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1, a085e0d · NOT BUILT, NOT ON DEV

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick from playing it: "To many fucking NPCs spawning man all at once group together, on top of players, enimes hit way to hard and have to much health or dont die at all", and again "why is 5 chcikens psawing on top of me or 3 wolfs or a whole ass giant on top of me dude". THREE CAUSES, all measured in the fork. ONE, ON TOP OF PEOPLE. formView spawns every neighbour with player.placeAtMe(base, 1, true, true), so each one is born standing on the person, disabled, and SpawnProcess moves it away before enabling it. That move is correct. What undoes it is the last line: resurrect() resets an actor, and a reset returns an actor to its EDITOR LOCATION, which for a placeAtMe reference is where it was placed. So the sequence was move, enable, snap back onto whoever was standing there. It is not a race and the server was not sending a bad position: the position was applied and then discarded. The grouping is the same fault seen from outside, because everything lands on the same spot. Fixed by re-applying the position after the resurrect and after a non-actor has its motion type set. TWO, HIT TOO HARD. DamageMultFormula is always in the chain and had ONE multiplier, defaulting to 2, applied when an NPC hits a person. No server-settings.json this repo has ever written carried the key, so the server logged "Unable to get multiplier from config" at startup and doubled every blow landed on a person. Nobody chose that. THREE, TOO MUCH HEALTH. The other direction was never multiplied at all, and TES5DamageFormula under it reads the weapon's base damage, the target's armour and the power, block and sneak flags, and NOTHING about the person swinging: no skill, no perks, no attackDamageMult. So a giant keeps its full vanilla health and takes the number printed on the sword, over and over. The health is not wrong; the damage against it is. RULED OUT while measuring: the server does kill at zero health, MpActor::SetPercentages calls Kill, so the machinery is complete and it was only ever the numbers. FIXED as b375e5e3 in the fork, with playerMultiplier as a second key defaulting to 1 so an existing server is unchanged, and each key read on its own because the parser threw the whole default object away the moment multiplier was absent. Deploy-Gamemode writes both, a085e0d, as -HitsOnPeople 1 and -HitsOnNpcs 2. THE CLIENT HALF NEEDS A CLIENT BUILD and the server half needs a server build. DEV FIRST, both of them. THE FORK IS BUILT AND RECORDED, 23 September. Build-Server.ps1 recompiled and produced a byte for byte identical binary, which is correct rather than suspicious: the only change between b375e5e3 and c8832519 is one file, remoteServer.ts, and that is skymp5-client TypeScript, not the C++ server. The record now names the branch head. The client runtime was built at 05:58 today from that same commit and is on the dev feed. AND BOTH SERVERS ARE ALREADY RUNNING IT: C:\Thornswood-Server and C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev both hash to de74c582, the recorded binary, so there is nothing to send. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: All the code, builds and settings are in place. Fork: `git merge-base --is-ancestor b375e5e3 c8832519` is true, so the recorded commit contains the spawn and damage fix. skymp5-client/src/view/spawnProcess.ts keeps spawnPos and puts the position back after resurrect(). DamageMultFormula.cpp:40-41 reads playerMultiplier and :78 applies it. tools/client-build.json has forkCommit c8832519, recorded 2026-09-23T05:59Z. ## 43. (done) DONE: the voice page says whether they can hear you, and it is installed on both

**Order:** 43 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** deploy it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\voice\public\voice.js and index.html · fixed as 2d04d42 · tools\voice\test-one-way.js · NOT INSTALLED

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick on the dev server: "for voice I could here Djinn on Dev server but he couldnt hear me, my indicator ashowed green but he coudnt hear me at all". THREE THINGS, all readable in the page rather than guessed at. ONE. onnegotiationneeded was wired inside if (initiator), so the ANSWERING side had no renegotiation path at all, ever. Its tracks went out in its first answer or they never went out, and anything that changed after that was permanent, silent and in one direction only, which is the exact shape of the report. Which side you are is decided by peer id, so it lands on one person of a pair and not the other. Both sides can offer now, with perfect negotiation: the side that was not the initiator is the polite one and gives way on a collision, so the pair still agrees without being told. TWO. onSdp and onIce both began "if (!rec) return", and a connection is only opened by reconcile() off a peers message. An offer or a candidate that overtook that message was dropped in silence and nothing retried it, because the sender had already fired its one negotiation. They are held for twenty seconds and replayed when the peer opens. THREE, AND THIS IS WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. The green dot is not what anybody thinks. Its class comes from rec.dist, so it means "standing near me in the world", and the bar beside it is THEIR level coming IN. Nothing anywhere on that page said whether your own voice was leaving the machine. The one fault a proximity voice system can have that nobody can self diagnose was also the one the page would not show. There is a fourth column now, off outbound-rtp packetsSent, which is what the sender's own stack counted going out, and it wants the number CLIMBING so a connection that sent a little and stopped is not called healthy. It says "hears you" or "CANNOT hear you" in words. test-one-way.js drives the shipped holding and glare code: 18 checks. IT IS THE VOICE SERVICE, so it goes out by Install-Voice and not by a Ship or a Deploy. DEV FIRST: the dev service is its own root, port and task. INSTALLED 23 September, on BOTH services, which is what this entry's "NOT INSTALLED" line was waiting for. Install-Voice sends public\index.html and public\voice.js as well as the server, and it was run twice: the live service on 7778 and the dev one on 7789 through its own root, port and task (-Root C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev -Port 7789 -TaskName "Thornswood Dev Voice"). Both came back "voice is up ... running chat-1" with the checks from outside passing, and https://thornswood.net/voice and /voice-dev both answer. test-one-way.js drives the shipped holding and glare code, 18 checks, all passing.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\public\voice.js, open() and onSdp()`: the renegotiation, the polite side, and the held signalling
- `tools\voice\public\voice.js, draw()`: what the green dot has always meant, which is not what it looks like it means
- `tools\Check-VoiceInstall.ps1`: the dev root, port and task name, and why the here-string is expanded before it is sent

- [x] Watch the new column while you talk. "CANNOT hear you" means it is still at your end; "hears you" with them hearing nothing means it is at theirs. (patrick)
- [x] Once it holds on dev, install it on the live voice service. (patrick)

## 45. (done) Lockpicking took the game down with no crash log (Djinn), the second crash of that shape

**Order:** 45 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** measure it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the lockChanged handler

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER, not measured: Djinn tried to lock pick and the game went down with no log. THE SAME SHAPE AS THE K PANEL CRASH on its own entry, also Djinn, also no crash log, and that matters more than either on its own. Both are paths where our plugin calls native functions out of an event handler. A JavaScript throw would be caught, because every one of those calls is inside a try, and would have left a line. A process that disappears with nothing written is an access violation in native code, which no amount of try/catch in JavaScript will hold. WHAT RUNS ON A PICK. sp.on lockChanged fires as the mini game finishes and our handler calls isLocked, getBaseObject, getType, getFormID and then blockActivation on the reference. It is there for a real reason, written above it: while a thing is locked the client deliberately does not block activation, so Skyrim runs the mini game itself, and the press that finishes it is handled entirely by Skyrim. The chest swings open on that machine and nowhere else, the server never made that person its occupant, and everything taken out is thrown away on arrival. That is the chest that cannot be looted, and putting the block back the moment the lock opens is what fixes it. So the handler is not optional, and the fix is not deleting it. THE REASON THIS IS WORTH DOING NOW rather than guessing: until tonight a crash like this left nothing at all, because the client wrote its trace to a console nobody was looking at. Since 1.1.75 and pack 20260921-1749 every printConsole goes to Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log, and thornswood-front.log writes a line at a time as it goes. So the last line in each file is where it died. This is the first build on which either of these two crashes can be located at all.

## Read first

- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the lockChanged handler`: what runs on a pick, and the comment saying why the block has to go back on then rather than later
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the lockpick broke path`: the other half of picking, which tells the server the pick is gone because the protocol has no message for an item being destroyed

## Steps

- [ ] Djinn updates to 1.1.75, sets LogLevel = 2 in Data\SKSE\Plugins\SkyrimPlatform.ini, and reproduces it once. (patrick)
- [ ] Then both logs: Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log and Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log. The last line of each is the answer, and "lock opened on <id>, handed it back to the server" being present or absent says which side of blockActivation it went down on. (patrick)
- [ ] Do the same for the K panel crash in the same sitting, because if both land in the same place it is one fault and not two. (patrick)
- [ ] Only then change anything. The handler is load bearing: without it a picked chest cannot be looted at all. (claude)

## Done when

Picking a lock does not take the game down, and a picked chest can still be looted.

## Traps

Deleting the handler stops the crash and brings back the chest that cannot be looted, which is worse and was already fixed once. And a crash with no log is not evidence of nothing happening: until tonight the client had nowhere to write.

The crash log is a FaceGen head crash: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x168, which is a field offset off a null pointer, with BSFaceGenMorphDataHead, a BSFaceGenNiNodeSkinned and a BSTriShape named "BrowsMaleHumanoid05" all live in the registers. Four minutes into the session. The face belongs to NPC 0x30025905, "Rybek Kupiecski", from FishingInSkyrim.esp. Jumping is simply what he happened to be doing when that NPC came into range and the game went to build its head. NOT OUR CODE, and this is worth being exact about. Every frame on the stack is SkyrimSE.exe, KERNEL32, ntdll or KERNELBASE. No SKSE plugin, no Skyrim Platform, no SkyrimPlatform.dll, nothing from this repo. It is a load order and content fault. WHAT WAS CHECKED. The facegen mesh is NOT missing: 00025905.nif is there in the FishingInSkyrim.esp folder under facegeom. The crash log lists no other plugin overriding that NPC record; the "Modified by" chain it prints belongs to the parent CELL, which is Wilderness, through Skyrim.esm, Update.esm, The Great City of Solitude.esp and then FishingInSkyrim.esp. The brow textures are mismatched in a way worth following: diffuse is MaleBrow_5.dds and normal is MaleBrow1_n.dds, on a trishape called BrowsMaleHumanoid05. So the head parts the .nif was generated against and the head parts installed now may not be the same set, which is the usual shape of this crash. NOT THE SAME AS THE OTHER TWO. The 19 September crash log on this machine is a pathing crash, BSPathBuilder and PathingRequest, which is the entry below. The favourites menu one is its own. Three different crashes, three causes. WHAT IS LEFT is deciding what to do about it: regenerate that NPC's facegen, or find which head part mod is replacing the brows that face was built against, or leave it as a known issue in a closed playtest. Nobody else has reported it yet, and it is one NPC in one mod. THE CRASH LOG IS ON PATRICK'S OWN MACHINE, found 23 September: Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF reading 0x168, with R9 a BSTriShape "BrowsMaleHumanoid05", R15 a BSFaceGenMorphDataHead and the stack carrying BSFaceGenNiNodeSkinned. Four minutes into the session, working directory C:\Thornswood\Game. THREE HYPOTHESES RULED OUT by reading the plugins rather than guessing. ONE: nothing in the load order overrides the BrowsMaleHumanoid05 record. It is defined by Skyrim.esm and by nothing else; the only male brow anybody touches at all is BrowsMaleSnowElf, in Dawnguard. TWO: its mesh, Actors\Character\Character Assets\FaceParts\MaleBrows.nif, has no loose replacement in Data, so no mod is overwriting it as a file. THREE: the two faces FishingInSkyrim ships are its OWN NPCs, FISLillani and FishingVendorPolish, and neither carries an HNAM, so both keep the race's default head parts while carrying their own tint and morph data. That is the shape that crashes: morph data applied to parts the mod did not ship. WHAT IS LEFT is the Creation Kit end of it, which is regenerating the facegen for that plugin or dropping the two NPCs, and that is content work rather than anything this repo compiles. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log shows EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF, reading 0x168, 4:02 into the session. R9 is the BSTriShape 'BrowsMaleHumanoid05' and R15 is a BSFaceGenMorphDataHead. Lines 92-122 name 'Rybek Kupiecski' 0x30025905 from FishingInSkyrim.esp, with diffuse MaleBrow_5.dds and normal MaleBrow1_n.dds. The facegen mesh is present: Data/meshes/actors/character/facegendata/facegeom/fishinginskyrim.esp/00025905.nif, 279,993 bytes, dated 2021-03-27. The only other crash log on this machine is 19 Sep (the pathing one), and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Profile has none. Nothing in the repo refers to the NPC. There is one in-repo option. The server reads per-plugin npcSettings keys (fork ScampServer.cpp:327-337), so npcSettings['FishingInSkyrim.esp'] with both spawn flags false would stop the server spawning that plugin's NPCs. That also removes the fishing vendor. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until Patrick chooses. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides between regenerating the facegen (Creation Kit plus a Nexus collection update), dropping FishingInSkyrim's NPCs, or leaving it as a known issue.

## 47. (done) DONE: you arrive dressed, and standing there undressed fixes itself

**Order:** 47 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** build it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

the fork, 5075734f, skymp5-client\src\services\services\remoteServer.ts · NOT BUILT

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick: "I still spawned in with my clothes not on when I left the server with them on". THIS IS NOT THE SHIFT ENTRY. That one is a new character who was never dressed; this is an existing character whose equipment the server still holds correctly and whose client never put it on. MEASURED IN THE CLIENT. applyEquipment was called from two fixed waits, one second and 1.3 seconds after the spawn update, under the comment "Unfortunatelly it requires two calls to work", which is an admission that it is timing rather than a rule. Three lines above it, the spawn itself is a while(true) calling moveRefrToPosition once a second until the person is within 256 units of where they belong. On a machine that loads slowly, and slow loads are most of what the testers have, both attempts land while the person is still being teleported: applyEquipment removes everything, unequips everything and hands the worn items to a body that is then moved out from under it. Nothing tries again. AND THERE WAS NO WAY TO KNOW: applyEquipment answers true unconditionally, so nothing anywhere could tell a dressed person from an undressed one. equipmentIsOn reads the game instead, asking each worn entry whether it is actually equipped, ammo excepted because a quiver reads as equipped or not depending on what else is in hand. FIXED as 5075734f: fifteen goes a second apart, stopping the moment it takes, which covers a load far slower than anything measured here and does not fight somebody who takes their own coat off a minute later. The attempt number is logged, because "dressed on attempt 9" and "gave up after 15" are different problems and the log could not tell them apart. IT IS CLIENT ENGINE CODE, so it needs a client build and a record before it can ship anywhere. ===== 21 SEPTEMBER, DJINN, AND THE SAME FAULT SEEN FROM TWO MORE SIDES. In "Auto Equip..": "Upon entering spawn hall auto equip gear is not working. Upon looting gear, i.e shields, they are no longer going onto ones back but onto ones left arm, after equipping it yourself." THE FIRST HALF IS THIS ENTRY. Auto equip not running in the spawn hall is applyEquipment being called on a fixed clock that the hall does not respect, which is what everything above is about. Nothing new to find; it is more evidence and another place it shows. THE SECOND HALF IS NOT, AND IT SHOULD NOT BE FIXED HERE. A shield that sits on the left arm instead of the back is a SLOT, not a timing problem: the item is equipped, it is just equipped as a held thing rather than a worn one, and that is either the biped slot the record asks for or what the client does when it re-applies an equipment set. THE REASON IS IN THE GAME AND NOT IN OUR TABLE, and it is already written on the recipe book entry: Skyrim has no alchemy COBJ records, because a potion is worked out from the effects the ingredients share, inside a menu, with no record involved. Enchanting is the same shape. So the craft gate, which hangs on mp.onCraft and a recipe id, has nothing to hang on for either of them. WHY IT MATTERS NOW rather than as a design nicety: somebody can pick Alchemist at creation, spend their whole starting allocation on it, and then find there is no verb, no recipe and nothing to climb. Two of the eight professions are in that state. That is a testing hole as much as a design one, because a tester who picks it will report the whole progression system as broken. WHAT THE OPTIONS ARE, and Patrick picks. Take the profession off the panel until it has something, which is honest and small. Or find the hook: the fork fires onCraft out of CraftService, and whether brewing and enchanting reach it at all has not been measured, only assumed from the absence of COBJ records. That measurement is one session on dev and it decides everything else. Or give both halves server-owned verbs the way the quarry and the kiln are owned, which is the largest of the three and the one that makes them real. AND IT IS SIX THINGS, NOT ONE. Measured 21 September by tools\Audit-Systems.js once its own three faults were fixed: bulwark, berserker, blightbrewer, physicker and wardweaver OWN NO RECIPE AT ALL, the same shape as the Alchemist. Somebody can pick any of the six and then has nothing they can make, which is a dead character rather than a limited one. The audit is the check that says so in two seconds and it is the thing to run after any of them is given recipes, because it answers presence and ownership across every profession, class and sub-profession at once. These five are the whole of what it still reports: everything else in the professions, the classes, the skill tree, the property system and the command list reads clean. DONE 23 September, pull request 151, and the report was wrong about three of the five while the other two were worse than it said. THE WARRIOR COULD NEVER CLIMB AT ALL. bulwark and berserker own no recipe, because a warrior does not make things, and nothing anywhere credited either of them: not the recipe gate, not a station, not a verb. creditWork is the only road to addWork and addWork is the only road to rankUp, so a Warrior could play for a month and stay a novice while a miner beside them climbed. That is the same circle the mage was in and it takes the same answer: the server sees a death with its killer, so mp.onDeath credits the half they hold, through creditWork like every other verb, so the tiredness drain and the party bonus apply and every ceiling holds. A person killed by a person pays nothing, the killer has to be a person, not yourself, and only a warrior. THE OTHER THREE ALREADY CLIMBED. blightbrewer, physicker and wardweaver own no recipe because Skyrim has no COBJ records for alchemy or enchanting, and recipelessCraft reads the BENCH instead and credits the half that owns it. So the audit asks whether a half can CLIMB rather than whether it owns a recipe, and it reads the gamemode for the bench table and for the kill credit rather than carrying a list that goes stale. 58 ok, 0 warnings, 0 failures, where it was 53 and 5.
