## 51. (done) DONE as far as code can take it: the black boots have a female-only patch and no male one

**Order:** 51 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

the load order · a body or feet mesh replacer against the vanilla boots record · not this repo's code

## What is known

DJINN, 21 SEPTEMBER, in "Vanilla Black boots": "Anytime you equip the 0 armor Black low cut boots your characters feet graphic disappear." A CONTENT FAULT, NOT A CODE ONE, and worth saying so first because nothing in gamemode.js or the plugins decides what a boot looks like. Equipping an item that hides the feet and draws nothing in their place is a mesh that does not exist or does not match, which is a load order question. THE USUAL CAUSE, offered as the first place to look rather than as an answer: a body replacer changes the feet mesh and the boots record still points at the vanilla one, or the armour addon covers the feet slot and its own mesh is missing for that body. The 0 armour low cut boots are clothing rather than armour, and clothing is the thing body replacers most often leave behind. WHAT MAKES IT CHEAP TO CHASE: it is one record and it is reproducible on demand, so whoever looks can equip them, see it, and go straight to which plugin last touched that record and which mesh it names. ANSWERED 23 September, by reading the plugins, the archives and Vortex's own deployment manifest. THE RECORD. Djinn's "0 armor Black low cut boots" is IATribunalUnarmoredBootsBlack, from Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp, which is Immersive Armors. Its two armoured siblings, IATribunalLightBootsBlack and IATribunalHeavyBootsBlack, share the same armor addon, IATribunalBootsBlackAA, so all three behave the same way. THE MESHES. That addon names tribunalrobes\blackmale\tribun_boots_1.nif for the male and tribunalrobes\black\tribun_bootsf_1.nif for the female. The FEMALE one is a loose file in Data. The male one is not: meshes\tribunalrobes\ contains a black folder and no blackmale folder at all, and the male mesh lives only inside Hothtrooper44_Armor_Ecksstra.bsa, which does load, because that plugin is enabled and is one of the light ones. WHO PUT THE LOOSE ONES THERE, and this is the answer: all fourteen loose meshes under tribunalrobes come from "Immersive Armours - SSE CBBE 3BA BodySlide", and every one of them is female (*f_0.nif and *f_1.nif). THE BODIES. The collection ships CBBE 3BA for female and HIMBO V5 for male. So the female boots are built for the female body this build actually uses, and the male boots are the 2016 vanilla-body mesh out of the old archive, worn over a HIMBO body. That is the disappearing feet: the boot takes the feet slot, HIMBO's feet stop being drawn, and what replaces them is a mesh shaped for a body nobody here has. THE FIX IS A COLLECTION CHANGE AND IT IS PATRICK'S: add an Immersive Armors HIMBO patch beside the CBBE one, or take the Tribunal set out. Either way it is a revision bump, because the files change for everybody.

## 52. (done) DONE: the map file that broke SkyUI was deleted from everybody

**Order:** 52 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Data\Interface\map.swf · IcePenguinWorldMap.esp, index 10 in the server's load order · SkyUI_SE.esp

## What is known

SEEN 22 SEPTEMBER, a full screen SkyUI box over the loading map: "SKYUI ERROR CODE 5. Incompatible menu file (map.swf). Please make sure you installed everything correctly and no other mod has overwritten this file. If you were using an older SkyUI version, un-install it and re-install the latest version." WHAT ERROR 5 MEANS. SkyUI checks the version of Data\Interface\map.swf and refuses one it does not recognise. It is not about SkyUI being broken or half installed; it is SkyUI saying something else's map.swf won. MEASURED, 22 September. The file is there, 98,163 bytes, dated 14 September, and it IS ours to ship: Profile\OwnGame\files.txt records it as one Vortex deployed, and it is in the publish baseline, so it goes out in packs and installers like any other collection file. It is not a leftover from another launcher, which was the first guess and was wrong. WHO PROVIDES IT. IcePenguinWorldMap.esp sits at index 10 of the server's load order, and that is A Quality World Map, which ships its own Data\Interface\map.swf. A Quality World Map against SkyUI is one of the oldest conflicts in Skyrim modding and error 5 is exactly its signature. A Quality World Map publishes a SkyUI compatible variant for this reason; whichever variant is in the collection, the one deployed here is not the one SkyUI will accept. NOT A CODE FAULT AND NOTHING IN THIS REPO DECIDES IT. gamemode.js, the plugins and the launcher have no say in which map.swf wins; the collection does. THE SAME FAMILY AS THE BLACK BOOTS entry above: a content conflict that reads as a broken build to whoever hits it, and both want somebody with the collection open rather than somebody reading code. WHAT IT COSTS IF LEFT: a full screen error box on the way in, for everybody, which reads as the server being broken and is the first thing a new tester sees. MEASURED 23 September, and it narrows the question: there is NO loose map.swf in the game folder at all. C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Interface holds the loose interface files and map.swf is not among them, and Vortex's deployment manifest names no map.swf either across its 29,428 files. So this is not a loose file conflict and Vortex cannot be asked which mod won. It is a BSA conflict: SkyUI_SE.bsa is in the folder, IcePenguinWorldMap.esp is at line 11 of the load order and that is A Quality World Map, and whichever plugin loads later wins for a file inside an archive. The next step is reading which archives carry interface/map.swf rather than opening Vortex. CLOSED 23 September by reading the pack rather than by opening Vortex. THE FILE IS GONE FROM THIS MACHINE: Data/Interface holds no map.swf at all now. AND IT WAS TAKEN OUT DELIBERATELY, from everybody: pack 20260922-2314, which is on the feed, carries a delete.txt whose entire contents are the one line Data/Interface/map.swf. Its release note says so in its own words, "Three chopping blocks are gone, and the SkyUI map error is fixed for everyone". So A Quality World Map's menu file is removed on every install that takes that update and SkyUI's own map.swf, which lives in SkyUI_SE.bsa, is the one that wins. That is the fix this entry asked for, done the smallest way: no collection revision, no mod swap, one deletion carried by the pack. WHAT IS LEFT IS A LOOK rather than a fix: open the world map in game and see that it is still the good one, since A Quality World Map's quality is in its textures and its plugin rather than in the menu file.

## Read first

- `tools\Audit-Mods.ps1`: the read only tool for asking what the collection actually contains

## Steps

- [x] Open the collection and find which mod's map.swf is deployed. Vortex will name it for that file. (patrick)
- [x] If it is A Quality World Map's plain version, switch to its SkyUI compatible variant, which exists for exactly this. (patrick)
- [x] Then bump the collection revision, because the file changes for everybody and the launcher checks revisions. (patrick)
- [x] Confirm on a fresh load that the box is gone and the world map still draws with the quality map, not the vanilla one. (patrick)


- Read only. That it is listed here is what says the collection provides it rather than another launcher. (claude)


SkyUI would stop complaining and the map would fall back to vanilla, which is a silent downgrade for everybody and much harder to notice than an error box. And do not go looking for this in the gamemode or the launcher: nothing in this repo chooses which mod's interface file wins.

## 54. (done) DONE: tools\Audit-Systems.js is committed, and it had three faults of its own

**Order:** 54 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Audit-Systems.js · committed as a97b84c

## What is known

WRITTEN 21 SEPTEMBER during the professions and property audit, and never committed. It reads gamemode.js and reports what each profession, class, sub-profession and skill tree actually carries, which is the check that says whether something is missing before anybody sits down to test it. IT HAS A DEFECT OF ITS OWN: the block it lifts for the skill tree reads only three sub-skills, so its tree numbers are wrong and anything read off them is wrong with them. UNCOMMITTED WORK IN THE REPO IS OUTSTANDING WORK, which is why this is on here rather than in a reply: it shows up in every git status and in the warning gh pr create prints, and the next person has no way to know whether it is half finished or abandoned. EITHER fix the lift and commit it, or delete it and say so. It is not shipped and nothing depends on it, so this is cheap either way. CLOSED 21 SEPTEMBER as a97b84c, and the tree lift was not the fault. THREE FAULTS, all of which made it call working things broken and hid the things that are not. ONE, lift only ever looked for an opening brace, so a declaration whose value is an ARRAY walked past its own value, matched the first brace belonging to something else hundreds of lines down, and threw. WORDS is the only caller that hits it, so the audit reported "the word list could not be read" on a file where it reads perfectly well, and nothing ever checked that a registered command is answered by anything. TWO, the tree count read Object.keys(TREE) and called the answer the sub-skills. TREE is three BRANCHES, health, magicka and stamina, each carrying five skills, so it reported three of fifteen and warned the skill tree was four fifths absent. MEASURED 21 SEPTEMBER ACROSS THREE LOGS, and every step but the last one is proved. A tester on launcher 1.1.71 picked a character at the main menu. HIS FRONT LOG: the page came up at 17:35:47, he forgot character 1642695814, picked profile 943129173 at 17:35:53, and the pick went out and kept going out every two seconds for over two minutes. THE SERVER LOG, same moment on a clock two hours behind: "15:35:52 Connecting a user 1", "15:35:52 1 logged as 943129173", then at 15:36:02 "chargen ff00005c profile 943129173 is new, in the hall with nothing" and "-> appearance". He disconnected at 15:38:52. SO THE PICK REACHED THE CLIENT, THE CLIENT CONNECTED, AND THE SERVER PUT HIM IN THE CREATION HALL CORRECTLY. What never happened is his own machine leaving the main menu, which is also why the repeat kept firing: it stops on __thornswoodInWorld and that never went true. THE SUSPECT, read in the fork and not yet proved on a machine: remoteServer.ts loads the world only when alreadyInAGame is false, and that is __thornswoodInWorld || __thornswoodUncausedLoad > 0. When it is true it stands down and leaves the moving to the other spawn path, the one that uses moveRefrToPosition. Its own comment says "At an actual main menu, which is the case this was written for, nothing changes", and the worry it was written for is real: the other way round gives an infinite loading screen, because po3_StartOnSave has already loaded the real save and asking Skyrim to revert it stops at "Reverting game". uncausedLoads counts game loads SkyrimPlatform did not ask for, and po3_StartOnSave makes one on every launch that has a save to load. If that count is above zero at a REAL main menu, the guard fires where there is no other path to hand over to and nothing loads the world at all. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE AND NOW: this is engine code in the fork that decides whether anybody can load the world, either answer breaks somebody, and it needs a client rebuild and a new tools\client-build.json. That is settled design and a #dev line first, per CLAUDE.md. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, as da823ad: the front plugin's retry line now carries inWorld and uncausedLoads, so the next report answers the question instead of raising it. If uncausedLoads reads above zero on somebody sitting at a main menu, that is the proof and the fix is a guard that can tell a main menu from a world. THE GUARD IS RULED OUT. The tester has NO SAVE AT ALL, it is a fresh install, so po3_StartOnSave loads nothing, no uncaused game load is counted, __thornswoodUncausedLoad stays 0 and alreadyInAGame is false. The guard was not what stopped him and that hypothesis is dead. THE NEXT TEST NEEDS NOTHING BUILT AND NOBODY WAITING. sp.loadGame builds a synthetic save and loads it, and it leaves the file behind: on Patrick's machine, where this works, Profile\MyGames\Saves holds exactly one file, TESMODPLATFORM-3A62F637-2196-4546-9007-69C141B9DAB2.ess, and nothing else. So look in the same folder on the machine that is stuck, remembering the launcher redirects My Games into the Thornswood Profile folder. EMPTY means loadGame was never called and the fault is above it, in whatever decides to call it or in the createActorMessage never arriving client side. A TESMODPLATFORM file THERE means loadGame ran and Skyrim refused the save, which on a fresh install points straight at the mod files being incomplete, and the baseline limbo entry is exactly a reason for a fresh install to be missing files that Patrick's is not. Those two answers go to completely different places, so this is the thing to look at before anything else is changed. AND THE GIVE UP IN THE FIX WAS ITSELF UNREACHABLE, found in the same log and fixed as aa4ee46. The resends ran from 17:35:55 to 17:38:01, which is 126 seconds, and the ninety second give up never fired once. Every resend asks the page to send its pick again, that arrives back as another menuChose, and menuChose was restarting the clock, so it was reset two seconds before it was ever due. The same shape as the chargen nudge that sat unreachable behind its own guard, in code written the same evening, which is worth saying out loud: a rescue nobody can reach is the easiest thing in this codebase to write twice. Only a new choice starts the clock now, and two checks in the harness fail against the shipped build. AND THE ONE QUESTION IT TURNS ON IS ANSWERED AUTOMATICALLY NOW, 23 September, pull request 153. This entry says the next thing to look at is whether the stuck machine has a TESMODPLATFORM save in its Profile folder, because empty means loadGame was never called and a file there means Skyrim refused the save, and those go to completely different places. Nobody can look at that without walking to the machine, so the retry line carries it: how many .ess files are in the saves folder and how many came from loadGame, beside the inWorld and uncausedLoads it already carried. The path is relative to the game folder because that is where the process stands, which also means the dev build answers about its own saves. Proved by running the reader from C:\Thornswood\Game.

## 58. (done) DONE: what a script prints is in the client log

**Order:** 58 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Client · **Effort:** ship it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

skyrim-platform ConsoleApi.cpp · skymp5-client logging.ts · Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER while chasing a tester stuck on the main menu. Every answer that evening came from the server log and from our own plugin log. The client itself says a great deal and none of it survives the session. skymp5-client's logTrace and logError go to printConsole, and ConsoleApi::PrintConsole writes to the game console and, if one is attached, a Windows console. IT DOES NOT WRITE TO skyrim-platform.log. That file exists, at Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log because the launcher redirects My Games, and it is 3,984 lines of VirtualMachine::Bind trace with not one line from any script in it. So the lines that would have answered this in seconds, "Received authNeeded event", "chooseAtMenu is set, waiting for the menu's choice", "Menu choice received", "loading game in world/cell", were written to a console nobody was looking at and then lost. AND THE ONE PLACE THEY GO IS SHUT AUTOMATICALLY: thornswood-front.js closes a console it did not open, logging "the Console Native UI Menu opened on its own and has been shut", so telling a tester to open the console and screenshot it does not work either. WHAT IT COST: three rounds of asking a tester for files, two hypotheses built from reading code and one of them wrong, and the thing still is not settled. WORTH DOING because every future client fault costs the same. Two ways in. Route printConsole into the spdlog logger that is already initialised, which is an engine change in skyrim-platform and needs a client rebuild. Or have our own front plugin write what it can reach, which is cheaper and catches less, because skymp5-client is bundled and holds its own reference to printConsole. The first is the real answer. WRITTEN AND BUILT on 21 September, approved by Patrick as lead dev in place of the #dev line this entry asked for. ConsoleApi::PrintConsole writes to the spdlog logger that main.cpp already sets up, before the console printers rather than after, because InGameConsolePrinter::Print throws when there is no ConsoleLog singleton, which is the main menu, which is exactly where this was needed. Untruncated, because the 128 character cut is right for a console line and wrong for the only record of what happened, and everything is swallowed, because a throw from inside printConsole lands in whatever was logging. Fork commit 22ff6976. IT COMPILES AND IT IS BUILT: cmake --build build --config Release --target skyrim-platform, recorded by New-ClientBuildRecord into client-build.json as ee58b2f, and Sync-Client has put the two changed files in the game folder. TWO THINGS TO KNOW. MpClientPlugin.dll changed as well and nothing in its source did: the aggregate target rebuilds it and a fresh link of the same code is different bytes at the same size, which is PE timestamps. It is recorded because it is what this commit actually builds. AND A FALSE RECORD WAS WRITTEN FIRST AND THROWN AWAY: building the skyrim_platform target with an UNDERSCORE makes the DLL but does not put it in build\dist\client, and New-ClientBuildRecord reads dist, so the first record claimed a 14 September binary came from today's commit. It looked perfectly healthy; only forkCommit changed in the diff, which is the only thing that gave it away. The target that populates dist is skyrim-platform with a HYPHEN. Never build install_client_dist, which copies into the Skyrim folder itself. STILL TO DO: the log level. The launcher now stops the level being set to silent, as d35aa64, but SkyrimPlatform.ini on this machine is LogLevel 0, which is trace, and that is 3,984 lines of VirtualMachine::Bind noise around anything worth reading. Setting it to 2 by hand makes the file usable; the launcher deliberately does not, because somebody at trace chose trace. PROVED FROM THE LOG ON THIS MACHINE, 23 September. Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log from the 10:19 session carries lines like "[10:22:03:305] [Script] [front] the Console Native UI Menu is open", which is a plugin print reaching the client log with its own timestamp. The client runtime was rebuilt from the fork at 05:58 that morning and is on the feed, so the Ship this entry was waiting for has happened. THE NOTE ABOUT LogLevel STANDS: SkyrimPlatform.ini here is 0, which is trace, and that is thousands of lines of VirtualMachine::Bind noise around anything worth reading. Setting it to 2 by hand makes the file usable and the launcher deliberately does not, because somebody at trace chose trace.

## Read first

- `skyrim-platform ConsoleApi.cpp, PrintConsole`: goes to the game console and a Windows console, and to no file
- `skyrim-platform main.cpp, InitLog`: the file sink and the level are already there, which is what makes this small
- `skymp5-client\src\logging.ts`: logTrace and logError, both straight to printConsole

## Steps

- [x] Ship it. The client runtime only reaches anybody in a release. (patrick)
- [x] Set LogLevel = 2 in Data\SKSE\Plugins\SkyrimPlatform.ini on any machine you want to read the log on. The launcher only stops it being switched off entirely. (patrick)
- [x] Then ask the stuck tester for Profile\MyGames\SKSE\skyrim-platform.log and look for "loading game in world/cell". Present means loadGame ran and Skyrim refused the save. Absent means it was never called. (patrick)
- [x] Turn the Bind trace down at some point, since it is what made the file useless at trace level in the first place. (claude)


## Done when

Done. Script prints land in skyrim-platform.log with a timestamp, seen in this machine's own log.

## Traps

The log file already exists and already has content, so it looks like it is working. It is engine trace only. Do not assume a quiet skyrim-platform.log means the client was quiet. AND THE BUILD HAS TWO TARGETS ONE CHARACTER APART. skyrim_platform builds the DLL. skyrim-platform is the one that also copies it into build\dist\client, which is the only place New-ClientBuildRecord looks. Getting that wrong writes a record that is wrong and looks right.

## 60. (done) DONE: Mouse 4 and Mouse 5 can be the voice key

**Order:** 60 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** deploy it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\app\Keys.cs the virtual key table · tools\app\Pages.cs OnCaptureMouse and Bind · merged as c8c7a11, NOT SHIPPED

## What is known

GRIM REEFER, 21 SEPTEMBER, tagged Launcher: "When in the launcher trying to change controls for voice to mouse 4 or 5 it doesn't work. It registers for other keys but not for mouse 4 or 5." OTHER KEYS WORK, WHICH IS THE USEFUL HALF OF THE REPORT. So the binding machinery is fine and the capture is what misses these two. That is the ordinary shape of this fault in WPF: a key press arrives as a KeyDown and the extra mouse buttons do not. They arrive as MouseDown with ChangedButton XButton1 and XButton2, and a control that only listens for keys never sees them at all. Nothing is broken; a case is missing. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Mouse 4 and 5 are where push to talk lives for a lot of people, precisely because they are not keys the game uses. Somebody who cannot bind them either gives up on voice or binds it over something they need. THE OTHER HALF, and it is worth checking in the same sitting rather than finding out after: whether the GAME can read those buttons once they are bound. The launcher writing XButton1 into the profile is no use if the plugin that listens for the key never sees it either. Both ends, or neither. ===== FIXED 22 SEPTEMBER, and almost nothing had to be added. The diagnosis in this entry was right: a key press arrives as PreviewKeyDown and the two thumb buttons do not, they arrive as PreviewMouseDown with ChangedButton XButton1 and XButton2, and the window was only listening for the first kind. WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE: BuildDik has bound Mouse 4 to 259 and Mouse 5 to 260 all along, the client's own DxScanCode enum calls those MouseButton3 and MouseButton4, and the Controls page already binds 265, the wheel, for another mod. The gaps were the capture and the VIRTUAL KEY table: Keys.Set refuses a code Known does not hold, and 0x05 and 0x06 were not in it, so even a capture that saw them would have been turned away. The names match the DIK table because Set translates by NAME, the two numberings disagreeing being the whole reason that function exists. ONLY THE THUMB BUTTONS ARE TAKEN. Left, right and middle fall through unhandled so the page keeps working while it waits, and binding push to talk to the attack button is not a thing to make one click away. BOTH ENDS CHECKED, which this entry's own trap warned about: the plugin reads the key from Thornswood.ini and listens on buttonEvent, which is the event that carries mouse codes, so 259 and 260 reach it the same way 47 does.

## Read first

- `tools\app, the controls page`: where a key is captured, and the case that is missing
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-voice.js`: the reading end. A bind the game cannot see is not a bind

## Steps

- [ ] Find what the controls page listens on for the voice bind. If it is a key event only, that is the whole fault.
- [ ] Add the mouse case: XButton1 and XButton2, written into the profile in whatever shape the plugin already understands.
- [ ] Then check the reading end. The plugin has to recognise the value the launcher wrote, or it binds and does nothing.
- [ ] Remember the C# 5 rule for anything in tools\app: no interpolation, no ?., no nameof, no expression bodied members, no out var.

## Commands

- Start in the repo. (claude)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```
- Read only, stays on this machine. What the launcher last wrote as the voice key, which is the shape a mouse button has to be written in. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content C:\Thornswood\Profile\voice-ptt.txt
  ```

## Done when

Mouse 4 and Mouse 5 can be set as the voice key in the launcher AND holding one actually talks in the game.

## Traps

Binding it in the launcher and never checking the game end is how this gets closed twice. The extra mouse buttons do not arrive as key events at either end.

## 61. (done) DONE: Thornswood will not start out of a shared Skyrim, and the Play button makes the folder

**Order:** 61 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** ship it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\app\Paths.cs Collection · tools\app\Swap.cs Apply · tools\app\ShellOwnGame.cs · warned as fa02dc1, NOT OUT YET

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER on the site, "Lingering Skyrim File Issue (the other server Profile Issue)" by a tester who also plays the other server and Daedric RP: "Remnant files from other versions of Skyrim to cause Daedric RP login info to lock up all version of Skyrim and make it unplayable." The screenshot is Thornswood branded with AUTHORIZATION, ID: UNDEFINED, CHANGE ACCOUNT and PLAY. They fixed it themselves: "when I cleared all my files for Skyrim in the local files as well as the %LOCALAPPDATA%. I was able to use a backup of the other server to fix it." WHAT THAT SCREEN ACTUALLY IS, and it is the useful part: it is skymp5-client's STOCK authorization widget, not our character selector. Ours is what gameData.chooseAtMenu produces, and thornswood-front.js replaces any page that is not ours. So that screen means our plugin was not running and our launcher did not start that session. WE ARE ALREADY IMMUNE TO THE MECHANISM HE DESCRIBES, by three separate decisions that were all made on purpose. OwnGame.Foreign returns true for Data\Platform\PluginsNoLoad\, commented "The client's per machine sign in data. It holds an access token", so Thornswood's own folder never takes another server's sign in out of the Steam copy. Ship-Rules keeps that folder out of every pack and installer. Leaks.cs removes only the exact bytes that once shipped and deliberately leaves another server's own sign in alone, because that is theirs. And AutoJoin.SetChooseAtMenu writes the flag, reads it back and THROWS rather than starting the game when it did not take, so a normal Thornswood Play cannot reach that screen. SO THE QUESTION IS NOT WHAT BROKE, IT IS HOW THAT SESSION STARTED. Either the game was launched some other way, or that install is a shared Skyrim folder rather than Thornswood's own one. Both are worth knowing, and the second would mean somebody is running Thornswood in a layout the 20 September decision says is not supported any more. FOUND IT: THE SHARED SKYRIM. Patrick, 21 September: he runs it normally, Play in the launcher, with the separate folder, "we keep having this issue with everyone where some of our stuff appears in other servers when launching and vice versae". And: "look at the background, that is our background". THAT IS THE CLUE THAT SOLVES IT. Paths.cs sets Collection = the own game folder does not exist and a Steam copy does, and in that mode Game is the STEAM COPY, Live and LiveMyGames are the shared Windows folders, and Swap.Apply returns at its first line so nothing is redirected at all. Vortex has deployed the Thornswood collection into that same shared copy, SO THE ART, THE MENU AND THE MODS ARE ALL OURS AND CORRECT. What is not ours is Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client-settings.txt, because it is ONE FILE and every launcher on the machine writes it. Ours puts chooseAtMenu and a profile id there on every Play. Another server's puts its own. The game reads whichever wrote last, and thornswood-front.js does nothing at all without chooseAtMenu, so the stock SkyMP login box comes up reading ID: UNDEFINED behind our own backdrop. My Games and LocalAppData leak the same way and for the same reason. IT IS NOT A NEW FAULT, it is the layout the own game folder decision of 17 and 20 September exists to end, still running on the machines of everybody who declined the offer. THE OFFER IS THE GAP: made once at startup, declined once, and never mentioned again, so somebody who said no in September is still sharing a Skyrim now with nothing anywhere saying so. WARNED AS fa02dc1: the launcher says it every start, in the log and on the status line, naming the folder and what is shared, and points at the button in Settings, Maintenance. That is the smallest honest change; it does not fix anybody, it stops the next report costing an evening. CLOSED, NOT JUST WARNED ABOUT. Patrick, 21 September: "we we were supposed to make it so it doesn't dp that". He is right, and the warning on its own was a half measure against a decision that had already been taken. CLAUDE.md carries it plainly: "Decided by Patrick on 20 Sep: nothing here supports another server's install any more." The own folder was built and the launcher restarts into it, and the shared layout was left underneath as something a person could decline their way into and then stay in for ever. DONE AS d117831: StartPlay refuses before anything else, including the Discord door, because a shared Skyrim is not an install this supports. StartPlay is the only way into a fresh start, so there is nothing to walk around: the other entries into Play are the path a game already running comes back through. NOBODY IS LEFT WITHOUT A WAY FORWARD, which is the part that took the care. When the folder can be made, the offer goes up then and there rather than pointing at a button on another screen. When it cannot, OwnGame.WhyNot names the one thing stopping it and every one of its answers already says what to do: press Downgrade first because Steam updated Skyrim, turn the Thornswood profile on in Vortex and let it deploy, or install on the same drive as Skyrim because links only work inside one drive. THE COST IS REAL AND IT IS PATRICK'S TO WEIGH: anybody currently in the shared layout cannot play until they build the folder or clear that blocker, and the different drive case means moving an install rather than pressing a button. That lands the moment this ships, on everybody at once, in a closed playtest. The startup warning from fa02dc1 stays, because it is what makes the next report readable and it names the folder. SHIPPED AS 1.1.74 AND 1.1.75. 1.1.74 carried the warning, 1.1.75 the refusal and the button. AND THE BUTTON IS THE SHAPE PATRICK ASKED FOR: "well make it so the launcher allows for it to be a button". Refusing on press and explaining in a dialog was the wrong shape when the Play page already had a pattern for exactly this, so the button now reads MAKE THORNSWOOD'S OWN FOLDER and pressing it does that, beside INSTALL THE MODS FIRST, DOWNGRADE FIRST and UPDATE FIRST. Ranked below those four on purpose: every one of them is also a reason OwnGame.WhyNot gives for the folder not being makeable yet, so putting this first would tell somebody to make a folder that cannot be made and hide the step that unblocks them. The refusal in StartPlay stays underneath as the thing that cannot be walked around. IT IS LIVE NOW, so anybody in the shared layout is already seeing it and cannot play until they press it or clear the blocker it names.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Paths.cs:51-80`: Collection, and that it silently switches Game, Live and LiveMyGames to the shared ones
- `tools\app\Swap.cs, Apply`: returns at its first line under a collection, so nothing is isolated
- `tools\app\ShellOwnGame.cs, AskOwnGame`: the offer, and Decline, which is the thing that lasts for ever
- `tools\app\AutoJoin.cs, SetChooseAtMenu`: writes the one shared file every Play, reads it back and throws, which is why the fault appears on the NEXT launch rather than ours

## Steps

THE BACKDROP AND THE MODS LOOK PERFECT IN THIS MODE, because Vortex deployed our collection into the shared copy. Only the one settings file is somebody else's, and that is the file that decides who you are. Do not read correct looking art as evidence that the install is ours. ## 62. (done) DONE: the launcher said "Voice: already configured" and testers read it as a failure

**Order:** 62 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\app\Voice.cs:704-712

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by a tester as a fault. It was not one. Voice.Configure takes a force flag; Reconfigure passes false, and when the config it would send is the one the page already has it returns early. That skip is deliberate and the comment above it says why: the page opens a socket for every config handed to it and the service keeps a peer per socket, so sending the same one twice leaves a ghost on the roster announcing where the last slot was standing. Nothing was stale either, because the page load path calls Configure(log), which forces. So the line meant voice was up and there was nothing to redo, and it sat one word away from the success line below it, which is why it read like a refusal. FIXED AS e4e9712: it now reads as the working state it is. The early return itself is untouched, because that is what stops the ghost peers.

## Steps

- [x] Reword the line so it reads as voice being up. Keep host, port and profile in it, because those are what make a report useful. (claude)

## Done when

The launcher log line for an unchanged voice config reads as a working state, and the early return itself is untouched.

## Traps

Do not delete the early return to make the message go away. It is what stops the ghost peers. The wording was the defect, not the behaviour.

MY MISTAKE, 20 September 23:18, found the next morning when Check-LiveGamemode was run. Publish-Server was run to put the equipment fix on the live box. It packs whatever is in dist\server, and dist\server\gamemode.js had been checked four hours earlier and was the live one. Between that check and the publish, something ran Deploy-Gamemode, which copies the repo's gamemode into dist. So the publish carried commit 36a01c3's gamemode to the live server: the class gates, farming, and the ore and plant tables, none of which was meant to leave dev. MEASURED AFTERWARDS: the live file is 539,349 bytes, which is 36a01c3's 501,032 plus one carriage return for each of its 38,317 lines, so it is that commit exactly. NOBODY HAS CONNECTED TO THE LIVE SERVER SINCE, so it reached no one. THE FIX IS STAGED AND NOT APPLIED. dist\server\gamemode.js now holds the pre-progression file again, byte for byte, sha256 e04ec527, and the one it replaced is kept beside it as gamemode.js.progression-<stamp>. Deploy-Server sends it. I could not run that: the harness refuses production deploys from here on three separate routes, and working around that would be working around the point of it. THE LESSON, and it is the reason this is an entry rather than a line in a reply: dist is a build folder that more than one script writes to, and Publish-Server packs it without saying what is in it. A publish should print the hash of the gamemode it is about to send and refuse one that is not the hash of a commit. IT HAPPENED AGAIN ON 21 SEPTEMBER, THE OTHER WAY ROUND. A command block written by Claude ended in ".\tools\Ship.ps1" with no -Channel dev, and a bare Ship is a MAIN release. 1.1.67 went public to every installed launcher carrying a day of untested work, when Ship's own header says the order plainly: "New work goes out on dev first and gets broken there; a plain Ship afterwards promotes it all to main." ROLLED BACK the same evening: the public feed was put back to 1.1.66 from commit 83b773d, the release was taken off Latest with gh release edit --latest=false, and nothing was deleted. Dev was put back on 1.1.66.1 and the work reshipped there as 1.1.67.2. TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING. A main Ship copies main's baseline over dev's, and only a DRY RUN makes a backup, so dev's own position in the feed is gone and cannot be recovered; that is the same failure the comments in Ship describe from 17 September. And the version numbers have split: the repo says 1.1.67 because the main Ship committed that bump, while the public feed is on 1.1.66, so the next main release bumps to 1.1.68 and skips 67. Nothing is broken by the gap but it will look like a lost release to somebody reading the history. AND A DRY RUN BURNED A NUMBER TOO. 21 September ended 1.1.66 -> 1.1.69, with 1.1.67 lost to the rollback and 1.1.68 lost to a dry run that bumped Updater.cs and never put it back. Ship already knew this shape of fault, having twice had a dry run consume the next real release on 17 September, and it backs up version.json and the baseline for exactly that reason; Updater.cs is the same fault with a different face and was missed. Fixed as e146aa4 by calling the Unbump function that was already written for it, and whose own comment says "a failed run burns a number and the launcher people are running claims a version that was never published". A dry run is a run that does not publish. e146aa4 is on main, checked 23 September, and the Unbump it calls was already written for exactly this. Nothing else is owed.

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER while working out why the property system could not possibly work in game, and it is older and wider than that day. TWO FACTS THAT ONLY BITE TOGETHER. First: the publisher tracks ZERO plugins. Not one .esp or .esm is in published.json, so no plugin has ever travelled in a pack; the launcher downloads them from the server instead, which the server log says in as many words, "55 plugin files published at /api/servers/thornswood/plugins/ for the launcher". Second: Deploy-Server compared NAMES. Its own comment said it sends "whatever the new list names that is not there yet", so a plugin the VPS already had by name was never sent again however much its contents moved. WHAT THAT MEANT: Thornswood-Content.esp is the one plugin in the load order this repo edits, and every edit to it since it was first installed had reached nobody. On 21 September alone that was the rename off another server's prefix, sixteen dead books removed, and the handle, the deed, the key and the mold added. The gamemode went live calling for records that were not in the file any client had, and it came up clean and said "[property] ready, 4891 doors across 852 buildings" while being unable to hand over a single deed. FIXED, on main as fa1e90f, in two parts. Deploy-Server asks the VPS for name AND size and sends anything that differs; size rather than a hash because it is one ssh call for the whole folder either way and hashing 60 plugins is 28MB of reading on the box that is also running the server. And OUR plugin is taken from the repo rather than from a game folder: $Data is the Steam copy, which is right for the other 59 because Vortex deploys them there, but ours is built by scripts here and installed by Install-ThornswoodContent.ps1 whose default target is C:\Thornswood\Game and not Steam at all. There were four copies of it on the machine at three different sizes and a deploy sent whichever one the Steam folder happened to hold. The repo is where it is made, so the repo is what goes up. PROVEN: the deploy afterwards said "changed: Thornswood-Content.esp 151,288 -> 141,234 bytes" and the server came up with it.

## 68. (done) DONE: Ship commits nothing at all now

**Order:** 68 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Ship.ps1, the source commit at the end of a main release

## What is known

FOUND 21 SEPTEMBER, and it did no harm this time. A main Ship commits and pushes the source when the release is out, which is what lets the other machine pull exactly what shipped. It commits THE WHOLE TREE. On 21 September a change to Shell.cs and ShellOwnGame.cs was finished and compiling but not yet committed when Ship ran, and it went out inside 56af203 "1.1.75: Thornswood runs from its own Skyrim, never a shared one", a message that says nothing about the Play button that was actually in it. NOTHING HALF WRITTEN CAN SHIP, because Ship builds the launcher before it publishes and a compile error stops the release. What can happen is the opposite: work that is complete goes out under a message that does not describe it, and the history stops being a record of what changed and why. CLAUDE.md is strict about this for a reason it states plainly: "a commit that changes eight things cannot be reverted when one of them is wrong". A release commit that quietly carries somebody else's work is the same fault wearing a version number. IT IS ALSO A RACE WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: two people working while a Ship runs is how it happens, and neither of them sees it. WHAT TO DO IS PATRICK'S CALL. Ship could refuse to run with a dirty tree, which is the strict answer and would have stopped tonight's release. Or it could commit only the files it changed itself, version.json and Updater.cs, and leave the rest, which keeps the history honest without ever blocking a release. The second is the smaller change and the one that cannot bite at a bad moment. RESOLVED, read off the script on 23 September. Ship.ps1 says it in its own words where the git add -A used to be: "SHIP NO LONGER COMMITS OR PUSHES ANYTHING." The version is bumped and committed by Bump-Version.ps1 beforehand, the Git gate refuses a release with anything uncommitted or unpushed, and by the time anything is published the repository already says exactly what shipped. That is the strict answer this entry left to Patrick, and it is also what let enforce_admins go on. The one git write left is in the RELEASES feed repo, not this one, and it adds version.json alone: "Dev follows main".

## Read first

- `tools\Ship.ps1, the Source section at the end`: what it commits and pushes, and how wide it casts
- `CLAUDE.md, one fix per commit`: the rule this quietly works around, and the reason given for it

## Steps

- [x] Decide which: refuse on a dirty tree, or commit only what Ship changed itself. (patrick)
- [x] Whichever it is, say what it skipped, because a release that silently leaves work uncommitted is its own trap. (claude)

## Done when

Done. A release commit contains the release and nothing else, because Ship makes no commit at all.

## Traps

It looks harmless because the build gate means nothing broken can ship. The cost is to the history, which is only noticed later, when somebody needs to revert one thing and finds it welded to a version bump.

## 69. Nothing is code signed: SmartScreen warns forever, and one GitHub login is all that stands between a stranger and every installed machine

**Order:** 69 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Old number:** 14

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:222-330; tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:79-90 · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:369-381, 405-418, 815-875

## What is known

Start the Trusted Signing identity validation today, because it takes days and nothing else about signing can begin until it clears. Then sign the installer and the launcher, and check the signer in SelfUpdate before the swap. The existing host pinning and checksum stay as a second layer UPDATE 17 September: Microsoft cleared the installer as a false positive, submission 20a8542e-6f21-415d-91b1-e15663cf45a3, and removed the detection. That clearance is for the binary that was submitted, so every new build is a new file and can be flagged again. It lowers the urgency for today's download and changes nothing about the underlying cause. EVERYTHING BUT THE CERTIFICATE IS DONE, 18 September. Three commits: 1143fcd adds tools/Sign-Artifact.ps1, one implementation driven by a gitignored tools/signing.json, wired into the launcher build so it signs the exe and the setup stub together or leaves both alone. de231da signs the installer after its payload is attached, which is the right order and one its own loader already expects, because Bootstrap.cs scans backwards for its magic precisely because a certificate lands after the trailer. f87a0bb adds the signer check to SelfUpdate, in front of the copy rather than after it, since once a file sits at exe.new the swap happens on the next start whatever the check says. PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the same call was compiled with the same Framework csc at langversion 5 and pointed at real files. It accepts a matching signer, refuses a different one and refuses an unsigned file. That test also turned up something worth knowing: the call reads embedded signatures only, so notepad.exe reports unsigned while Windows calls it Valid, because system binaries are catalog signed. WHAT IS LEFT is the certificate itself. Start the Azure Trusted Signing identity validation, which is a manual review with a photo ID and takes days, then write tools/signing.json and fill in Updater.ExpectedSigner in the same release that first ships a signed exe. CORRECTED 18 September after reading the current Microsoft documentation, because two things I had said were wrong. The service is called Artifact Signing now, not Trusted Signing. And validation does NOT take days for an individual: the 1 to 20 business days figure is organisation validation. An individual does a Verified ID check on a phone through AU10TIX and the portal status reaches Completed in minutes. This can be finished today. TWO THINGS THAT WILL STOP IT COLD. Individual developers must be located in the United States or Canada. And the Azure billing account on the subscription must have an Account Type of Individual, with a legal name and sold-to address matching the government ID, because the form is filled in from the billing account and is read only. Fix the billing account first if it does not match. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the certificates last three days, so the timestamp is what keeps a signature valid and is not optional. Sign-Artifact.ps1 now defaults to the service's own timestamp authority, commit 93a1e75. The endpoint in metadata.json must name the same region the account was created in, or signing fails with a bare 403. ACCOUNT TRAP, 18 September. Azure kept landing on an organisation directory called CCCS, because that sign-in is a work or school account. That is not a directory to switch out of: everything created under it lives in that organisation's tenant and its billing account is Organization type, so individual validation cannot run there. Being blocked is the kind outcome. A Public Trust certificate carries the validated identity, so signing under that account would put an organisation's legal name on every Thornswood binary, for a personal project, without their permission. Use the personal Microsoft account in a private window instead. AZURE FOR STUDENTS DOES NOT HELP and is worth saying out loud because it is offered on the way in. Verifying academic status uses the school account, so it lands back in the same tenant, and its subscription is credit based rather than an Individual billing account. Pay-as-you-go on the personal account is what creates the Individual billing account this needs. THE COST, since it is a running one: Basic is 9.99 US dollars a month for 5,000 signatures, against two or three files per release. Premium at 99.99 is not needed. A traditional certificate is a few hundred a year plus a hardware token, so this is the cheap route. CHECKED AGAINST AZURE, 18 September, and the Azure half is right. TWO THINGS WERE WRONG IN C:/tools/metadata.json AND ARE NOW FIXED. Its Endpoint read https://westus2.codesigning.azure.net/ which is the region NAME, not the endpoint tag. Azure reports the account's own accountUri as https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net and that is now what the file says; the old one is kept beside it as metadata.json.before-fix. That mistake is exactly the bare 403 the documentation warns about and it never mentions regions, so it would have been a long evening. Do not type the endpoint from the table, ask the account for its own accountUri. Its CertificateProfileName was still the placeholder YOUR_EXACT_PROFILE_NAME, which is not a mistake so much as getting ahead: there are no certificate profiles on the account at all yet, because the identity validation has not been done. SO WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT is the identity validation in the portal, then the profile, then the signer role, then filling in that one remaining field. Everything before and after that is in place. TICKS CORRECTED 18 September, which is what you asked me to check. Azure reports no certificate profiles on ThornswoodSigning at all. A profile cannot be created without a completed identity validation, so its absence is proof that the chain from the validation onwards is unfinished, and the steps from there down have been unticked. The one thing I cannot see from here is the validation's own status, because identity validation is portal only and has no CLI or management API surface. Open the account, Identity validations under Objects, and read what the status says. In Progress means it is still working, Action Required means the phone half is waiting for you, Completed means only the profile is missing and that is one command. It does not: westus2.codesigning.azure.net does not resolve at all, so signing would have failed on DNS before it reached anything. The correct host, wus2.codesigning.azure.net, resolves to 48.192.88.101 and answers 403 to an unauthenticated browser. That 403 is the endpoint working. It is a signing API behind an application gateway, not a web page, so refusing a browser with no token is exactly right and is not a sign of a problem. WRONG FORM, seen 18 September. A browser tab read New organization validation. That is the default and it is not the one an individual wants: it asks for a legal business entity, a website on a domain that entity owns, and a business identifier. The Individual form is behind a dropdown on the Identity validations pane that opens on Organization, so it is genuinely easy to miss. Change the dropdown to Individual first, then New Identity, then Public. Everything else on the account was confirmed correct from a portal screenshot: ThornswoodSigning, West US 2, Basic, Account URI https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net/ matching metadata.json, and the directory is the personal one rather than CCCS. The profile command in this entry now carries that id so it can be pasted when the status reaches Completed. It is worth checking against a current build rather than assumed: the clearance covers the binary that was submitted and every new build is a new file that can be flagged again. Moving them is part of the folder consolidation proposal for #dev. AUDIT OF 25 SEPTEMBER, what one GitHub login can do: the launcher downloads and runs any pack version.json lists with a matching hash, the hash comes from the same file, and the host check (Updater.cs:389-411) admits any github.com release, not only Thornswood-Releases. Worse, each feed check saves updateRepo, serverAddress, siteUrl, voiceUrl and collectionUrl from the feed into config.json (Shell.cs:4548-4585), so one bad feed commit moves every launcher somewhere else for good. ## Read first

- `tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:75-95`: the reputation argument stated in the file's own words: a new binary every release is a new hash every release
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:365-430`: the AllowedHosts array and the download that refuses an update with no checksum, the layer that already exists
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:815-873`: SelfUpdate, the swap with no verification at all, and the File.Copy at :821 the signer check goes in front of
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:218-300`: the compile section that ends with csc and no signing step

Use a fragment, not the whole line: certificate authorities reorder and add fields between renewals and an exact match would refuse every update the day the certificate renews. This is the last thing to change and it ships in the same release as the first signed exe, never earlier, or every launcher in the world stops updating. (claude)

## Done when

Get-AuthenticodeSignature on the built Thornswood.exe reports Valid with the expected subject rather than NotSigned, the installer reports the same after its payload is attached, and Updater.ExpectedSigner names that certificate. Everything except the certificate itself is in place as of 18 September: the build signs when signing.json exists and says plainly that it is not signing when it does not.

## Traps

CATALOG SIGNATURES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS CHECK, found by testing on 18 September. X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile reads embedded Authenticode only. Most Windows system binaries are catalog signed, so notepad.exe and curl.exe both come back as unsigned from this call while Get-AuthenticodeSignature calls them Valid. That is harmless here, because signtool writes an embedded signature and that is what we will ship, but it makes notepad.exe a useless thing to test against. Use pwsh.exe, node.exe or gh.exe, which are all embedded signed. ExpectedSigner is empty on purpose and must stay empty until the release that first ships a signed exe, or every update stops working for everybody. Match on a fragment of the Subject rather than the whole line, because certificate authorities reorder fields between renewals. Updater.cs needs a line in #dev before anybody edits it. The launcher is C# 5 only, and CreateFromSignedFile throws on an unsigned file rather than returning null, so the throw is what unsigned looks like. Signing changes the file hash, so the first signed release invalidates every checksum published for the previous one and must go out as one complete release, launcher and installer together. Signing the small binaries while the 527 MB payload still has no hash check at all only moves the problem.

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/how-to-signing-integrations the client tools installer, metadata.json and the signtool arguments
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/tutorial-assign-roles the two roles: Identity Verifier to create it, Certificate Profile Signer to use it
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation why reputation per file hash is the problem signing solves
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.x509certificate.createfromsignedfile the call the launcher uses, and that it throws on an unsigned file

## 72. (done) DONE: the restart window no longer strands anybody, and the announcement goes through

**Order:** 72 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** find it, then small · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

VPS  ·  game server  ·  tools\gamemode.js:3455-3472 describes it in a comment and nowhere else  ·  client side it reads as Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log saying the server says it is restarting, staying put  ·  tools\Restart-Server.ps1 is the fix  ·  tools\Request-Restart.ps1 is NOT

## What is known

REPORTED AGAIN 20 September by Patrick, NPCs are gone again, and it is already written down inside gamemode.js and has never been on this list. The comment at 3455-3472 records it from 17 September: one existing character, 13 reconnects after two kicks that had no process restart behind them, every one of them landing dead with no hits and no deaths and all the NPCs gone, while the same character reconnected fine after the 01:00 process restart and fresh characters always worked. A kick with nothing restarting behind it leaves the actor in a state where the reconnecting client is never sent the world. MEASURED 20 September at 11:10. Patrick's session log carries the server says it is restarting, staying put at line 64, immediately after ready, so he joined inside a restart window. At the same time https://thornswood.net/api/public reported up true and online 0 while he was standing in the world. The server did not have him as a connected person. That is the same failure from the other side, and it is why there are no NPCs: the world is never sent. THE FIX RIGHT NOW is a process restart, tools/Restart-Server.ps1, then reconnect. THE TRAP, and it is a bad one: Request-Restart.ps1 does NOT restart the process. Its own header says so. It warns people and kicks them, which is precisely the kick with no restart behind it that causes this. Reaching for it to fix this makes it worse. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNFIXED: gamemode.js was changed so that update mode no longer kicks, which closed one way in. restart mode still kicks and still relies on a process restart following it, and nothing enforces that they go together. Joining during the countdown is a second way in that the comment does not cover and that today's log shows happening. Two things to decide: make restart mode refuse unless a process restart is actually going to follow, and refuse or hold a login that arrives while a restart is armed, rather than letting somebody into a world that will not be sent. FIXED AS FAR AS THE SERVER CAN, 20 September, commit 79b6a13, and the rest is a #dev call. A character arriving on a tick inside the restart window is now told, in chat, that the server was restarting as they arrived and to quit to the launcher and come back if the world looks empty, and the server logs it. That does not stop it happening; it stops it being silent, which was most of the cost. The server cannot refuse the connection because there is no login hook to refuse it in, and it must not kick, because the kick is the cause. The window test is written the same way the online writer's is so the warning and the file the client reads cannot disagree, and both copies were lifted out and driven through nothing armed, counting down, just finished and long finished: 18 assertions, and every one of them also asserts the two copies agree. Request-Restart.ps1 now prints what it does not do and names Restart-Server.ps1, because its update and restart modes both end in a kick and the consequence was only ever written inside gamemode.js. Deploy-Server was always fine; running it by hand is where the half happened. STILL OPEN AND NOT MINE TO SETTLE: whether restart mode should refuse unless a process restart is actually going to follow, and whether a login arriving mid countdown should be held rather than warned. Both change behaviour the two machines rely on, so they are a few lines in #dev first. AND THE SCRIPT NOW SEES IT THROUGH, commit 8458f5a. The warning added earlier told you to run Restart-Server.ps1 afterwards and then trusted you to. Request-Restart.ps1 -ThenRestart waits out the countdown and bounces the process itself, so the kick and the restart cannot come apart. It passes -Now, because the room was just cleared on purpose and the online check would otherwise refuse on whoever has already reconnected, who are exactly the people it is for. A missing or failing Restart-Server is said out loud and exits non-zero rather than leaving somebody thinking it was done. -ThenRestart with -Cancel, and with -Mode notice, are both refused before anything reaches the VPS. Checked without touching the server: both refusals throw ahead of any ssh, and Restart-Server.ps1 does take every parameter this passes it. NOT LIVE EITHER, measured 20 September. The warning is in gamemode.js, which Ship.ps1 does not carry: grepping Ship.ps1 for gamemode returns nothing, so 1.1.58 and 1.1.59 both went out without it. It needs Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 then Deploy-Server.ps1, and the same single ssh hash described under entry 5 says whether that has happened. THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS DONE TOO, commit 7251917, and it no longer needs a #dev line because Patrick waived it on 20 September. Warning at the end was not enough: it still let somebody kick the room and walk away. The kick and the process restart are now inseparable. -Mode update and -Mode restart are REFUSED OUTRIGHT unless the caller says which half is coming: -ThenRestart for the script to bounce the process itself, or -RestartFollows for a caller that does. Deploy-Server.ps1 passes -RestartFollows because it stops and starts the task a few lines later, so that path is unchanged. notice needs neither because it disconnects nobody, and neither does -Cancel. Seven assertions, all stopping before any ssh. A second fault turned up while testing it and is fixed in the same commit: -Cancel fell through the tail block and announced a kick it had just called off. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE is holding a login that arrives mid countdown. There is no login hook to refuse it in, and the only lever available is a kick, which is the cause. The warning stays as the answer to that half, and this entry's done-when allows it: told to wait rather than landing in an empty one. If that is not good enough it is a launcher change, refusing Play while the online file says restarting, and that is Shell.cs territory. Only restart mode needs -ThenRestart or -RestartFollows now; update and notice disconnect nobody and go through. The header of Request-Restart says which is which. 79b6a13, 7251917 and c5abe7b are all on main, checked 23 September, and the dev server is running that gamemode. Only restart mode needs -ThenRestart or -RestartFollows; update and notice disconnect nobody and go through, which is what the header of Request-Restart says.

## 74. (done) DONE: a throwaway build touches nothing outside its own folder

**Order:** 74 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, the Shortcut section at the end

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER by doing it. The launcher was compiled into a scratch folder to check the client self-heal change, using the same -Root the GitHub workflow uses: .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root <a temp folder> -NoPause. It built fine. It also rewrote the Desktop Thornswood.lnk to point at the exe in that temp folder, restarted Explorer to refresh the icon, and said so in one line among thirty: "Thornswood.lnk points at the exe now". Patrick's Desktop icon was pointing into a Claude scratchpad until it was put back by hand. THIS IS ENTRY 45 COMING BACK IN A DIFFERENT SHAPE. That one was every launcher build repointing the Desktop icon at the DEV launcher, and it was closed. The shortcut step is still unconditional: it points at whatever this run built, wherever that was. CI never notices because a GitHub runner has no Desktop and nobody is looking at it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ICON. -Root is how you compile without touching the install you play on, which is exactly what somebody does when they want to check a change compiles, and it is the one situation where rewriting the real shortcut is guaranteed wrong. A temp folder gets cleaned up, and then the icon points at nothing. THE FIX IS A CONDITION, not a new switch if one can be avoided: write the shortcut only when the build went to the root this machine actually plays from. A -NoShortcut switch would work and would have to be remembered every time, which is the same as not having it. ===== AND IT ALSO CLOSES A RUNNING SKYRIM, found the same way on 22 September and worse than the shortcut. Building into a scratch folder with -Root printed "Skyrim is still open (SkyrimSE), closing it / Closed" and shut Patrick's game mid-session. He read it as a crash and said so; there is no crash log for it, because there was no crash. The shortcut and this are the same fault: the steps at the end of that script act on the machine's real install whatever -Root was, and CI never notices because a runner has no Desktop and no game running. Both should be conditional on the build root being the one this machine plays from. Counted three times in one evening for the shortcut and once for the game. SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.90, with the gamemode on both servers, the voice service reinstalled and the site republished. The 22 September fix told the dev build apart from the play install and stopped there. There is a third kind of root: a throwaway one. A compile check, the build step in CI which uses $RUNNER_TEMP, or a Claude proving that a file still compiles. None of those match -DevBuild, so every one of them wrote Thornswood.lnk to the Desktop pointing into a temporary folder that was then deleted, and restarted Explorer to be sure the change took. IT HAPPENED AGAIN ON 23 SEPTEMBER, the fourth time, which is what prompted fixing the cause rather than the shortcut. A root that is neither real install now gets its shortcut inside its own folder only, and does not clear the icon cache either. Proved by running a scratch build and reading the Desktop shortcut back: unchanged, and the build says "a throwaway build, so the Desktop is left alone entirely".

## Read first

- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, the Shortcut section`: it runs unconditionally, whatever -Root was
- `.github\workflows\build.yml, the Build the launcher step`: the -Root form this was found with, and why CI never sees the problem

## Steps

- [x] Make the shortcut step conditional on the build root being the real install root rather than running every time.
- [x] Say in the output when it is skipped and why, so a build into a scratch folder does not look like it failed to do something.
- [x] Check the Explorer restart goes with it. Restarting somebody's Explorer to refresh an icon for a throwaway build is worse than the wrong icon.

## 75. (done) DONE: the client runtime is a named download with its own checksum

**Order:** 75 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Publish-Update.ps1 and the baseline at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json · tools\app\ClientRuntime.cs Heal · tools\Ship-Rules.ps1

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER while making the launcher repair itself, and it is the soft spot under that whole entry. A pack carries WHAT CHANGED since the last publish. The six files in client-build.json change rarely, so they are in a pack only on the releases where they happened to move, and they are absent from every other one. Measured: the four packs published after the client was recorded at 05:04 on 22 September were 3 MB, 0 MB, 0 MB and 0 MB, and SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll alone is 15.6 MB. So on the evening the repair shipped there was nothing on the feed for it to repair FROM, and it had to be forced by clearing six entries out of the publish baseline by hand and shipping again. THAT WORKED AND IT IS NOT A MECHANISM. It depends on somebody remembering, on a file in %LOCALAPPDATA% that is deliberately outside the repo, and on the one pack that carries them staying on the feed. ClientRuntime.Heal walks back forty updates looking, which is a scavenger hunt standing in for an address. WHAT IT SHOULD BE: the client runtime published as its own asset, once, whenever client-build.json changes, with its url and sha256 recorded in version.json beside the launcher and the packs. Then Heal asks for it by name, gets all six in one download, and never walks the feed at all. It is about 18.3 MB and it changes a few times a month. THE SHAPE IS ALREADY THERE. Ship-Rules.ps1 reads client-build.json into a set; Publish-Update already uploads assets and writes version.json; Updater already downloads a url with a mandatory checksum, and Updater.Fetch exposes exactly that. This is a publish step and a field, not new machinery. WHILE IT IS NOT DONE, the forty-update walk is the fallback and it works as long as pack 20260922-2202 is on the feed. If somebody prunes old packs, the repair quietly stops being able to repair, and the symptom will be a tester with a red Client row and a launcher log saying it looked in the last forty updates and did not find them. BUILT AND LIVE, found on 23 September by reading version.json rather than the entry. The feed carries a clientRuntime field: url, sha256, bytes 6,538,349 and forkCommit c8832519, which is the same commit tools\client-build.json records, so what is published is the current runtime. Publish-Update.ps1 builds client-runtime-<commit>.zip and uploads it whenever that record moves, and both of those zips are sitting in the dist folder. AND THE LAUNCHER ASKS FOR IT BY NAME: ClientRuntime.cs takes v.clientRuntime.url and hands it to Updater.Fetch with the recorded sha256, and only falls back to the forty update walk when the field is absent. So the scavenger hunt is the fallback rather than the mechanism, which is exactly what this entry asked for. Nothing here depends on anybody clearing a baseline by hand any more.

## Read first

- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1, the baseline block around line 206`: what a pack contains is the difference against %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json, which is why the client is usually absent
- `tools\app\ClientRuntime.cs, Heal`: the forty-update walk this would replace, and the order it tries sources in

## Steps

- [x] Publish the six recorded files as one asset whenever client-build.json changes, and record its url, sha256 and bytes in version.json.
- [x] Have ClientRuntime.Heal try that asset first, before Keep and before the pack walk. Keep the walk as the fallback for a launcher newer than the feed.
- [x] Then the forty-update walk can go, or stay as a last resort with the cap lowered.
- [x] Until then: do not prune pack 20260922-2202 off the releases repository. It is the only one carrying the client runtime. (patrick)

## 76. The progression and economy rulebook: classes, professions, sub-professions, ranks and a fifteen skill attribute tree

**Order:** 76 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Design · **Effort:** work it out, large · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Nowhere yet · the nearest thing in code is the flat sixteen in tools\gamemode.js CHARGEN, and lore\ has none of it

## What is known

GIVEN BY PATRICK ON 20 SEPTEMBER, in full, and it is the spec the other three entries below depend on. It is recorded here verbatim in substance because it arrived in chat and chat is gone when the window closes. Nothing in it is built yet. 

THE LAW OF EXCLUSIVITY. You are locked to one Class, one Profession and one Sub-Profession. Nobody can do everything. Lacking a skill means trading, roleplaying or finding a Master to teach you. 

CLASSES, THE VERBS, 100% EXCLUSIVE, ONE EACH, no perks and no cross-class teaching. Hunter is the only class that can loot an animal body. Fisher is the only one that can catch fish. Gatherer is the only one that can harvest flora and materials out of the world. Miner is the only one that can mine ore veins. Farmer is the only one that can plant and harvest crops. 

PROFESSIONS. One Profession and one Sub-Profession, which is the half you specialise in. Within your own Profession you automatically know NOVICE work of your sister sub-profession: a Platewright knows novice Edgewright work. You cannot progress past novice in it unless a Master Edgewright teaches you. Outside your Profession you can do nothing by default. To learn novice skills of another Profession you must be formally apprenticed to a Master of that specific Sub-Profession, you can never progress past novice in a secondary Profession, and you may only do this TWICE, excluding your sister sub-profession. 

THE MAGE EXCEPTION. Mages pick two schools and two starting spells, both in one school for a deep start or split for a wide one, or save a spell point. You must use a spell of the level below to level up. Ranking up unlocks higher-tier spells and one more spell point at the same time. At Master a Mage picks a third school and two more spell points. At the College each semester you can study for two more spell points. Outside the College each semester you may choose a school if you have not already got one from a master or an earlier semester, and study for one spell point and novice spells only. A NON-MAGE CANNOT USE MAGIC AT ALL. To learn a spell they need the spellbook AND a Master Mage willing to apprentice them, and they can only ever learn two novice spells, from one school, which must match the college's school. 

RANKS, earned by doing the work and roleplaying, never by sleeping or grinding offline. Novice is the basics: simple items, iron, leather, minor potions. Advanced is the everyday work: steel, elven, standard potions. Expert is high demand craftsmanship: glass, ebony, high-tier potions. Master is the peak, and unlocks the Master Perk and the right to take Apprentices. 

THE EIGHT PROFESSIONS, their halves and their Master Perks. WARRIOR: Bulwark (tanks, shields, heavy armour) or Berserker (damage, two-handed, dual wield). Warlord: teach novice combat to non-warriors, and master-tier maneuvers. MAGE: sub-professions are the chosen schools. Archmage: a third school, and authority to apprentice non-mages. ALCHEMIST: Blightbrewer (poisons and harm) or Physicker (medicine and restoration). Master Chemist: two potions per batch. COOK: Hearthcook (dinners, meats, stews) or Confectioner (desserts, breads, sweets). Grand Chef: two food per batch. SMITH: Platewright (armour) or Edgewright (weapons). Mastercraft: temper to Legendary, past normal limits. ENCHANTER: Bladebinder (weapons) or Wardweaver (armour and apparel). Twin Souls: two enchantments on one item. TAILOR: Liverywright (robes, uniforms, faction dress) or Haberdasher (common and fine clothing). Master Weaver: clothing gives hidden armour or weather protection without weight. WOODWORKER: Charburner (firewood, coke, campfires) or Woodwright (bows, arrows, instruments). Master Carver: campfires and kilns give maximum warmth. 

THE ATTRIBUTE SKILL TREE. Fifteen sub-skills across Health, Magicka and Stamina, bought with skill points; maxing one grants its Master Perk. HEALTH. Vitality, max health, Cheat Death: once a day a fatal blow leaves you at 1 HP. Fortitude, regen, Troll's Blood: regeneration is not stunted in combat. Might, melee damage, Devastating Blow: power attacks often stagger or knock down. Resilience, armour rating, Unshakeable: immune to stagger while blocking. Toughness, resistances, Purified Blood: immune to all disease, 75% poison resistance. MAGICKA. Capacity, max magicka, Archmage's Vessel: a burst of regeneration below 10%, on a cooldown. Clarity, regen, Leyline Attunement: magicka regenerates at full speed while casting or channelling. Potency, spell effect, Overcharge: 15% chance of double damage or double duration. Ward, magic resist, Spellbreaker: 25% chance to absorb a hostile spell and refill magicka instead. Efficiency, cost, Font of Magic: once a day, all spells cost nothing for 15 seconds. STAMINA. Endurance, max stamina, Tireless: sprinting and power attacks drain 50% less. Vigor, regen, Second Wind: full stamina the instant it empties, five minute cooldown. Agility, speed, Windwalker: 10% faster and no fall damage. Burden, carry weight, Pack Mule: no speed penalty up to 50 lbs over. Precision, critical and ranged, Lethal Aim: ranged attacks ignore 50% of physical armour. 

WHAT THE CODE HAS TODAY, AND IT DOES NOT MATCH. gamemode.js CHARGEN holds ONE FLAT LIST of 16 so-called classes with a starter kit each: warrior, hunter, mage, smith, miner, woodworker, alchemist, bard, cook, enchanter, farmer, fisher, merchant, priest, scholar, thief. There is no Class/Profession split, no sub-professions, no ranks, no skill tree and no perks anywhere. FIVE OF THEM HAVE NO HOME IN THE NEW RULEBOOK: bard, merchant, priest, scholar and thief. TWO IN THE RULEBOOK DO NOT EXIST: gatherer, the class that harvests flora, and tailor with its two halves. The launcher sends class, half and gathering keys already, gamemode.js:1786 onward, so the shape is half anticipated, but the tables behind it are the old flat sixteen. Deciding what happens to those five, and to every character already carrying one, is the first thing this needs and it is Patrick's call. WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE ENFORCED, measured on 20 September against the server source at C:/Thornswood-Dev/skymp, whose HEAD is what runs (git diff against the recorded binary commit is empty). The server offers eleven gamemode hooks and the gamemode subscribes to four. onCraft, onTakeItem, onPutItem, onDropItem and onEatItem are live on the VPS today with no subscriber. A handler returning false blocks; undefined allows. onActivate is refuse-before on the server: ActivateEvent fires at MpObjectReference.cpp 484-486 and ProcessActivateNormal at 490 runs only if nobody blocked. GATHERER AND MINER: gamemode only, in onActivate, and the gamemode already does this for salt and charcoal and shrines. FLOR and TREE are refused after the local fact, though: the client does not block those kinds, so the pick plays and the ingredient sits in the local pack until the next server inventory write, then vanishes, which testers will report as a bug unless the client is told. Any new base answered in onActivate must also go in publishServerBases (1912-1945) or the front re-activates it and it fires twice. HUNTER CANNOT BE ENFORCED WITH WHAT EXISTS. ProcessActivateNormal (1419-1560) has no branch for a dead actor at all, and the shipped client blocks dead actors (12424-12426). Read from source: corpse looting appears not to work on this build for anybody. Gating it means MpObjectReference.cpp growing a corpse branch, which is engine work and a server rebuild. FISHER: unknown. Only Fishing in Skyrim's kit items are in the repo; if the spots are spell or script driven there is no hook, since there is no cast hook anywhere. FARMER: nothing exists, no mod, no station, no record, no design; that is a #dev decision before any hook is chosen. CRAFTING BY RANK AND THE SISTER HALF: enforceable in onCraft, after the local craft, once a recipe-to-half table exists; nothing maps COBJ records to halves anywhere today, and that table is the work. MAGE SCHOOLS CANNOT BE LOCKED: no cast hook, and spell lists live client side. TREE PERKS THAT CHANGE STATS need a new server binding or a client plugin: the server exposes only percentages, and PapyrusActor::SetActorValue warns it executes locally and does not affect server calculations. AND THE BOOK PATH IS DEAD CODE THAT STILL SHIPS: beginClass has no caller, chooseClass and chooseDestination are reachable only through chargenReadBook, whose guards need stages nothing sets, yet chargenReadBook still runs first on every mp.onReadBook and swallows a writ read. ## Done when

The rulebook is written down somewhere a person can read it, in lore\ or on the site, the five trades with no home in it have a decided fate, and gatherer and tailor exist. Nothing below this entry can be built until that is true.
