## 77. (done) DONE: Pick your character in the game's main menu, not in the launcher

**Order:** 77 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, large · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\app\Chars.cs, CharSync.cs, Creation.cs, Roster.cs and the Pages that show them · server side tools\gamemode.js chargen, which is told the choice by the launcher

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 20 SEPTEMBER: remove the character selector from the launcher and select the character in the main menu the way the other servers do. WHY IT IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE: the launcher choosing first is load bearing in the current design. gamemode.js:500-512 says Skyrim Unbound's own room and appearance menu only survive because they run BEFORE the client's loadGame() reload, and the two menus that run after it never appear at all. That is the same reload that killed Unbound's own trade and location lists. An in-game selector runs after the reload, so whatever replaces this has to be the plugin's own UI rather than a Skyrim menu. The launcher's choice is also what the chargen decision reads: entry 5 is a fault caused by that very choice being posted for every character it has ever made. Removing the selector removes that input, which may simplify chargen considerably or may just move the problem. Read entry 5's fix first. DONE IN TWO HALVES ON 20 SEPTEMBER, patrick/progression, not yet on dev. THE GAME HALF, commit c87da23: creation happens in the game. After the face, the character enters a 'choosing' stage; the server gives the shift, opens the K panel on their screen through the property's updateOwner script with the nine towns, and reminds them in chat every thirty seconds and after a reconnect. /pick class, /pick profession and the new /pick town are taken in any order and the third one moves them to the inn. No twenty second wait, no warrior in Whiterun. This is also what fixed 'stuck in the room again' on dev: the dev gamemode asks the dev voice service for launcher choices and the launcher posted them to the live one, so nothing ever arrived. THE MAIN MENU HALF, the fork commit b950b920 plus the plugin and the page: with gameData.chooseAtMenu set the client waits at the main menu instead of logging in as gameData.profileId; thornswood-front.js loads the page on tick (update does not fire at the menu), hands it thornswood-characters.json from the launcher, and thornswood-select.js draws one card per character and one for a new one; the pick is one browserMessage ('thornswood','select',profileId) that the client logs in as and the plugin writes to thornswood-choice.txt for the launcher. After a minute with no pick the client falls back to the last profile, so an old page still gets in. Both new files are machine files in Ship-Rules. THE LAUNCHER HALF, commit 3aa37ef with the plugin, the page and the client record: done the same day in the launcher, tools/app and tools/ui.xaml, compiled with 0 errors and the same four warnings as before. Play means Play: the two-slot bar, StartAs, the creation dialog (Creation.cs), CharSync.cs and Account.cs are gone, with a dated comment at each place. Before the game starts, Chars.Prepare points the save junction at one folder (Profile\Characters\saves), scrubs it, writes gameData.chooseAtMenu true with the last played id (or the spare) as gameData.profileId, writes thornswood-characters.json (every played row from profiles.txt with name, race, trade, town, where and hours from the roster, plus a spare id minted on a slot 0 row), deletes a stale thornswood-choice.txt, fetches the voice token for the last id, and checks every known id plus the spare in with the site in the background so the door knows them. While the game runs, the existing 2 s timer polls thornswood-choice.txt; on a pick it records the character (a spare becomes a played row and a new spare is minted), fetches the voice token for that id (Voice.Reconfigure(int)), checks it in again, and AddPlaytime at close is by that id. The client settings are never written while the game runs. Checked by a second agent against a nine point contract: every point met, two things it found are fixed in the same commit (the Server page still named the picker; a Skyrim started by hand after the launcher opened would have had its settings rewritten under it, now Play goes straight through as for a running game), and Help item 2 says what the hall does now. LEFT ON PURPOSE: old installs keep Profile\Characters\1, 2 and active.txt, unused; AutoJoin.SetProfileId, Chars.Read and Chars.Who have no callers; Add-Characters.ps1 stays because it installs po3_StartOnSave, and Characters.ps1 stays but lists a register nothing feeds (its own entry below). The per-id check-ins are queued, not awaited, before Process.Start, so a very quick pick at the menu could reach the door before the site's list has that id; the door's list refreshes every 30 s and a pick takes longer than that, and enforce on the VPS has not been measured. ## What is known

ASKED FOR BY DJINN in Discord, 20 September 19:12: 'a playtester checking sheet so when they start testing they can log in to the log and when they log out so we can keep track for records'. WHAT THERE WAS: the launcher counted its own sessions and minutes per install and sent them nowhere, and the site kept a last played stamp per Discord account in linked.json. The console had Test these and Test results, which is what to try and what happened, and nothing about who was on or for how long. BUILT fcedc8f: the launcher makes one session id at Play, posts the start, and posts the end with the minutes and whether the person quit or the launcher closed the game for an update; the site keeps one row a session (session id, the Discord id and name from the ticket and never from the body, the profile, the build, the launcher version, start, end, minutes, why, and a staff note), refuses a ban Discord confirms, and holds one account to thirty starts an hour so nobody can roll a capped log over; the console's Play sessions tab lists them newest first with the week's totals and a note box staff type into, which is the sheet part. Nobody has to remember to sign in or out. FOUR THINGS THE REVIEW CAUGHT AND I FIXED before the commit: the comment claimed the ban check stopped the log being scrubbed when any linked account could have done it (the thirty an hour is what stops it now); open rows were counted in the week's totals so the session and people counts climbed while the hours did not (they are counted on their own and said separately); 'still playing' was a claim the site cannot make about a machine that died, so it reads 'no end reported'; and the zero state said 'under a minute of it' for nothing at all. OUT ON DEV 19:33 in pack 20260920-1933-dev with launcher 1.1.62.1, and the site is deployed, so the tab is live at thornswood.net for anybody with an admin role. Harnesses: the routes 47 checks, the console tab 32, the console's other tabs 34, the launcher compiles with 0 errors. LEFT: (a) it goes to main with the next release; (b) a session whose end never posts stays open for good, and whether a row open for a day should be closed by the site or left visible is a decision for Patrick and Djinn; (c) somebody who connects without the launcher leaves no row, because only the launcher reports; (d) Shell.cs is on CLAUDE.md's list of files that want a line in #dev first, and today's edits to it (the Play lock, the update close, the start line, and this) are owed one before Djinn pulls. OUT ON MAIN 19:35 as launcher 1.1.63, pack unchanged. The tab is live and fills as people play. LIVE ON MAIN since launcher 1.1.63 and unchanged since. The tab fills as people play. What this entry still names is a look rather than a fix: a tester plays, the row lands with both ends, and Djinn reads the week on one page. The four caveats written into it stay true and are worth keeping: a session that ends with the machine going down has no end, the retention is a decision nobody has made, somebody who connects without the launcher leaves no row, and Shell.cs edits want a #dev line before Djinn pulls.

## 80. (done) DONE: every launcher build repointed the Desktop Thornswood icon at the dev launcher

**Order:** 80 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Patrick's machine, measured 22 September · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, the Shortcut block · -Root defaults to C:\Thornswood-DevBuild

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER while looking for dev build files inside the play install, and it is the thing that was actually wrong. The Shortcut block wrote Thornswood.lnk to the Desktop pointing at whatever -Root was, and -Root defaults to C:\Thornswood-DevBuild. So EVERY compile repointed the Desktop icon called "Thornswood" at the DEV launcher, which follows the dev feed and joins the dev server on 7787. That includes the compile check a Claude runs and the one inside Ship, so it happened constantly and silently. MEASURED: the Desktop Thornswood.lnk pointed at C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe and was written 9/21 23:47:03, the minute the dev build was last compiled. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the shortcut kept the right name and the right artwork, and the Start menu was correct the whole time, Thornswood.lnk at C:\Thornswood and Thornswood Dev.lnk at the dev build. Only the Desktop was wrong, and the Desktop is what gets used. FIXED as a3890d2. A build names its shortcut after the build it is: Thornswood.lnk for the play install, Thornswood Dev.lnk for a -DevBuild root. A dev build also takes away a Thornswood.lnk it finds pointing into its OWN root, and leaves one pointing at the play install alone, because that one is not its to remove. CI is unaffected: it passes -Root under RUNNER_TEMP, which does not end in -DevBuild. PROVED BY A REAL BUILD, not by reading: the build printed "removed a Thornswood.lnk in C:\Thornswood-DevBuild that pointed at the dev build", "Thornswood Dev.lnk points at the exe now" and "the play install's own Thornswood.lnk is left alone", and the Desktop Thornswood.lnk still points at C:\Thornswood afterwards. The Desktop icon on this machine was also repointed by hand, since the fix only governs the next build.

## Done when

Done. A dev build leaves the Desktop Thornswood.lnk alone, proved by running one.

## Traps

Do not "fix" this by having the dev build stop writing a shortcut at all: it needs its own, and it had one. The two names are the fix. Build-Launcher.ps1 is run by CI, so anything added to that block runs on a runner too.

## Where it lives

Patrick's machine · C:\Thornswood\_dist, 940 files, 10,933.3 MB · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:157 $DistDir = Join-Path $Root '_dist' · tools\Ship.ps1:550 $zip = Join-Path $Root '_dist\Thornswood-Setup.zip' · C: has 23.7 GB free

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER, and it is the thing he meant by the dev files touching his client files. The Desktop shortcut was a separate fault and is fixed; this is the real one. THE SHAPE OF IT: $Root is the play install, C:\Thornswood, and the release machinery builds inside it. Publish-Update.ps1 sets $DistDir to $Root\_dist and Ship.ps1 writes $Root\_dist\Thornswood-Setup.zip. So every release stages, zips and leaves its output in the folder the launcher manages and Patrick plays from. Nothing about the game needs it there. It is there because $Root was the only path in scope. MEASURED 22 SEPTEMBER, and the number is the argument: C:\Thornswood\_dist holds 940 files and 10,933.3 MB. That is 62 pack zips going back to 15 September, kept forever because nothing prunes them, including pack-20260917-1606-1 through -7 at about 6.6 GB together and pack-20260917-1619-1 through -3 at about 2.7 GB, which are the 11.3 GB near-miss run and the run after it. Plus _dist\stage at 877 files and 955.9 MB, Thornswood-Setup.zip at 508.5 MB and Thornswood-Setup.exe. C: HAS 23.7 GB FREE. A release that stages a full pack needs several GB of that, and the play folder is where it is spent. This is not tidiness: it is the disk the game runs from. THREE MORE THINGS ARE IN THERE THAT ARE NOT THE CLIENT EITHER. C:\Thornswood\tools holds four scripts from 16 September, Clean-OtherServer.ps1, Find-DaedricFiles.ps1, Find-DaedricOnline-All.ps1 and Restore-KzlContent.ps1, which are about the OTHER launchers and are not Thornswood's own tools. C:\Thornswood\_quarantine holds logo.nif and Mainmenuwallpaper.dds. config.json.before-voiceurl is a hand backup from 17 September. AND TWO OLD GAME FOLDERS: Game-old-20260917-1623 and Game-old-20260917-2233, 41,880.9 MB each by apparent size. How much real disk they hold is NOT measured, because the big files are hard links by design and an apparent size says nothing about what deleting them frees. Measure before deleting, and measure by counting names per file rather than by size. WHAT THE CHANGE IS: $DistDir stops being derived from $Root. It belongs beside the dev tree rather than inside the thing being shipped, and a -DistRoot switch with a sensible default is the whole of it. Old packs want a keep-the-last-N rule in the same change, or the new folder fills up the same way. WHAT TO BE CAREFUL OF, because this is the machinery that publishes: Ship-Rules.ps1 decides what is ours by path, Publish-Update reads and writes several things under $DistDir including reference-plugins.txt, and the baseline that decides what has changed since the last release must keep pointing at the same place or the next release recomputes everything and offers the whole collection as an update. That is the 29,063 file, 11,368.1 MB near miss of 17 September, and it is exactly this area of the code. CLOSED 22 SEPTEMBER, commit c3b5fb8. $DistDir no longer comes from $Root. Releases stage under C:\Thornswood-Dev\dist, one folder per install root so main and the dev build keep the separate areas they always had. -DistRoot moves the lot, and Ship passes it to Publish-Update and Package-Thornswood so all three agree on one answer rather than each deciding for itself. -KeepPacks, ten by default, prunes older packs AFTER the upload and never before it. MEASURED WITH A NEW TOOL RATHER THAN GUESSED. tools\Measure-Reclaim.ps1 counts the names on each file through GetFileInformationByHandle, one open per file instead of a process per file, so thirty thousand files take seconds. C:\Thornswood\_dist: 941 files, every byte with ONE name, so 10.9 GB real. THE OLD FOLDER IS GONE and 10.2 GB came back, 22.3 GB free to 32.5 GB. Checked before deleting, not after: the baseline lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json and never lived in _dist, and of the 61 pack zips in there NONE was in the published feed. The two biggest sets, pack-20260917-1606-* at about 6.6 GB and -1619-* at 2.7 GB, are the aborted 11.3 GB near-miss run and the run after it: built, never published, never referenced. The installer and the ten newest packs were moved across first. A DRY RUN PROVED THE BASELINE SURVIVED, which was the whole risk: "0 added or changed, 0 removed". THE TWO OLD GAME FOLDERS ARE MEASURED AND LEFT. Game-old-20260917-1623 and -2233 read 41,880.9 MB each and free 1,468.6 MB each, because 40,412.3 MB of each is hard linked to the live game folder. So deleting both frees 2.9 GB, not 83.8 GB. They are backups from 17 September and free space is no longer pressing, so they stay until somebody decides otherwise. That is what this entry meant by measure first. ALSO OUT OF THE PLAY INSTALL: the four other-launcher scripts from C:\Thornswood\tools, which exist nowhere else, moved to C:\Thornswood-Dev\other-launcher-scripts rather than deleted. _quarantine removed on Patrick's word, since he no longer plays vanilla Skyrim or other servers. C:\Thornswood is now the client and nothing else. ONE THING MISSED, found 22 September. Publish-Installer.ps1 still defaults -OutDir to C:\Thornswood\_dist, the folder this entry took away. Package-Thornswood is not affected when it publishes, because it passes its own -OutDir. But the recovery line it prints when publishing fails says to run .\tools\Publish-Installer.ps1 with nothing after it, and that looks in a folder that no longer exists. Change the default to C:\Thornswood-Dev\dist\Thornswood\_dist, or work it out the way Ship and Publish-Update do, and make the recovery line name the folder. THE LAST LINE IS DONE, 23 September, pull request 154. Publish-Installer.ps1 defaulted to C:\Thornswood\_dist, which was deleted in the very move this entry is about and took 10.2 GB with it, while Package-Thornswood builds into C:\Thornswood-Dev\dist\Thornswood\_dist. So running the publisher on its own threw "not built" and named a folder nobody has, and that bare command is exactly what Package's own recovery line tells you to run when publishing fails. The default is the folder Package builds into now, and the recovery line names the folder, reading the same -OutDir the run used so it is right even when somebody passed their own. Checked afterwards: Thornswood-Setup.exe and Thornswood-Setup.zip are both in that folder.

That needs uploading as part of the revision. THREE. ## 83. (done) DONE: a wipe reported success and left the live world untouched

**Order:** 83 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Handover · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\Wipe-Saves.ps1 · fixed as pull request 99 · the VPS, C:\Thornswood-Server and C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER BY RUNNING IT, and it had been wrong every time before. The survey walks every folder under C:\ holding a server-settings.json and emits a ROOT line for each. The reader kept a single $root, so it held whichever came LAST, and the move and the restart used only that one. On the VPS the last one is C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev. So a wipe took the dev world, left the live world alone, and printed a list of BOTH as though it had taken both. Measured straight after a run that reported success: C:\Thornswood-Server\world still held 2,177 files and private\characters.json was still there, while the dev ones were gone. AND THEN THE FIRST FIX HAD ITS OWN BUG, which is worth as much as the original. Roots were matched to scheduled tasks by a plain contains test, and C:\Thornswood-Server is a PREFIX of C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev, so the dev task claimed the live folder: it stopped the dev server twice, never stopped the live one, and moved the live world out from under a server that was still running. Each task now takes the LONGEST root its action mentions, read off the task itself. The -Task parameter is gone with it, because it named one task and decides nothing now, and a parameter that reads like it works is worse than no parameter. -Yes was added in the same change so a release can be run start to finish with nobody sitting at it. Read-Host reads the console rather than standard input, so a scripted wipe cannot answer the typed confirmation however it is fed: piping, and redirecting stdin from a file, both come back empty and the script stops with "Left alone." The list of what would go is still printed first.

## Commands

- LEAVES THIS MACHINE. Wipes every server it finds. -Yes skips the typed confirmation, for an unattended run. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Wipe-Saves.ps1 -Yes -NoPause
  ```
- LEAVES THIS MACHINE. The same thing, asking first. Type WIPE. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Wipe-Saves.ps1
  ```

## Done when

Done. Both worlds are empty, both tasks are running, and the live server was stopped and started cleanly afterwards.

## Traps

A script that prints a list and then acts on part of it reads exactly like one that acted on all of it. Nothing about the output said otherwise: the summary listed both servers and the move listed one, and only somebody counting the lines would notice. When a tool reports on more than one thing, check that what it DID matches what it LISTED, on the box, not in the output.

## 84. (done) DONE: A dev session on /sessions shows what was said on dev, not the live server's lines

**Order:** 84 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Site · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\docs-app\server.js chatSlice and /api/session-logs · tools\docs-app\public\index.html drawLogs · WAITING ON Deploy-Docs

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER: "I also want the what people said to be in each persons session so they are all organized in one place and by person with the other logs and files", then "remove the whole what people said page and just in /sessions under each person correctly split". WHY IT WAS WRONG BEFORE: the chat log was a page of its own, a day at a time, for everybody at once. Answering "what did this person do" meant reading a session on /sessions, working out when it ran, going to the other page, picking the day, filtering by name, and holding the two together in your head. WHAT THE SPLIT IS, and it is the part that can be silently wrong: a chat line carries profileId and at, a session carries profile, start and end. chatSlice matches both, using the same window the server log slice already widened by a minute either side, because the launcher stamps the session and the voice service stamps the line and those are not the same moment. A slice too wide puts somebody else's words, or last night's, into a report about behaviour. A slice too narrow drops what was said. Neither looks like a fault on the page: both render as a tidy list. The lines come back inside /api/session-logs, and drawLogs shows them as a details block beside that session's logs, downloading as chat-<profile>.txt with the rest. Slash commands are kept and marked. A line from a connection that could not show a signed token is marked unproven. Voice is not recorded. A session that runs over midnight reads both day files. GONE WITH IT: /api/chat, the /chat route, its entry in LEVEL, its nav entry, its title and its draw branch, and 5,049 characters of page code. tools\test-session-chat.js is 21 checks against the real function, most of them the boundaries one at a time. LEFT: Deploy-Docs, which is what puts it on the site. DONE 24 September, pull request #298, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: The chat shown under a session on /sessions now comes from the voice service that session actually ran on. Before this, every session read the live service's folder, C:\Thornswood-Voice\chat. So a dev session showed nothing, or showed what the same profile number said on the live server in that window. chatSlice now takes the session's channel and chooses the folder by the same rule serverLogSlice uses for the server log: dev reads C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev\chat, and main or an unstated channel reads the live folder. /api/session-logs passes row.channel in. For a dev day with no dev file, the reason text now says the dev log is the one missing. The docs-app README names the dev folder too. MEASURED: The dev chat folder comes from the repo, not a guess. voice-server.js:195 writes chat to path.join(HERE,'chat') unless THORNSWOOD_CHAT_DIR is set. Neither Install-Voice.ps1 (task line :197) nor vps-dev-instance.ps1 (run file :80-86) sets that variable. vps-dev-instance.ps1:23, Get-Logs.ps1:77 and voice\README.md:50-57 all put the dev service in C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev. Get-Logs -Dev pulled logs\dev\voice.log from C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev on 23 Sep, and it reads "listening on 127.0.0.1:7789", the dev port. logs\dev\health.json shows auth on and bind 127.0.0.1, which is the shape Install-Voice.ps1 installs. The code is at tools/docs-app/server.js: CHAT_DIRS at :1199, chatSlice(profileId, from, to, channel) at :1227, the folder choice at :1231, and the call at :2765 (chatSlice(row.profile, from, to, row.channel)). tools/test-session-chat.js went from 21 to 36 checks, all passing. I ran the new harness against the pre-change server.js in a scratch copy and it failed 8 of the 36, including "and never the live server's lines for the same profile", which is the bug itself. STILL TO DO BY A PERSON: For Patrick: merge, then .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1. That sends the site app off this machine and is what makes the fix visible. After the deploy, open a dev session on /sessions, go to More details, and confirm "What they said" shows that person's dev chat. It is configurable: THORNSWOOD_DEV_CHAT_DIR overrides the dev folder, and if unset it defaults to C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev\chat. Nothing on the VPS needs to change. Once the site is deployed and a dev session has been checked, the entry's doneWhen holds for dev and live. They do not read any file this change touches. It is worth an entry if the sweep is ever meant to run under 5.1. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. ## 85. (done) DONE: the site asks Discord once for the whole member list, not once per person

**Order:** 85 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Site · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\docs-app\server.js guildMembers and memberOf · pull request 101 · WAITING ON Deploy-Docs

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER in the live server log while reading a deploy. "[thornswood door] the site could not reach Discord, keeping the list as it was: rate limited by Discord" at 16:44, 16:49, 16:54, 16:59, 17:04 and 17:09. Once per refresh, every five minutes. THE CAUSE: /api/allowed walks every linked account and asked Discord about each one separately. standingCached holds an answer for sixty seconds and BOTH the live and dev doors ask every five minutes, so the cache was always cold by the time they came back. About forty lookups per door, two doors, every five minutes, in a burst. THE FIX: guildMembers asks for the whole guild once and caches it the same sixty seconds; memberOf reads that list and only asks about one person when it has to, which is a full page of 1000 back (the page limit rather than the whole guild, so a miss proves nothing) or a refused bulk call. IT NEEDS THE SERVER MEMBERS INTENT, which is a switch in the Discord developer portal and may be off. A 403 comes back and every caller falls through to the single lookup it used before, so this can only help or change nothing. WORTH CHECKING THAT SWITCH while this is going out, because with it on the whole thing is one request. THE BUG IN THE FIX, caught by the test and worth as much as the original: the cache guard tested the payload, so a failure was never remembered, because a failure stores null and null is falsy. A guild with the intent off would ask for the whole list ONCE PER PERSON, ten refused list requests for ten people on top of their ten single lookups, which is worse than not having the change. Keyed on the timestamp now. tools\test-discord-members.js is 15 checks and COUNTS THE REQUESTS, because that is the whole point of the change and the one thing that cannot be seen by reading the answer. LEFT: Deploy-Docs. CONFIRMED WORKING 22 SEPTEMBER, and two things said along the way were wrong. Measured from the VPS with a script that reproduces docs-app\server.js discordGet exactly, same module, same header shape, same host, with the token read on the box and never printed: GET /guilds/{id}/members?limit=1000 answers 200 with ALL 21 MEMBERS IN ONE REQUEST. So the Server Members intent is on and the change does what it was written to do: one request per door refresh where it was about forty one. WRONG THING ONE: an earlier probe using Invoke-WebRequest got 403 on every guild endpoint and that was read as the intent being off. It is not. Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends a browser shaped request and Discord refuses it at the edge with a BARE 403 AND AN EMPTY BODY. A real Discord 403 always carries JSON, a message and a code. The empty body was the tell, it was noticed, and it was talked past anyway. Patrick said the intent was already enabled and he was right. THE RULE: probe an API the way the thing under test calls it. The site is node, so the probe is node. WRONG THING TWO, which followed from the first: the clean door refresh at 17:45:30 was called "the rate limit window resetting, not the fix". With the intent on, it was the fix. 17:25, 17:30, 17:35 and 17:40 were all rate limited, and 17:45 was the first refresh after the deploy. THE SITE WRITES ITS CONSOLE OUTPUT NOWHERE, which is why none of this could be read directly and why it took two wrong turns. That has its own entry below.

## Commands

- Read only. 15 checks, counting requests. Must say 0 failed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node .\tools\test-discord-members.js
  ```
- LEAVES THIS MACHINE. Sends the site app. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1
  ```
- Read only, TALKS TO THE VPS. After the deploy, the rate limit line should stop appearing every five minutes. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Server-Log.ps1 -Tail 40
  ```

## Done when

Done. The bulk member list answers 200 with 21 members in one request, and a door refresh costs one request instead of forty one.

## Traps

A cache that stores a failure as null and then tests the stored value for truthiness is not caching the failure at all, and the case it fails on is the one where the thing is already broken. AND THE PROBE TRAP: do not test an API with a different client from the one under test. Invoke-WebRequest gets a bare empty bodied 403 from Discord where node gets 200 with the same token. An error body that is empty, when the service always sends JSON, means the request never reached the service.

## 88. (done) DONE: revision 5 is out, the server follows it, and two releases went with it

**Order:** 88 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** run it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 47

## Where it lives

Patrick's machine · Nexus collection ombo2a revision 5, published 22 September · %APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\mods\collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z · C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt still names the five plugins revision 5 removed · tools\app\OwnGame.cs WhyNot · tools\Ship-Rules.ps1 Get-ShipLoadOrderDir · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 -Vortex -NewOrder

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER while building a replacement for a staleness check that had never worked, and it is the more serious half of that finding. MEASURED, from Vortex's own state database and not guessed: the collection installed on this machine is collection_ombo2a_2_2026-09-15T21-08-00Z, revision 2, installed 15 September. Patrick says Nexus is on revision 4. So the machine is two revisions behind the collection it publishes. WHY THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. The server's load order is derived from THIS machine's Vortex deployment, and so is the reference plugin list that ships in every pack. So the server has been built against revision 2. Anybody installing the collection today gets revision 4, a different mod set, which does not match the server's manifest, so the positional check refuses them Play. The check is working exactly as intended; the problem is that it is protecting a server built from a stale collection. AND NOTHING SAID SO, which is the entry underneath this one. CollectionProblem decided staleness by asking whether po3_StartOnSave.dll existed, a file the collection has never carried and Add-Characters.ps1 installs by hand, so this machine read as fine while drifting two revisions. PATRICK'S OWN MACHINE DOES NOT SHOW THE FAULT, and that is worth stating plainly: it matches the server perfectly, because both are on revision 2. The people who cannot play are the ones who did it right. THE FIX IS A SEQUENCE AND NOT A COMMAND. Update the collection in Vortex to revision 4, let it deploy, then re-derive everything from it: the load order moves, so the server has to be rebuilt and a release has to carry the new reference list, and that is one complete release with the server. Expect the plugin set to have changed across two revisions; Deploy-Gamemode keeps the order the server already runs and names anything new or gone, which is the output to read carefully rather than skim. CORRECTED 22 SEPTEMBER, and the correction is a trap worth more than the original entry. This was written as "update to revision 4 and rebuild the server". That is only the first half. The mod removals that are wanted, TavernGames, Respawn - Death Overhaul, the three SunHelm plugins and possibly the Immersive Armors swap, ARE A NEW REVISION: editing a collection in Vortex and uploading it publishes one. SO THE ORDER MATTERS AND GETTING IT WRONG IS SILENT. Publishing a new revision from the profile currently installed here would cut it from REVISION 2, which would quietly undo everything revisions 3 and 4 added, Start On Save among them, and hand that to everybody as revision 5. Nobody would see it happen. It is the same fault as the server being derived from a stale deployment, pointed at Nexus instead, and it would be harder to notice because the collection would look freshly published. THE ORDER: update Vortex to revision 4 first so the profile holds what 3 and 4 added; confirm with Check-ShipReady that it reads 4; THEN make the removals; THEN publish revision 5; THEN update Vortex to 5, because the server must be derived from exactly what people download and not from a local profile that resembles it; then Deploy-Gamemode, Deploy-Server and one release. The revision gate helps here rather than getting in the way: after 5 is published Vortex will know 5 is newest, so Deploy-Gamemode refuses until the machine is actually on 5. That is the behaviour wanted. DONE 22 SEPTEMBER, THE VORTEX HALF, IN THE ORDER THIS ENTRY ASKED FOR. This machine went to revision 4 first (collection_ombo2a_4_2026-09-16T15-44-44Z), revision 5 was built from that profile and published on Nexus the same evening, and this machine was then updated to it: collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z. So 5 was cut from 4 and nothing 3 and 4 added was lost. What went into 5 is the entry below. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE SERVER AND ONE RELEASE, and six things found on the way change how they have to be run.
ONE, A LOOP THAT STOPS MAINTENANCE. Settings, Maintenance, Bring it up to date from Vortex refused on 22 September: "5 of Thornswood's 96 plugins are not in" the Steam copy, "so Vortex has another profile deployed". It is not another profile. OwnGame.WhyNot refuses if even one plugin in the reference list, Profile\Default\plugins.txt, is missing from the Steam copy, and that list still names the five plugins revision 5 took out. The reference list is only rewritten when a pack is applied (Updater.cs:533). A pack takes its reference list from Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt (Get-ShipLoadOrderDir) and its files from C:\Thornswood\Game, and only Maintenance refreshes either of those. So Maintenance waits for a release and a release waits for Maintenance, and any revision that removes a plugin walks into it. Shipping anyway would pack revision 4's files and list, and once the server names RaceCompatibility.esm and Playable Rieklings.esp, Get-ReferenceInServerOrder stops it because the old list does not enable them. THE WAY THROUGH WITHOUT CODE: take the five names out of Profile\Default\plugins.txt by hand, keeping a copy, and Maintenance runs. The next pack rewrites that file anyway. THE LASTING FIX is in OwnGame.WhyNot, which should tell another profile apart from the collection having moved on, for instance by the revision in the collection folder's name. That is a launcher change with its own #dev line, not part of this release.
TWO, DEPLOY-GAMEMODE NEEDS -VORTEX. Without it, it reads C:\Thornswood\Game\Data and Profile\Default\plugins.txt, and both are revision 4 until Maintenance and a release have run. -Vortex reads the Steam copy and the Vortex profile's Plugins.txt, which are revision 5, and Deploy-Server already sends plugins from the Steam copy. It also needs -NewOrder: RaceCompatibility.esm, which the Rieklings need, carries the master flag, and Deploy-Gamemode refuses to put a new master on the end of an order the world is keyed to. -NewOrder means a wipe. Patrick chose that when he added the Rieklings, and taking five plugins out of the middle would have re-keyed the world anyway.
THREE, THE GATE IS BLIND WHILE VORTEX IS OPEN. This entry said that once 5 was published, Deploy-Gamemode would refuse until the machine was on 5. Only with Vortex closed. Get-CollectionNewest reads Vortex's state database, and while Vortex runs the file with its newest writes cannot be read, so Newest comes back 0, which counts as unknown and is never mentioned. Close Vortex before Check-ShipReady or Deploy-Gamemode. Entry 48 has the fix.
FOUR, THE RECIPE TABLE IS STALE. Immersive Armors is now the script free version, whose plugin has 845 fewer tempering recipes than the one tools\recipes.json was read from, and recipes.json names Immersive Armors on 2,118 lines. Build-RecipeTable.ps1 rebuilds it from the plugins and writes its block into gamemode.js, so it runs before Deploy-Gamemode.
FIVE, NEMESIS AND THE LOOSE FILES COME BEFORE MAINTENANCE. Maintenance copies the Steam copy's Data into Thornswood's folder, and Package-Thornswood ships whatever in there Vortex did not provide. So the other servers' leftovers (entry 84) come out of the Steam copy first, and Nemesis, whose output there is from 11 September and was built for another mod list, is run against revision 5 first.
SIX, PUBLISH-INSTALLER ON ITS OWN LOOKS IN THE WRONG PLACE. Package-Thornswood publishes itself at the end unless given -NoPublish, passing its own output folder, C:\Thornswood-Dev\dist\Thornswood\_dist. Publish-Installer.ps1 run by itself still defaults to C:\Thornswood\_dist, which has not existed since entry 45. Run it by hand only if Package says it could not publish, and give it -OutDir. Entry 45 has the fix. DONE 22 SEPTEMBER, all of it, and the numbers are worth keeping. The reference list had the five removed plugins taken out by hand to break the deadlock between Maintenance and the release (backup at Profile\Default\plugins.txt.rev4.bak, 96 enabled down to 91). Maintenance then ran: the collection went from 29,444 files to 29,682, and 68 of those are Data\Platform\Distribution, which is the whole point. Build-RecipeTable rewrote 1,877 recipes for the new order. Check-ShipReady read READY on 20 checks. Deploy-Gamemode -Vortex -NewOrder built 57 plugins, 8 master-flagged, 0 positions changed, Thornswood-Content at index 23 rather than 22. Deploy-Server put up three plugins and Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp shrank from 1,722,345 to 1,121,002 bytes, which is the script free Immersive Armors arriving. Wipe-Saves emptied both worlds. TWO RELEASES, NOT ONE, and the second was Ship catching something nobody had. Release 20260922-1719 went out and Ship said: "the launcher changed but is still version 1.1.80, anyone already on that version will never be offered this build". It was right. Pull request 96 had added 158 lines across Checks.cs, Config.cs, Shell.cs and Updater.cs AFTER 1.1.80 shipped, and that is the code that reads which collection revision you are on and says so. So the release telling everybody to update to revision 5 was shipping without the thing that checks it. Bump-Version to 1.1.81, pull request 100, and release 20260922-1722 delivered it. THE BASELINE AND DELTA MODEL WORKED ON ITS FIRST RUN WITH NO CODE WRITTEN. Release 20260922-1719 read: "the collection provides 29,682 file(s), which are not published", then "1 added or changed (0.0 MB), 0 removed, 68 more were the collection's files, left alone". The entire release was one changed file and the plugin list. AND THE INSTALLER IS 0.36 GB, down from 511 MB. Package-Thornswood: 799 files kept where it was 871, 18,436 files and 9.9 GB left out because the collection provides them, payload 0.36 GB, one file, published. That is the 143 MB the client runtime was costing, gone, with nothing edited to make it happen. The 160 MB written on the entry before was wrong: it compared an unzipped size against a zipped one.

## Read first

- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:250-300`: the block that keeps the order the server already runs and names what is new or gone; this is the output that matters on a two revision jump
- `tools\LoadOrder.ps1`: Get-CollectionRevision, which is how the number is read, and the comment recording this finding
- `tools\app\OwnGame.cs:118-150`: WhyNot, where one missing plugin from the reference list stops Maintenance
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:255-262`: Get-ShipLoadOrderDir, why a pack's reference list comes from Profile\OwnGame and not from Vortex
- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:169-178`: what -Vortex reads instead of the own folder and the reference list
- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:390-410`: the refusal a new master-flagged plugin gets without -NewOrder

## 89. (done) DONE: Confirm at the end of character creation never landed, because the live server drained the dev voice queue

**Order:** 89 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

C:\Thornswood-Server\server-settings.json thornswoodVoicePort · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 · fixed as pull request 104

## What is known

FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER FROM A SCREENSHOT. Patrick could not finish a character: the Review page said "Sent. The server is checking." and nothing ever came back. The server log showed him reaching "chargen ff000000 -> choosing (the face arrived), panel opened" at 18:51:11 and then NOTHING. IT IS NOT THE COLLECTION, THE LOAD ORDER OR THE WIPE, all of which went out the same evening and all of which were the obvious suspects. HOW A PICK ACTUALLY TRAVELS, which is the thing worth keeping: slash commands do NOT go over the game connection. The panel sends every choice as a chat line, "/pick town whiterun". The voice service receives it, queues it rather than broadcasting it so nobody else sees it, and the GAMEMODE DRAINS THAT QUEUE over loopback with GET /commands. Three processes, and the middle one is the voice service. WHAT WAS WRONG: two voice services run on that box. 7778 is Thornswood Voice, the live one, out of C:\Thornswood-Voice. 7789 is Thornswood Dev Voice, out of C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev. C:\Thornswood-Server\server-settings.json said thornswoodVoicePort = 7789. So the LIVE game server was draining the DEV voice service. Measured at the moment of the fault: 7778 had peers 1 and queuedCommands 38, which is every retry Patrick made; 7789 had peers 0 and queuedCommands 0. HOW IT GOT THERE, proved rather than guessed. Only Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 and Publish-Server.ps1 write that key, and both write 7789 into the DEV settings. Deploy-DevGamemode was run against C:\Thornswood-Server, the live folder, on 20 September at 23:13, and left its own server-settings.json.before-20260920-231351 there. THAT BACKUP HOLDS NO thornswoodVoicePort AT ALL, which is what turned a theory into a fact. AND IT SURVIVED EVERY DEPLOY SINCE. Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 reads server-settings.json back and adds to it, force writing only loadOrder, name, port, offlineMode, dataDir and the npc and damage settings. A key nobody sets there lives for ever once anything puts it in. So two days of live deploys, including the two releases on 22 September, all carried it forward and none of them said a word. WHAT FOUND IT: THE CHAT LOG, which was only added that afternoon. It held every single "/pick town whiterun", at 18:51:42 and then on every retry at 18:51:57, 18:52:00, 18:52:01, 18:52:28, 18:52:29 and again at 19:04:28. That one read ruled out the client, the panel, the chat socket and the voice service in one go and left only the gap between the queue and the drain. FIXED, both halves. On the box: thornswoodVoicePort set to 7778, backup kept as server-settings.json.before-20260922-191145, live server restarted. It then logged "voice position feed running, pushing to 127.0.0.1:7778" and the 38 queued commands drained on the first poll. In the repo, pull request 104: Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 has a -VoicePort defaulting to 7778 and WRITES IT EVERY DEPLOY rather than inheriting whatever is in the file, and says so in yellow when it finds a value that is not its own, because a value that is not ours means a dev deploy was pointed at this folder. Setting it beats defaulting to it: gamemode.js already falls back to 7778 when the key is ABSENT, and absent was never the problem. A wrong value was, and a fallback cannot correct that. CONFIRMED WORKING at 19:14:05, "creation finished for ff000000: miner, smith/edgewright, home whiterun", and again at 19:22:57 for a second person with the whole sequence in it: "chargen ff000001 home = whiterun (WhiterunBanneredMare) -> done". That "home =" line had never appeared once before that evening.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:723-731`: GET /commands, the queue the gamemode drains over loopback. This is the path a slash command takes, and it is not the game connection
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-skills.js:1770-1773`: send() pushes a pick and calls tell(pick, words). The panel talks to the server as a chat line

## Traps

THE THREE PROCESS PATH IS THE TRAP. A pick looks like it goes from the panel to the server, and it goes panel, chat, voice service, queue, gamemode. When a pick does not land, ask which voice service is queueing it and which one the game server is draining, before looking at anything else. AND server-settings.json IS ADDITIVE: Deploy-Gamemode reads it back and force writes only the keys it knows about. Anything else in that file, however it got there, survives every deploy silently. ## 90. (done) DONE: the revision check only knew one of the two shapes Vortex writes, so it went blind the moment it was right

**Order:** 90 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\app\Shell.cs CollectionProblem · tools\app\Checks.cs CollectionRevision · tools\LoadOrder.ps1 Get-CollectionRevision · tools\Publish-Update.ps1

## What is known

CLOSED 22 SEPTEMBER, pull request 96. CollectionProblem returned "stale" when po3_StartOnSave.dll was missing, on the reasoning that the collection provides it and it carries no plugin, so the plugin count cannot see it. THE FILE IS NOT IN THE COLLECTION AND NEVER HAS BEEN: the installed collection.json lists 100 mods and it is not one of them. Add-Characters.ps1 puts it into a build by hand from an archive in Downloads. So the test was wrong both ways. Anybody who installed the collection properly and skipped that script read as behind. And Patrick, who had run it, read as fine while two revisions behind, which is the entry above. A NUMBER NOW. Vortex names the collection's mod folder collection_<slug>_<revision>_<when>, so there is a revision to read. Publish-Update writes it into version.json off the SHIPPING machine's install, because that deployment is what the release agrees with; it is not a claim about what is newest on Nexus. The launcher reads its own and compares. BEHIND AND AHEAD GET DIFFERENT WORDS, and ahead never had any. Behind names both numbers and says to open the collection. Ahead says the server has not caught up, that nothing is wrong with their install, that Play will refuse them on the load order until the server is rebuilt, and that rebuilding it is ours. Before this, somebody who had done everything right and was further forward than the server was refused with a load order message and no way to know it was not their fault. 0 is silence in both directions, never a guess: an older feed carries no number, and a wrong one tells everybody to reinstall a collection that is already correct. tools\test-collection-revision.js is 22 checks. The rule lives in C#, PowerShell and the test because the three cannot share code, so six checks assert the shape of the other two copies and one asserts the StartOnSave test has not crept back. REOPENED 22 SEPTEMBER, one hole. Get-CollectionNewest in LoadOrder.ps1 reads Vortex's state database with ReadAllBytes. While Vortex is running, the file with its newest writes could not be read, the catch swallowed that, and Newest came back 0 with revision 5 already published. 0 is silence by design, so with Vortex open nothing ever says the machine is behind, which is exactly when somebody is working in it. Worth trying first: open each file with FileShare.ReadWrite instead of ReadAllBytes. If Vortex will not allow even that, say so (newest unknown, close Vortex) instead of saying nothing. ALSO: the line above saying Start On Save was never in the collection was true of revision 2. Revision 3 added it (entry 49). REOPENED 22 SEPTEMBER, and the new fault is worse than the one this entry was closed on. MEASURED with Vortex running and the machine on revision 5: Get-CollectionState returns Have 5, Newest 0, Behind False. Newest comes from Get-CollectionNewest, which reads Vortex's own state.v2, and Vortex holds that LevelDB open while it is running, so the read returns nothing and the function answers 0. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE GATE. Behind is computed as ($have -gt 0 -and $newest -gt 0 -and $have -lt $newest), so a newest of 0 makes Behind False no matter how far behind the machine actually is. Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 then deploys without complaint and Check-ShipReady.ps1 ticks that check green. The refusal that was added on 22 September to stop the server being built from a stale collection is OFF whenever Vortex is open, which is most of the time somebody is working on the collection, which is exactly when it matters. It is not lying about the number: it prints newest 0 in the detail. It is the verdict that is wrong, and the verdict is what people read. THE FIX IS TO REFUSE ON AN UNREADABLE NEWEST RATHER THAN PASS ON IT. A revision check that cannot read the newest revision has not checked anything and should say so and stop, the same way Deploy-Server refuses a binary it cannot hash. Either that, or read the revision from somewhere Vortex does not lock. Until it is fixed, the workaround is to close Vortex before Check-ShipReady or any Deploy, and that workaround is a thing to remember, which is what this entry says should not be relied on. THE CAUSE WRITTEN ABOVE IS WRONG AND THE REAL ONE IS WORSE. Corrected 22 September. It is NOT the Vortex file lock. Get-CollectionNewest was measured with Vortex fully closed and still answered 0. WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: the function knew ONE shape, the transition Vortex writes the moment it notices a newer revision than the one installed, "newestVersion","from":"3","to":"4". That shape only exists WHILE THE MACHINE IS BEHIND. The moment revision 5 was installed there was no transition left to record, Vortex wrote the plain current value instead, the regex matched nothing, and it answered 0. SO THE GATE WENT BLIND ON THE DAY IT WAS ADDED, and precisely at the moment it started being correct to pass. Behind is false when either number is unknown, deliberately, so the refusal added that same day to stop a stale collection reaching the server passed without checking anything, hours later, in the same sitting. THE PLAIN SHAPE, measured off this machine's own state.v2 rather than guessed a third time: 6E 65 77 65 73 74 56 65 72 73 69 6F 6E 03 22 35 22, which is the key, then ONE length byte, then that many bytes of JSON: "5". A deleted key writes a length of 0 and no value. FIXED as pull request 103. Both shapes are read and the highest wins. The length byte is matched as a bounded control character class rather than a wildcard, because a bare four character wildcard steps over a quote and reads the number out of a neighbouring key. AND THE OTHER HALF: Deploy-Gamemode refuses an unreadable revision now rather than falling through, the way Deploy-Server refuses a binary it cannot hash. A check that cannot read its numbers has not checked anything, and until this "up to date" and "could not tell" were the same answer to anybody reading the bool. -IgnoreRevision is the way past it. tools\test-collection-newest.ps1 is 16 checks. It builds a state.v2 out of those exact bytes and points the SHIPPED function at it through APPDATA. VERIFIED AFTER: have 5, newest 5, behind False, known True, where it read newest 0 before, and Check-ShipReady reports "the collection here is the newest Vortex knows of (revision 5, newest 5)" as a real check on 21 checks rather than a note on 20. NO RELEASE IS OWED: LoadOrder.ps1 and Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 only ever run on Patrick's machine, so the pull is the change.

## Steps

- [ ] Read the state files with FileShare.ReadWrite, and when a file still cannot be read, say that the newest revision is unknown and to close Vortex. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\LoadOrder.ps1 -Pattern 'ReadAllBytes'
  ```

## Commands

- Read only. With Vortex OPEN this returns Have 5, Newest 0, Behind False, which is the defect. With Vortex CLOSED it returns the real newest. Run it both ways to see it. (claude)

## Traps

 Behind False does not mean up to date. It also means "could not tell", and the two are indistinguishable in the verdict. Read the Have and Newest numbers, not the tick. AND THE LESSON THAT COST TWO WRONG CAUSES: the first guess was the Vortex lock and the second was the regex being close enough. Neither survived looking at the bytes. When a reader of somebody else's file format returns nothing, dump the bytes around the key before writing a word about why.

## 93. (done) DONE: every session's logs are collected, and one that went wrong says so

**Order:** 93 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Website · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\app\Discord.cs SessionLogs and SendPendingLogs · tools\docs-app\server.js /api/play/logs, /api/session-logs, /api/session-keep · tools\discord\bot.py watch_trouble · tools\test-session-logs.js

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER: collect the logs so he no longer has to ask, so testing can narrow a fault down without a round trip, and so that when the server goes public there is something to point at when somebody is suspended. Shipped in 1.1.79, commits b75a62b and 96e9dae. THE LAUNCHER SENDS THEM AS THE GAME CLOSES, which is the only moment it can: the game truncates its own logs under Data\Platform at every start. Eight files, the tail of each. AND AGAIN AT THE NEXT START when a session ended without them, because a launcher that was killed never runs SessionEnd and that crash is exactly the session somebody wants afterwards. A marker file remembers; it clears on 200, on 409 and on 404, which is what stops a dead marker being retried for ever. WRITTEN ONCE, because it is evidence. A second set for the same session is refused and the attempt recorded on the first, or anybody who knew the endpoint could do something worth banning for and then post a clean set over the top. The Discord id comes off the ticket, never the body, and a sha256 of every log is recorded so a copy pasted into an argument months later can be held against the one on the box. KEPT BY AGE, NOT BY THE ROLLING LIST: a year, and Keep as evidence holds one indefinitely and records who held it. Tying them to sessions.json would have deleted an old incident the moment two thousand newer sessions had happened. THE SERVER HALF IS NOT STORED. It is sliced out of the game server's own log on demand by the session's window, because that log is already on the box and a second copy would go stale against the first. TWO COLOURS ON THE PAGE. Red is a crash or an unhandled throw and the bot says so in #staff-general. Yellow is a session that failed for a reason already understood, an update that did not install or a load order that did not match, and Discord hears nothing, because there are a lot of those. Red is looked for first. NEVER THE CARD, only the session: one bad evening out of forty does not make a red person. THE LAUNCHER'S OWN BLOCKERS AND WARNINGS COME WITH THE LOGS and carry more than the launcher's window shows: which plugin, absent or merely wrong bytes, and the size, CRC and manifest index the server wanted. More details under a session names each file, expands each on its own and downloads each. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, and it matters for the ban case rather than the testing one: nothing records what anybody SAID. Chat and voice are not logged, so an argument about behaviour is still one person's word against another's. That is its own entry. TWO THINGS WENT WRONG AND WERE FIXED THE SAME DAY. The bot first announced in #news, because TROUBLE_ID fell back to the watcher's channel and never reached the name lookup (109c80e); the deploy log is what showed it. And the pack tidy threw on the 1.1.79 release reading .Count on a scalar under Set-StrictMode (8cd6252), which without StrictMode tests clean in a bare prompt.

## Done when

Done and shipped in 1.1.79. A session that crashes is red on the page and said in #staff-general; one stopped by an update or a load order is yellow and silent; More details gives every log with a download.

## Traps

Write-once is the point: never add a path that lets a set be replaced. The trouble markers are deliberately few, and a looser one ("error") turns every session red and makes the whole thing useless; there is a check for exactly that. The bot treats whatever is already in trouble.json at startup as said, so a crash while the bot was down is on the page and not in Discord, which is the right trade.

AND THE PEOPLE IN THE WORLD ARE TOLD, which is the trap written on this entry and the part it would have been easy to skip. The rules page now says plainly that text chat is kept with a name and a time, that VOICE IS NOT RECORDED and nothing reads their machine, why it exists, that it protects them as much as anybody because it is what shows they did not say the thing, who can read it and how long it is kept. ## 103. (done) DONE: nine packs carried a voice token, and the next release takes it back

**Order:** 103 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** measure it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Your PC · the release folder Publish-Update writes and Repair-Manifest.ps1 reads · the VPS copy of the packs

## What is known

FOUND 20 SEPTEMBER, commit 15c472a fixes the rule: Data\Platform\voice-token.txt, one person's signed join token for the voice room, was never on the machine-files list in Ship-Rules, while voice-port, voice-status and voice-ptt beside it were. Publish-Update packs anything not on that list that differs from the baseline, so a pack built on a machine that had played could have carried Patrick's token. The token lives sixty minutes and proves one profile id to the voice service only, so a stale one opens nothing; but a token in a pack that hundreds of installs download is a token in the open, and the rule was the fault, not luck. NOT MEASURED YET: the scratchpad copies of the dev and main manifests do not list it, and no local pack record was found this session; the release folder and the packs on the VPS are where the answer is. MEASURED 23 SEPTEMBER, which is the thing this entry said had not been done, and the answer is yes. The token file first existed on 18 September (b2a9f9d) and the packing rule that excludes it landed on 20 September (15c472a), so the window is thirteen published packs. NINE OF THEM CARRY game/Data/Platform/voice-token.txt: 20260918-1615, 20260918-2340, 20260919-1416, 20260919-1546, 20260919-1944, 20260919-2010, 20260919-2044, 20260920-1103 and 20260920-1124. The other four do not. Counted by listing the NAMES inside each zip; no token was opened or printed, which is what this entry asks for. WHAT IT IS: a signed join token proving one profile id to the voice service, sixty minutes long, so every one of these expired in September and opens nothing. The fault was the rule rather than the damage. THE FIX IS THE ONE map.swf TAUGHT: leaving a file out of new packs does nothing for the machines that already have it, so DataPlatform\voice-token.txt goes on  in Ship-Rules.ps1 and the next release deletes it from every install that took one of the nine. Harmless on a working machine, because the launcher writes a fresh token at Play and an update is applied before that. Pull request 155. AND THE PUBLISHED PACKS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, which is a correction to what this entry asked for: rewriting a release asset changes its sha256, version.json records that hash for every pack, and a launcher that took the old one would fail its checksum and stop. Breaking the feed to remove an expired token is the worse trade.

## Done when

Done. The nine are named and counted, the path is on the delete-always list so the next release removes it from every install that got one, and the reason for leaving the published assets alone is written down.

## Traps

Do not print a token while checking. grep -c is enough.

Either way the three routes should not stay as they are. DELETED 23 September, pull requests 156 and 157, which is the first of the two answers this entry offered. A route that answers 403 to every real caller is a thing somebody will one day try to fix instead of delete, so /whoami, /claim and /owners are gone, along with the owners map and owners.json, saveOwners and its four second timer, steamOf, the SECRET that only those three routes read, and the two fields in /health that reported on them. 151 lines out of voice-server.js. toolsCharacters.ps1 existed only to read /owners and is deleted with them; its own header already said the register had not been fed since 20 September. Install-Voice no longer sends secret.txt, because sending a secret nothing reads is worse than sending nothing, and the nightly backup stops pulling secret.txt and owners.json off the box for the same reason. PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: all five voice harnesses pass, the service was run on a scratch port where /health and /ice answer normally and the three routes answer 404, and after installing on BOTH services the live and dev /whoami answer 404 from outside while both /health answer normally. The dead files are deleted from C:Thornswood-Voice and C:Thornswood-Voice-Dev, leaving only token-key.txt, which is the live join token signing key. THE IDENTITY THAT FLOWS is unchanged and is the site's linked.json, keyed by Discord id.

## Done when
