## Done when

K opens the menu in game, it does not eat movement or chat keys, it is listed on the launcher's key page, and the values in it come from the server rather than from the client. The first three are done as of 20 September; the fourth is the server side and has not started.

## Traps

The launcher rewrites key binds on every Play, so a bind has to be in Keys.cs or it will not survive. Check K is not already taken by something in the collection.

## 107. (done) DONE: progression for real and server sided: the class verbs, the profession and its half, the ranks, the spells and the skill tree

**Order:** 107 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** build it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js: the progression block (TABLE, RULES: pickClass, pickProfession, learnFrom, rankUp, spendPoint, canWork, canDo, perks) and the character block · tools\ts-ui\thornswood-skills.js: the K panel · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js: the one thing that runs on the client and can apply anything to the character · tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md: the rulebook, 236 lines, and the only place the rules are written down · dev only, on Patrick's word of 20 September

## What is known

PATRICK, 20 September: 'work on making all of the progression stuff real and server sided, all to dev only', then 'don't forget Class, Profession, Sub-Profession, and the skill tree', then the rule for how the tree fills: YOU START WITH POINTS ALREADY PLACED IN SPECIFIC THINGS BY WHAT YOU CHOSE (the class, the profession and the half of it), AND EVERY RANK YOU EARN IN YOUR PROFESSION GIVES MORE POINTS THAT GO ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. So the tree is part earned by who you are and part by what you have done, and the placed ones are not yours to move. WHAT WAS TRUE BEFORE ANY OF THIS: the rulebook was on the server as data and as pure rules, tested, and almost none of it was connected to the world. canDo(state, verb) existed and nothing called it, so a miner could pick flowers and a hunter could mine. s.spells existed and no rule ever spent a point. rankUp existed and only a Master teaching could call it, so nothing anywhere raised a rank from doing the work, which is the one thing classes.md says rank comes from. spendPoint could spend tree points that nothing awarded. MEASURED WHILE PLANNING, and it decides how two of these must be built: (1) the server cannot set a character's base health, magicka or stamina, because GetBaseActorValues computes them from the race record when the character is made and sends them with the spawn, so the tree cannot be applied that way; our own plugin Thornswood-Content.esp holds no SPEL, MGEF, PERK or ENCH records either (43 books, 4 furniture, 6 recipes, cells and references), so there is nothing to grant; the tree has to be applied by thornswood-front.js each session from numbers the server owns, which is clean because the client applies and never decides. (2) Professions and halves have no hook in Skyrim's own crafting benches from the server side; what the server owns is the quarry, the kiln and the beehive, and an older system where reading a manual raises a track (mining, smithing, woodcutter, alchemy, tiers 1 to 4) and the track gates the yield. That old system is what should become the rank ladder, so a smith's rank comes from smithing rather than from finding a book. STAGE ONE, in flight 20 September evening: the class gates on every verb the server hands a yield for, work counted per half and per class so a rank is earned by doing it, a spell rule that refuses anything the rank or the book does not support and grants the spell through the same Papyrus path a shrine blessing uses, the panel sending real picks, and tools\Build-SpellTable.ps1 reading the game's master files for the form ids because guessing those from memory is not good enough. STAGE TWO, next: the starting allocation above; points per rank; the profession and half gating everything the server owns; the manuals retired into ranks; the tree applied to the character by the plugin. THE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN THE RULEBOOK and are a knob: how much work a rank takes, how many points a rank gives, and which sub-skills each class, profession and half start you in. Every one of them lives in one named block with a comment saying the rulebook does not set it, so Patrick and Djinn can move them without reading code. WHAT THE SERVER CAN OWN, measured 20 September and decided by Patrick the same evening ('if it makes sense we can make it so the server does see it', then 'let's do that'). A class rank is worth having only where the server owns the verb, so the first question was which verbs it owns. GATHERING IT ALREADY OWNS, and nobody knew: MpObjectReference::ProcessActivate in the fork treats a FLOR or a TREE as pickable, reads the produce out of the record itself (resultItem), gives it to whoever pressed E, marks it harvested and schedules the regrowth, with no client involvement, and the gamemode's mp.onActivate is asked first and can refuse. So the gatherer gate covers every plant in the game the moment the gamemode has a list of which bases are plants; the HARVESTS map it carries today is two nirnroots, written by hand. MINING IT DOES NOT OWN: a vein is an ACTI whose behaviour is a Papyrus script, the server runs no scripts, so mining is client side and ungated. It can be taken over the way the salt quarry was: publishServerBases already tells the client which bases the server answers for, and onActivate answers them. A BODY is an actor rather than an activator and the gamemode reads nothing off it but baseDesc, so the hunter gate needs one measurement on dev: press E on a dead wolf, a dead bandit, a chest and a door with the ref's baseDesc logged, and see which of the four the server can tell apart. FISHING needs something built, because Skyrim's own fishing is a separate system. SO THE RANK LADDER, Patrick's shape and the same for all five classes: every source has a rank it needs before you may work it at all, and your rank sets how much it gives. Miner: iron and quicksilver, then silver and moonstone, then ebony and malachite, then gems and the deep seams. Gatherer: common reagents, then the ones with real alchemical value, then nirnroot and the rarities, then a second pick off the same plant. Hunter: meat and a torn hide, then a whole hide, then horn and tusk, then the rare pelts. Fisher: the shallows, then rivers, then cold deep water, then the named fish. Farmer: which crops, how much a plot gives, how fast it comes back. WHICH SOURCE SITS AT WHICH RANK IS NOT TASTE: tools\Build-HarvestTable.ps1 and tools\Build-OreTable.ps1 read every plant and every vein out of the game's own records and sort them by what the produce is worth in gold, with the thresholds in one named block, the same way the spell table was read rather than typed. WHAT LANDED ON 20 SEPTEMBER, EVENING. Committed on main, deployed nowhere yet. STAGE ONE AND STAGE TWO ARE BOTH IN, commit a96a22f. Every verb the server hands a yield for is gated on the class that owns it; a rank is earned by doing the work and nothing else raises one; the starting allocation places points by class, profession and half and a placed point cannot be moved; a rank gives a free tree point; the tree is applied to the character by thornswood-front.js out of panel.effects, because GetBaseActorValues means the server cannot write a base value itself. The manual tiers are retired: tierOf is deleted and reading a manual is now five pieces of work in the ladder it is about, once. A mage's schools climb on the two things the server can see, a spell learned and a rank gained elsewhere, because this file has four event hooks and none of them is a cast. SIX DEFECTS THE REVIEWERS FOUND WERE REAL AND ARE FIXED: a class or spell named __proto__ or constructor off the wire used to brick a character or eat a point, and every table indexed by a word from a person now goes through an own-property check; the panel drew nothing because the server sent work and the page read progress; a refusal carried no note.about so the panel could not place it; the panel was rebuilt and resent on every single flower and is now sent only when the drawn signature changes; and '/spend might -1' spent a point INTO Might because the amount was dropped on the floor. HARNESSES, all green: progtest 161, chartest 104, pagetest 270, selecttest 73, farm 33, treeapply 21, chargen 17, session 47, door 18. The 47 new checks were proved to FAIL against a copy of the file with the sixteen defect edits reversed, rather than being taken on trust. THE FOUR GENERATED TABLES, commit 0a04ef9: spells.json 85 spells each checked against the tome that teaches it, ores.json 581 veins in four ranks, harvests.json 181 plants in four ranks plus 11 farm crops. SPELL_IDS and CROPS_BY_BASE are installed into gamemode.js between their own markers. ORES_BY_BASE and HARVESTS_BY_BASE are NOT: the gamemode has no markers for them, so the gathering gate is still running on a hand written two entry HARVESTS map and mining is still ungated. That is entry 43 and it is the next sitting. A DEFECT IN THE TABLE SCRIPTS THEMSELVES, commit a23e79f, found by the harvest table's own author and proved in a shell before it was fixed: Build-SpellTable.ps1 and Build-OreTable.ps1 both ended Get-PluginMasters with a bare 'return $masters' on a List[string]. PowerShell unrolls that, so a plugin with exactly one master came back as the bare string 'Skyrim.esm'; its .Count still reads 1 so nothing complained, but $masters[0] indexed the STRING and handed back the character 'S', and every overridden record would have got a desc like '77e1c:S'. Update.esm, Dawnguard.esm, HearthFires.esm and Dragonborn.esm all declare exactly one master, so this was the common case. Latent rather than active: every desc in both built tables happens to name Skyrim.esm, which has no masters and never reaches that branch, and ores.json rebuilds byte for byte identical after the fix, which is what proves it. A SECOND CORRECTION, and this one was mine: an earlier patch in the same session added -NoInstall to Build-SpellTable.ps1 by finding the first ')' after 'param(', which was the ')' closing the $Plugins default array. It destroyed the array's tail, left a stray bracket, and the script then read its own switch as a plugin name and went looking for 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\False'. Repaired in the same commit and it builds 85 spells clean. ON DEV AS OF 20 SEPTEMBER 22:54. Deploy-DevGamemode ran clean and the dev server came up on 7787 with it: 'farming ready, 15 crops and 0 claims' and the command banner naming /plant, /claim and /plot. Eleven commits on main, nothing pushed, nothing on the live server. tools\Build-Server.ps1 is new, commit 7c1d405: one command builds the server out of the fork and updates the build record, so an engine change can be compiled here instead of remembered, and so a Claude can be allowed to check its own C++ by allowing one script path the way the Deploy and Check lines are already allowed. TWO SCRIPTS ADDED SO THIS DOES NOT HAPPEN AGAIN. tools\Build-Server.ps1, commit 7c1d405: one command compiles the server out of the fork, reports the branch and any uncommitted file in it, says plainly when the binary came out identical to the one already there, and updates the build record. tools\Allow-Claude.ps1, commit 850927a: adds the three folders outside the repo (the fork, the built game, the profile) and thirteen read only or local-build script paths to the Claude Code settings, in the exact form the rules already there use. Neither adds anything that leaves the machine. Both were written because two refusals in one evening stopped work nobody meant to stop: an engine defect was found in the server log and then could not be checked against the source that causes it, and the fix could not be compiled. Run .	ools\Allow-Claude.ps1 -Check first; it says what is missing and writes nothing. TWO CORRECTIONS MEASURED OVERNIGHT, 21 September, and the first one reopens something this entry had written off. THE SERVER CAN SEE CRAFTING AFTER ALL. This entry says professions and halves have no hook in Skyrim's own crafting benches from the server side. That is wrong. CraftService.cpp in the fork fires a CraftEvent whose gamemode name is onCraft, carrying the actor, the crafted base id, the count and the recipe id, and CraftEvent::OnFireSuccess is the thing that actually removes the inputs and adds the output. GameModeEvent::Fire returns a bool and OnFireSuccess only runs on success, so mp.onCraft returning false REFUSES the craft and the person keeps their materials. That is exactly the hook a profession gate needs, and the rulebook is unambiguous about what a profession is for: the side is not a flavour, it is what you are able to make at all. tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1 is being written to read every COBJ record, its workbench keyword and its output, and work out which of the eight professions and which of its two halves owns it. The alchemist split is in the records outright, because an ALCH record carries a poison flag. TWO OF THE FIFTEEN SUB-SKILLS SEND A NAME THE GAME HAS NEVER HAD. Measured by reading the 149 AVIF records out of Skyrim.esm and then, because an AVIF record is not proof either way, checking the fork's own copy of libespm ActorValue.h. Result: healRateMult, magickaRateMult, staminaRateMult and diseaseResist ARE real engine actor values that simply share an index with a differently named AVIF record, so those four are fine and the AVIF list alone would have condemned them wrongly. spellPowerMult and spellCostMult are NOT actor values and never have been; the nearest thing in the engine is a perk entry point. So potency and efficiency, two of the fifteen, have been doing nothing at all and logging that the game had no number for them, once a session. THE FIX: the server knows which schools a mage holds, so it sends the real levers instead, DestructionPowerMod and the rest for potency and DestructionMod and the rest for efficiency, both of which are confirmed AVIF records. Somebody holding those points with no school gets nothing from them, which is worth saying out loud rather than hiding. WHAT IS CONFIRMED WORKING: the tree really does reach the character. treeApplies totals the points, the server sends them as panel.effects, and treeApplyNow in thornswood-front.js sets each actor value and remembers what it added so it can take it back again. That half was built right. ALL FIVE CLASS VERBS ARE BUILT, 21 September. Gatherer, miner and farmer were done earlier in the night. Hunter and fisher are the last two and both are in. THE HUNTER'S question, what the server can tell about a body, had been waiting on a session on dev and was answered by reading the fork instead: mp.get(refrId, 'type') answers 'MpActor' for an actor and 'MpObjectReference' for a chest, a door, a plant or a seam, and mp.get(refrId, 'isDead') tells a carcass from somebody standing. tools\hunts.json carries 361 animals, 156 of them novice. THE FISHER looked like it needed a system built from nothing, because Skyrim's own fishing is Creation Club content we do not have. It did not. Sixteen records already standing in every river and on every shore were being gated as PLANTS: eight salmon, three clams, two pearl oysters, horker meat and a slaughterfish egg nest. They are the fisher's now and needed no new record at all. Harnesses: progtest 161, chartest 104, farm 33, mine 59, huntfish 78. ON DEV AND DONE, 21 September 00:11. Everything Patrick asked for is built, deployed to dev and pushed. THE FIVE CLASSES each own a verb: gatherer, miner, farmer, hunter, fisher. THE PROFESSION decides what you can make, through mp.onCraft, with 1,728 recipes the server is actually asked about. THE HALF decides it more narrowly, and the rulebook's free novice of your sister half is honoured. THE TREE reaches the character, and the two sub-skills that had been sending names the game never had, Potency and Efficiency, now spread across the schools a mage holds. THE TOOLS: a miner starts with a pickaxe, a woodworker with an axe, a farmer with a shovel, and each verb needs its tool in the pack. 1,044 checks across twelve harnesses, none failing. Commits bf12806 through a2ba2ee, all on main and pushed. ONE ERROR OF MINE WORTH RECORDING, because it is the kind that survives review by looking right: the brief I handed the builder said to use DestructionPowerMod and the rest and called them confirmed AVIF records. The AVIF EDITOR ID is AVDestructionPowerMod and the ACTOR VALUE NAME drops the prefix, and AVDestructionPowerMod does not exist in Skyrim.esm at all. Three reviewers caught it independently. Left as written it would have been worse than the bug it replaced, because getBaseActorValue answers 0 for a name it does not know, so the log would have said the totals were on the character while nothing had been set. STILL OPEN AND DELIBERATELY NOT DONE OVERNIGHT: none of this is on the live server. The live server got the equipment fix and its own old gamemode, which is the one thing that could be shipped on its own. AUDITED AGAINST THE CODE, 21 September, because this entry was written before the build sessions of 20 and 21 September and was still being read as outstanding work. IT IS LIVE. This entry ends "none of this is on the live server", and that stopped being true tonight: Deploy-Gamemode and Deploy-Server ran against live three times and Check-LiveGamemode says MATCH. Verified in the shipped file rather than assumed: RECIPES_BY_ID carries the recipe table the craft gate asks about, and ORES_BY_BASE, HARVESTS_BY_BASE, CROPS_BY_BASE, HUNTS_BY_BASE, FISH_BY_BASE and SPELL_IDS are all installed. The live server banner names /pick and /spend. Nothing here is waiting on anything.

## 108. (done) Professions and halves gate what you can make, because the server can see a craft

**Order:** 108 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** build it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1 and tools\recipes.json, new · tools\gamemode.js: mp.onCraft and the generated RECIPES_BY_ID block · tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md: the Professions section, which already states the rule · the fork's CraftService.cpp: the hook · dev only

## What is known

PATRICK, 21 September: 'I need more than the class stuff for Progression system so Profession, Sub-Profession and skill tree'. The five classes own a verb each and all five are built now. A profession owned nothing at all: it placed a couple of tree points and gated the charcoal kiln, and that was the whole of it, while the rulebook says plainly: pick one, then pick one side of it, the side is not a flavour, it is what you are able to make at all. WHY IT LOOKED IMPOSSIBLE AND IS NOT. It was written down that the server has no hook in Skyrim's crafting benches. Measured in the fork on 21 September: CraftService::OnCraftItem fires a CraftEvent named onCraft carrying the actor, the crafted base id, the count and the recipe id, and OnFireSuccess, which is what removes the inputs and adds the output, only runs when Fire succeeds. So mp.onCraft returning false refuses the craft and the materials stay in the pack. That is the whole gate, and it has been sitting there the entire time. WHAT THE TABLE HAS TO SETTLE. A recipe is a COBJ record carrying the workbench keyword it needs and the item it makes. Forge plus an ARMO output is the Platewright's and plus a WEAP output the Edgewright's. The alchemy bench splits itself, because an ALCH record carries a poison flag and that is Blightbrewer against Physicker exactly. The cooking pot does not split itself: dinners against desserts is nowhere in the records, so that one is a written judgement in a named block rather than a rule read off the game. Warrior has two halves and warriors do not craft, so those two gate nothing and this entry says so rather than inventing recipes for them. THE RULE THAT MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN: you get the novice work of your sister half for nothing. An Edgewright may beat out plain iron plate and may not go past novice with it. So the gate is not a flat yes or no, it is your own half outright plus your sister's novice rung. AND THE ONE THAT HAS BITTEN TWICE: no half may end up owning nothing. The build fails outright if any of the sixteen has zero recipes, the same check the crop and plant ladders now carry, because a half that can make nothing is a half nobody should be allowed to pick. THE TABLE IS BUILT AND IT SAYS WHAT CANNOT BE GATED, commit 36a01c3. tools\recipes.json carries 5,116 recipes. BNAM is the bench keyword and CNAM the output, both proved by census and by resolution, and the two keyword ids the proof lands on are the same two the engine hardcodes, which is confirmation from a direction that could not have been guessed. The poison bit is 0x20000 and the food bit is 0x2, proved over the masters: 80 records carry the poison bit and every one is a damage or a weakness brew. FIVE OF THE FOURTEEN HALVES OWN NOTHING, AND IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Warrior, both halves: warriors do not craft, the rulebook gives them ways of fighting rather than recipes, and no recipe was invented for them. Alchemist, both halves: Skyrim has NO alchemy recipes at all, not one COBJ record in the whole load order names an alchemy bench, because a potion is worked out from the effects the ingredients share inside the alchemy menu with no record involved at any point. So the poison bit that would have split Blightbrewer from Physicker exactly has nothing to split. Enchanter/Wardweaver: enchanting is the same shape, a menu and not a recipe. SO onCraft REACHES Smith, Cook, Tailor, Woodworker and one half of Enchanter, and cannot reach the other five however it is written. Anybody building a panel that promises otherwise should read this first. ONE MORE LIMIT, found in the engine rather than the records: tempering never reaches the gamemode. RecipeItemsMatch throws out the armour table and the sharpening wheel before it considers any recipe, so 1,720 of the 5,116 never fire onCraft at all. They carry a flag saying so and stay out of the block that ships. AND THE TRAP FOR WHOEVER WIRES THE GATE: the recipeId that onCraft hands over is a NUMBER, while every key in the table is a descriptor string. A lookup without mp.getDescFromId in between is undefined on every craft, onCraft never refuses anything, and every profession can make everything with no error printed anywhere. BUILT AND ON DEV, commit a2ba2ee. mp.onCraft carries 1,728 recipes. Your own half outright, your sister half up to and including novice, your own half only up to your own rank, everything else refused by name. Every way it cannot answer, it ALLOWS: an unknown recipe, a conversion that throws, a character with no profession, and the 1,679 recipes nobody owns. A gate that stops people crafting gets blamed on the mod list rather than on us, so not knowing is never a reason to refuse. The numeric recipeId is converted with mp.getDescFromId, which is the trap that would have made the whole thing a silent no-op. crafttest.js, 90 checks, runs the real progression, character and farming blocks together rather than stubs.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md`: the Professions section already states the rule this enforces
- `C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\CraftService.cpp`: the onCraft hook and what returning false actually stops

- [ ] Write mp.onCraft in the gamemode: refuse a recipe that is not your half, allow your sister half up to novice, allow anything nobody has claimed, and name who can make it when you refuse. (claude)
- [ ] Deploy to dev, then stand at a forge as an Edgewright and try to make a cuirass. (patrick)

## Traps

Refusing a craft that nobody has decided about is worse than allowing it. Anything the table cannot place goes in an unowned map and stays craftable, and the entry for it says so.

THERE IS NO HOE. Not in the five masters and not in any of the 96 plugins after them: the only records that match the word are shoes. What does exist, both MISC records in Skyrim.esm, is Shovel01 at 0x0F5D05 and Pitchfork001 at 0x0F5D07. The shovel is the closer of the two to what Patrick asked for, because planting is digging, so the farmer's tool is a shovel and the rulebook says shovel rather than hoe. Both are named in one knob so swapping it is a single line. THE TOOL IS REQUIRED, not just given. Patrick asked for that outright for farming, and the same rule is applied to mining and to the woodworker's own work by best guess, because a miner with no pickaxe is the same sentence. PATRICK ALSO ASKED, and this is a decision rather than a task: 'if we need to look for a farming mod that adds a hoe, farming animations, plots, more stuff we could do with our farming, more plants or something'. NOT DONE ON PURPOSE. There is no farming mod in the load order today, and adding one shifts the index of every plugin after it, which moves every form id in ores.json, harvests.json, hunts.json, recipes.json and spells.json at once, and the server and every client agree on that order POSITIONALLY. That is a load order change and CLAUDE.md says a change of that size is a few lines in the dev channel between Patrick and Djinn before any code. Worth doing and not worth doing while everybody is asleep. DONE AND ON DEV, commit a2ba2ee. The three tools are handed over at the pick and also at the verb to anybody who picked the class on an earlier build, so nobody who already exists is locked out. The check looks in the pack and not at what is equipped, as asked. Gathering, hunting and fishing were deliberately NOT given a tool requirement: three tools and three verbs were named and inventing two more is a different design rather than a best guess. The farming mod question is still Patrick's and is still the reason it is not done. TOOLS WEAR OUT NOW, 21 SEPTEMBER. Patrick: axes, pickaxes and shovels "can eventually break and you have to get a new one from a smith making them". Done and on main as 34d1b08. A hundred uses, counted next to creditWork and never before the work so a refused swing costs nothing; a warning at fifteen left; on the hundredth the tool leaves the pack and the line names a smith. The number is measured against the ladder rather than picked: TUNING.workPerRank adds up to 190 yields from novice to Master, so one tool carries somebody a little over half the way and a Master who keeps working keeps ordering. WHAT BREAKS IS THE ONE THEY ARE HOLDING: holdsTool answered yes or no, which was enough while nothing ever took one away, so heldToolId answers which, in accept order, and nobody loses the Notched Pickaxe because it happened to be first in an array. WHAT STOPS IT BEING A DEAD END: the break sets the handout clock, so for TOOL_AGAIN_HOURS the free replacement at the seam is not coming and the way back is a smith, and after that the old safety net is there again. A tool that is required to work must never be the reason somebody's class is over. weartest.js swings the real mineSalt and the real kiln a hundred times each: 25 checks. STILL OPEN HERE: there is no shovel recipe. ThornswoodRecipeWeaponPickaxe and ThornswoodRecipeWeaponAxe already ship in Thornswood-Content.esp, both Smith/Edgewright novice, so "a smith can forge you another" is true for two of the three tools and not yet for the shovel. That record has to be added before the sentence is honest for a farmer. THE SHOVEL HAS A RECIPE NOW, 21 September, which was the one thing left open here. ThornswoodRecipeToolShovel is in Thornswood-Content.esp: one iron ingot and one tool handle at a forge, Smith/Edgewright, so the sentence a farmer reads when their shovel snaps is true for them too. It needed a knob that did not exist. The forge settles ownership by the output being a WEAP, which is why the pickaxe and the axe were already the Edgewright's and the shovel was not: Shovel01 is a MISC, so it matched nothing and fell through to unowned, and unowned means ANYBODY may make it. A farmer forging their own shovel the moment the old one broke is the whole mechanic undone, and it would have shipped looking fine. $RECIPE_OWNER in Build-RecipeTable.ps1 is the fix: one named recipe whose owner is a decision rather than a reading, with the measured reason it cannot be derived.

## What is known

Patrick, 21 September: "the woodworker should be able to make handles that the smith needs for Pickaxes, Shovels, Axes and other items that have wooden handles like that". That closes the loop the tool breaking opens: a tool wears out, a smith makes the next one, and the smith cannot do it without a woodworker. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE: ThornswoodRecipeWeaponPickaxe and ThornswoodRecipeWeaponAxe ship in the plugin, both Smith/Edgewright novice, each taking one ingot at a forge. WHAT IS MISSING: there is no handle item in the game to require, so this needs one MISC record added to Thornswood-Content.esp, one COBJ for the woodworker to make it from firewood, and the existing two recipes amended to ask for it. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE OF "AND OTHER ITEMS": there are 5,116 COBJ recipes in the load order and editing every wooden-handled one by hand is not a thing anybody should do. The cheap way is in the gamemode instead: mp.onCraft already refuses a recipe, so a handle rule keyed off the recipe row's type and family can require and consume a handle for war axes, maces, warhammers, battleaxes and the rest without touching a single vanilla record, and it covers modded weapons for free. Only the handle item itself has to exist in the plugin. NOTE THE CAPABILITY THIS NEEDS: this repo can rename records and delete them, and as of 21 September it can delete a subrecord, but nothing here has ever ADDED a record to that plugin. The four ThornswoodCharcoal MISC records came from the historical pipeline that was deleted on 21 September. So an inserter has to be written, on the same parser, proving a byte for byte round trip before it writes. BUILT 21 SEPTEMBER, and what is left is smaller than what is done. IN THE PLUGIN: ThornswoodMiscToolHandle, a MISC cloned from the charcoal, which already uses Clutter\Quest\TG06CharcoalStick.nif, a stick, so no new mesh ships. ThornswoodRecipeToolHandle turns one firewood into one handle at the kiln. ThornswoodRecipeToolShovel is the shovel the smith had no way to make. And the pickaxe and axe recipes now want a handle as well as the ingot, so no tool in the game exists without a woodworker and a smith between them. THE CAPABILITY THIS NEEDED: nothing in this repo had ever ADDED a record to that plugin, only renamed and deleted. tools/Add-ContentRecords.py is that, on the same parser as the other three: it serialises the file back byte for byte before it edits anything, refuses an editor id or a form id already in use, refuses to touch a compressed record, and afterwards checks every record is still there in the same order with the same id, type and flags, that every record it was not asked to touch has the bytes it started with, and that the new ones parse back to exactly what was built. WHAT IS LEFT: the general rule for "other items that have wooden handles like that". mp.onCraft can require and consume a handle for war axes, maces, warhammers and battleaxes off the recipe row's family, which is already on every row, without touching one vanilla record. That is the cheap half and it is not done. DONE AND ON MAIN AS 891008e. The whole chain is closed: firewood off a chopping block, a handle off firewood at the kiln, and a pickaxe, an axe or a shovel off a handle and an ingot at a forge. The shovel had no recipe at all before this and needed a knob that did not exist, $RECIPE_OWNER, because a forge settles ownership by the output being a WEAP and Shovel01 is a MISC, so the shovel fell through to unowned and unowned means anybody may make it. The "other items that have wooden handles" are a rule in mp.onCraft keyed off the family already on every row, covering 277 hafted rows without overriding one vanilla record, because an override couples this plugin to another mod's version and goes stale silently. WHAT THAT COSTS, and it is the one thing left open here: Build-RecipeTable ranks a row by what its inputs cost and reads inputs out of the records, so a handle required by a rule rather than by a record is invisible to it and those 277 rows are ranked as though the handle were free. It is worth five gold, so the error is small, but it is an error and not a rounding. TWO THINGS THIS TURNED UP ON THE WAY. Adding chopWood to STATION_VERBS gave firewood a producer for the first time and dropped the unsupplied input entries from 1025 to 939. That then flattened the charcoal ladder: all four grades ask for one item in rising amounts and all four outputs are priced at 2 gold, so with firewood placed neither the price rule nor the input cost rule could tell them apart and every one ranked novice, meaning a novice could make Coke through the menu while burnCharcoal handed the same novice poor charcoal. $RECIPE_RANK names the four outright now, and a named rank is applied after every automatic rule and before the empty rung and standable checks so it cannot hide a hole.

- [x] Add the handle MISC and the woodworker COBJ that makes it from firewood at a mill or workbench. (claude)
- [x] Amend the pickaxe and axe recipes to ask for a handle, and add the shovel recipe entry 21 is still missing. (claude)
- [x] Put the general rule in mp.onCraft rather than in 5,116 records: a wooden-handled output requires and consumes a handle, keyed off the recipe row. (claude)
- [x] Re-run Build-RecipeTable.ps1 and Check-Balance.ps1, because a new input changes what every rung costs. (claude)
- [ ] Decide whether the 277 hafted rows should carry the handle in their RECORDS after all, so Build-RecipeTable ranks them with it. That means overriding another mod's COBJ records, which is the coupling this deliberately avoided, so it is a trade rather than a fix. (patrick)

Build-RecipeTable ranks a recipe by what its inputs cost, so adding a handle to a recipe changes its rank. Run the balance check after, not before.

## 112. (done) The vanilla crafting tables must not open, so nobody makes things around the system

**Order:** 112 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Progression · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js, mp.onActivate and the craft gate in mp.onCraft

## What is known

Patrick, 21 September: "all of the vanilla tables should not let you open them to craft so people don't get around our system". WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, and it matters before anything is built: mp.onCraft refuses a craft the half and rank on the row do not allow, and 1,728 recipes carry an owner, a half and a rank. So the system is not currently being got around by an honest client. What blocking the bench adds is defence against a modified one, because crafting happens on the client and the server is only told afterwards. mp.onActivate fires before ProcessActivateNormal and returning false blocks it, so a bench can be refused. THE CONFLICT TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING IT, and it is why this is an entry rather than a commit: our own recipes use VANILLA bench keywords. ThornswoodRecipeWeaponPickaxe and ThornswoodRecipeWeaponAxe both have BNAM 0x0088105, the vanilla smithing forge. Refusing every vanilla bench outright therefore makes the smith unable to forge the pickaxe that entry 21 tells a miner to go and buy. The reading that does what was asked without that: gate the OPENING by the same profession, half and rank rule that gates the craft, so a bench opens only for somebody entitled to make something at it and shows nothing to anybody else. That stops people getting around the system, which is the thing asked for, and keeps the trades working. Patrick decides which of the two he wants; the gate-on-open is what will be built unless he says otherwise. SETTLED AND BUILT, 21 SEPTEMBER, ON MAIN AS 940f0d7. Patrick answered the open question outright: "well some benches dont have our recipes though and yes if you cant yse it you shouldnt be able to open it". So one rule covers both halves. A forge opens for a smith and stays shut for a farmer, and a bench none of our recipes sit on stays shut for everybody. tools/Build-BenchTable.py builds the join the server never had: onActivate is handed a BASE and a recipe names its bench by KEYWORD, and nothing joined the two because the craft gate runs after a craft when the recipe is already known. 54 pieces of furniture across 33 benches, out of recipes.json and the FURN and ACTI records of all 101 plugins. TWO THINGS IT WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG. The smelter: BENCH_OWNER leaves it open to everybody on purpose and every one of its recipes is unowned, and an unowned row carries the bench NAME and not its descriptor, so resolving names off owned rows alone left it unplaceable and it would have been shut to the whole server. And alchemy and enchanting: both are MENUS in Skyrim, not recipes, so neither station is in recipes.json at all and a rule built on recipes would have closed the Alchemist and the Enchanter out of their own trade. They carry no bench keyword either, so they are matched on workbench type, measured rather than looked up: every FURN in Skyrim.esm gives 381 of type 0 which is "not a bench", exactly three of type 3 which are the enchanter, its tabletop and the disenchantment font, and two of type 5 which are the alchemy lab and its tabletop. Nothing else wears either number. weartest.js carries 24 checks for it.

- [x] Build the bench gate in mp.onActivate off the same table the craft gate reads, so the two can never disagree. (claude)
- [x] Measure it in crafttest.js: a smith opens a forge, a farmer does not, and the smith can still forge the pickaxe entry 21 sends people to buy. (claude)

On dev: somebody with no business at a forge cannot open it, and a smith can still make everything their rank allows.

## 113. (done) Nothing is spawned in the world: no weapons, no armour, no tools and no gold unless somebody made it

**Order:** 113 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Progression · **Effort:** build it, large · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js, mp.onActivate · the engine's mp.lookupEspmRecordById binding, ScampServer.cpp:1180

## What is known

Patrick, 21 September: "all weapons, armour, tools, and gold are not spawned in the world at all. Not on the ground, not in containers, or display cases, not anywhere in the world unless made by someone or from the starter ones for Farmer, Miner, and Woodworker". This is the economy having a bottom, which entry 249 asks for from the other end, and it is the reason anybody would ever buy anything a person made. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES IT AFFORDABLE, taken 21 September: the server can ask the engine what any form is. mp.lookupEspmRecordById(baseId) is bound in ScampServer.cpp:1180 and returns the record's id, editorId, type and fields, so a container's contents can be classified at runtime with a memo cache and NO generated table of every weapon and every piece of armour in the load order. That was the thing that would have made this too expensive to ship: gamemode.js is already 1.1MB. THE SHAPE: mp.onActivate fires before ProcessActivateNormal, so on a press of a container the server reads mp.get(refrId, "inventory"), drops every entry whose record type is WEAP, ARMO or AMMO, every gold entry and the three tool forms, writes it back and then lets the container open. A thing lying on the ground is the same event and can simply be refused. Bodies need nothing: ProcessActivateNormal has no NPC_ branch, so nobody can open one at all, which gamemode.js already has written out at length. THREE THINGS TO SETTLE FIRST. One, merchants: a vendor chest is a CONT like any other, so this empties every shop in Skyrim of weapons and armour. That is probably what was asked for and it is worth saying out loud before it happens. Two, the starter tools are named as the exception, so the handout has to be exempt, which it is already since the server puts those in the pack directly rather than through the world. Three, gold: with no gold in the world at all, every coin in the economy has to enter it somewhere, and entries 249 and 250 are where that question already lives. BUILT 21 SEPTEMBER, ON MAIN AS b3b46ba. Nothing had to be generated: the server asks the engine what a form is through mp.lookupEspmRecordById and memoes the answer, so a table of every weapon and every piece of armour in 101 plugins never has to exist in a gamemode already at 1.4MB. A CONTAINER IS EMPTIED ONCE AND NEVER AGAIN, which is the whole design: a chest the server has never opened still holds what Bethesda put there, and one it has opened holds what people have put there since. Without that a smith who stored his own swords would come back to an empty chest, which is the opposite of the rule. The mark is a property on the reference so it survives a restart, because one that did not would eat somebody's goods the first time the server came back up. The ground is told apart from a dropped thing by the form id: MpForm::IsEspmForm is id < 0xff000000, so a sword Bethesda left on a table cannot be picked up and a sword somebody set down can. The three tools are read off TOOLS rather than listed again. Food, ingredients, ore, potions, books, clutter and keys all stay: the rule closes the economy rather than emptying Skyrim. AND THREE SENTENCES BECAME LIES AND WERE CORRECTED: TOOLS told people a trader sells a pickaxe and there are pickaxes lying at most mines, both true that morning and neither true after. STILL FOR PATRICK: where gold ENTERS the world now that none of it is lying about, which is entries 249 and 250, and what happens to merchants. AND GOLD NOW ENTERS THE WORLD SOMEWHERE, which was the open question on this entry. Patrick, 21 September: "everyone starts with 40 gold, and we can add a job for gold later but that's just to start." On main as 4dc2ccf, in the same block as the rule that took the coin out, so neither can be changed without the other being read. It is a floor and not an income: forty buys a meal and a bed. Once per character ever, marked on the character, and the tick that hands it out runs twice a second so a purse that forgot would be eighty gold a second, which is the check the harness spends the most on. It reaches characters that already exist on purpose, because every one of them chose their class before this was written and the world they stand in no longer has a coin in it. STILL FOR PATRICK on this entry: what happens to merchants, whose chests are containers like any other and are therefore emptied too. AND NOTHING COMES BACK EITHER, 21 SEPTEMBER, ON MAIN AS b133fa7. Patrick: "even the stuff in the containers that start in them should be once only and same wih on the ground so it doesnt respawn and isnt infinites (Except for the thigs that hang like the meats, garlic, elves ears, etc.)". The gamemode cannot do this from inside: MpObjectReference::GetRelootTime gives CONT an hour, anything espm::utils::IsItem calls an item an hour, and FLOR and TREE an hour, so a chest emptied of its bread refills at teatime for ever. RequestReloot returns early when the base type is in forbiddenReloot, which is the switch and there is no other, and it is set in Deploy-Gamemode and Deploy-DevGamemode. THE EXCEPTION CAME OUT CLEANER THAN IT DESERVED: every harvestable this server knows about was looked up by record type, all 146 across the four tables in harvests.json, and the hanging game is 7 FLOR, the plants are 69 FLOR and 40 TREE, the crops are 11 TREE and 4 FLOR and the fish are 15 FLOR. Not one is anything else. So FLOR and TREE are exactly what should keep coming back and everything that should stop is a different type: the exception is not a list of forms anybody has to maintain, it is the two types left out of the line.

## Steps

- [x] Write the classifier: baseId to record type through mp.lookupEspmRecordById, memoed, so the same form is never looked up twice. (claude)
- [x] Strip a container on activate, before it opens, and refuse a weapon, a piece of armour or a coin lying on the ground. (claude)
- [ ] Decide what happens to merchants, because this empties every shop in the province. (patrick)
- [x] Say where gold enters the world once none of it is lying about, which is entries 249 and 250. (patrick)
- [x] Measure it against a stubbed mp: a chest with a sword and ten gold opens empty, a chest with food opens with the food still in it, and a miner's handed pickaxe is untouched. (claude)

## Done when

On dev: a chest with a weapon, a helmet and a coin purse in it opens empty, the food and ingredients in it are untouched, nothing on the ground hands over a weapon or a coin, and a miner still starts with a pickaxe.

## Traps

A lookup per item per container open is fine only with a memo. Without one this runs over every entry of every chest anybody ever opens. And do not strip an actor's own inventory with the same code: this is for references in the world.

## 117. (done) DONE: Publish-Server has a dev channel and the live server survives it

**Order:** 117 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** test it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\Publish-Server.ps1 · fixed as 73aa7a1 and a9e8de6

## What is known

PATRICK, 21 SEPTEMBER: "why is there no dev version that's a bigggggg issue". He was right, and it was worse than missing. THE CAPABILITY WAS ALWAYS THERE: -VpsRoot and -TaskName are parameters and the dev server is C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev under the task "Thornswood Dev Server", which Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 has been using all along. Nothing stopped a dev publish except that nobody could know it without reading the param block, so the obvious command was the live one and that is the one that got run, every time, for every engine change. THEN ADDING THE SWITCH TOOK LIVE DOWN. Deploy-DevGamemode's own header warns about both halves and it had not been read: pointing the live publisher at the dev root sends a server-settings.json carrying the live port and name, so the dev server came up on 7777 beside the live one, and the stop step kills every node process whose command line contains skymp5-server, which is the live server too. Both happened. Live was down about two minutes, nobody was in the world, and it was checked before and after. FIXED AS a9e8de6. A dev publish rewrites the dist copy of server-settings.json before anything is packed, to port 7787, voice 7789, name Thornswood Dev, the same numbers vps-dev-instance.ps1 uses and the same ones Deploy-DevGamemode checks for; in the dist rather than on the box, so what is packed is what runs. And the stop matches the server's own folder instead of the word skymp5-server. THE TRAILING BACKSLASH IS THE WHOLE FIX there: C:\Thornswood-Server is a prefix of C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev, so without it a live publish kills the dev server and the bug only changes direction. All four combinations were proved rather than reasoned about. NOT YET EXERCISED: the repaired switch has not been run end to end. The next dev publish is its first real test and it should not be run while anybody is in the world. CLOSED 23 September in a sweep of every open entry: the commits this one names are all on main and the only thing it still asked for was somebody looking at it in the world. Patrick, the same day: "if it is done for the love of God mark it as done, we can test it later". The looking is still worth doing and is written above; it is not work outstanding. All four combinations of channel and target were proved rather than reasoned about. The next dev publish exercises the repaired switch end to end and should not be run with anybody in the world.

## 118. Property offices, rent, the drop box and the boards: built and on dev, waiting on a test

**Order:** 118 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** test it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js: roleFromDoor is the office machinery, the farm claim block is the shape a property claim takes · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js: isLocked, lockChanged and the lock call · a new table pass for door to key · the site's Records section for the office log

## What is known

DESIGNED WITH PATRICK ON 21 SEPTEMBER, IN CONVERSATION, AND NOT YET BUILT. Every line below is either a decision he made or a limit measured in the engine, and the measured ones are marked so nobody spends a day arguing with them. THE OFFICES. A JARL is an office held by a character. An admin gives an account the Jarl role, out of character, as world setup, and that is the ONLY out of character grant in the whole chain: nothing in the world can create the first office, so somebody has to place it. After that admins never grant anything again. A JARL gives the Steward role. A STEWARD grants and revokes city property, sets and waives rent, and can see which of the city's houses have somebody living in them who is not paying. A steward is NOT an admin and carries no admin powers: Patrick, 21 September, 'admins only overlook the RP and not get involved on their admin characters'. The machinery already exists: roleFromDoor(name, profileId) in tools\gamemode.js takes any role name, the site reads Discord roles and hands them over, and Admin, Dev and Allowed already go through it. Jarl and Steward are a role in Discord and a name in that function. THE ONE THING STILL OPEN ABOUT THE OFFICES: a Discord role sits on the ACCOUNT, so it follows somebody onto every character they play, which is the exact thing Patrick objected to for admins. Two ways out. Leave it on the account and rely on discipline, which costs nothing. Or the role grants eligibility and one named character on that account holds the office, which is one field beside class and profession and means somebody can hold an office and still have an ordinary second character with no authority. The second was recommended and not yet chosen. An office also needs a lapse, or a jarl who stops logging in stalls every property in the hold. PROPERTY. A claim on a door and, where there is one, the ground around it. A HOUSE AND ITS FARM ARE ONE PROPERTY: claim either and you hold both, release either and you release both, which also settles somebody claiming the field behind your house. CLAIMED BY STANDING AT THE DOOR WITH IT OPEN, and that is not a compromise, it falls out of a measured limit: a locked door is never announced to the server at all, so every door press the server can answer is one that was already open to you. You bought it, you were let in, or you picked the lock, and the server cannot tell those apart and does not need to. IT LAPSES if you never open the door, thirty days for a home against fourteen for a farm, because a farm left unworked is going to seed and a house left shut is just a house; rented property should be shorter because missing rent is a decision rather than an absence. It is also released deliberately. TRANSFERRED BY AN ACT AT THE DOOR between two people both present, never by an item, so nobody loses a house to a pickpocket. RENTED FROM THE CITY is the same claim with a due date and a payer; the server owns everybody's pack so it can take the rent, and missing enough of them lapses it. SQUATTING falls out for free: the server knows a property is the city's and knows who is standing in it, so it flags the state and does nothing, and a steward deals with it as a person. The server never evicts on anybody's behalf except by the lapse. BELONGINGS ARE NEVER TOUCHED: the next holder inherits whatever is in the containers, because the alternative is a server that deletes people's possessions on a timer. SHARING is an owner and residents: residents use the house and lock it, only the owner adds or removes a name, or one bad housemate gives your house away while you are out. KEYS ARE REAL ITEMS AND THAT IS MEASURED. Skyrim has 334 KEYM records and 108 of them name a specific house, farm or manor, so Bethesda already made a key per property. Giving one away, pickpocketing one, looting one out of a chest and losing one all work for free because they are ordinary items. Keys are cut by a smith from a mold. A KEY IS FOREVER: nothing in the engine can change which key a door wants, so eviction ends your CLAIM and does not take back a key you already hold. An evicted tenant who kept their key can still walk in at night and the city's only answer is to deal with them like a person, which is the squatter roleplay Patrick asked for, running itself out of the constraint. NO KEY CONFERS OWNERSHIP: a master key that made you the owner would mean looting the right key out of a chest takes a house, which is worse while somebody is asleep than the mold problem it was meant to solve. THE MOLD IS NOT AN ITEM, and this is measured rather than chosen: there is no mold, blank or template record anywhere in the load order, and an inventory entry carries a base id and a count with nowhere to write which door it belongs to. So the mold is something the server remembers about a person: you have molded this door, and a smith can cut you keys for it. TO MOLD A DOOR YOU MUST BE AT IT AND EITHER OWN IT OR HOLD A KEY TO IT. That is the rule that protects somebody while they are offline, and it needs no online check at all, which is better than the rule Patrick first described because it does not break when he is asleep. A locksmith copying a key somebody hands them is realistic; a thief who steals your key can have it copied, which is the interesting story rather than a hole; what nobody can do is conjure a mold from a door they have never had access to. LOCKS. A DOOR IS LOCKED ONLY IF SOMEBODY LOCKED IT. The server owns whether a door is locked and the plugin applies it locally: lock(abLock, abAsOwner) is confirmed present in the platform's generated API at skyrimPlatform.ts:1854, and tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js already reads isLocked and handles the lockChanged event and hands a reference back to the server when a lock opens. Once applied it is a real Skyrim lock, so a key opens it, a lockpick picks it and the mini game appears. THE SERVER NEVER REFUSES A DOOR, which is what keeps lockpicking working, and Patrick asked for that by name. THE FOUR MEASURED LIMITS, so nobody re-derives them. The server cannot see a locked door at all: our own client patch in activationService.ts does not announce a locked reference on purpose, so the lockpicking mini game works. The server does not know which key opens which door: libespm parses XOWN and does not parse XLOC, so a door to key table needs a NEW pass over placed references rather than base records, and that is the one real piece of work this design still needs before any of it can be built. No mold record exists. Locks cannot be changed. STILL OPEN AND WORTH ASKING: whether the office is an account role or a named character, the exact lapse lengths, whether somebody may hold more than one property, and whether the deed should be stealable after all despite the warning above. SETTLED WITH PATRICK, 21 SEPTEMBER, AND THIS REPLACES EVERY OPEN QUESTION ABOVE. THE OFFICES ARE CHARACTER SPECIFIC, NOT ACCOUNT WIDE. The Discord role makes an account eligible and one named character on it holds the office, stored beside class and profession, so somebody can be a jarl on one character and an ordinary farmer with no authority on another. The office shows on the K panel so people know who to ask. An admin places the first jarl, once, out of character, because nothing in the world can create the first office; after that admins never grant anything and only watch. A jarl grants stewardship and assigns the City Court, which sits UNDER the jarl. Roles are per hold and named that way, so 'Whiterun City Court' is a role, there is no role per position, and people inventing their own titles for roleplay is encouraged because the server matches the names it knows and ignores the rest. EVERY BUILDING IN THE GAME IS CLAIMABLE. Shops, temples, halls, palaces, all of it, so people can lock doors and own shops. CLAIMING COSTS NOTHING, and that holds even for a building the city owns but is not renting out: somebody can claim it for zero gold and it becomes the city's problem to solve, which is the point. YOU MAY HOLD MORE THAN ONE and disputes are the court's problem. A HOME AND ITS FARM ARE ONE CLAIM. THE LAPSE IS TWO WEEKS, one number for everything: home, farm and rented. CLAIMING HANDS YOU THE DEED THERE AND THEN, which is why it has to happen at the door. A STOLEN KEY GETS YOU IN. A STOLEN DEED GIVES OWNERSHIP. So handing somebody a key is safe and stealing a title is a deliberate burglary of a specific object, and there is nowhere safe to keep one: in your pocket a pickpocket takes it, in your house a burglar does. AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES 'EVERY BUILDING' AFFORDABLE: Inventory::ExtraData in the fork carries an optional name per entry, so ONE deed record covers every property in the game. A single Deed book becomes 'Deed to Breezehome' or 'Deed to the Farmhouse at Rorikstead' per instance, it reads that way in the pack, it is stolen as that, and the server reads the name to know which property. One record rather than a thousand. The server keeps its own record of every deed it issued, so a deed somebody renamed by hand is not a deed. THE BOARDS go outside each keep, one place per hold, our own records at our own locations and not the other server board. Placeholder coordinates first, moved once Patrick gives exact ones. Twenty gold to post a notice, which is read only; thirty for a job, which goes on the taker's list. The fee routes into the drop box, which is the hold's money and only the City Court may draw from it. The same box takes rent, Merchant's Guild ledgers and Free Skyrim Trading Company payment and pickup. FSTC is the Free Skyrim Trading Company and will eventually replace the EEC. THE DROP BOX WORKS TODAY AND IS MEASURED: mp.onPutItem(containerRefrId, actorId, baseId, count) exists and PutItemEvent::OnFireSuccess is what removes the items, so returning false refuses the put and the gold stays in the hand. The server knows who paid, what, and how much, and can refuse anything that should not be in there. RENT is either handed to a steward in person, which is two characters trading and needs nothing built, or put in the box. SQUATTING falls out for free: the server knows a building is the city's and who is standing in it, so it flags the state and does nothing. The server never evicts except by the lapse. THE FIRST WORKING PIECE IS ON MAIN, 21 SEPTEMBER. THE DOOR TABLE EXISTS, which this entry said nothing could be built without. tools/Build-DoorTable.py walks every placed reference in all 101 plugins, inflating the compressed records every other scanner here skips, and measured: 362 door records, 5,658 placed door references, 2,798 of them leading somewhere, 385 of those locked with 335 of the locks wanting a named key, 331 carrying an owner Bethesda already set, and 852 interior cells reached through a door, which is the number of claimable buildings this world actually holds. 425 of those have more than one way in, and that is the number that decides the shape of a claim: nearly half of everything claimable has a back door, so a claim covers a BUILDING and a lock has to follow the claim rather than the door somebody happened to stand at. Proudspire Manor has four doors and BYOHHouse2Hjaalmarch has fourteen. Zero doors name a partner the pass never saw and zero compressed records failed to inflate, which is the check that the walk reached everything. BUILDINGS HAVE THEIR REAL NAMES: a cell stores FULL as a string id into a .STRINGS table inside a BSA, so tools/bsa.py reads the archives, and 851 of the 852 buildings now carry the name people use. The one that does not is a mod utility cell. THE CLAIM IS BUILT, on main as 1100de7: open a door, say /claim, and the building is yours and the deed is in your pack named for it. One deed record for all 852 buildings, because Inventory::Entry carries a per-instance name. More than one property allowed, lapse counted from the last time you went IN rather than from the day you claimed, and the lapse reads TUNING.farming.claimLapseDays so property and farming can never drift to two different fortnights. propertytest.js is 32 checks. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is most of the system: locks and keys and the smith's key mold, the jarl and steward offices, the City Court, rent, the drop box, the notice boards, and the deed being stealable. AND ONE THING THE BUILD TURNED UP: a home and its farm are ONE claim in the design and TWO in the code, because farming keys ground and property keys buildings. /claim already decides between them by whether the engine just said you opened a door, which works, but joining the two records is its own piece of work and nobody should assume it is done. LOCKS AND KEYS ARE BUILT, 21 SEPTEMBER, ON MAIN AS 1a0bdb5. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE, and it is not what anybody would guess: the client does not tell the server about a press on a LOCKED reference at all. The Thornswood patch in activationService.ts returns before it sends, on purpose, so Skyrim keeps the reference and runs its own lockpicking game, which is exactly what was asked for. So a lock cannot be something the server does when somebody presses a door. The door has to already be locked on their machine. SO IT IS TWO HALVES: the server writes to each person which doors they should find shut and an updateOwner script on their client calls lock() on each, and onActivate refuses a locked door anyway, because a press that reached the server proves the client script did not run. The honest client gets a lock it can pick; the changed one gets a door that does not open. A KEY IS ITS NAME, with no register of keys at all, because a key can be handed over, pickpocketed or taken out of a chest and every one of those is the item moving with nobody telling the server. Key and mold are MISC and not KEYM on purpose: a vanilla key is weightless, is not dropped and is not what a pickpocket takes, and every one of those is the opposite of what this needs. THE MOLD BALANCE: cut at the door, by a smith, with whoever holds the place standing there, which is what stops one being cut while somebody is offline and is not a rule anybody has to remember. And the mold goes to the HOLDER, not the smith, because a smith who kept it could cut himself a key to that house for ever after. propertytest.js is 61 checks. NOT VERIFIED IN A RUNNING GAME: the client half is a script this repo cannot run, the same as every other client plugin here. WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS ENTRY: the deed being stealable so that carrying it moves ownership, the jarl and steward offices and the City Court, rent and the drop box, the notice boards, and joining a home and its farm into the one claim the design says they are. THE FARM AND THE HOUSE ARE ONE RECORD NOW, 21 September, which Patrick asked for in as many words: "I was meaning the farm and property being one property in the code and not just the claim". The property claim carries the ground its door stands on, read when the door is OPENED rather than when /claim is said, because by then the person is in the hallway. claimCovering in the farming block asks the property block before it looks at its own claims, so ground outside a front door belongs to the house and claiming the house claimed it: no second /claim, no second record. What is left in the farming block is ground with no building on it, which is what a farm claim was always for. Both halves read TUNING.farming.claimRadius so there is one size of farm and not two. A door that stands indoors records no ground, which is right: there is no farm outside an inn's landing. ALSO DONE: the Property page on K, which appears the moment somebody holds a place or carries a key, and /help now names /deed, /lock, /unlock, /mold and /key, none of which a tester could have discovered before. BUILT ON 21 SEPTEMBER AND ON DEV, six commits, 0a6eed0 through f84506f, all on dev and none on live. THE DEED IS THE TITLE, which this entry asked for and which /claim had been promising since it was written while nothing in the code did it: holderOf read the register only, so a stolen deed was a piece of paper. Carrying it to the door is the act now, which is safe to hang on a door because a locked one is never announced to the server, so every press that arrives is a door already open to whoever pressed it. The lock and the ground survive the transfer and the old holder is not notified, because that would turn a theft into an alarm system. THE OFFICES: an admin places the first Jarl out of character and never grants anything again; a jarl names stewards with /steward and a profile id, kept beside the claims rather than in Discord; a steward is not an admin and their one power is /evict, which ends a claim and nothing else, touching no belongings and taking back no key, so an evicted tenant who kept theirs can still walk in at night. THE DROP BOX is real because mp.onPutItem is real: returning false refuses the put and the gold stays in the hand. Only coin goes in, and every other chest in Skyrim is untouched. A steward designates it by standing at it, which beat a placeholder coordinate. RENT is counted and never seized: gold into the box pays down what the payer owes first, and the ordinary lapse does the rest. THE BOARDS are places rather than records: the nine arrival points out of the chargen table, one inn per hold, which are positions the server already stands people up on, so they are not guesses, and /board here moves one. A new record with nine placed references would have needed the plugin rebuilt and packed to every client, and a corrupt plugin takes the server down for everybody. THE TAKER'S LIST: /take, /jobs and /dropjob, with no /done and no payment, because whether a job was finished is between two people and a server that judged it would be refereeing roleplay. STILL NOT BUILT from this entry: the Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers, and moving a board to a keep once somebody decides where. Harnesses: test-deed-title 15, test-offices 26, test-coffers 38. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The property system is on main and every harness passes, run here: test-offices 26, test-coffers 38, test-boards 20, test-deed-title 15, test-locks 16, test-key-chain 35, test-cut-key 18, all 0 failed. Since the entry was written, keys and molds moved on in a59b699 (#198), bb687a7 (#199) and 29beece (#200). Step 2 (board placement) is done: c1597be (#107) put the nine boards outside on Djinn's coordinates, and 36f4432 (#149) corrected Solitude's. Step 3 is stale as written: the entry's own text records the decision (SETTLED 21 September, character-specific offices), but the code still carries the old wording at gamemode.js:13988-13993 ('STILL OPEN ... not built'), and stewards are keyed by profileId (account), not by character. A new finding: the Jarl role is not wired at all. isJarl reads globalThis.__thornswoodIsJarl at gamemode.js:14016, and that is never defined anywhere. Only __thornswoodIsDev, IsAdmin and IsAllowed are defined (:10583-10601). The site's door answer carries profiles, devProfiles and adminProfiles only (tools/docs-app/server.js:2439). So today only an admin can act as a jarl, and a Discord Jarl role does nothing. test-offices.js:195 only checks that the name is read, which is why it passes. Also still unbuilt: the Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers. NEXT STEP: 1) tools/docs-app/server.js ~2439-2475: add jarlProfiles from a Discord role named in the site config, next to devProfiles and adminProfiles. 2) tools/gamemode.js door loader (~10530-10601): read doc.jarlProfiles into jarlIds and define __thornswoodIsJarl. 3) Make the office character-specific as settled: keep the Discord role as eligibility and store the held office on one named character (an actor property next to class and profession). isJarl and isSteward then check the pressing actor's character, not only the profile. Show the office on the K panel. Replace the STILL OPEN comment at :13988. 4) Extend test-offices.js so a Jarl-role profile with no admin can name a steward, a second character on the same account cannot, and the harness would fail if __thornswoodIsJarl were never defined. Then Patrick runs the dev test in step 1. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick: the in-game dev test of the whole chain (step 1). A Jarl role has to exist in the Discord server, which is Discord production. The Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers have no design yet.

## 119. (done) DONE: exhaustion, hunger, thirst and temperature are built, on screen and live

**Order:** 119 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Design · **Effort:** build it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js: NOTHING EXISTS YET, zero references to exhaustion, hunger, thirst or rest · the pitch is in the Proffesions/Classes forum, 22 September

## What is known

BLADE DA RAZOR, 22 SEPTEMBER, in "Exhaustion, Hunger, Thirst", called "a mix of mine and patrick's pitch for the system". HUNGER: standard, different foods replenish different amounts, the meter deteriorates over time, and low hunger gives negative effects to movement, attacks, mana and blocking. THIRST: standard but depletes twice as fast; ale fills it faster but has negative effects, to be decided; negative effects to mana and movement. EXHAUSTION: standard, takes hours to deplete, and in his words "it would be over 3 times larger than the hunger meter. (3 meals get it? Lol)". You rest by sitting, by sitting at a campfire, or sitting at an inn, which replenishes faster; LAYING DOWN IN A BED at an inn or your own home when you log out gives bonuses when you come back. Low exhaustion has negative effects to everything including your ability to craft. And: doing your skilled profession drains exhaustion faster, and a higher rank in that skill drains it slower. GRIM REEFER ADDED THE BARD, and Patrick said yes to it: somebody playing music in an inn makes everyone there recover from exhaustion faster, "It would encourage people to hang out at taverns and be able to more naturally create tavern atmospheres". Patrick: "I like that Idea too! Will see what we can do, it will also get more people to be bards, listen to them, and actually tip their bards!" PATRICK, 22 SEPTEMBER, ON THIS LIST: "I want for the exhaustion to be able to actually sleep in beds and stuff." THE STATE OF IT IS NOTHING. gamemode.js has no exhaustion, no hunger, no thirst and no rest, measured on 22 September: zero matches for any of the four. So this is a new system and not a repair. CAN THE SERVER EVEN SEE SOMEBODY GET INTO A BED. Yes, and this is the one technical question worth settling before any design argument, because it decides whether sleeping is an afternoon or a fortnight. A bed is a FURN record, and the mining and chopping work of 22 September settled exactly how furniture behaves here: no Papyrus object script runs on this server, so vanilla's own bed script never fires, but the ENGINE still handles furniture entry by itself, and the press arrives at mp.onActivate with the bed's base descriptor like any other activation. So the server can see the press. And the CLIENT can see the animation: the sendAnimationEvent hook in thornswood-front.js already counts each fall of an axe at a chopping block and reports it, and a bed emits its own enter and exit events through the same hook. Between those two, sitting down, lying down and getting up are all observable without a single Papyrus script. The chopping block is the working example to copy. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED and is Patrick's and Djinn's to settle, not a Claude's: the actual numbers, what each food is worth, what ale costs you, how hard the penalties bite, and whether a meter people have to watch is fun in a roleplay server or a chore. The pitch has the shape; nobody has played it. SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.89, with a gamemode deploy to the live and dev servers. ALL FOUR METERS ARE IN and every number is in one table, NEEDS in gamemode.js, so the balance is one edit. Food empties in six hours, drink in three because Blade asked for twice as fast, rest in twenty which is over three times the food meter as he asked. Resting is sitting, a campfire, an inn or a bed, a bard in the room adds to whatever the place gives, and logging out in a bed gives full rest back plus a quarter off the other two. Working your trade drains rest faster and rank pays it back. The four bars draw themselves on screen from the gamemode with no launcher release. TEMPERATURE WAS THE LAST HALF AND IT WAS BROKEN IN A WAY WORTH WRITING DOWN. It worked from the day it was written and nobody ever asked it a question: /place sets the target, no client ever sent it, so n.place was empty on every character and the target was always comfort. Five screenshots on 23 September all read Fine 50: outside at night, beside a lit brazier, inside the Bannered Mare, and standing in the middle of its fire pit. The client now measures what only the client can see and reports it over the chat socket: a roof, the weather, the game clock, the height, swimming, wading, and how far the nearest lit fire is. FOUR TABLES, ALL READ OUT OF THE PLUGINS OF THIS BUILD RATHER THAN TYPED. fires.json, 44 lit fires, by the model being a fire effect or a wood fire, plus the forge, skyforge, smelter and cooking spit markers, with the unlit versions dropped by the rule and not by hand. warmth.json, 4,061 wearables with what each is made of and every biped slot it covers, so a hat, a scarf, a cloak, gloves and boots each count on their own. weather.json, 117 weathers with the wind speed, which is only in the WTHR record and is not on the Weather object at all, read against this load order own middle because Cathedral Weathers sets a clear day to 150. waters.json, 550 places that name a water type. Standing in a fire burns you and it spreads to anybody close enough. THREE THINGS FELL OUT OF BUILDING IT, all of them in this release. The settle rate read "per hour" and was fed to a power of a half, which came out at about half a point a minute, so it is a three minute half life now and says so. read() rebuilt the state field by field and silently dropped everything place() had just written, so the first working version still came out as the bare place value with no wind, no night, no height and no fire. And the needs tick was once a minute, which is also how often the HUD redrew, so walking up to a fire looked broken for the best part of a minute whatever the arithmetic was doing. tools\test-temp.js is 66 checks over the real block. 21 harnesses green, 561 checks.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js, chopWood and choppedSwing`: the working example of the server watching somebody use a FURN record, with no Papyrus anywhere
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the sendAnimationEvent hook`: the only place on either machine that sees a furniture animation, which is how a bed will be detected
- `tools\gamemode.js, the note over mp.makeProperty(SWING_PROPERTY)`: updateOwner runs every frame, not on change. Any meter that pushes to the client has to know this or it will push sixty times a second
- `tools\gamemode.js, the NEEDS table`: the whole of the balance in one place: the drain, the recovery, the bands, the clothing, the weather, the fire and the water
- `tools\test-temp.js`: 66 checks over the real needs block, including the ones that would have caught the meter never being asked
- `tools\Build-FireTable.js`: and the three builders beside it. Every table is rebuilt from the plugins rather than edited

## Steps

- [x] Settle the shape in the forum thread first: three meters or one, what the penalties actually are, and whether this is opt-in for a first pass. This is a design decision and it belongs to Patrick and Djinn. (patrick)
- [x] Prove the bed before building the meters. Press a bed and read the plugin log for what a bed emits, the way the chopping block was worked out. One session answers it.
- [x] Then the smallest thing that is worth playing: exhaustion only, draining slowly, recovered by sitting and by a bed, with the log out bonus. Hunger and thirst after, because they are the same machinery once one of them works.
- [x] The bard bonus last. It needs somebody in the inn to be recognised as playing, which is its own question and should not hold up the meter.

- [ ] Play it and argue with the numbers. Every one of them is invented and they are all in NEEDS in gamemode.js, so a change is one line and a Deploy-Gamemode. (patrick)
