## 120. (done) DONE: friends, parties, journals, trading and mutes, all on a key press

**Order:** 120 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** build it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js: actorOf() at :16253, the roster at :8980-9301, the command register pattern at :12706-12853 · tools\ts-ui\thornswood-skills.js: the panel contract every menu already uses · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-voice.js:120 lastWho, and the per-peer GainNode at :687-695

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER, in one message, and it is three features sharing one piece of plumbing. PARTY ON P: a friends list, who is online, invite, a name tag colour for people in your party, them on the map and the compass, and an experience bonus for playing together. JOURNALS ON J: more than one journal, pages inside them, and sharing either a whole journal or a single page with a friend. AND THE KEY PROMPTS, which is the part he was most direct about: "when you look at someone, you are prompted to press buttons: one for friend, one for trade, and one for mute. Currently the looking at people doesnt have the trade menu and when it did you had to use youyr cursor and a bunch of other bs I just want to press a key while looking at them." WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT BEING USED. The client has getCurrentCrosshairRef and the crosshairRefChanged event, both available and referenced nowhere in this repo, which is exactly "who am I looking at" and is the whole reason the old trade menu needed a cursor. The voice plugin already keeps lastWho, and mute is a per-peer GainNode it already holds, so muting the person you are looking at is a gain of zero and nothing new. The panel contract in thornswood-skills.js is how every other menu on this server is drawn, so P and J are pages rather than new machinery. The roster already knows who is online, and the register pattern is how a command gets wired up. DO THE KEY PROMPTS FIRST. They are the smallest of the three, they are the one he complained about by name, and they are what the other two hang off: a friend request is "the person I am looking at", which is the same lookup. SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.90, with the gamemode on both servers, the voice service reinstalled and the site republished. BUILT AS ONE THING, because all three verbs start with the same question and neither machine can answer it alone: the client has a form id under the crosshair and no name, the server has every name and no crosshair. The server publishes who is near you on a property and the client matches the crosshair against it. getCurrentCrosshairRef and crosshairRefChanged were available the whole time and appeared nowhere in this repo before today, which is exactly why looking at people did nothing. AND THE TRADE MENU HE REMEMBERED IS NOT COMING BACK: it was OldTradeMod, an old-mod mod, and neither it nor OldModTweaks is in this build. The launcher was still carrying EIGHT key bindings for the two of them, writing into two ini files that do not exist, which is both why the key did nothing and where the cursor he remembers came from. Those rows are gone and Thornswood's own are in their place. WHAT SHIPPED. G adds or removes a friend, H offers a trade, L mutes somebody, all three only while they are under your crosshair, with a panel naming them and the keys. P is friends and party, J is journals. Friends are mutual when accepted and one sided when dropped, so you can take somebody off your list without telling them. A party is a session and dies with the server, on purpose. Work done with your party in the same cell counts fifteen percent more, banked and paid as a whole extra piece every seventh rather than rolled for, because there is no such thing as 1.15 of a log. Muting is the server's to remember and the voice page's to do: the per-peer gain node was already there and nobody is told they have been muted. Journals are many, with pages, and sharing is a live view rather than a copy, so a correction reaches them too. Trading is two piles and two confirmations, and ANY change to either pile takes both confirmations back; the piles are checked against the real inventories at the moment of the swap and a trade that no longer works is refused whole rather than half done. tools\test-social.js is 66 checks over the real blocks.

## 121. (done) DONE: green names, markers on the map, and an arrow to each of them

**Order:** 121 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

the game rather than the overlay · a quest alias or a MapMarker reference · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js would own it

## What is known

THE ONE PART OF THE PARTY MENU THAT DID NOT SHIP, and it is said on the panel itself rather than left to be discovered. Patrick, 22 September, asked for a party menu that lets people "see their name tag colour, see them on the map and compass". Everything else in that sentence is live; these two are not. WHY THEY ARE NOT. A compass marker and a map marker are things inside the game: a quest alias pointing at a reference, or a MapMarker reference enabled for that person. A browser overlay draws over the screen and cannot put anything into Skyrim's own compass, and the name above somebody's head is skymp5-client's, drawn by the client and toggled by F1. So all three need the plugin or the client fork, not the panel, which is why they were left out rather than half done. THE LIKELY SHAPE. The server already publishes who is near you and who is in your party on the thornswoodNear property, so the plugin has the list and the form ids without asking for anything new. A compass marker is the smallest of the three to try first. SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.91, with the gamemode on both servers. TWO OF THE THREE TURNED OUT TO BE REACHABLE WITHOUT TOUCHING THE CLIENT, which is the opposite of what this entry assumed. THE NAME. skymp5-client draws the tag itself, in formView.ts, with createText(x, y, name, [1,1,1,0.8]), and a plugin cannot reach into that. But the client hands the id straight back out: SweetTaffyNicknamesService writes every one into sp.storage.idTextNickname keyed BY FORM ID, which is the same key the server's party list carries, and setTextColor takes the id. So it is a table lookup and one call. Party members are written in the same green the HUD uses for a meter that is fine, and it is PUT BACK to the client's own white when they leave: a colour that is never removed leaves the last party you were in green for the rest of the session, after which the colour means nothing at all. THE MAP. MapMarker is STAT 0x00000010 in Skyrim.esm, read out of the file rather than remembered. One marker per member, named after them, addToMap(false) so there is no fast travel because somebody's position is a thing to walk to, moved to wherever the server last said they were, and deleted when they leave. Not persistent, so it cannot outlive the session. THE COMPASS IS NOT SKYRIM'S AND THE PANEL SAYS SO. That one draws quest targets and map markers and nothing a plugin can add an arrow to; putting a party on it properly needs a quest with an alias per member inside an esp, which is a Creation Kit change and a new master for everybody. So there is a strip of our own under it: arrow, name, distance, green for the same room and gold for somewhere else. AND IT IS FRESHER THAN THE SERVER'S OWN PUSH. Voice already receives everybody's position five times a second and thornswood-voice.js hands that table out through who() now. Membership comes from the server where it belongs; the positions come from the feed that is already arriving. Fifteen times more often, for nothing new. THE SERVER HALF is a second list, thornswoodPartyAt, with no distance test and no cell test at all, sent only to people in a party. thornswoodNear could not be used: near is everybody within 2,600 units in the same cell, which is the right answer for "who am I looking at" and the wrong one for a marker, whose whole point is that they are somewhere else. tools\test-party-markers.js is 42 checks, and the bearing maths is RUN rather than read, including the case that only breaks once somebody turns away from north.

## 123. (done) DONE: the race menu stopped reopening every login for a character that already had a face

**Order:** 123 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** fix it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js, closeRaceMenu · the fork: skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\MpActor.cpp and skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\ActionListener.cpp

## What is known

REPORTED BY firstreconboone ON 22 SEPTEMBER: "Character is already made, however upon logging into game the options popped up." Every login, on a character that had been played for days. IT WAS A LOOP AND THIS SERVER OWNED ONE HALF OF IT, read out of the fork rather than guessed. MpActor::ApplyChangeForm runs on every login and forces isRaceMenuOpen true whenever the stored appearance is empty, with the comment "Actor without appearance would not be visible so we force player to choose appearance". And ActionListener::OnUpdateAppearance only STORES an appearance while the server thinks the menu is open: isAllowed is IsRaceMenuOpen(), and an upload that arrives when it is false is thrown away without a word. Put the two together. The engine opens the menu because there is no face on file. The chargen tick closes it a second later, correctly, because the character is obviously not new. The person makes a face anyway, the upload is refused, the dump stays empty, and tomorrow the engine opens it again. For ever. The log had been printing the evidence the whole time: "already has a character carrying 4 things, not in the hall, no face, so creation is skipped for them". Nothing in it reads as an error. FIXED by refusing to close the menu for somebody the server has no appearance for. They get one race menu they can click straight through, it is accepted because the flag is still set, and it never opens again. A read that throws counts as having a face, because one extra menu once is the cheaper of the two mistakes.  SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.89, with a gamemode deploy to the live and dev servers. 

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js, closeRaceMenu`: the guard, and the two quotes out of the fork it is built on

  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```

  ```powershell
  .\tools\Chargen-Log.ps1
  ```

Somebody who has played logs in and goes straight into the world. Deployed 23 September; the next login by an affected character is the proof.

## Traps

Closing the race menu is not free. It is what makes the next appearance upload be discarded, which is the whole bug, so anything calling setRaceMenuOpen(false) has to ask whether there is a face on file first.

## 125. The ladders have to line up across classes and professions, or one of them is dead weight

**Order:** 125 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** measure it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\ores.json, harvests.json, hunts.json, recipes.json: the five ladders that have to agree · tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1, the reverse index and the ranking · tools\Check-Balance.ps1, the chain report · dev only

## What is known

PATRICK, 21 September: 'we also need to make sure the different tiers match across so like farmer matches with tiers of cook for their recipes, miner and smith, woodworker and miner and so on, so there isn't an imbalance'. He is right and it is checkable rather than a matter of taste. THE SHAPE OF THE CHECK: every recipe has inputs, and every input is something a class produces at some rank. A novice Hearthcook recipe whose inputs include a crop only an expert Farmer may grow is an imbalance, and so is an expert Platewright recipe whose inputs a novice Miner can bring in all day. So: for each recipe, take the highest producer rank among its inputs and compare it to the rank the recipe itself sits at. Report every half where the two disagree by more than one rung. WHAT IS MISSING BEFORE IT CAN RUN: tools\recipes.json records how MANY inputs a recipe has and not WHICH. The CNTO subrecords are already parsed by the build script, so carrying the form ids through is a small change to a script that already reads them. WHAT CAN BE SAID ALREADY, from the rank spreads as they stand: plants 57 novice, 61 advanced, 24 expert, 5 master. Ore veins 88, 310, 159, 24. Animals 156, 150, 47, 8. Crops 5, 4, 2, 0. The crop ladder is the thin one, which is a consequence of there being only eleven farmable records in the whole game, and it is the one most likely to hold a cook back. THE CHECK EXISTS, tools\Check-Balance.ps1, commit 94f8955, and it found three walls on its first run. Cook/Confectioner has nothing at advanced, so becoming an Advanced Confectioner opens no recipe at all. Enchanter/Bladebinder has nothing at advanced and nothing at expert: 160 of its 161 recipes are novice and the last is master. Those are numbers to argue about rather than defects to fix quietly, so they are reported and nothing was moved. The producing ladders are all sound: ore 88/310/159/24, plants 46/61/24/5, animals 157/150/47/8, water 11/2/1/1, crops 5/4/2/0. The crop ladder is the thin one and that is a consequence of there being eleven farmable records in the whole game. WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO is follow one recipe to the class that makes its inputs, because recipes.json records how many inputs a recipe has and not which. THE CHAIN IS READABLE, 21 September, and it turned the whole rule over. The three empty rungs were not a threshold problem: they were the wrong measure. Measured on the table this repo built: Cook/Confectioner has 28 recipes and TWO distinct output prices in the whole half, 18 at 6 gold and 10 at 14. Enchanter/Bladebinder has 161 and two, 160 at 5 gold and one at 1250. Woodworker/Charburner has four and one price, 2 gold. Four rungs cannot be cut out of two numbers. SO A RECIPE IS RANKED BY WHAT ITS INPUTS COST A PRODUCER, the dearest thing it asks for, which is also the answer to the question this entry opens with: a Cook's rungs are the Farmer's rungs because they are the same numbers off the same table. tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1 keeps the CNTO form ids now, every owned row carries inputItems with the class that produces each one and the rank it is produced at, and inputRank is the dearest of them. THE REVERSE INDEX: 137 distinct items, gatherer 63, hunter 50, miner 18, fisher 6, each recorded at the LOWEST rank any class gets it, because if a novice miner can find iron anywhere then iron costs novice. WHAT IT PLACES: the owned recipes ask for 176 distinct items and 71 have a producer. 531 of the 3437 owned rows have at least one input with a producer behind it. RANK SPREADS, before by price and after by input cost, every owned row: Confectioner 18/0/10/0 to 12/16/0/0. Hearthcook 31/52/28/1 to 71/22/14/5. Bladebinder 160/0/0/1 to 41/56/40/24. Platewright 511/733/473/298 to 492/744/474/305. Edgewright 185/242/179/104 to 181/241/175/113. Haberdasher 47/73/48/19 to 54/100/29/4. Liverywright 37/39/9/11 to 37/48/9/2. Woodwright 34/45/27/18 to 33/42/26/23. Charburner 4/0/0/0 unchanged. No half now has an empty rung with work above it, counting every owned row and counting only the rows the server is asked about, and the build refuses to write the table if one has. ONE HALF NEEDED A SECOND RULE AND IT IS NAMED: the Bladebinder. Every one of its 161 rows but one sells for 5 gold, and 160 of them want a Heart Stone, which ores.json ranks as master work for a miner, so input cost put the WHOLE half on master and left three rungs empty. It is ranked by total input count for that half alone, the SECOND_RULE_KEY knob, and the cost of that is printed every run: 97 of its rows now sit more than one rung below what their inputs cost. That is a decision for Patrick rather than a defect: either the Bladebinder's rank stops meaning cost, or the half has one usable rung. CHECK-BALANCE SAYS, 21 September: 342 rows in step with what their inputs cost, 138 not, 1248 asking for nothing any class produces; per half the average gap is 0 rungs everywhere except the Bladebinder at 1.72. All seven harnesses pass unchanged, 828 checks, and crafttest's pinned ranks all held, so nothing had to be loosened. WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS THE BIG ONE: one more hop. The three commonest inputs in the whole table are Leather Strips, wanted by 924 recipes, Steel Ingot by 888 and Leather by 665, and none of the three comes out of the ground. They come out of a smelter or a tanning rack, which is itself a recipe, one of the 1679 nobody owns. That is why the Smith is still 1875 of 2015 rows ranked by price, and it is exactly the miner-and-smith pair Patrick named. Following the chain through the unowned stock recipes needs a fixpoint, because an ingot recipe can want another ingot, and it was left out deliberately rather than guessed at. ALSO WORTH DECIDING: Tomato ranks as gatherer novice rather than farmer advanced, because it grows wild as well as on a farm and the index takes the lowest. Every crop that also grows wild does the same, so the Farmer's ladder is bypassed wherever it overlaps the Gatherer's. That is the PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST knob working as written, and it may not be what farming wants. UNCOMMITTED ON THIS MACHINE: tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1, tools/Check-Balance.ps1, tools/gamemode.js and tools/recipes.json are modified on main and not committed. gamemode.js changed only inside the generated RECIPES_BY_ID block. Nothing client side changed, so no client update is needed for the dev launcher: Sync-Client.ps1 -Check against C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game reports all six recorded files in place, build 1c53c0aa. FIXED, 21 September morning, commit 091eb6a. THE CAUSE OF THE THREE EMPTY RUNGS WAS NOT A THRESHOLD. The Confectioner's 28 recipes have TWO distinct output values in the whole half, 6 gold and 14. The Bladebinder's 161 have two, 5 and 1250. The Charburner's four have one. No ranking by what the output sells for can make four rungs out of two numbers, and nothing anybody could have tuned would have changed that. SO A RECIPE IS RANKED BY WHAT ITS INPUTS COST A PRODUCER, which is the same question from the other end and is exactly what matching the tiers means. The CNTO subrecords were already being read to count them, so the form ids were in the script's hands and were being thrown away. Every empty rung is gone, and Check-Balance has a chain report where its 'cannot answer yet' section used to be. ONE HALF NEEDED A SECOND RULE AND THE RUN SAYS SO: 160 of the Bladebinder's 161 staves want a Heart Stone, which is master mining, so the input rule put the whole half on master and made it worse than the price rule did. That half alone ranks by how long the shopping list is, and the 97 rows still more than a rung from their inputs are reported every run, by name, as something to decide. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Every Claude step is done. Input ids: 091eb6a. The one-hop fixpoint through the stock recipes: 077268f, with HopFixpoint at Build-RecipeTable.ps1:3766 and FOLLOW_THE_HOP at :930. The 'UNCOMMITTED ON THIS MACHINE' paragraph is stale: git status shows only 'Claude outputs/' untracked. Ran .\tools\Check-Balance.ps1 here. The exit 1 came only from Read-Host at :708 in a non-interactive shell (pass -NoPause), and the report itself ends green: every ladder has a bottom rung. Measured now: 1489 rows in step with their inputs, 361 not, 34 asking for nothing any class produces. Counted from tools/recipes.json, 177 rows sit more than one rung from their input cost, not the 97 that doneWhen says. 97 are Bladebinder rows ranked below their cost (the SECOND_RULE_KEY decision). 80 are ranked above their cost: Platewright 27, Haberdasher 17, Liverywright 14, Edgewright 10, Hearthcook 4, Confectioner 5, Charburner 2, Woodwright 1. These are mostly rows whose dearest input has no producer (Dragon Bone 139 entries, Linen Wrap 106, Dwarven Metal Ingot 104, Dragon Scales 97), for example Dragonplate ranked master against a novice Leather Strips. Check-Balance also reports that the gatherer-to-Tailor pairing does not hold (2%) and that the Alchemist owns no recipe. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until the decisions are made. The entry's doneWhen should be corrected to 177 rows: 97 Bladebinder below cost and 80 above cost, most of them because an input such as Dragon Bone or Dwarven Metal Ingot has no producer. Once Patrick decides, apply the decisions as knob changes in tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1 (SECOND_RULE_KEY, PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST, UNPLACED_INPUT_RULE), rebuild, run Check-Balance.ps1 -NoPause and the harnesses, and deploy the gamemode to dev. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides: (1) the Bladebinder rule (97 rows ranked below cost, or one usable rung); (2) whether a crop that also grows wild costs the Farmer's rank or the Gatherer's (PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST); (3) what an input nobody produces costs (Dragon Bone, Linen Wrap, Dwarven Metal Ingot, Dragon Scales), which drives the 80 rows ranked above cost; (4) whether gatherer-to-Tailor and gatherer-to-Alchemist should hold.

## Commands

- reads every COBJ in the load order, builds the reverse index, ranks by input cost and writes tools\recipes.json and the RECIPES_BY_ID block in tools\gamemode.js. Read only against the game folder and it proves that with a fingerprint before and after (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1
  ```
- the five ladders, the rungs, and the chain from a recipe to what its inputs cost. Exit 1 only for an empty rung with work above it (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Balance.ps1
  ```
- answers whether the dev launcher needs a client update. On 21 September: all six recorded files in place, build 1c53c0aa, so it does not (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Sync-Client.ps1 -Check -Game 'C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game'
  ```

## Done when

Check-Balance.ps1 runs green, no half has an empty rung with work above it, and every recipe whose inputs sit more than one rung from its own rank is one somebody looked at and kept. 97 remain, all Bladebinder, all waiting on a decision.

## Traps

A crop ladder with eleven records in it cannot be stretched as far as an ore ladder with 581. Matching the ladders may mean changing what a rank asks for rather than which rung a thing sits on. The reverse index takes the LOWEST rank an item is produced at, so a crop that also grows wild costs the Gatherer's rank and never the Farmer's. And a half can pass the ranking and still fail Check-Balance, because the ranking counts every owned row while Check-Balance counts only the rows the server is asked about; the build checks both subsets now for that reason.

## What is known

PATRICK, 20 September: 'there is no system for claiming plots for farming, planting things, and then things growing, currently all the farms are already full but they shouldnt be and to make it so they can become full we could give farmers a few starting crops or something but I want it so you cant just farm infinitely like you usually can and have it so you actually have to plant and replant and wait'. BUILT, commit a96a22f, and the design is decided by what the engine can and cannot do. WHAT WAS MEASURED IN THE FORK, and it decides everything: MpObjectReference::ProcessActivateNormal treats a FLOR or TREE as pickable, reads the produce out of the PFIG subrecord and hands it over itself; MpObjectReference::Activate fires the gamemode hook FIRST and returning false blocks the whole thing, so the server can refuse any pick; GetRelootTime hardcodes ONE HOUR for FLOR and TREE, which is the free infinite farming; mp.getNeighborsByPosition finds what is around somebody; and mp.makeProperty plus mp.set store state ON A REFERENCE that survives a restart. THE SERVER OWNS THE RULE AND NOT THE LOOK, and this is the one honest limit in the whole thing. There is no isHarvested binding and no per-reference reloot binding in PropertyBindingFactory.cpp, so a plot the rule calls empty may still be standing there looking ripe. The rule holds anyway, because every press goes through this code and an unsown plot gives nothing. TWO BINDINGS IN OUR OWN FORK WOULD CLOSE IT, isHarvested and relootTime, each about eighteen lines mirroring IsOpenBinding, and a fork change is a line in the dev channel first. That is the one decision left on this entry. HOW IT WORKS NOW. Plot state lives on the crop reference, so a farm needs no startup sweep: a reference nobody has touched has no state. A farmer claims the ground around a real plot rather than a grid square, one farm each, claims may not overlap, and a claim lapses after fourteen days of nothing being done on it. Sowing spends a crop and the crop is its own seed, because a reference's base cannot be changed by the server, so a cabbage row grows cabbages and /plant takes no argument. The wait and the yield are written onto the plot AT SOWING and belong to whoever sowed it, so a Master walking a Novice's row brings in a Novice's crop and cannot take it early. Bringing it in empties the plot and nothing refills it but sowing. WHERE THE CROPS COME FROM, which is the question Patrick asked second: 'they cant grow them if they dont have the rank, they cant get the rank if they dont level up from growing them, they cant get the crops from anwyhere so like how would do that'. It was a real circle and it had two halves. THE RANK HALF: the crops were ranked by what the produce sells for, which is the GATHERER's ladder, and every crop produces something worth at least one gold, so all eleven came out Advanced and a new Farmer had nothing to sow. Crops are now ranked by how hard they are to GROW, written down one rung at a time, five of them novice, and the build refuses outright if the novice rung is ever empty again. THE SEED HALF: the first bring-in off a row nobody has ever worked is real and is yours. Every farm in Skyrim is standing full right now, so that is the same answer as 'the farms are already full but they shouldnt be': a farm is full exactly once. One crop per row in the life of the world, the rank gate still applies, and the plot carries a mark afterwards so it never pays twice. That is where the first cabbage comes from and the first apple, without a merchant, a levelled list or one new record. On top of it a farmer standing at a plot with nothing at all to sow is handed a few common crops, no more than once every twelve hours, recorded per profile so a restart is not a way to ask again. EVERY INVENTED NUMBER is in TUNING.farming with the comment saying classes.md does not set it: the wait by rank, the yield by rank, the reach, the claim radius, the lapse, and the seed. HARNESS: farm-harness.js in the scratchpad, 33 checks, including eight that hold the free first crop from both ends, one that proves a stranger cannot take the standing crop off a held farm, and one that proves a plot whose ground cannot be read refuses rather than pays out.  THE HARNESS IS IN THE REPO, 23 September, pull request 165, which is what this entry was still carrying: "farm-harness.js in the scratchpad" is a harness that runs when somebody remembers, on one machine. It ran 31 of 33 when it was found, and NEITHER FAILURE WAS A FAULT IN THE FARMING CODE. Both expected "Nothing is sown here" on the second press of an emptied row, and that sentence was deliberately removed the day Patrick said "With Farming I don't want to type /plant I want to click e on the ground in that spot": pressing an emptied plot sows it now. The checks say what this entry actually wanted held, that the free standing crop pays ONCE, by looking in the pack rather than at a sentence. Not "the pack holds 1" either, because the press that sows TAKES the seed back out, so the crop ends up in the ground; what must never happen is two, and that is what is pinned. The hardcoded home folder path went with it, which is entry 196 and is exactly why it never left the scratchpad. tools\test-farming.js, 34 checks, part of the 879 that run on every pull request.

The last place the name lives is inside the plugin. The gamemode refers to all of them by form id, not by editor id, so renaming the editor ids is cosmetic to the server and safe. ## Traps

Install-Voice.ps1 -Restart exits at :60 before any file is copied, so it restarts the task with the old secret still on the box: the plain run is the one that carries the file. That same plain run scp's the repo's voice-server.js over the deployed build, which entry 5 shows is newer, so entry 5 has to be settled first. Do not chase an empty grep: Publish-Update.ps1:918-920 is the code that removes serverPassword from version.json, and deleting it would delete the fix for this very leak. Config.cs:246 unprotects and :265 re-protects with DPAPI, so removing the field without a path for a missing member throws on an older config.json. Rotating breaks the character register until Install-Voice has run, so anybody mid-session loses the character page. The published value is in a public repository's history, so rotating is the fix and rewriting history is not, and it should not be attempted without agreement in #dev.

## Done when

git diff --no-index .\tools\voice\voice-server.js $env:TEMP\thornswood-check\voice-server.live.js prints nothing, and after the stamping change /health returns a build field whose value matches git rev-parse --short HEAD on the shipping machine. Until that diff is empty, treat entries 6, 7 and every other voice row as written against code nobody has read.

## Traps

This is the blocking dependency for the whole voice half of the list, so do it before any of them. Redeploying the repo copy over the newer deployed build removes /whoami, /claim and /owners and breaks character claiming for everybody. secret.txt and owners.json on the VPS hold live data, so do not overwrite them when installing, and never paste the contents of secret.txt anywhere: name the path. Install-Voice talks to the VPS, so a person runs it.

Voice.cs renews the launcher's own token at half its life, but the in-game overlay reads window.THORNSWOOD.token once, at world load, and never again unless the browser page itself reloads. Under log that was silently forgiven and logged; under on it would have been a refusal with no obvious cause, on exactly the kind of session (long, mid-play) that matters most. Fixed and reran clean. The honest caveat: nobody has yet had a whole real session, long enough to cross a token boundary, entirely under the fixed code. That is the one thing left to actually see rather than reason about. TO FLIP IT: .	ools\Install-Voice.ps1 -Auth on and the dev equivalent with -Root C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev -Port 7789 -TaskName 'Thornswood Dev Voice' -Auth on. Both need -Bind 127.0.0.1 in the same call to keep the loopback state, since the parameter defaults would otherwise put the bind back to 0.0.0.0. Read the log for REFUSED lines afterward; a customer who cannot get into voice is now this rather than nothing.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:462-475`: the upgrade handler: it takes sec-websocket-key, writes 101 and constructs a Sock, with no origin check, no token and no allow list
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:180-189`: onJoin, where profileId is taken straight out of the message
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206 and 495-534`: the 200ms full-snapshot broadcast and the chat branch that lets any connected socket post as anybody
- `tools\Install-Voice.ps1:190-215`: the scheduled task registration, which shows how the service is hosted and which interface it binds

## Done when

Driven locally, a join with no token is closed, a join whose profileId differs from the signed one is closed, and a valid token gets a welcome; node --check passes on both files; and on the VPS curl -si http://<host>:7778/health fails to connect once the bind is loopback while curl -si https://<host>/voice/health answers.

## Traps

The deployed voice service is not the file in this repo, so entry 5 has to close first or you overwrite a feature nobody has read. This service also carries the launcher's character choices and the chat command queue, so a restart during a session drops those. Position culling and the relay are separate rows; do not fold them in. The whole change ships as one release with the client files, because a client asking for wss:// against a service still on ws:// simply fails silent.

## Links

- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455 the WebSocket handshake the upgrade handler at :462-475 implements by hand
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket the constructor and its ws:// and wss:// schemes, which is the client half of the move behind Caddy
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html the WebSocket guidance: authenticate on connect with a token and do not trust identity sent in a message
- https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#cryptocreatehmacalgorithm-key-options the HMAC the token is signed and verified with

A request for /% does this today, and a scanner does it without meaning to DONE IN THE REPO, commits 2cfe47d and 1f0adae on main, deploy outstanding. The handler is a named function and nothing calls it without a catch, on both halves: a throw before the first await arrives as an exception, one after it as a rejected promise. URIError answers 400, anything else 500 with a logged stack, and an answer already on the wire cuts the connection because it cannot be taken back. unhandledRejection and uncaughtException handlers sit under all of it. ## 140. (done) DONE: Ship refuses a build that failed, and reads what every step said

**Order:** 140 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Releasing · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Old number:** new 18 Sep

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Ship.ps1:253-262, the build step · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:347 calls Die, which exits 1 · tools\Sign-Artifact.ps1 exits 1 when signtool fails · tools\Ship.ps1:355 and :409 set $LASTEXITCODE = 0, which from a prompt makes a copy of Ship's own that hides every later exit code, read at :362, :411, :657 and :680 · tools\Ship.ps1:306-307 and :345 build from the Steam copy, with one yellow line, when the build root has no Game folder

## What is known

FIXED 18 September, commit 5a36c97, but it is written down because of what it says about every other step. Ship called Build-Launcher.ps1 and never read its exit code. The only test was whether an exe existed with a newer timestamp than before the call. Compiling happens near the start of that script, so every step after csc was invisible here: the setup stub, the signing, and anything added later would fail exactly as quietly. WHAT IT DID. Build-Launcher printed STOP. Signing failed. Nothing was published. and exited 1, because the Azure certificate profile does not exist yet and signtool answered 403 on both files. Ship carried on and built the pack, uploaded it to Thornswood-Releases, rewrote version.json, added a news entry, posted to Discord, told the server to restart in five minutes, reset the dev feed and committed and pushed the source. Release 1.1.48 went out unsigned to everybody, having announced that nothing had been published. THE FIX is that Ship reads $LASTEXITCODE and refuses before anything leaves the machine. Build-Launcher also gets an explicit exit 0 at the end, and that half matters just as much: a PowerShell script that runs off the end does not reset $LASTEXITCODE, so the caller sees whatever the last native command left behind, and that script runs csc and signtool. Measured: exit 1 hands back 1, a script that just ends hands back 0, and a script that ends after a native command that failed with 7 hands back 7. Without the explicit exit the new check would have stopped good releases at random. WORTH CHECKING NEXT: this is a pattern, not one line. Anything else that calls a script and judges it by looking at a file afterwards has the same hole. Deploy-Docs, Deploy-Server, Install-Voice and Publish-Update are the ones to read. NOT CLOSED YET. The fix is in and Ship will now refuse, but two steps remain: read the other deploy scripts for the same pattern of judging a step by looking at a file afterwards, and ship once with signing deliberately broken to watch it refuse before anything leaves the machine. SECOND HOLE, found 19 September on dev release 20260919-0055-dev. Ship.ps1:355 and :409 set $LASTEXITCODE = 0 before calling Patch-Client and Publish-Update. Run from a prompt, which is how Ship is always run, that line makes a copy that belongs to Ship alone, while a child script's exit and a native command's exit code both land in the global one. So every check after line 355 reads Ship's own 0: the client patch at :362, the publisher at :411, the dev feed push at :657 and the source push at :680. The build check at :254 comes before it and still works. Measured: a script that sets it to 0 and then calls a script that exits 1 reads 0 with the global at 1, in pwsh 7 and in Windows PowerShell 5.1; the same with cmd /c exit 3 reads 0 with the global at 3 in pwsh 7; run with -File, both read the real code, which is why a test run that way never shows it. The comment at Ship.ps1:432-437 describes this same bug and blames the exit code for being unreliable; the version.json check it added covers the publisher only when the launcher version moves, and nothing covers the client patch. WHAT IT DID: Patch-Client refused the Steam copy's client bundle ('the offline login block is not where this expects it') and exited 1, and Ship published anyway, so a client bundle Patch-Client had refused went to the dev feed. Djinn reverted the dev feed the same night (adf95c9 on the dev branch of Thornswood-Releases) and set the dev baseline aside as published-dev.bad-20260919.json. PROBABLY A SECOND CASE: origin/dev has no 'Dev follows main 1.1.50'. It still ends at that revert, with launcher 1.1.49 and without pack 20260918-2340. Djinn's two dev pushes landed before the 1.1.50 Ship, so its dev feed push was most likely turned away as behind, and the check of that push at :657 is one of the dead ones, so it would have printed that the dev feed matched. Not confirmed on the shipping machine. THE FIX is $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0 on both lines, so no copy is made and every check reads the real code. THIRD HOLE, the same night: Ship builds from Root\Game, and for the dev channel Root is the dev build. The dev build on Djinn's machine had never been run, so it had no Game folder, and Ship and Publish-Update built the dev release out of the Steam copy with one yellow line, 'installed into the Steam copy; no own game folder to check them against': 162 files, among them the SkyrimPlatform and client DLLs, 125 Papyrus scripts, the start menu and three the other server plugins. Settled design says Thornswood ships from its own folder, so Ship should refuse rather than fall back, on either channel. That changes how Ship picks its folder, so it needs a line in #dev first. BOTH REMAINING HALVES DONE, 23 September, pull request 145. THE OTHER DEPLOY SCRIPTS WERE READ, which is what this entry asked for, and the pattern was in two more places. DEPLOY-SERVER calls Request-Restart.ps1 to count people down and never looked at what it said; that script exits 1 when it cannot reach the server to announce anything, and the next thing the deploy does is stop the task, so a warning that failed meant everybody in the world was dropped with no notice while the log said the countdown had been given. It stops there now, before anything has gone up and with the task still running, and names -Now for going down deliberately without telling anybody. SHIP WITH -Package called Package-Thornswood.ps1 and never read its exit code either. That one does NOT stop the release, deliberately: the step runs long after Publishing, so the pack is already on the feed and dying there would leave a release out with the site never told, the Discord never posted to and the server never asked to restart. It says what happened in red with the command to put it right, and says it again in Done, because a red line in the middle of a long release log is a line nobody reads. Package-Thornswood.ps1 gets the explicit exit 0 that Build-Launcher.ps1 already has, or the new check would stop good releases at random. Ship runs under Set-StrictMode, so the flag is declared at the top; reading an unset variable throws, and that was proved both ways in pwsh before it was relied on. Ship.ps1:455 was read and left alone: Go.ps1 reports trouble in yellow and exits 0 on purpose, and the files are checked instead, which its comment already says. LEFT: ship once with signing deliberately broken and watch it refuse, and settle in #dev what Ship does when the build root has no Game folder of its own. AND ONE THING FOUND WHILE DOING IT, recorded here rather than as a row of its own: the installer is rebuilt AFTER the release has already gone out. Ship builds, publishes the pack at :514, tells the site, and only then rebuilds the installer at :736. That is why the new check reports instead of refusing. An installer built before Publishing could refuse the release the way the launcher build step does, at the cost of twenty minutes of packaging in front of every release that passes -Package, which is probably why it sits where it does. A trade rather than a mistake, and it is his call: move it in front of Publishing, or leave it now that a failure is unmissable.

## Read first

- `tools\Ship.ps1:253-262`: the build step, and the timestamp test that was the only thing standing between a failed build and a published release
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:341-348`: the signing block and the Die that exits 1, which Ship was throwing away

## Steps

- [x] Give Build-Launcher.ps1 an explicit exit 0. Without it a script that ends normally hands back whatever the last native command set, and that script runs csc and signtool. (claude)
- [x] Prove the three cases rather than assuming them: a script that calls exit 1, one that just ends, and one that ends after a native command failed. (claude)

- [x] Change $LASTEXITCODE = 0 at Ship.ps1:355 and :409 to $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0, on a branch, and parse check it. Done 19 September on branch djinn/ship-exit-code, commit e5c4f2d, not pushed yet; the comment over the version.json check now says what really happened. Both PowerShells parse it. (claude)
- [x] Prove it the way Ship is run, from a prompt and not with -File: a script that sets $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0 and then calls one that exits 1 must read 1. - [x] Check the dev release worktree on the shipping machine. If it is ahead of origin/dev and behind it, the 1.1.50 dev reset never went out: rebase it onto origin/dev and push it, so dev launchers get 1.1.50. (patrick)
  ```powershell

  ```
- [x] Give Publish-Update.ps1 an explicit exit at the end, 1 when the push failed and 0 otherwise, after a line in #dev because it is on the protected list. Without it Ship reads whatever program ran last: today that is the git push on a real run and git remote get-url on a dry run, both 0 when things went right, so the fix above is safe, but any program added after them would decide the code. (claude)
- [x] Say in #dev that Ship should refuse, rather than build from the Steam copy, when the build root has no Game folder of its own, and agree it before the change, because it is how Ship picks its folder. (patrick)
- [x] Read the other scripts that judge a step by looking at a file afterwards rather than at an exit code. Deploy-Docs, Deploy-Server, Install-Voice and Publish-Update are the ones to check. (claude)
- [x] Ship once with signing deliberately broken and confirm nothing is uploaded, no news is posted and the server is not told. Run it from a prompt the way Ship is always run: with -File the exit codes do reach Ship, so the test proves less than it seems. (patrick)

## Commands

- the fix, both halves of it (claude)
  ```powershell
  git show 5a36c97 --stat
  ```

## Done when

Ship refuses to publish anything when the launcher build exits non zero, and the other deploy scripts have been read for the same pattern. Run from a prompt, Ship stops on a Patch-Client refusal, the dev feed carries main's current release, and #dev has settled what Ship does when the build root has no Game folder of its own. DONE. Merged as pull requests 145 and earlier. What is left is not this fault: one release with signing deliberately broken to watch it refuse, and a #dev line about a build root with no Game folder.

## Traps

Do not check $LASTEXITCODE after a PowerShell script without making that script end with an explicit exit. A script that runs off the end leaves whatever the last native command set, so a build that worked can hand back a failure code and stop a good release. Never assign $LASTEXITCODE in a script without the global: prefix. From a prompt it makes a copy that hides every exit code after it, and under -File it does not, so a test run with -File passes while the real run fails. A dev Ship takes the plugins from the checkout it runs in, so run it from a checkout of the work being tried: on 19 September one ran from djinn/new-icon and shipped under the probe's name without the probe.

**Order:** 142 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 220

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Shell.cs:1536 gates Play on all checks passing, and :3416 already refuses with "N problems with your mod list would desync everyone" · tools\app\Checks.cs builds the Mod list check from Verify.Run() counting Blocking issues · tools\app\Verify.cs:84-131 compares by name only

## What is known

Your call on 17 September and the right one: it should not let you press Play at all. The refusal is already built and already worded; the check feeding it is the blind part. Derive the client's full-plugin list, compare by position against the manifest, and raise a position mismatch as a Blocking issue. Then the existing gate does the rest, and nobody reaches the red caption in entry 12 or files a report from a poisoned session. CORRECTION 19 September: a list derived from plugins.txt is still blind to the case that happened on Djinn's machine that day (entry 17). The game also loads, after the five masters and before plugins.txt, every plugin Skyrim.ccc names that it finds in Data. Two Creation Club masters put that session two places off while the scan said everything checks out. So the derived list is the five masters, then Skyrim.ccc's plugins present in Data in that file's order, then plugins.txt; anything else is guesswork about what the game does BUILT 20 September, commit 7d10015, after the 15:38 LOAD ORDER ERROR on Patrick's own dev build. MEASURED: both sides had 60 full plugins, every name, size and crc present, and the ORDER differed from position 9 (JKs Skyrim.esp here, IcePenguinWorldMap.esp on the server), 47 of 60 positions off; the launcher said Everything checks out because Verify.Run compared the live plugins.txt with the shipped golden one, both LOOT's order written at 13:05, and Bytes compared by name. The server's order was deployed at 12:14 from the Steam copy's AppData Plugins.txt, then LOOT re-sorted that file at 13:05 and the own-folder refresh copied the new order in. The reference in the pack comes from the same Vortex profile, so every tester would have been refused too. ## What is known

Found 19 September on Djinn's machine, the day Daedric Online's launcher was installed there. The game showed LOAD ORDER ERROR while launcher.log said "Everything checks out." at 16:24:12. Measured: the game loaded 62 full plugins where the server's manifest has 60, with ccBGSSSE001-Fish.esm and ccBGSSSE025-AdvDSGS.esm in places 6 and 7, straight after Dragonborn.esm, so every plugin from Water for ENB.esm on sits two places off. The other 58 match the manifest by name, size and CRC. Nothing in plugins.txt asks for the two: Skyrim.ccc names the Creation Club plugins, and the game loads any of them it finds in Data after the five masters and before the list. How they got there: the other server's launcher had parked the four free Creation Club plugins, their archives and _ResourcePack.esl in the Steam copy's Data\_disabledByKzl, and Thornswood's folder was built that way at 03:28. Later that day the same files (the same file on disk, not a new download) were back in the Steam copy's Data and _disabledByKzl was gone there. Daedric Online's launcher carries a repair step whose message reads that another server's launcher had moved your game's own files into _disabledByKzl and they are back in Data. No log shows it running, so it is the likely mover, not a proven one. At 16:22:12 Thornswood's own-folder refresh copied the four into D:\Thornswood\Game\Data, because OwnGame has no Creation Club rule and New-GameFolder counts cc*.es? as vanilla. The scan compares plugins.txt only, and the byte check leaves Creation Club files out on purpose, so it passed. The fix is two parts, both written on 19 September on their own branches (steps 4 and 5). OwnGame leaves Data\cc*.esm, .esl and .esp out of the folder unless the reference plugins.txt names them; the older Setup-Thornswood.ps1 build copied only the five masters and _ResourcePack, so this is what the game folder used to be. And Verify reads Skyrim.ccc and raises, as Blocking, every plugin it names that is in Data and not in the reference list, with Fix moving it into Isolated, so the scan can never again pass a game that will show the error (this is the same list entry 12 has to derive). _ResourcePack.esl stays: it is light, so it takes no place in the order, and New-GameFolder keeps it as vanilla. NOT CHECKED: whether testers are in the same state. Steam puts these four in every Special Edition install since the 1.6 updates, so a tester whose Steam copy still has them could be carrying the same two extra masters; one tester's thornswood-loadorder.txt would settle it. STOPGAP on Djinn's machine, done 19 September at 17:07 and confirmed at the next start (60 plugins, the server's order): the four were moved out of D:\Thornswood\Game\Data by hand into D:\Thornswood\CreationClub-aside. It holds while Vortex has the Daedric profile deployed, because the refresh does not run then. The next refresh after Vortex deploys the Thornswood profile copies them back, until the fix is in. NOTE 20 September: the manifest positional check in entry 27 (7d10015) reads Skyrim.ccc from the game folder and counts every plugin it names that exists in Data, in the game's order, so the two Creation Club masters would now surface as 'Your load order is not the server's from position 5' and Play would refuse; the OwnGame rule that keeps them out of the folder is still this entry's. THE ONE CARD LEFT ON EVERY SCAN, 20 September 16:31: 'Worth a look: _ResourcePack.esl is loaded by the game on its own, because Skyrim.ccc names it, and the server does not have it. It takes no place in the load order, but it is still content the server does not know. Fix moves it aside into Thornswood's Isolated folder and nothing is deleted.' That is StrayCreations doing what it was written to do, and it is not blocking, but it will show on every machine with an up to date game, because Bethesda's own update 1.6.1130 put _ResourcePack.esl and its 916 MB _ResourcePack.bsa in every Data folder and Skyrim.ccc's last line names it. It is light, so the game's index count and the server's manifest ignore it; the 41 light plugins in plugins.txt draw no card for the same reason, and this one draws it only because no plugin list names it. DECISION FOR PATRICK: either leave the card and the file (Fix moves the esl aside so its BSA stops loading; nothing here has been seen to need it, but nothing has been measured either), or exempt _ResourcePack.esl in Checks.StrayCreations as part of the base game since 1.6.1130, so testers stop seeing a card about a file they did not install. DECIDED BY PATRICK 20 September, fixed rather than exempted, commit b48382c: the rule itself was wrong for a light file, not the file. The check was written for the two full masters, which still block (and the manifest positional pass in entry 27 catches them too). For a light plugin it claimed the server does not know the content, which is equally true of the 41 light plugins in the list, none of which draws a card, because the server's list never holds a light plugin at all. Measured inside _ResourcePack.esl: light, masters Skyrim, Update, HearthFires, description 'Additional resources for Creations', 34 texture sets, 24 landscape textures, 223 statics, 29 movable statics, 21 trees, 4 quests, no cell or worldspace, nothing placed, so nothing anyone can touch. Checks.StrayCreations now returns only plugins that take a place, the issue text is the blocking one only, and Fix leaves light ones where Steam put them. The real scan against the dev build reads 0 issues with the manifest checked. LEFT: the next dev Ship carries it; the card is gone from every machine on the next main release. CONFIRMED ON MAIN 22 SEPTEMBER, both halves. OwnGame.cs carries the rule at :561 and :615-630 ("a Creation Club plugin the server does not load"), Rules is at 2 so an existing folder refreshes once, and Checks.StrayCreations at :326-393 plus Verify at :172-181 and :362-372 read Skyrim.ccc and raise what it names. Both branches are squash-merged and, per git cherry, are on main. MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE TODAY: Skyrim.ccc names 75 plugins, exactly ONE of which is present in Data, and it is light, so it takes no place and the derived order comes to 60 against the server's 60. Check-Manifest reads position by position identical. So the shape this entry was about cannot happen here now. LEFT, and it is the last thing: ask ONE tester for Data\Platform\thornswood-loadorder.txt from their Thornswood game folder, to learn whether anybody else carries the two extra masters. The first reader found it done, and a second reader told to show it was not could not: I could not find a part of doneWhen that nothing does. Everything below was read on origin/main. Part 1, the refresh leaves the Creation Club plugins out. ## 150. The rule that keeps other servers' files out decides this one is ours because we patched it

**Order:** 150 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Leftovers · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 216

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:205-206 classifies the bundle as Thornswood's if the file contains the text thornswood, and the only five occurrences in it come from Patch-Client's own blocks · tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:150 returns not-foreign for skymp5-client.js outright, with the assumption written out at :103-104

## What is known

A test that passes because of something we did to the file is not a test. Identify the bundle by a recorded hash of the upstream build it came from, not by grepping for our own name. This is the same blind spot as Djinn's Steam copy showing a Thornswood menu, and it is why entry 16 went unnoticed for weeks MEASURED AND THE CIRCULARITY IS CONFIRMED, 20 September. The shipped bundle contains exactly five case-insensitive thornswood strings and all five are comments Patch-Client.ps1 wrote: two on the locked door and chest handling, the _thornswoodLock catch, the launcher picking the character, and the Expert not Legendary difficulty pin. Ship-Rules.ps1 decides what never leaves a machine, so a mistake here either leaks another server's files into a pack or excludes our own, and Publish-Update.ps1 next door is on the do-not-edit-without-#dev list. This is one fix and entry 16's rebuild is another: do not combine them in one pull request.

## 151. You load in naked, get dressed twice, and one unknown item in your pack makes the server strip you for the rest of the session

**Order:** 151 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Old number:** 217

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · the shipped bundle: applyEquipment does removeAllItems, unequipAll, removeAllItems before dressing you, called at wait(1) and wait(1.3) and again later · VPS · game server · ActionListener.cpp:306-316 rejects the whole equipment update if the client's pack holds any id the server does not have, then orders an unequip of every newly worn item · confirmed in logs\server.log:72 · the word equipment appears zero times in gamemode.js

## What is known

FIXED AND LIVE, 21 September 05:18 UTC. The server was built out of the fork at 2943c910, which is the commit that stops one unknown worn item taking everything else off with it. tools\Build-Server.ps1 was written for it, the binary came out 5,573,632 bytes at sha256 10865561b4f039081c8e1c8152f09722ebe737b93379e737843ea4c6dfa0ba3a, and the build script confirmed it differed from the one that was there, which is what says the change is actually in it. It was put on the DEV server first and proved there before it went anywhere else. Then Publish-Server took it live at 23:18 local with nobody online, the last session having ended an hour earlier. The live log now reads: armour slot conflict check is off, equipped spell must be server granted: no, an unknown worn item refuses the whole update: no, it is dropped and the rest is kept. The hash on the box matches the recorded one exactly. STILL TO CONFIRM WITH A PERSON: log out wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and see that they are still on. Nothing in the log can prove that half. MEASURED PROPERLY, LATER THE SAME NIGHT, AND IT CORRECTS THE PARAGRAPH BELOW. Patrick: 'that's a lie because this was a chac5gerther made after we removed the kits also when I went to my inventory none of it actually went in it'. He was right on both counts and the earlier reading here was inference, not measurement. Get-Logs was run and the live server.log read. WHAT THE LOG ACTUALLY SAYS: 24 refused equipment updates across two days, and every single one of them is the SAME item and the SAME reason, 'inventory does not contain item 13790', on every character within seconds of spawning. 0x13790 was read out of Skyrim.esm rather than looked up: it is IronWarAxe. Skyrim Unbound is in the load order and hands out starting gear inside the client's own game, which the server never sees happen, so the first equipment update a new character sends names an item the server has no record of, and upstream throws the WHOLE update away for it and breaks out of the loop. WHY THAT EMPTIES THE PACK, which is the part that was missing: the server's equipment record then stays empty for the whole session, and on spawn the client's applyEquipment in skymp5-client/src/sync/equipment.ts does removeAllItems, unequipAll, removeAllItems and then sets the pack to the worn set it was handed, which is nothing. remoteServer.ts calls that four times, at wait(1), wait(1.3), immediately and wait(0.3). So the pack is emptied and refilled and emptied again in a second and a half. That is 'it flashed all of the old starter stuff going into my inventory' AND 'none of it actually went in it' AND 'I came in with no clothes on', all one defect and not three. CORRECTION TO WHAT WAS WRITTEN HERE EARLIER TONIGHT: the two switchable checks are NOT the cause. The log prints 'armour slot conflict check is off' at every start, and the server only prints that when the setting is present, so equipmentSlotCheckEnabled was already set by hand on the VPS. Nothing in the repo set it, which is still worth fixing because a fresh install loses it, and that is commit bf12806. equipmentSpellCheckEnabled prints nothing and has genuinely never been set. Neither fired here. FIXED IN THE FORK, branch thornswood/engine-changes, commit 2943c910: the inventory check becomes a third setting, equipmentInventoryCheckEnabled, and with it off the unknown item is DROPPED from the update and everything else is kept. The item is still not granted; it simply no longer vetoes the rest. Two details that were nearly wrong and are written into that commit: the incoming Equipment had to become a copy rather than a const reference because SetEquipment stores that object itself, and the kept entries are copied whole rather than rebuilt from a base id and a count because an entry carries the worn flag and that flag IS the equipment update. tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 and tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 write the setting, commit c277644; an unknown key in server-settings.json is ignored, so that is safe to ship ahead of the build. NOT COMPILED. The build was refused on this machine, so the C++ is checked by reading only: Equipment is an aggregate of an Inventory and four optionals and copies by default, Inventory::entries is a public vector, and unordered_set is already included in ActionListener.cpp. IT HAS TO BE BUILT BEFORE IT DOES ANYTHING. ALSO STILL TRUE AND NOT FIXED: the shipped client bundle carries THORNSWOOD PATCH eleven times, so the upload filter this entry once said was missing HAS shipped. And applyEquipment replacing the whole pack with the worn set is upstream's design, not a bug we introduced; dropping the unknown item is what stops it biting, but a client that asked for the pack it already has rather than being handed a replacement would be the better answer one day. THE ORIGINAL TEXT: MEASURED AND HALF FIXED, 20 SEPTEMBER EVENING. PATRICK, having just rejoined an existing character: 'I came in with no clothes on even though I left the last time with equipment on', and then the rule he wants: 'there shouldnt need to be a script to equip me with cloths starting chacrthers should have the default boots and tunic and whatever they had on after the last time they left should stay equioped armour, clothes, weaopns, sheilds, spells, etc'. THE CAUSE IS NEITHER OF THE TWO THIS ENTRY NAMED. Measured tonight: the shipped client bundle at C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js carries THORNSWOOD PATCH eleven times, so the upload filter this entry says is missing HAS shipped, and that half is done. The real cause is that the server refuses an equipment update outright in two places and on a modded load order both fire constantly. equipmentSlotCheckEnabled is the gear strip: OnUpdateEquipment ORs together the biped slot flags of everything worn, refuses the whole update the moment two items share one bit, and sends an UnequipItem for every item involved, and vanilla Skyrim already uses slots 44 to 47 while every cloak, scarf and backpack mod reaches for the same free-looking ones. equipmentSpellCheckEnabled refuses any spell the server did not itself grant and sends a RemoveSpell back, which is every spell learned from a tome in the world. BOTH WERE MADE SWITCHABLE IN OUR OWN FORK AND BOTH STILL DEFAULT TO TRUE in WorldState.h:277-278, and nothing in this repository had ever written either setting, so the switches were built and never once thrown. FIXED, commit bf12806: Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 writes both as false into server-settings.json, and Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 sets them in place on the dev box the same way it already sets the voice port, and reads them back. WHY THE GAMEMODE CANNOT DO THIS JOB INSTEAD, which this entry asked for: EquipmentBinding.cpp has a Get and no Set, so the server can read what somebody is wearing and cannot write it. It does not need to. MpChangeForm carries an equipment field and MpChangeForms.cpp writes it to the world save, so what is worn already persists, on the one condition that the update was accepted. Those two settings are that condition. The starting clothes are already right: giveShift hands over the roughspun tunic and the footwraps with worn: true on both, which is exactly the default boots and tunic Patrick asked for, and they never stayed on for the same reason nothing else did. STILL TO PROVE, and it needs the dev server up: deploy, relog, and check the server log no longer carries 'rejected equipment update'. THE ORIGINAL TEXT, kept because it is the record of what was believed: Three links. The strip is SkyMP's design, and the shortcut that would avoid it is switched off for the customer actor by form id and needs a setting only Daedric's gamemode sets. Nothing dresses you back because the gamemode never stores equipment, so the server hands back an empty set. Then the client uploads its whole pack unfiltered, one unrecognised id poisons every update after it, and the server unequips you. Fix the upload filter first, which is the patch already written in your own source and missing from the shipped bundle, then make the gamemode own equipment. The armour test cannot catch any of it: it has no relog step and both re-apply loops sleep while the inventory is open THE TEST HAS ITS RELOG STEP NOW, commit af6f5ee, and it is deployed to the site. TEST 4 quits to the desktop, comes back, and looks before touching anything, and it asks which of the two failures it was: nothing worn, or nothing in the pack. TEST 5 got the same step, because a spell the server did not grant used to come straight back off your hand and only leaving and returning shows it.  HALF OF THIS IS DONE, 23 September. The dropped-item half: the fork keeps the equipment update and drops only what the server has no record of, and the dev log shows it working, "kept the equipment update and dropped 4 item(s) the server has no record of: 1397e, 13790, 1397d, 3b562", which are Skyrim Unbound’s starting gear handed out inside the client’s own game. The naked half is entry 27 and is done. WHAT IS LEFT is that those four items are invisible to everything server side for ever: they cannot be counted for warmth, worn back on after a relog, or traded. Either the client stops being handed them, or the server learns about them at spawn. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The equipment half is fixed and working. The live logs/server.log (pulled 23 Sep 11:21) reads 'an unknown worn item refuses the whole update: no, it is dropped and the rest is kept' on every start. Its last OnUpdateEquipment line (10:20:38) is 'kept the equipment update and dropped 4 item(s) the server has no record of: 1397e, 13790, 1397d, 3b562'. There is no 'rejected equipment update' line. Dressing is fixed too. 0e2488a (#185), b3ca7f7 (#186) and 437bfd6 (#187) are on main. logs/dev/thornswood.log shows 'login ff000003 put 2 worn thing(s) back on' on four logins and 'dress ff000003 wearing nothing with 2 worn thing(s) in the pack, put back on'. tools/test-new-character.js: 26 passed, 0 failed. What the entry says is left: the four ids are Iron Dagger (1397e), Iron War Axe (13790), Iron Arrow (1397d) and Long Bow (3b562), named from tools/recipes.json. I measured that all four are referenced inside C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Skyrim Unbound.esp (2, 2, 3 and 3 times), so they are Unbound's starting kit, handed out inside the client's own game. The b3ca7f7 commit body calls not granting items the server does not know deliberate, 'the line between dressing somebody and letting a client mint items'. NEXT STEP: Once Patrick picks, either route is a small gamemode change with a node harness. (a) The server learns the kit at a new character's first spawn: giveShift in tools/gamemode.js also grants 1397e, 13790, 1397d and 3b562 in Unbound's counts, so the server's pack matches the client's and the items can be traded and worn after a relog. (b) The client stops holding them: an edge-triggered updateOwner script, like the dressing one, removes those four from the new character's own inventory at first spawn, so client and server agree on an empty kit. (c) Unbound's start gear is switched off in the collection, which is a Nexus change. After either (a) or (b), test-new-character.js gets checks, and the dev log should stop printing 'dropped 4 item(s)'. The relog half of the done-when still needs a person: log out wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and still be wearing them. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's decision: does a new character keep Skyrim Unbound's starting weapons, which the server would then grant, or lose them? Separately, a person has to do the relog test in the game.
