## 154. (done) You cannot sprint and you cannot jump, while walking and running are fine

**Order:** 154 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** work it out, large · **Who:** Djinn · **Old number:** 212

## Where it lives

Reported 17 September · nothing in tools\gamemode.js or tools\ts-plugins\*.js touches stamina, carry weight or regeneration, checked · known.md:42 says the server owns health, magicka, stamina and actor values · known.md:32 records SunHelm as the one mod whose scripts still run, writing stamina on a timer against a server that corrects it · SunHelmSurvival.esp, SunHelmDiseases.esp and an Embers patch are all enabled · Read end to end 19 September: nothing in the client bundle, the server or our own plugins stops a jump on this server, so the jump half is not in the code · probe merged to main 19 September as 94b0f1f, pull request 69, and shipped to everyone in 1.1.50 (pack 20260918-2340) · ANSWERED 19 September from the probe's own lines in Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log: every jump and every sprint reads "refused ... the animation graph turned it down" with stamina 100 (100%), speed 369, running yes, in the air no, encumbered no and controls on · SHIPPED AND STILL BROKEN, 19 September: 1.1.53 carries the AI driven and IsNPC corrections and both are refused exactly as before, with every gate reading clear

## What is known

NOT FIXED. 1.1.53 shipped two corrections, AI driven and IsNPC, and jump and sprint are exactly as broken. The probe lines from that build are what rule them out: "jump: refused, JumpDirectionalStart went through and the animation graph turned it down. stamina 100 (100%), speed 369, running yes, in the air no, bSprintOK yes, IsNPC no, bIsSynced no, bAnimationDriven no, controls on." Every gate clear, both events still refused. The corrections stay in, because AI driven has no getter and nothing else keeps it off, but they are not the cause and must not be counted as a fix. THE USEFUL PART is bSprintOK reading yes. It is the only condition on the sprint transition, in 0_master and in mt_behavior both, and a transition that is being evaluated cannot refuse with its only condition satisfied. So that transition is not being evaluated at all: the state machine holding it is not the active one, and the jump transitions sit in the same place. The question is now which branch of the graph the character is in, not which flag is set. RULED OUT and worth not repeating: stamina (100 per cent at every refusal); the behaviour files (read against the vanilla graph they were generated from, the jump transitions carry no condition and the only sprint condition is bSprintOK); stray Nemesis patches (the generated animationdatasinglefile.txt against its vanilla base shows Precision and the Nemesis base and nothing else, so Ultimate Dodge Mod, Ultimate Combat, Character Behaviors Enhanced and the rest were never ticked); the instrument (animationSucceeded is a real string in SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll, so "refused" is a reading and not an artefact); and the folder the launcher builds, because the behaviour files in it are byte for byte the ones in the Steam copy Vortex deploys into. THE NEXT STEP IS NOT A VANILLA TEST. Launching Skyrim from the Steam copy was suggested on 19 September and Patrick ruled it out, correctly: Steam updates its copy on launch, every one of these servers runs a downgraded exe, and the price is the install, a re-downgrade and an Anniversary upgrade nobody wants. The four variables the probe now reads answer the same question from an ordinary session. bIsInMT reading no while running means the character is not in the branch that holds jump and sprint, which makes this the graph and the mod list. All four reading normal while both events are still refused means the graph is in the right branch and something between the key and the graph is doing it, which makes it this server. If an offline run is ever genuinely needed it is the Thornswood folder's own skse64_loader.exe with MpClientPlugin.dll moved aside under the .thornswood-off suffix, never Steam's copy. Branch djinn/jump-gate-measure adds bIsInMT, IsFirstPerson, bAttached and currentDefaultState to the line, writes a line for a press that WORKED as well as one that did not (suppressing success is why the last log read as though nothing ever succeeded), and tallies how many animations succeeded at all so a flag that is never true cannot pass for a graph that refuses everything. STILL BROKEN ON 20 September and the probe has not been fed. The corrections in 1.1.53 were ruled out and the probe now reports bIsInMT, IsFirstPerson, bAttached and currentDefaultState, which decide between the two remaining answers: bIsInMT reading no while running means the character is not in the branch holding jump and sprint, so it is the graph; all four normal with both events still refused means the graph is right and something between the key and the graph is doing it, so it is this server. THE LOG HAS NO PRESS LINE IN IT. C:/Thornswood/Game/Data/Platform/thornswood-front.log from the 20 September session holds two setup lines, jump is key 57 and sprint is key 56 and IsNPC was cleared, and nothing else, though the build says every press writes a line whether it worked or not. So either nobody pressed jump after the plugin loaded, or buttonEvent never sees those keys, and if it is the second that is itself the answer. NEXT STEP IS A MINUTE OF SOMEBODY'S TIME and a Claude cannot do it: get in the world, press jump and sprint several times each, leave, and read the probe lines out of that log. Not through Steam's copy; the no-steam note says why. THE PROBE FIRED AND IT NAMES THE CAUSE, 20 September, 11:10, seven presses in a live session with the game running. This is the minute of somebody's time this entry has been waiting for and the answer is not either of the two it predicted. WHAT EVERY PRESS SAYS: 'jump: refused, JumpDirectionalStart went through and the animation graph turned it down', and the same for sprint with SprintStart. So the idle event is sent and accepted; the graph refuses it. Conditions at the moment of the press, identical on all seven: stamina 100 (100%, base 100), regen 5 x 100%, speed 344, running yes, sprinting no, in the air no, encumbered no, sneaking no, swimming no, mounted no, weapon out no, bSprintOK yes, bIsSynced no, bAnimationDriven no, bAttached 0, currentDefaultState 0, controls on. FIRST, WHAT IS RULED OUT. bIsInMT reads YES, so the character IS in the branch that holds jump and sprint. This entry named 'bIsInMT reading no while running means it is the graph' as one of the two remaining answers. It is not that one. bSprintOK is yes, so the sprint gate is open and is not the problem either. SECOND, THE CAUSE. IsNPC reads YES at every one of the seven presses. The plugin's own message says IsNPC is what takes both out of the graph, and line 73 of that same log says it cleared it earlier in the same session. So the flag comes back after it is cleared. WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN IT SOUNDS: ownTheCharacter() in tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js:1405-1424 already runs on a timer, by its own comment, and already re-clears IsNPC every time it sees it set. The saidIsNpc flag only stops it SAYING so twice, it does not stop it clearing. So the clear is repeating and the flag is still set at press time. Setting the graph variable is not making it stick. The early returns are not the explanation: the press lines record mounted no and controls on, and the input lines around them record menu no. ONE MORE NUMBER WORTH KEEPING: the hook counter goes 34, 37, 42 events across the presses while the successes stay frozen at 14. Fourteen animations worked, presumably at load, and every single one since has failed. THE NEXT STEP IS CHEAP AND DECISIVE and does not need anybody in the world: read IsNPC back immediately after pc.setAnimationVariableBool('IsNPC', false) on line 1417 and log both values. That separates the two remaining possibilities. If it reads false straight after the set and true again at the press, something is re-setting it continuously and the question is what; the likeliest candidate is that in SkyMP the local character is a server spawned actor whose base record is an NPC, so the graph variable is re-derived rather than owned by us. If it reads true straight after the set, the setter is failing silently, and it is failing inside a try that swallows the error, so add the catch text to the log line. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY: the note above saying the log holds no press line and so either nobody pressed or buttonEvent never sees those keys was right about that log and is now overtaken. buttonEvent sees them fine. The earlier log was a session in which they were not pressed after the plugin loaded. FIXED 20 September, commit 8fee236, and it is the timing after all. ownTheCharacter clears IsNPC on a two second heartbeat, and the graph reads the variable on the frame it handles the event, so a clear up to two seconds early is not there when it counts. bSprintOK a few lines above is held every frame for exactly that reason and IsNPC was not. It is now cleared in the buttonEvent handler, which runs from the input handler before the graph updates, and held clear across the frames a press is resolved over, because sprint is a hold and the frame the graph acts on is not always the frame the key arrived. THE WRITE IS ALSO READ BACK, which is the measurement this entry has been asking for and it now costs nobody a second session: if the log says IsNPC was written false and read back true on the same frame, the write is not taking and the answer is not timing at all. A setter that throws now says so with the reason instead of being swallowed. Nothing is said when it simply works. Checked by lifting holdNpcClear and varBool out of the file and driving them with a fake character: 11 assertions across already clear, a write that takes, a write that does not, a setter that throws, and a build with no such graph variable. Not deployed yet: this is a game plugin, so it needs a Ship. AND THE CLEAR IS NOW GUARDED, commit ec77404, which the first version was not and should have been. It runs on every heartbeat frame and had none of the three refusals ownTheCharacter has directly above it. The one that matters: race creation hands the character over on purpose, so the unguarded version was writing to the animation graph all the way through somebody making a face, which is the exact area two other reports on this list are about. Dead, sitting in something and on a horse are the other two, and nobody jumps in any of those states so none of them costs a press. A throwing isOnMount still lets the clear run, because the guard is a refusal to act on a known state rather than an unknown one. 17 assertions in total now. WORTH KNOWING: 1.1.58 shipped the UNGUARDED version. The guard is committed and needs the next Ship to reach anybody. WHY THIS IS NOT CLOSED, stated plainly on 20 September so nobody re-reads it as done. The fix is in and shipped in 1.1.59, and the guard in ec77404 with it. But closed means jump and sprint work in the world, and that cannot be established from this machine: it needs somebody to press both keys in a session and the log read afterwards. THE CLIENT SOURCE WAS CHECKED AS A ROUTE AND IT IS NOT ONE. Now that the fork's client source is in hand, grepping all of skymp5-client/src for IsNPC, setAnimationVariableBool and AIDriven returns nothing at all. The client bundle does not set this flag, so the fix cannot move there and the plugin is the right place for it after all. Whatever sets IsNPC is below that, in the native layer or in how the actor is spawned. SO THE NEXT STEP IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS A MINUTE OF SOMEBODY'S TIME: get in the world, press jump and sprint several times, and read the log. The readback added in 8fee236 now answers the open question without a second session: a line saying IsNPC was written false and read back true means the write is not taking at all, and its absence means something re-sets it between the write and the press. CLOSED 20 SEPTEMBER. Patrick played on the dev channel with pack 20260920-1302-dev and launcher 1.1.61.1, the first release carrying the fork's own six client files, and jump and sprint work. Every hypothesis on this entry that pointed at the mod stack, Nemesis, the IsNPC flag and the death whitelist is closed with it: the cause was the other launcher's build of MpClientPlugin.dll, which entry 27 found and entry 11 removed. It reaches everybody when patrick/progression is merged and shipped on main, which is the release step on entry 7. Until that Ship, main still runs the old client and cannot jump.

## What is known

Internal tooling goes behind a build flag, an admin check or a separate package. It is never on an unmodified function key in a retail client DONE 23 September, and the flag was already there rather than invented. The file still ships and MarkKey stays in toolsemotesThornswood.ini, both deliberately and both for the reasons this entry's own trap gives: Ship refuses a release when the plugin folder and the source differ by a byte, so a half done removal stops every release, and the ini is not packed, so removing the key would change nothing for anybody who already has one. **Order:** 160 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Djinn

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · Profile\MyGames\SKSE holds six crash logs from 18 and 19 September and they are the same crash down to the address · Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 · tools\New-GameFolder.ps1, Test-KeptOut · CORRECTED 19 September: the fix went into New-GameFolder.ps1, which builds the other server's and Daedric's folders, not Thornswood's. Thornswood's is built by the launcher in tools\app\OwnGame.cs. The 21:51 crash log still has InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 loaded and the same fault.

## What is known

MEASURED FROM THE CRASH LOGS, 19 September. All six are EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION executing 0x0000656D6167, which is the four characters "game" being called as code. The return address at the top of the stack is InventoryInjector.dll+0x3AA85 and R13 holds that library's own Hooks::IconSetter::ProcessListFunc, with FavoritesMenu and MagicFavorites in the live objects beside them. Inventory Interface Information Injector calls through a freed pointer while it is building the favourites list. What frees it is this server: SkyMP rebuilds the character's inventory from the server's copy after an equip, and the Papyrus VM in every log has a TESModPlatform.Add queued at the moment of the fault, so items were being written underneath the menu as it was drawn. THE FIX on branch djinn/favourites-menu-crash is to stop shipping the library: it is the code that faults, it is not built here, 1.1.1 from 2023 is its last release, and nothing else in the build asks for it (the string InventoryInjector appears in no other SKSE plugin, moreHUD, moreHUD Inventory Edition, Crafting Categories and QuickLoot IE included). What goes with it is the icons its JSON files add to inventory rows, the I4 Icon Addon and nothing else. No plugin is enabled or disabled, so the load order does not move and the server manifest is untouched. A second, separate bug found in the same place is on branch djinn/favorites-menu-name: thornswood-front.js asked Ui.isMenuOpen for "Favorites Menu" and Skyrim's name is "FavoritesMenu", so for as long as somebody had Q open our own plugin believed no menu was open at all, and the magic menu was missing from that list outright. ALSO FOUND, not fixed: the bundle applies a server inventory update to a reference on the next frame at onUpdatePropertyMessage with no menu guard, while the periodic apply for your own character thirty lines away does wait for isBadMenuShown. That is the same crash class for containers and belongs with entry 20. WRONG FOLDER, corrected on branch djinn/i4-out-of-the-right-folder. 52af856 put the exclusion in New-GameFolder.ps1. That script builds the other server's and Daedric's folders, which its own header says; Thornswood's folder is built by the launcher, in OwnGame.cs. So nothing was removed: the crash log from 21:51 on 19 September, after 1.1.53, has InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 still loaded and the same fault at 0x656D6167 with FavoritesMenu and MagicFavorites on the stack, and the source path and "Running IconSetter.processList hook" visible in the stack strings. Worse, the change would have taken the library out of two other servers' folders, which are not ours to edit, so it is reverted byte for byte. The exclusion now sits in OwnGame.Skip beside the Creation Club one; a file already in the folder goes on the next refresh, because the sweep at the end removes anything in the record that the pass did not take and that came from Vortex. Compiled with the Framework csc, 48 files, exit 0. ONE DETAIL CORRECTED: I4IconAddon.esp IS a plugin and it is in the load order at FE:5. It stays loaded and inert once the library is gone, so the load order still does not move, but the earlier wording said no plugin was involved and that was wrong. AND THE FOLDER HAS TO BE REBUILT: shipping the launcher does not delete the file by itself. Settings, Maintenance, Thornswood's own Skyrim folder, Refresh. THE REPO HALF IS DONE AND WAS ALREADY DONE, measured 20 September; what is left is a person. The exclusion lives in tools/app/OwnGame.cs:627-628, skipping both Data/SKSE/Plugins/InventoryInjector.dll and anything under the InventoryInjector folder, put there by 5f88499 after the first attempt went into New-GameFolder.ps1, which builds the other server's and Daedric's folders rather than ours. On disk now: the dll is gone from C:/Thornswood/Game and the newest crash log anywhere is crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38, which predates the fix shipping. So two of the three conditions in the done-when are met. THE THIRD IS NOT MINE: a tester opens Q, equips a favourite, opens Q again, and the game does not close. Until somebody does that this stays open. WORTH RECORDING: a grep for InventoryInjector limited to ps1, json and md finds nothing and reads as though nothing enforces this. The enforcement is in C#. Search the whole tree. AND THE PAUSE ITSELF LEAKED, reported by Djinn 20 September: 'the Q favorite menu that was pausing the game in Thornswood is still lingering and causing that to happen while playing the other server'. That is a second fault in the same place and it has its own entry below; this entry is still the crash and the library. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The repo half is on main and has shipped. tools/app/OwnGame.cs:564 skips 'it crashes the quick favourites menu', and CrashesUs at :602-607 matches Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll and the InventoryInjector folder. The fix landed as c024f7a (#82). The favourites menu name fix is in: tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js:854 and :3886 use 'FavoritesMenu' and list 'MagicMenu'. Measured on disk: Test-Path C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll is False. The InventoryInjector folder is there but holds 0 files. Profile\MyGames\SKSE now holds only two crash logs. crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38 is the pathing one (entry 140). The new crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59 has no InventoryInjector in its module list and no FavoritesMenu. It is a different crash: a read of 0x168 with BSFaceGenMorphDataHead and BrowsMaleHumanoid05 on FishingInSkyrim.esp's NPC 'Rybek Kupiecski' 0x30025905. So there is no favourites crash since the fix. No plugin log (thornswood-front.log, thornswood-input.log) shows the favourites menu being opened, so nothing proves the Q test has been done. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change in the repo. ## 163. A third crash, on dev 1.1.94.1: an access violation at SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D (Blade Da Razor, 25 September)

**Order:** 163 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

the staff sessions page, Blade Da Razor's red session on 25 September · the crash-*.log in it · tools/docs-app/server.js:1374 (the alert) and lineAround (the line it quotes)

## What is known

REPORTED 25 SEPTEMBER by the site's trouble alert: "A session went wrong. Blade Da Razor, on the dev build, launcher 1.1.94.1. something threw and nothing caught it", quoting Crash Logger's first line: Unhandled exception "EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION" at 0x7FF6AC81799D SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D, cmp r9, r12. NOT THE SAME ADDRESS as either crash on file: the FaceGen head crash is at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF (entry 44), and the pathing one jumped into heap memory (the entry above). Nothing in the repo or on this list names +0CF799D. ONE ODD THING, worth reading the log for: the alert copies Crash Logger's line as it is (server.js lineAround, trimmed only), and cmp r9, r12 compares two registers and touches no memory, so that instruction cannot be what read the bad address. Either the fault was the jump to that address, or the code there changed while another thread ran it (a plugin patching the game at runtime does that); the registers, the stack and the probable call stack in the log say which. NOT READ YET: the whole crash log is on the staff sessions page, which a session here cannot open. What to read in it: the probable call stack (only SkyrimSE.exe, or SkyrimPlatform.dll, the SkyMP client or another SKSE plugin on it), the objects Crash Logger names in the registers, and how far into the session it went. One report is not a pattern. READ 25 SEPTEMBER, the whole log Patrick pasted (CrashLoggerSSE 1.24, crash time 24 September 22:47:42 on Blade's clock, 23 minutes into the session, E:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game, SkyrimSE.exe 37,157,144 bytes, which is 1.6.1170). NONE OF OUR CODE IS ON IT. The crashing thread is one of the game's own job threads (BSJobs::JobThread on the stack), and every frame, probable and scanned, is SkyrimSE.exe, KERNEL32, ntdll or KERNELBASE: Address Library ids 69378+0x1ED, called from 69380+0x361, from 69344+0x8A, from 68445+0x3D, the thread's start. No SkyrimPlatform, no MpClientPlugin, no SKSE plugin. THE FAULT DOES NOT ADD UP AS A SOFTWARE ONE. Windows says the thread tried to EXECUTE memory at 0x7FF6FEDED89D, while the instruction it stopped on is at 0x7FF6AC81799D (SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D), a register compare that cannot fault. The execute address is 1.3 GB past the start of SkyrimSE.exe, whose furthest object in this log is 50 MB in, and it is inside no loaded module. A fault address that is not the instruction's own, on an instruction that cannot fault, in the game's own code with nothing else on the stack, is most often an unstable machine (an overclock, a memory profile such as XMP, or heat) rather than a bug. One log cannot prove that. THE QUEST IN R9 IS MOST LIKELY A BYSTANDER: Crash Logger names any register that happens to point at a game object, and R9 held AWAconquest (0x1A000FEF, Solitude Arena.esp, not running, stage 0) while being compared with a pointer into the job system's own globals (R12, SkyrimSE.exe+32580C8), which is not quest code. Memory was not short: 19.6 of 31.8 GB in use, the game at 6 GB private. The log also says Hyper-V, which is how Windows 11 with Memory Integrity looks to it and is not a cause by itself. WHAT SETTLES IT is a second report: the same SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D and 69378 again means a real fault in the game's job system with something feeding it; a different address each time on Blade's machine means the machine. BLADE'S ANSWER, 25 September, through Patrick: the PC is overclocked "for sure" and he thinks XMP is on, and he was in a small village in the Rift when it went. That fits the reading above: an unstable machine rather than anything in the game or ours. Left open for a second report, which is what would say otherwise.

- [x] Ask Blade what they were doing when it went: where, what they had just pressed, who was near. (patrick)

- [x] Ask Blade: is the PC overclocked, or running a memory profile such as XMP, and do other games crash on it? Did it happen again? (patrick)
- [ ] On a second crash at SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D from anybody, look up ids 69378, 69380 and 69344 in the Address Library and name the job it was running. (claude)

## 167. Identity on the game server is a number the client picks, so anyone can be anyone, including the admin

**Order:** 167 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 15

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · offlineMode set by tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:185 · tools\gamemode.js:2274-2296, 2362-2392, 3097-3108 (admin is a hardcoded id) · Everyone's PC · tools\app\AutoJoin.cs:247-260

## What is known

The server never takes identity from the client. Either SkyMP's non-offline flow, or a short-lived signed token from the site after Discord sign-in, verified before the actor is bound to a profile. Admin becomes a role on a verified identity rather than a number in the source. Every other control is keyed on this, so fixing it makes all of them real at once MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: In-world identity is still a claim. The fork's offline login (C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-server\ts\systems\login.ts:233-237) emits spawnAllowed with gameData.profileId unchecked, and Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:469 writes offlineMode true. admins() still falls back to the hardcoded 816507994 (gamemode.js:19198-19205), and the comments at gamemode.js:18664-18672 and 19230-19238 still call the profile id a claim. Voice has real proof: /token (voice-server.js:727-760) mints an HMAC token after the site's /api/play/owns answers, and onJoin (:392-424) takes the id from the token. But AUTH defaults to 'log' (voice-server.js:520, Install-Voice.ps1:46), so unproven joins keep the id they claim. commands.push (:932-937) also drops the proven flag, so handle() (gamemode.js:18194) cannot tell the two apart. NEW HOLE, found reading the code: /api/play/join (server.js:2150-2157) adds any profileId to the caller's linked list without checking whether another Discord account holds it. /owns checks the caller's own list first (server.js:2531-2533). Every profile id is broadcast to every voice peer five times a second (voice-server.js:430-443). ## Traps

A ban here is keyed on profileId, which the file itself calls a claim and not a fact, so turning enforce on without entry 29 gives a door that a stranger walks around by editing one number in a settings file. The door refresh throws the whole allow list away on one failed lookup, so enforcing before that is fixed risks a Discord hiccup locking everyone out at once, which is exactly the outage the watch-only comment was written to avoid. tools\app\Door.cs is on CLAUDE.md's do-not-touch-without-a-line-in-#dev list. This is a coordinated release: the server decides and the launcher explains, so both go out together.

## 169. The Discord ticket, a thirty day credential as good as identity, is sent in clear HTTP every time a character is made

**Order:** 169 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 17

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Creation.cs:670-684 · VPS · voice · the /choose route

## What is known

A choose route on the site over HTTPS that checks the ticket and relays to the voice service over loopback, which is already the shape of the owns route in the other direction. Take the ticket out of the choose body. The launcher protects it with DPAPI on disk and then puts it on the wire in the clear PART DONE 24 September, pull request #223. WHAT CHANGED: Voice.FetchToken in tools/app/Voice.cs now sends the Discord ticket only when the voice address it posts to starts with https:// (case-insensitive). For any other address it sends nothing, returns no join token, and writes to the log: "Voice: no join token, because the voice address is not https and the Discord ticket only goes over https. Voice may be refused." Before this, VoiceBase fell back to http://address:7778 whenever VoiceUrl was empty. That covers a new install until its first update check and the feed's deliberate rollback. In both cases FetchToken posted the ticket in the clear. A new harness, tools/test-voice-ticket.ps1, takes the real FetchToken and JsonEscape text out of Voice.cs, compiles it against stubs, and points it at a loopback socket that records every byte it receives. MEASURED: The change is 20 added lines in tools/app/Voice.cs, just after the url is built (line 561) and before the body is built. The check is at Voice.cs:577-581. Before the change: tools/test-voice-ticket.ps1 run against the old Voice.cs (git show HEAD saved to the scratchpad) gives 10 passed, 8 failed under both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. In the old code the ticket reached the raw http port and came back with a token, both with an http base and with no config (conf null). After the change: 18 passed, 0 failed under both pwsh and 5.1. Nothing connects to an http address, including one written in capitals and one with https later in the path. An https address is still asked for a token (the socket saw a TLS connection). The ticket never shows up in readable bytes. The "not linked to Discord" path is unchanged. Build-Launcher.ps1 into $env:TEMP\ts-build-144 exit 0 and produced Launcher\Thornswood.exe (3,215 KB). The PowerShell parser finds 0 errors in the new .ps1. I confirmed the triage findings in the code: VoiceBase's http fallback is at Config.cs:67-75, and the empty voiceUrl rollback is at Shell.cs:4374-4378. Roster.cs:94 and every Discord.cs ticket post go to Discord.Site, which is https://thornswood.net (Discord.cs:54). A failed fetch is retried by RenewToken five minutes later (tokenGot set to now-25 minutes, checked on the 2 s tick at Voice.cs:971). The voice service's default THORNSWOOD_VOICE_AUTH is log (voice-server.js:520), so on the fallback paths the join goes through unproven rather than being refused. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, after merge: none of this has gone out yet. It goes out with the launcher on the next dev Ship (.\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "..."). No site, voice or gamemode deploy is needed. Still open on entry 144, not done here: (1) Close the raw voice ports. tools/Caddyfile:27-30 still lists "only then THORNSWOOD_VOICE_BIND=127.0.0.1 and the two ports close" as not done. Install-Voice.ps1:39 defaults -Bind to 0.0.0.0, and nothing in the repo records the dev service's bind. This is VPS work for Patrick. (2) The doneWhen playtest: a character made against the dev server still gets its trade and town. Creation now happens on the K panel in game, so this can only be confirmed by testing. (3) The entry's title and todo still describe Creation.cs and /choose, which are gone (3aa37ef, c87da23). Someone with list access should reword it around the /token fallback. I did not edit the To Do List. Side effect to know about: while VoiceUrl is empty, voice joins go through unproven. With THORNSWOOD_VOICE_AUTH=log that is allowed and logged. If it is ever set to on, voice is refused on the rollback path. That is the intended trade: no voice proof rather than the ticket in the clear.

## 172. (done) DONE: the Google Ads tag is gone, and so is everything it would have needed

**Order:** 172 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Website · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Old number:** new

## Where it lives

VPS · site · tools\docs-app\public\home.html, the AW-18458864483 block in the head, loading unconditionally · it covers every public route, because server.js hands that one file to all of them and swaps the body in through /api/page · no privacy page exists yet, which is entry 33

## What is known

The tag went live on 17 September, verified on thornswood.net. Google Ads expects Consent Mode v2 for visitors in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, and the snippet as pasted does not have it. Consent has to default to denied and be set BEFORE gtag.js loads, which means a block above the existing script rather than beside it. Getting the order wrong is the usual mistake and it silently does nothing. Four signals matter: ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization and analytics_storage. Deny all four by default, show a banner, and call gtag('consent','update',...) when somebody chooses. Keep the choice in localStorage and read it back on the next visit so nobody is asked twice. Region targeting is allowed, so the honest minimum is to deny by default in the EEA and the UK and leave everyone else as they are. That is one region array rather than a worldwide banner. This is a sibling of entry 33 and not a duplicate of it: that entry writes the privacy page, this one is the gate that has to exist before the tag may fire. Neither closes the other, and the privacy page has to name Google either way.  REMOVED 23 September rather than fixed, and that is Patrick’s decision in his own words: "we can remove the Google Ads tag and anything related to it we will not be using Google Ads". Pull request 166, deployed the same night. A fetch of https://thornswood.net finds no gtag, no googletagmanager and no AW- id anywhere. WHAT STANDS WHERE IT WAS is a comment saying it was there, whose decision it was and what went with it: the tag loaded on every public page, so Google was handed the address of every visitor before they agreed to anything, and that needed a privacy page naming Google and a consent gate for the EU and the UK, because an unconditional load is not what Google Ads expects. Neither is owed now. The comment ends with the one thing that matters for next time: if anything like it comes back, it comes back with the privacy page and the consent gate in the same change, not after it.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html, the head`: the tag as it ships today, loading with no consent call in front of it
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:164-172`: PUBLIC_PAGES, which is why one file carries the tag onto every public route
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\`: where privacy.md will live, from entry 33, which this has to agree with

Before this, the mute stopped at the in-game page, and that page has no connections once it is in relay mode. The list now travels on the same file channel push to talk uses. The in-game page's setMuted sends the ids to the voice plugin as a 'thornswood-voice-muted' message. The plugin writes them into voice-muted.txt. Voice.cs reads that file on its 100ms pass and posts a 'muted' message to its page, both when the list changes and whenever the page loads. voice-host.html sets a muted person's gain to 0 before distance is considered, and also before your own position is known and from the moment a connection to them opens. setMuted also accepts (profileId, on) now, so the entry's doneWhen call works as written. Ship-Rules.ps1 keeps voice-muted.txt out of every pack. MEASURED: tools/test-voice-mute.js runs the real voice-host.html script, the real ts-ui/thornswood-voice.js and the real ts-plugins/thornswood-voice.js in a vm with a fake browser, file system and audio graph. It also checks Voice.cs and Ship-Rules.ps1 by text. On the pre-change files (taken from HEAD into the scratchpad) it reports 9 passed, 21 failed. On the branch it reports 30 passed, 0 failed. The failing checks on the old code include the launcher page leaving profile 123, muted, in the same cell at zero distance, at gain 1 (the reviewer's measurement), and setMuted(123, true) muting nobody. On the branch the same case gives gain 0 in both pages, and doneWhen passes as written: setMuted(123, true), then place() with 123 in your cell at zero distance, gives gain 0. The changes are voice-host.html place() (new first test inside forEach, plus the no-position branch), open() starting a muted person's gain at 0, the 'muted' handler at the end of the message listener, Voice.cs PassMuted plus the mutedSeen reset in Configure(log), and the plugin's writeMuted beside the browserMessage handler. node --check passes on all changed .js files and on the voice-host.html script, Ship-Rules.ps1 parses with 0 errors, and Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root %TEMP%\ts-build-151 exits 0 with no compiler message on Voice.cs. ## 178. (done) DONE: a sixteen year old answering in a sentence no longer reads as a yes

**Order:** 178 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 6

## Where it lives

VPS · bot · tools\discord\bot.py:324-352 (said_yes), used at :447

## What is known

Verified: it tests the affirmative-prefix list before the number, so "16" is flagged but "I'm 16", "im 16" and "yeah 14" are not. It never auto-rejects, it only decides whether to put CHECK THIS ONE on the ticket a human reads, so nobody is auto-admitted. But the one automated safeguard goes quiet exactly when a minor answers naturally. Move the digit check above the prefix check and return false on any number under 18  FIXED 23 September, pull request 166, and the bot is on the box. said_yes checked the yes words first, and "I’m 16" starts with "i’m ", which is in that list, so a sixteen year old answering in a sentence read as a yes and the thread was never flagged. That is the one answer the function exists to catch. A NUMBER BEATS A WORD now: any number between 1 and 120 in the answer is read as an age, and if the smallest of them is under eighteen it is a no, even beside a bigger one, because "my brother is 30, im 16" is not a yes. Anything over 120 is a year or a postcode and is ignored, so "born in 2009" does not become an age of 2009. A text with no age-like number in it falls through to the words exactly as before. The function never rejects anybody by itself: a no puts a line at the top of the thread for a person to read.

- `tools\discord\bot.py:340-351`: the order that is the defect: empty at :340, _NO prefix at :341-342, _YES prefix at :343-344, and only then the digit scan at :346-351
- `tools\discord\bot.py:444-450`: the one call site, `if not said_yes(gave):` at :447, so you can see the only consequence is a CHECK THIS ONE prefix and nothing rejects
- `tools\discord\content.py`: where the channel copy lives, in case the question text changes alongside

## 181. The door's allow list stops refreshing somewhere past a hundred linked accounts, and one rate-limited lookup throws the whole list away

**Order:** 181 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 57

## Where it lives

VPS · site · tools\docs-app\server.js:1316-1329 (a sequential await loop), :522-551 (no 429 handling) · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:2434-2437, 2462 (a ten second timeout)

## What is known

Keep the membership in memory from the bot's gateway events rather than re-deriving it one account at a time on every refresh. The bot already has the members intent. Honour Discord's documented rate limit headers, and treat a partial failure as partial rather than discarding everything PART DONE 24 September, pull request #226. WHAT CHANGED: /api/allowed now sends a new field, failedProfiles: the profile numbers of every linked account whose Discord lookup failed. lookupFailed and lookupFailedWhy are unchanged. When the site names who failed and at least one profile came back, the gamemode door's refresh() writes the fresh answer for everybody else and gives each failed profile the standing it had in the old allowed.json: the same place in profiles, devProfiles and adminProfiles, and the same people row. So a failed lookup can no longer let anybody in or turn anybody away. The early return is still there. The door keeps its whole list when the site reached Discord for nobody, when the site is older than this change and does not name who failed, or when failedProfiles is empty. enforce is never touched. MEASURED: tools/test-allowed-failed.js takes the real /api/allowed route out of tools/docs-app/server.js and the real refresh() out of tools/gamemode.js. It runs the two together against made-up Discord answers and a made-up disk: five linked accounts, one of them rate limited, with a ban and a new tester arriving in the same refresh. On this branch: 39 passed, 0 failed. Against main's server.js and gamemode.js (HEAD c32b820, passed in through the SITE and GAMEMODE env vars): 21 passed, 18 failed, because the door writes nothing and the ban and the new tester both wait. I also ran both mixed pairs. With the new site and an old door the result is 25/14: the old door still sees lookupFailed true and keeps its whole list, which is what it did before, and it does not throw. With an old site and the new door the result is 21/18: there is no failedProfiles field, so the new door keeps its whole list, and the check 'a new door reading an old site keeps the whole list' passes. In both mixed runs every failure is the partial-write behaviour, which needs both halves deployed. The server.js changes are at the out object and the failed branch of the /api/allowed route (about lines 2440-2471). The gamemode.js changes are keepWhatFailed() (about 10743-10797), the early-return condition (about 10852) and the merge before the write (about 10889-10905). WHAT IS LEFT: These parts of entry 156 are not in this commit and are for Claude or Patrick. (1) discordGet (server.js, around line 649) still reads neither Retry-After nor x-ratelimit-reset-after. The triage plan is a module-level quiet-until time, set once per refresh and not a sleep for each account. (2) If the bulk /members?limit=1000 call is refused (Server Members intent off, a 403), memberOf falls back to one lookup per account. That brings back the burst and the risk of hitting the gamemode's 10 s timeout at around 100 accounts; the 100ms-per-call timing proof in doneWhen was not done here. (3) Keeping membership in the bot's gateway cache needs Patrick and Djinn to agree in #dev on which key the bot would POST with (entry 2's key rotation). (4) Patrick should read the live door and site logs from after #101 to see whether 'rate limited by Discord' still appears. Deploy order once merged: either half can go first, because both mixed pairs keep the old behaviour. Partial writes only start when both the site (Deploy-Docs.ps1) and the gamemode (Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1, then the live pair) are out.

The Papyrus VM is set only inside OnUpdate (main.cpp:76-86). CallNativeApi.cpp:77-79 throws "can't be called in this context" for any game call made without it. note() (thornswood-front.js:245-248) swallows that throw, so a note inside onStrike, which runs from the probe callback, would only have reached the log. Results: 35 passed with the fix, 15 failed on the code before it, and 16 failed on the obvious fix of calling note() inside onStrike, including the check that no game call is made from the probe. ## 192. Two of the three choices the launcher makes you agonise over do nothing in the game

**Order:** 192 · **Wave:** 4 Arriving in the world · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 50

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:760-761 (written), :772-773 (the only other reference, a log line) · VPS · site · data\site\classes.md:22-44 describes them as systems

## What is known

Either make them do something or say on the page that they are planned. A published systems page describes the system that runs. Somebody who spent ten minutes choosing between them and then finds no difference concludes the rest is the same MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Both choices now drive systems that run. The launcher's old state.half and state.gathering are migrated into the progression state (gamemode.js:16316-16324 and :17032-17054: the gathering maps to P.pickClass, and trade plus half map to P.pickProfession), and new characters choose in the K panel (3aa37ef). The half gates what can be made: canWork at gamemode.js:12403-12410, the bench gate at :9376-9404 and gateHalf at :17118-17123 (a2ba2ee, 21 Sep: "A profession decides what you can make"). The class gates the verbs: canDo at :12413-12416, and gate() at :17103-17109 with refusals such as "Only a miner can work a seam" at :17091-17097. classGate is called for mine (:1933, :2882), harvest (:5824), fish (:5876), loot (:5983, :6654) and farm (:13259, :13407, :13506) (8367a87, 077268f). classes.md (last changed 077268f, 21 Sep) describes this running system at :36-60 ("Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it"). applyLauncherChoice and the line numbers the entry cites no longer exist. node --check tools/gamemode.js passes. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: Most of the reviewer's case holds. c87da23 (20 Sep, on main) removed applyLauncherChoice, and the launcher no longer offers these choices: grepping tools/app/*.cs and tools/ui.xaml for half or gathering finds nothing. The class gate is real: classGate at gamemode.js:1330 is called for mine, harvest, fish, loot and farm, and it refuses anybody with no class (:17104). The half gate is real too: mp.onCraft at :9822 calls craftAnswer at :9453, and the fork's CraftService.cpp fires onCraft at recorded build c8832519. node --check passes. All of these commits come before launcher 1.1.90. Three parts of doneWhen or the entry's own requirement still fail. (1) The entry says "A published systems page describes the system that runs", and classes.md does not. The half only binds somebody who has chosen a profession. benchGate returns null when there is no profession (gamemode.js:9399: `if (!s.prof) { return null; }`). craftAnswer lets the craft through before any half or rank check (:9532), so somebody with no profession can make Master-rank work at any bench. That state lasts for good. The K panel has a "choose later" for class and profession (ts-ui/thornswood-skills.js:25-29, :1740-1742), and the server ends creation on the town alone (gamemode.js:17516: "The home is the one pick that ends creation. Class and profession may still be unset"). So never picking the half is strictly better for making things, and the half choice only takes options away. classes.md:22 says "What nobody gets is all of it", and :52 says "Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it". Neither mentions this. classes.md:7-9 and join.md:86 say "Take them in any order. The third one sends you to your inn", which is not what the code does. Entry 86 records the no-profession allowance as deliberate. No page says so, and no open entry covers it. (2) The literal code test in doneWhen fails. state.half occurs once in gamemode.js, in a comment at :16317, not more than three times. The half is now read as s.half, so this test is out of date rather than failed, but it is not met as written. (3) Deployment is second-hand. "The rendered page says so" and live status come only from To Do records (entries 85, 52, 160, 146). Nothing here measured them, because the VPS was not contacted. Deploy-Docs.ps1 notes that site pages can be edited on the site, so the live /classes page may not match the repo. The fix is to correct classes.md:7-9, :22 and :52, and join.md:86, to say that class and profession can be left for later and what that means at a bench. The alternative is to close the no-profession path in benchGate and craftAnswer. Either needs Patrick's decision. NEXT STEP: Close the entry. Nothing to build, and no page correction is needed: classes.md already describes what the server enforces. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: Read on origin/main at c13ada9. Most of the work is done. The launcher choice was replaced by class and profession picks in the K panel, the class gates the verbs, and the half gates the benches. node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js. Two parts of doneWhen are still not met. (1) The code test as written fails: state.half appears once in gamemode.js, in a comment at :16684. The count has fallen from three instead of rising above it, because the code now reads s.half. That part of the test is out of date more than failed. (2) The real gap is the entry's own requirement that the published page describes the system that runs, and it does not. benchGate returns null for anybody with no profession (gamemode.js:9468 `if (!s.prof) { return null; }`), and craftAnswer (:9522) makes the same allowance. The comment there calls it a first-evening allowance, but nothing ever makes the choice: creation ends on the home pick alone, and class and profession "may still be unset" (:17883-17885). So somebody who never picks a profession can make anything at any bench for good, and choosing a half only takes options away. classes.md:52-55 says "Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it". classes.md:22 says "What nobody gets is all of it". classes.md:8-9 says "Take them in any order. The third one sends you to your inn", but the home pick ends creation whether or not the other two are made. None of this is on the page. Fixing it means either correcting classes.md (and join.md:86, per the triage) or closing the no-profession path in benchGate and craftAnswer. That is Patrick's decision. The live /classes page was not measured. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: Entry 86 records the no-profession allowance at the bench as deliberate. It should either say that the allowance never ends, because creation finishes on the home pick alone, or be the place where that path gets closed. Right now no open entry covers the public pages being wrong about it.

## 193. The installer payload is publicly downloadable and redistributes about forty named third-party mods, including Bethesda's own assets

**Order:** 193 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Legal · **Effort:** change it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 8

## Where it lives

VPS · site · the payload answers 200 anonymously at 527 MB · tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:133-199 and the exclusion list that misses the Bethesda files · Your PC · Profile\OwnGame\files.txt

## What is known

The collection model is the right one and is already in place: people install the mods themselves from Nexus, under the mod authors' own terms. The payload undercuts it by shipping the same files. Take the third-party content out of the payload so it carries only what is yours, and put the download behind the same door as the rest TWO RELEASES BEHIND AS OF 1.1.70: Ship said so on 21 September. Thornswood-Setup.zip was built 20 September at 19:06 and the site is offering Thornswood-Setup-20260920-1902. Anybody installing from it sits through every release since on first launch. Nobody who already has the game is affected. Package-Thornswood.ps1 rebuilds it and takes about twenty minutes. AND IT IS WORSE THAN FORTY NAMED MODS, measured 22 September. Data\textures and Data\meshes in the game folder hold 565 files and 547.4 MB that Vortex has never deployed and does not know about: loose files dropped into the Steam copy's Data folder by hand. Vortex has 154 mod folders and none of them matches any of these names. So these are not on the list of forty, they are not on any list, and the installer hands them to everybody: LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary, LostArk, leifcrops, MCE, 0CCE, and the loose contents of textures\weapons, textures\interface, meshes\armor, meshes\actors and meshes\clothes. Also Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa, 2.8 MB at the Data root, loaded by no plugin in the list. The entry about what the new collection revision should carry has the full folder by folder breakdown with sizes. Whichever of these are somebody else's have to come out or be traced to a mod page and put in the collection; whichever are ours belong in the Thornswood Content mod, and then they leave the installer by themselves, because the packager already drops anything the collection provides. TRACED 22 SEPTEMBER, FOLDER BY FOLDER: the 565 loose files and 547 MB under Data\textures and Data\meshes that Vortex does not provide, read from Profile\OwnGame\files.txt, the file dates, and every archive in Vortex's downloads. CANNOT STAY, NOT OURS AND NOT A NEXUS MOD: textures and meshes\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary (155.0 and 11.7 MB) and textures and meshes\LostArk (64.7 and 43.3 MB), Lost Ark armour ports with HIMBO BodySlide builds, dropped 14 September 20:43 to 20:51, minutes before that day's Daedric Online collection downloads, in no archive and loaded by no plugin. textures\weapons\rpcustom (78.0 MB: apocalypse, balmung, dibella, hircine, zireael) and textures\weapons\saarthal (3.2 MB) with their meshes, dated 14 September 20:56 and referenced by nothing. textures\leifcrops (57.3 MB) and meshes\leifcrops, maple and tomato, dated 12 September 19:40, seven minutes before the other server collection download, not in KzlOnlineContent and referenced by nothing, so most likely that launcher's. ORPHANED BUILDS FOR MODS NO LONGER INSTALLED: meshes\MCE (29.8 MB, Mage Clothing Expansion and its 3BA patch) and meshes\0CCE (3.2 MB, Common Clothing Expansion and its 3BA patch). meshes\armor holds 54.6 MB of BodySlide output built on this machine: Common Clothes travel clothes (150 files, 43.5 MB), dragon priests matching Dragon Priests Retexture SE (24 files), and Immersive Armors' bosmer armour from one of the 13 slider sets still installed (18 files). meshes\clothes (2.9 MB) and the small dlc01, dlc02, creationclub, _byoh, surarmorcustommeshes, surwhiterunmeshes and pulcharmsolis folders are more of the same. BodySlide output is built for one person's body choice and has no place in anybody else's installer, whichever mod it is for. meshes\actors (17.8 MB) is Nemesis output from 11 September, which the build treats as ours and which wants regenerating, plus 17 FNIS Behavior SE first person files from a mod the collection does not carry, plus BodySlide body, beard and draugr builds. Three small strays: Armor_Replacer (Sentinel's resources), furniture\noble (Assorted Mesh Fixes) and architecture\riften (B. Noble Skyrim), none of them installed. OURS, 8 MB: textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds and meshes\interface\logo, made by Build-Backdrop and Go.ps1. They stay in the installer with the music and the video. MARKETPLACETEXTURES.BSA is Bethesda's, 2.8 MB, stamped the same as _ResourcePack.bsa, and missing from Package-Thornswood's list of Bethesda files, so it ships. NOT YET GONE THROUGH: the other not-from-Vortex files in Data\Scripts (rp_trapcactusscript, ski_*.pex, wbptlight*, dlc1vcmoondial*), Data\Interface (the RaceMenu swfs and map.swf), music\special\mus_maintheme.xwm, MCM\Settings, SKSE\Plugins\TrueHUD\RP_Bosses.ini, and the hashed UI assets and the Fonts, Images and Modules folders under Data\Platform. THE ORDER THIS PUTS ON THE RELEASE: the twelve whole folders come out of the Steam copy before Maintenance and before the next Package-Thornswood, and that step is in entry 46. What stays here is the rule side: keeping BodySlide output and other people's leftovers out of the installer by the Vortex record rather than by hand. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #227. WHAT CHANGED: Steps 1 and 2 of the triage plan are done. Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa is Bethesda's, and it is now left out of packs and the installer through a new $ShipBethesdaLeftAlone list in tools\Ship-Rules.ps1. Test-ShipMachine asks that list, so the file is never shipped and never listed as removed. It deliberately does not go in a vanilla list, because a vanilla rule would have put it in the next pack's delete.txt. Package-Thornswood.ps1 now prints a report after its filter loop. The report names, one folder at a time with sizes, the loose textures and meshes the installer is about to carry that are neither the collection's nor ours. Ours is the three menu backdrop files Go.ps1 writes. The report does not stop anything. MEASURED: MarketplaceTextures.bsa is 2,938,167 bytes. Its header lists 121 files in 5 folders, all under interface\marketplace (buttons for pc and xbox, and stars). It is dated 2026-09-10 11:08:10, five seconds after _ResourcePack.bsa (11:08:05). files.txt has it as L|O at line 561 (linked from the Steam copy, not Vortex), and _DowngraderBackups holds a 3,224,203 byte copy. Both pack baselines, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json and published-dev.json (943 keys each), list Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa, and that is why it cannot be a vanilla rule: Publish-Update.ps1:587-592 lists as removed anything that is not in the scan unless Test-Machine claims it. Run over the non-V lines of C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt, the new report names 24 folders, 563 files, 539.4 MB. The largest: textures\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary 155.0 MB, textures\weapons 81.2, textures\LostArk 64.7, textures\leifcrops 57.3, meshes\armor 54.6 (194 files), meshes\LostArk 43.3, meshes\MCE 29.8, meshes\actors 17.8 (128 files), meshes\LoA 11.7, meshes\0CCE 3.2. The 22 Sep total of 547.4 MB included our 8 MB backdrop, which is now excluded. The pack baselines list the same folders (meshes\armor 194, actors 128, LoA 30+25, LostArk 26+19, MCE 18, leifcrops 9+2), so packs have carried them too. The lifted report block ran cleanly under Set-StrictMode Latest in PowerShell 5.1 and 7, for 0, 1 and 24 folders. Against HEAD's scripts, test-ship-rules.ps1 fails 4 checks and then crashes on the missing Get-ShipLooseArt. With the change it passes 33 of 33. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, from the entry and the triage, none of it done here: (1) Delete the stray loose folders from the Steam copy and run Maintenance (the entry that owns that step). The report will then shrink to nothing. Warning: the pack baselines list those same 565-odd files, so the first pack after they are deleted lists them all as removed and hits Publish-Update's MaxRemovals guard. It needs -AcceptRemovals, and that is only right if taking them off every tester is what he wants. (2) Decide whether BodySlide output and the Nemesis output in meshes\actors (plus Data\meshes\animationdatasinglefile.txt and animationsetdatasinglefile.txt) ship at all. After that decision, the report can become a refusal with an allowlist in Ship-Rules and an -AcceptLoose switch. The refusal is left out on purpose because it would block every installer build today. (3) Decide how the download gets a door when the installer cannot sign in (server.js says /api/payload must stay public). A short-lived signed URL is one way, and the patrick/todo-189-download-is-the-door branch may cover it. (4) Rebuild with Package-Thornswood.ps1 and republish the installer. That goes to the live site. For the merger: entry 169 (patrick/todo-169-exclusion-lists) is folding the vanilla lists into Ship-Rules. $ShipBethesdaLeftAlone should stay a never-removed list, or be folded into 169's never-removed category. It must not go in its vanilla list. Not gone through, from the entry: Data\Scripts, Data\Interface, music, MCM, SKSE, and the Platform assets outside textures and meshes.

## Read first

- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:317-327`: the filter loop that decides what the installer carries: it calls Test-Vanilla, Test-Runtime, Test-ShipMachine, Test-Optional and Test-FromCollection, and never once calls Test-ShipOtherServer
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:119-162`: Test-ShipOtherServer, which already excludes Data\(Meshes|Textures)\(OtherServer|kzlcustommeshs) at :133-135 and Data\NirnLabUIPlatform at :141, so the rules exist and the installer simply never asks them
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:130-215`: the whole decision about what ships in order: Bethesda files at :133-138, foreign frameworks at :155, root files at :163, root dirs at :180, Test-Vanilla at :188 and the dot-source of Ship-Rules at :215
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:258-306`: the Vortex record branch and the Die at :273, which guards only the own-game-folder path at :271 while the Steam and Vortex branch at :281 carries on and prints "no Vortex record found, so this installer carries every mod file." at :302-305

An anonymous request to the download route no longer returns 200 with the zip.

## Traps

Do not add a deny list of mod names to Package-Thornswood: its own comment at :258-262 says the Vortex record, not a guess at which folders count as mods, is what decides, and a hand list will drift. The Die that refuses to ship an empty collection record guards only the own-game-folder branch at :271; the Steam and Vortex branch at :281 prints a warning and carries on, and CLAUDE.md says the Steam shape is what ships today. Data\Platform is skyrim-platform, which is GPLv3 and is entry 58, so those go out together or the notices file is wrong twice.

## What is known

One list, in Ship-Rules, read by both. Two lists that must agree will not, and this is the second time they have drifted. It is also the mechanism behind entry 56, so fixing it is how the redistribution stays fixed READ 23 September and NOT MERGED, because this entry's own trap says the NirnLabUIPlatform contradiction becomes load bearing the moment the lists merge and must be raised rather than resolved quietly. THE DRIFT IS REAL AND STILL THERE: Publish-Update.ps1 carries its own $vanillaDataFiles, $vanillaDataPatterns, $vanillaDataDirs, $vanillaRootFiles and $vanillaRootDirs, and Package-Thornswood.ps1 carries its own copies of the first four PLUS a $foreignDataDirs the publisher has no equivalent of at all: NirnLabUIPlatform, Nemesis_Engine, FNIS, CalienteTools, tools, Source, ModderResource, FOMod, Docs, readmes and ShaderCache. That is the ninety files. THE CONTRADICTION, IN THREE PLACES. Ship-Rules Test-ShipOtherServer says Data\NirnLabUIPlatform and NirnLabUIPlugin.dll are another server's and keeps them out of packs. Package-Thornswood keeps the folder out of the installer. Checks.cs says the opposite in its own words: "NirnLabUIPlugin.dll WAS on this list and must never go back on it. It is not another server's file. It is the browser backend this build runs on", and records that listing it made every press of Fix delete the plugin that draws the whole in-game interface. AND THERE IS A MEASUREMENT THAT BEARS ON IT: this machine's own plugin log from the 10:19 session opens with "browser backend: tilted". So the backend actually in use on this build is Tilted, not NirnLab, which is consistent with the packs and the installer having excluded it all along and with nobody noticing. That is the thing to settle in #dev before one list becomes two lists agreeing: either the file is ours and all three places should say so, or it is not and Checks.cs's note is out of date. ## 199. (done) DONE: The installer's download picks up where it stopped instead of starting over

**Order:** 199 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** replace it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 54

VPS · site · tools\docs-app\server.js:1142-1155 (a Range request was confirmed live to return 200 with the full length and no Accept-Ranges); public\home.html:870-874 promises resume

## What is known

Put it where the packs already are, or let Caddy's file server handle it, which does Range, ETag and conditional requests for free. Publish the SHA-256 beside the link. The right answer is already in this repo and applied to the packs; the installer is the one thing that missed it DONE 24 September, pull request #247, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: The site's /file/ route, which serves the installer payload, now handles byte ranges. Before, it answered every Range request with 200 and the whole file, so Bootstrap.cs threw its partial download away and started again from zero. The static route already had correct Range handling from the video fix. That logic is now one function, rangeReply() in tools/docs-app/server.js, and both routes call it. /file/ now sends Accept-Ranges on the 200 and on a HEAD. It answers a range with 206 and the exact Content-Range, a range past the end with 416 and bytes */size, and it keeps the attachment name on a 206. It also sends an ETag and a Last-Modified and checks If-Range against them, so a one-file installer downloaded in a browser can resume too, and never onto a different build. I took the node route rather than moving the file behind Caddy's file_server, so what serves the site does not change. MEASURED: New harness tools/test-file-range.js takes the real /file/ and static route code out of server.js, serves it from a node http server on 127.0.0.1 and sends it real requests: 47 passed, 0 failed. Against the pre-change server.js (git show HEAD) the same harness gives 22 passed, 25 failed, exit 1. The key check joins the first 123,457 bytes to the 206 for bytes=123457- and compares every byte with the original file. A scratch copy of the site (THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL=1, loopback port 39174, a 2,097,275-byte test payload) gave these answers. HEAD: 200 with accept-ranges: bytes, content-length 2097275, an etag and a last-modified. Range bytes=0-1023: 206, content-range bytes 0-1023/2097275, content-length 1024, content-disposition kept. bytes=1000000-: 206, content-range bytes 1000000-2097274/2097275. bytes=9999999-: 416, content-range bytes */2097275. curl -C - resumed a 700,000-byte partial and gave a file whose SHA-256 matches the original (4f6adfd6...). banner.mp4 with bytes=0-99 still returns 206 video/mp4. Code: rangeReply at server.js:577-636, static route call at server.js:2009, /file/ route at server.js:2059-2076. That takes a HEAD on the payload url showing Accept-Ranges: bytes, and curl -r 0-1023 returning 206 with Content-Range bytes 0-1023/<total>. Caddy's "encode gzip" does not compress application/octet-stream by default, but only the live answer proves the 206 gets through unchanged. The SHA-256 beside the download link is entry 173 and is deliberately not in this change. Whoever updates the To Do List should note on entry 174 that the node route was taken and the Caddy file_server move was not, so the #dev step about Caddy is moot. ## 203. The main menu draws the backdrop twice, and the picture it draws is 8.5 times too small, has no mipmaps, and is built to a plane shape the mesh disagrees with

**Order:** 203 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Trust · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** new

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo.nif and logo01ae.nif are byte identical, md5 5c3cf588, both named CivilWarMap01, both pointing at the same texture · Game\Data\textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds, 4096x4096 DXT1, 8,388,736 bytes, one mip level · source art tools\art\thornswood-art-1536.png at 1536 x 1024 · tools\Build-Backdrop.py defaults to the Steam copy, not C:\Thornswood\Game · brief tools\art\ART-PROMPT.md, measured spec tools\art\BACKDROP-SPEC.md

## What is known

Two defects, and the cheap one ships first. PART ONE, THE DOUBLE, CONFIRMED by Patrick on 17 September. Both logo meshes are byte identical copies of one replacer plane named CivilWarMap01, and both reference MAINMENUWALLPAPER.dds. Skyrim carries both names because the Anniversary Edition menu draws a second plate under the first, so whoever made this replacer overwrote both and the menu now draws the backdrop twice. The fix is one float: in logo01ae.nif the root BSFadeNode scale sits at offset 0x163 and reads 0.8; set it to 0.0 and the mesh collapses to a point and draws nothing. Four bytes, same file length, still parses, all five blocks intact, verified on a copy. Do not simply delete logo01ae.nif, because the game then falls back to the vanilla Anniversary Edition plate inside Skyrim - Meshes1.bsa and you get a Bethesda logo over the backdrop instead. Note also that neither mesh is in this repo and neither is in any of the 157 Vortex staging folders; they were dropped into the Steam Data folder by hand, six copies exist on disk, and nothing restores them if they go. Bring both into the repo in the same change. PART TWO, THE PICTURE. Ask the artist for 4466 x 3016 PNG, 8 bit RGB, sRGB, no alpha. The floor below which the build enlarges is 4450 x 3005. What is in the repo is 1536 x 1024, which is 2.897 times too narrow, 2.935 times too short and 8.5 times too few pixels. THE PLANE IS NOT 3:2: parsed from the mesh, the drawn aspect is 1.4807558229, so even a perfect 3:2 source is 1.283 percent wrong before anything is resampled. The nearest clean ratio is 77:52. The safe rectangle on a 4466 x 3016 source is left 107, top 622, right 4359, bottom 2394 for everything up to 21:9, and top 910, bottom 2106 if 32:9 counts. The brief's middle 80 percent of the width was needlessly tight; the true figure is 95.2381 percent. The texture should be BC7_UNORM with 13 mip levels at 22,369,796 bytes, picture in rows 0 to 3004 with the last row repeated rather than black, because black padding bleeds up into the picture at every mip level. DXT1 with a full chain is 11,184,952 bytes and is the cheap option. Exact header values are in BACKDROP-SPEC.md. STILL OPEN: the 105 percent of screen width figure that every safe-zone number scales from appears once in the repo, in a docstring, recorded as eyeballed. One dev build with a ruler in the picture settles it. Also open: whether to re-fit the mesh to a true 3:2 rather than matching the script to the mesh, which is a Patrick and Djinn call in #dev. IN FLIGHT 17 September: pull request 64 carries the measured spec and the corrected artist brief. It is open, green, and blocked only on the review. It is the correction half only. The artwork itself, the mesh fix for the double, and the Build-Backdrop.py changes are all still to do. MERGED 19 September: pull request 67 (d3f855e) adds tools/art/thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png, the overlook with the wordmark, measured at 1535 x 1024. That is one pixel narrower than the 1536 x 1024 this entry measures as 8.5 times too few pixels against the 4466 x 3016 the spec asks for, so the resolution half is still open. The pull request changed no mesh and not Build-Backdrop.py, so the double draw and the build changes are still open too. THE BANNER IS ON THE SITE, 20 September, commits f90ce3e then c60c5d0, and that is one of the three places asked for. The hero was ridge.svg, a generated ridgeline, and is now the ANIMATED banner: the same tools/launcher-header.mp4 the launcher plays in its title band, 1.0 MB, 24 seconds, H.264 with no audio, served as banner.mp4. The first attempt used the still PNG and that was the wrong asset, corrected within the hour. muted and playsinline because autoplay is only allowed without sound and iOS opens it fullscreen otherwise; the still is the poster, so it is both the first paint and what anybody who asked for less motion sees instead. Deploy-Docs lists the public folder rather than keeping names, so both files go out unnamed. NEITHER IN-GAME SLOT CAN PLAY IT, which is worth saying before somebody sees it and thinks it failed. Skyrim's main menu is a DDS texture, Data\textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds, and its loading screens are NIF meshes with their own textures. Both take a frame, never the animation. AND THE GAME SIDE IS MAPPED, NOT BUILT. The backdrop is built from tools/art/thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png by tools/Build-Backdrop.py, and commit d3f855e added the source picture and nothing else, so the built texture only ever existed on the machine that built it. That is exactly why Djinn is the only person who has seen it. Three things stand in the way: Build-Backdrop.py needs Pillow, which is not installed on Patrick's machine; Go.ps1 copies ts-ui and ts-plugins into the game folder and has no path for art at all; and the folder is rebuilt by OwnGame from what Vortex deployed with a sweep at the end, so a file of ours has to be shown to survive that sweep before any of this is worth building. Both were true and both were mine. FIRST, the site served banner.mp4 as text/plain: the TYPES map in tools/docs-app/server.js had no .mp4 and no .jpg, so both fell through to the default, and with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every answer a browser is not allowed to guess past that. The file arrived whole, status 200, correct bytes, and was refused. Nothing errored anywhere, which is what made it look like the wrong file had been published. The VIDEO was right from c60c5d0 and still is, same md5 as tools/launcher-header.mp4. It was the POSTER that stayed wrong until f98bfb4. The range handling was checked by lifting the branch out of server.js and driving it with a fake request, 18 assertions, including that bytes=-100 is the last hundred and not the first. NOT DEPLOYED YET: both commits sit on main on Patrick's machine. server.js changed, so this needs the full Deploy-Docs.ps1 with no switch, not the -Site form. Until that runs the live site is still serving the video as text. COVERED AT THE MENU, 20 September, commit 7515bcf: the character choice page now draws the site's banner behind its panel, the still at once and the loop over it if the browser decodes H.264 (unknown; the page says which in the front log as 'painting: ...'). So while the choice is up the doubled, soft menu backdrop is not visible. The meshes and the texture are untouched and this entry stands for the game's own menu before and after the page. Measured first: every game folder on this machine (Thornswood, DevBuild, the Steam copy) had both meshes at md5 5c3cf588 with root scale 0.8 and the texture at md5 dbb15e20, 4096x4096 DXT1, one mip level. PART TWO: Build-Backdrop.py rewritten to the spec (77:52, 3005 rows, last row repeated, thirteen DXT1 mips, writes into the repo) and run on thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png, the new painting: 11,184,952 bytes, 13 levels. It is a 2.7x enlargement and will read soft; the artist's 4466 x 3016 render is the only thing that makes it sharp and is the one item still open here. ## What is known

THE SHARE IMAGE WAS A PATH: og:image read /presence.png and nothing that unfurls a link resolves a relative one, so every link pasted anywhere came out as a grey box. og.png is absolute now, 1200x630, 174 KB, built from presence.png by putting the square logo on the site's own background rather than stretching it, with width and height declared beside it and twitter:image matching. presence.png is untouched, because it is the Discord rich presence art and that is square. THE FAVICON was 255,344 bytes, one 256x256 frame every browser downscales anyway; it is 16, 32 and 48 in one file at 10,723 bytes. AND NOTHING WAS CACHED: send() puts no-store on everything, which is right for a page holding somebody's data and wrong for a picture, and it also stops a browser answering with a 304, so every reload re-downloaded all of public/. Assets answer public, max-age=3600 with an ETag of size and modified time. MEASURED ON THE LIVE SITE after deploying: og.png answers 200 with that header and an ETag, a second ask carrying the ETag answers 304 with 0 bytes, the home page still answers no-store, and the og:image tag reads https://thornswood.net/og.png.

## Where it lives

VPS · site · tools\docs-app\server.js:1017-1038, :1034 and :1063 (the list is trimmed to a fixed 2000); no limiter anywhere in the file

## What is known

A per-address limit, a honeypot field or a captcha, keep the last few per sender rather than trimming one global list, and post new reports to a staff channel through the bot so they are read the day they arrive. The page promises somebody will read it. Being able to report a person at all is entry 39 DONE 24 September, pull request #264, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: Merged main into the branch and fixed the blocker the reviewer found. Main had not done this work; the branch's change still holds on top of it. What the branch does: - /api/report takes 5 reports an hour and 20 a day from one sender. Past that it answers 429 with Retry-After and a sentence, never a quiet drop. - The sender is the socket address, or the last X-Forwarded-For hop when the socket is loopback (Caddy). An IPv6 sender counts as its /64. The table holds only a salted hash. - Tickets and public reports are trimmed separately (2000 each), so neither can push the other out of inbox.json. - home.html has a hidden honeypot field. A post with it filled in gets a 200 and nothing is kept. - bot.py's watch_reports posts each new public report in the staff channel. The merge (1d04649) is against a pinned main at aec1cfd (#251). The one conflict was the list at the top of tools/discord/bot.py: the branch added a "Reports" line and main added "Holds" (#202). Both are kept. watch_reports still starts from on_ready beside main's ensure_hold_panel. server.js and home.html merged cleanly, and main's #241 change to the Discord check does not touch the report code. The fix (55e6e5d) is for the blocker. The limit was checked before `await body(req, 20000)` and counted only after the write. So posts sent at the same moment from one address, with their bodies held back, all got past the check. It now runs reportRefusal a second time after the body is parsed and the title checked, with the same 429 and Retry-After. jsonFile, putJson and reportTaken are all synchronous, so no other request can run between that second check and the count. The early check stays, so a sender already past the limit is turned away before the site reads 20 KB from them. tools/test-report-limits.js gains the check the reviewer said was missing. It opens 30 connections from one address over plain sockets, sends every set of headers, waits 400 ms, then sends every body. MEASURED: Race probe (30 connections from 203.0.113.60 through loopback, headers first, bodies held back and sent together): - Branch before the fix, run from a scratch copy: 30 taken, 0 refused. 62 of 64 checks pass; the two new checks fail. - After the fix: 5 taken, 25 refused, 5 rows written. 64 of 64 pass. Still true after the merge and fix, in the same harness: - Ten posts one after another from one address: 200 200 200 200 200 429 429 429 429 429, with Retry-After over 3000 seconds and a sentence. - Three tickets survive a flood of 1990 rows plus 50 more reports; public rows are held to 2000. - A made-up first X-Forwarded-For hop is still refused. - The honeypot post gets 200 and nothing is written. tools/discord/test-reports.py: 34 passed on the merged bot.py. STILL TO DO BY A PERSON: For Patrick after merge (not run here; both reach the VPS): - .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 for server.js and public/home.html. - .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly for bot.py. Carried over from the author, for the To Do List (I did not edit the list): - PUT /api/inbox writes back the whole list the hub loaded. A report or ticket that arrives while a staff member has /inbox open is erased on their next inbox click. This race was there before this branch. - noteSignIn still takes the first X-Forwarded-For hop, which is only safe while Caddy replaces the header rather than appending to it. - There is no captcha. The honeypot only stops scripts that fill in the rendered form; the rate limit covers direct JSON posts. Decision for Patrick to confirm: the entry asked to keep the last few reports per sender in the file. The branch caps per sender in memory instead (5 an hour, 20 a day) and splits the file by kind. Keeping a per-sender cap in inbox.json would mean writing a sender identifier into every row, and privacy.md says the sign-in log is the only thing holding an address. Because the table is in memory, a site restart clears it.
