## 230. The update feed only ever grows, and every launcher downloads all of it on every check

**Order:** 230 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 59

## Where it lives

GitHub · version.json, 59,496 bytes, 192 pack entries · Your PC · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:898 (appended, never pruned) · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:141-160

## What is known

A feed describes the current state, not the archive: a few hundred bytes naming the latest version and what is needed to reach it, served with an ETag. History belongs in release notes. The manifest-per-release entry further down does this properly; this is the interim MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The live feed is now 111,122 bytes with 227 packs, not the 84,588 bytes and 192 packs in the entry. It also carries 40 news items (19,621 bytes) and 32,019 bytes of pack notes. Updater.cs:152-209 Check() fetches api.github.com/repos/<repo>/contents/version.json with Accept vnd.github.raw (:53), and there is no If-None-Match anywhere (grep). Measured with curl: the contents API returns an ETag with Cache-Control public, max-age=60, and a repeat with If-None-Match got 304 Not Modified. But X-RateLimit-Remaining went from 55 to 54 on that 304. Customer launchers have no token (Updater.cs:57-67, and this machine's config.json UpdateToken is empty), so for them a conditional request saves the 111 KB and does not save the rate limit. The rate limit is the bigger problem. Shell.cs:1430-1447 runs CheckUpdatesInPlay every 15 ticks of 2 s, so every 30 seconds while the game runs. That is 120 API calls an hour against GitHub's 60 an hour for an unauthenticated address. Failures are swallowed there (Shell.cs:4518 catch {}), so after about half an hour of play the in-play update countdown stops seeing releases without saying so, and the next launcher start from that address gets the 403 message. raw.githubusercontent.com serves the same file with its own ETag and max-age=300 and has no API rate limit. The prune in entry 198 alone halves the document. NEXT STEP: Now: (1) Updater.cs Check(): keep the last ETag and body in Profile, send If-None-Match, and on 304 parse the cached body. C# 5, compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root temp. (2) Once Patrick picks the in-play fix, apply it in Shell.cs:1447 and CheckUpdatesInPlay. ## 233. (done) DONE: a release that did not push is not recorded as published, and the next run finishes it

**Order:** 233 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 28

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:1170-1221

## What is known

Record state after the last step succeeds, or mark the release failed and retry it whole. Publishing tools are idempotent: running again finishes what did not finish  FIXED 23 September, pull request 174. Publish-Update saved the baseline whatever happened to the push. The failure was reported honestly on screen, in red, and the baseline moved anyway, so the next Ship compared the build against a baseline that already included the release, found nothing changed and stopped with "Nothing to do": assets on GitHub, version.json not, no launcher able to see it, and the one command that would have fixed it refusing to run. The baseline moves only when the push succeeded now. A failure writes a note beside it with the id, the time and what went wrong, and the next run reads that and FINISHES THAT RELEASE. Reusing the id is the point: gh release upload --clobber puts anything missing into the release that already exists, and a new id would orphan a set of assets and add a release nobody can install. The note lives beside the baseline under LOCALAPPDATA, where neither an uninstall nor a rebuild reaches it, and the dev channel has its own. tools\test-publish-resume.ps1 takes the four helpers out by their markers and drives them: 17 checks, including that an unreadable note reads as no note rather than stopping a release, that a byte order mark is stepped over, that main and dev never see each other’s, and that clearing twice is not an error.

## Read first

- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:1171-1221`: the whole finding in fifty lines: $pushFailed is set at :1199 or :1209, Save-State at :1214 runs outside any conditional, and the honest red message follows at :1217-1221
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:422-425`: Save-State itself, and $StateFile at :178, so you know what a failed state would have to record
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:709-716`: the create then upload --clobber fallback, which is what already makes a retry of the same id safe
- `tools\Ship.ps1:500-600`: the caller, so you can see what Ship would have to read to resume rather than start again

## 236. Every launcher spends half the GitHub hourly quota checking for updates, and two people on one connection spend all of it

**Order:** 236 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 31

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Shell.cs:1198-1210 (a two second timer, checking every two minutes) calling tools\app\Updater.cs:141-205 (the Contents API, sixty an hour per address)

## What is known

Serve the feed from the site or a CDN rather than an API with a quota, check on the order of every fifteen to thirty minutes with a cached ETag, and take downloads through the browser download url, which is already an allowed host and has no limit. Two people in one house currently exhaust the budget between them. Entry 89 shrinks what each check downloads; this row is about how often and from where MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: It is worse than the entry says. Shell.cs:1447 now checks every 15 two-second ticks (every 30 s). Commit 0d5c5e9 on 20 Sep changed that from 60 ticks. That is 120 Contents API calls an hour per launcher in play, against GitHub's 60 an hour per unauthenticated address, so one person alone runs out after about 30 minutes. Updater.cs:163 still asks api.github.com contents/version.json. The start-up check (Shell.cs:4286) and ClientRuntime.cs:253 call Updater.Check too. GitHub's REST best-practices page says a 304 is free only when the request carries an Authorization header, and launchers send none, so an ETag alone saves nothing. The entry's trap is wrong about downloads: Publish-Update.ps1:999 writes https://api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/<id>, and version.json's launcherUrl, all 227 packs and clientRuntime point there, so every download spends the same quota. Shell.cs:4518 'catch { }' swallows a failed in-play check without logging it, so launcher.log (0 matches for 'too many update checks') cannot show whether it happened. AllowedHosts (Updater.cs:386-392) already holds github.com, objects/release-assets.githubusercontent.com and thornswood.net. WebClient follows redirects, and the sha256 check in Download (:425-446) covers integrity. NEXT STEP: Can be done now: (a) Publish-Update.ps1:999 writes each asset's browser_download_url for new releases. Those hosts are already allowed, so downloads stop spending the quota. Old packs keep their old urls. (b) Log a failed in-play check once per session (Shell.cs:4518), so a rate limit shows in launcher.log. Compile under a scratch root. Leave the 30 s interval alone, because the countdown depends on it. Left for Patrick: where the feed lives. The options are the site (scp'd by Ship the way Publish-News already does), raw.githubusercontent (its roughly 5-minute CDN cache breaks the 30 s countdown), or a flag the game server already publishes on its resource port. Moving the feed off GitHub moves the trust anchor for launcherSha256 onto the VPS while signing is off, so that is a security decision. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick chooses the feed host (site, CDN, or the game server's resource port) and accepts the trust change while code signing is off. Until then only the download urls and the logging can move.

## Done when

The launcher compiles and the GitHub build check is green, and after a session C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log shows the update check going to the new host with nothing against api.github.com, while the five minute warning and the game close still happen inside the server's announced window.

## Traps

Raising the interval is not one digit and it defeats the countdown. Shell.cs:4169-4175 is a written comment about this exact failure class, where a check that did not come back wiped the five minute clock every two minutes. At 450 ticks somebody is not told for up to fifteen minutes and the game does not close for up to thirty, long after the server has already put them back. The download path is separate and already fine: assets go through browser_download_url, which has no quota. A 304 still counts against the REST quota, which is the other reason to move off it.

## 239. (done) DONE: there was no way to plainly restart a service, so the only option was raw ssh

**Order:** 239 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** build it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Old number:** new

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Restart-Server.ps1, new on 18 September · it covers game, dev, docs, voice and bot · tools\Deploy-Server.ps1 redeploys the binary and tools\Request-Restart.ps1 only warns people, so neither was the right tool

## What is known

BUILT AND USED 18 September, commit 4103183. Until today nothing in the repo simply stopped a service and started it again. Deploy-Server redeploys the binary and Request-Restart warns people without restarting anything, so a plain bounce meant hand writing an ssh command. That is not a theoretical gap: the live server sat for ten hours on 18 September with no private folder, the fix was one restart, and there was nothing to run. It reads online.json first and refuses while anybody is connected unless you pass -Now, because a restart reads from a chair as the world freezing and then carrying on. It sends its remote command base64 encoded rather than in nested quotes, which is the trap that made a hash come back and then get run as a command on 17 September. It was used to bring the live server back and the door immediately refreshed 30 profiles from the site. Nothing is left on this one.

## Read first

- `tools\Restart-Server.ps1`: the script, and the reasoning for the online check in its own header
- `tools\Deploy-Server.ps1:142-170`: the warning and countdown logic this deliberately does not repeat

## 241. (done) DONE: Caddy is watched, over the public name, and its task has no time limit

**Order:** 241 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 21

VPS · tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:142-150; tools\Watch-Services.ps1:109-114 (Caddy is not in the watched list); tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:266-272

## What is known

The TLS terminator is the thing the public actually touches, so it is the first thing the health check looks at, and its liveness check is an HTTPS GET of the real hostname rather than a loopback port behind it. Make it a real service rather than a task with an execution time limit  DONE 23 September in two halves, pull requests 176 and 177, and the watcher is installed on the box. THE TIME LIMIT was already gone: the live Thornswood Web task reports ExecutionTimeLimit PT0S, restartCount 10 and two triggers, and Setup-Domain.ps1 and Deploy-Docs.ps1 both set Zero, so the three day default that almost certainly ended Caddy on 21 September cannot come back on a rebuilt box. THE WATCHING is this entry’s own point and it was still missing: Watch-Services checked the website on 3001, which is NODE, behind Caddy. Its own header said so. That is exactly the 21 September failure, where node answered 3001 all night while nobody outside could reach anything. Caddy is a check now, first in the list, asked with an HTTPS request to https://thornswood.net over the real certificate, because a loopback port cannot see this failure. Any HTTP answer counts, a 502 included, since a 502 is Caddy up with something behind it down and the next line says which. When it is down the watcher starts Thornswood Web and gives it 45 seconds rather than 25, because the first start after a gap waits on a certificate. AND ASKING THE BOX FOUND A SECOND THING: the installed watcher had six checks and this file had four. vps-dev-instance.ps1 appends dev game and dev voice to the installed copy in place, so -Install from the repo would have written the shorter list over the longer one and taken the dev pair off the watchdog with nothing said. The log shows what that costs: seven dev game restarts since 18 September and one dev voice. Both are in the file now. The box reports caddy, website, game, voice, bot, dev game and dev voice all up.

## Traps

Changing task settings in these scripts only reaches a task that does not exist yet: Setup-Domain.ps1:142 and Deploy-Docs.ps1:266 both skip registration when the task is already there, and Deploy-Docs's else branch calls Set-ScheduledTask with -Action only. So the fix does nothing on the live box until the task is unregistered and re-registered, which is a person's job and a brief outage of the thing the public touches. Restarting Caddy asks Let's Encrypt for a certificate on first start, and Let's Encrypt rate limits repeated issuance, so do not loop on restarts while testing.

## 243. Nothing outside the project is watched at all

**Order:** 243 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 144

## Where it lives

VPS · tools\Watch-Services.ps1 checks only local ports · GitHub · the workflow has no schedule, so nothing ever runs unprompted

## What is known

A nightly job that walks the first-run path: fetch the feed, resolve every asset URL, resolve the pinned depot manifests, check the store's current build, and go red when one of them moves. For a project this size that is one scheduled workflow, and it is how entry 86 would have been caught the day it happened PART DONE 24 September, pull request #232. WHAT CHANGED: This adds part (1) only: tools/Check-Outside.ps1, a read-only check that makes anonymous GET requests along the path a first install takes through services this project does not run. It reads the feed the same way Updater.Check does. It checks every pack, the launcher and the client runtime against the launcher's own rules: https, a host on AllowedHosts (read out of Updater.cs), and a checksum. Each asset is also checked against its repository's public release listing, which costs one listing per repository, not one request per pack. It downloads the first byte of the launcher, the client runtime and the newest pack. It compares Steam's public build (from api.steamcmd.net) with a new tools/steam-build.json and reports on the Nexus collection page. It never sends a token. It never requests thornswood.net or the game server, and it prints only the host of GitHub's signed redirect address. The depot manifest pins cannot be checked without an account that owns the game, so they are listed as unchecked. A new harness, tools/test-check-outside.ps1, runs the real logic against a table of fake answers and never uses the network. MEASURED: Live run on 24 Sep, anonymous, from this machine, in both pwsh 7.6.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Each run used 7 GitHub API calls: 58 left before, 51 after. Exit 1, for one reason: 164 of the 227 packs point at EvilPatrick06/Thornswood, whose release listing gives a stranger 404 (packs 20260910-2345 to 20260914-1917). All the other 63 packs, the launcher (asset 585078234, 302 to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, 3,292,160 bytes) and the client runtime (583111894, 6,538,349 bytes, which matches the feed) are listed in Thornswood-Releases, across 156 releases on two pages. The newest pack, 20260923-2137, downloads (90,471 bytes). Steam's public build is 24914197 (Steam changed it on 27 Aug 2026), now recorded in tools/steam-build.json. Nexus answered 403, so that is reported as unchecked. With -FeedUrl pointed at a file that does not exist on raw.githubusercontent.com the result was 404 and exit 1. Steam and Nexus were still asked. Two dead ends I tried along the way: the Nexus GraphQL endpoint answers GET with 404, and a GET of Steam's app info shows only the public branch. Harness: tools/test-check-outside.ps1, 60 passed and 0 failed in both shells. It fails without the script (0 passed, 1 failed). It also fails on each of three planted mutations: the server guard in Ask removed (2 failed), the signed address printed (1 failed), and the listing's second page dropped (14 failed). Found while building it: @() over a System.Collections.Generic.List[object] throws "Argument types do not match" in both PS 5.1 and 7, so the script enumerates through the pipeline instead (Check-Outside.ps1:267-269). WHAT IS LEFT: Parts (2) and (3), for Patrick. (2) The scheduled workflow .github/workflows/watch-outside.yml: cron plus workflow_dispatch, one windows-latest pwsh step that runs tools\Check-Outside.ps1, actions/checkout pinned to a full SHA, and no token. Before it can be written, Patrick has to decide three things. (a) The check is red on day one because of the 164 private-repo packs (entry 198). Should the nightly job wait for 198, or report those packs as a known list without failing on them? The script fails on them today, on purpose. (b) Is it acceptable to depend on api.steamcmd.net, a third party? The script already treats it as unchecked when it does not answer. (c) Should a Nexus API key be created and stored as a repository secret? Without one, the collection's revision cannot be checked, because Nexus answers a bare GET with 403 and its GraphQL endpoint answers GET with 404. Once merged, the schedule only starts from main, and GitHub turns scheduled workflows off after 60 days with no activity. (3) The doneWhen line "exits 0 today" cannot hold until entry 198 moves or rewrites those packs. The To Do List entry should be updated to say part (1) is done on this branch, with these measurements. Whenever Steam's public build moves, a person tries the downgrade on one machine and then writes the new build into tools\steam-build.json. The script says so when it goes red.

## 244. Nothing tells anyone when the bot is down, and the panel is the first thing a stranger touches

**Order:** 244 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 69

## Where it lives

VPS · bot · tools\Install-Bot.ps1:360-388 (a fifteen second restart loop with no failure count); tools\discord\bot.py:851-862

## What is known

A heartbeat to a free uptime monitor every minute, a webhook post from the wrapper's failure branch, and give up after a few fast failures instead of looping. This is the bot's own wrapper loop, not the watchdog's three-strikes rule in entry 99, which is right and should stay PART DONE 24 September, pull request #233. WHAT CHANGED: The bot's run.ps1 wrapper, which Install-Bot.ps1 writes on the VPS, now times each run. It used to restart the bot 15 seconds after every exit, forever. Now, if three runs in a row end within 30 seconds, it writes one [run] line into bot.log with the last exit code and exits 0. A run of 30 seconds or more resets the count. The watchdog's three-strikes rule in Watch-Services.ps1 (entry 99) is unchanged, and it is now what starts the bot again after the wrapper gives up. A new harness, tools/test-bot-wrapper.ps1, checks both the installer and the script it sends, then runs the generated run.ps1 for real with a stand-in in place of python. MEASURED: The change is at tools/Install-Bot.ps1:415-448, inside the run.ps1 here-string: the comment at :415, `$fastSeconds = 30 at :432, and the give-up at :444. The harness parses Install-Bot.ps1. It checks that the block that writes run.ps1 fills in only rootWin and Task (13 variables found, no strays), so a missed backtick cannot pass just because the file parses. It expands that block the same way the installer does, parses the script that gets sent, and parses the run.ps1 inside it. It then runs that run.ps1 under Windows PowerShell 5.1 from a temp folder. python is replaced by a batch file that exits with code 7. The 30-second threshold and the 15-second pause are checked at their real values first, then shortened to 3 s and 100 ms so the run is quick. On this branch the wrapper started the stand-in 3 times, stopped after about 2 s and exited 0. Its line in bot.log names exit code 7 and passes the installer's own read-back filter ^\s*\[(thornswood-bot|run)\]. Fast, fast, slow (6 s), fast, fast, fast made 6 starts, then it gave up. Result: 20 of 20 checks pass under pwsh 7 and under powershell 5.1. Against main's Install-Bot.ps1 (git show HEAD:), the same run started the stand-in 230 times in 45 s and never stopped, and 10 of 20 checks fail. From reading Watch-Services.ps1:160-230, not measured on the VPS: after the wrapper gives up, the watchdog starts the task at most 3 times an hour, and each start gets 3 quick tries. The worst case drops from about 4 starts a minute to about 9 to 12 an hour. WHAT IS LEFT: Three parts, for Patrick. (1) The alert from the wrapper's failure branch to a private channel: a webhook has to exist on the VPS first. He either lets dev-webhook.txt go up to the box, which reverses the rule in the comment at Install-Bot.ps1:167-174, or makes a separate webhook in a private channel and puts it in bot.env.json himself. Until then, doneWhen's "a deliberately rejected token produces one message in the private alerts channel" is not met; today the only trace is the [run] line in bot.log and the watchdog's note in C:\Thornswood-Watch\watch.log. (2) The one-minute heartbeat in bot.py to an outside monitor: he needs an account (for example healthchecks.io) and has to put its ping url in bot.env.json on the VPS. (3) Deploy: this reaches the box only through a full .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -NoToken -NoPause run, which re-registers the Thornswood Bot task and restarts the live bot. The entry's own deploy line, Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoToken -NoPause, would not send the new wrapper, because -CodeOnly exits at :252, before the runner section. The To Do List entry needs that line corrected. After the deploy, confirm with a look at C:\Thornswood-Bot\run.ps1 on the VPS (read over RDP; ssh is refused from here).

## What is known

Size-based rotation with a few kept, so reading last night's crash means opening a file you can actually open. The gamemode's own log also gives up permanently on the first failed write, which should raise something rather than silently disabling logging  THE SITE ROLLS ITSELF NOW, 23 September, entry 64: server.js owns its own handle and rolls at 4 MB keeping five. THE OTHER THREE DO NOT. server.log, voice.log and bot.log are all written by cmd >> from a scheduled task, and a log held open that way cannot be moved or truncated on Windows, measured on 23 September. So they need rolling AT START rather than on a timer, or the same in-process treatment where the service is ours (voice-server.js is). MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The site is done (#178, in-process roll). The rest is unchanged: Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:265-266 starts the server as cmd /c node ... >> server.log and :285-286 deletes server.log on -StartNow. Install-Voice.ps1:172 and :184 build voice.log the same way and :283 deletes it. vps-dev-instance.ps1:85 builds dev voice's voice.log the same way. Install-Bot.ps1:415-423 appends bot.log forever from the run.ps1 loop. gamemode.js:63-96 appends thornswood.log with appendFileSync forever, and when a write fails it sets logBroken and says so once on the console, which lands in server.log, and nothing else. Watch-Services.ps1:229-236 keeps the last 1000 lines past 2000, which discards rather than rotates. Measured tonight in the scratchpad: with `cmd /c "ping ... >> held.log"` running, Rename-Item, Clear-Content and FileStream SetLength(0) are all refused ('being used by another process'), Copy-Item works, and Rename-Item works as soon as the holder exits. So the entry's 'copy then truncate on a timer' step cannot work, and rolling at start, or in process, is the only way. A branch exists, patrick/todo-220-log-rotation, not merged: Nothing is live yet; it all needs Patrick's deploys, dev first. ## Traps

The cmd redirection is deliberate and its comment says why: a previous version piped through PowerShell and Out-File, which re-encoded the text and left the file unreadable past a point, and could hold the bot's own print() calls on its event loop. Watch-Services.ps1:146-154 discards rather than rotates; either fix it or say plainly in the runbook that it keeps only the last 1000 lines. Roll, never delete: deleting a log is how the evidence for the last crash disappeared in the first place.

The bot's overwrite is still allow 68608, deny 0: 1&lt;&lt;10 View Channel + 1&lt;&lt;11 Send Messages + 1&lt;&lt;16 Read Message History, taken from Discord's permission bit numbers, not from discord.py's names. The modelled live server has 50 channels and categories. Before the run, without Administrator, the bot cannot get into 47 of them: every channel and category except #say-hello, the Applications category and the hand-made open channel. That includes #staff-general, the staff #news, #news and #choose-your-hold. One run writes exactly those 47, once each, and nothing else. ## 254. Two pull requests that were each green turned main red together, because main does not ask for a branch to be up to date

**Order:** 254 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** GitHub & CI · **Effort:** decide it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

GitHub branch protection on main (required_status_checks.strict) · Claude outputs/todo-run/land.js

## What is known

FOUND 24 September. #328 (entry 197) added a check that the six client files ship by record; #306 (entry 128) made a client file ours only by its bytes. Each passed its own build and they merged an hour apart. Together the check failed, main was red from ac9df44, and every pull request after it went red for a change it never made. Fixed by #338, which asks the six by their bytes. WHY IT COULD HAPPEN: branch protection has strict off (read with gh api on 24 September), so a pull request merges on a build that ran against an older main. Two answers, and Patrick picks. (a) Turn strict on: every pull request has to be brought up to date and built again after each merge, which is safe and slow when twenty land in a row. (b) Leave strict off and have the landing helper bring each branch up to date and wait for a fresh build before it merges. (a) is one setting; (b) is code nobody else runs.

## Done when

Patrick has chosen, and the choice is in place.

## Traps

With strict on, a batch of twenty takes twenty builds in a row rather than twenty at once.

## 255. The shipped exe is compiled on your desktop while CI compiles the same source and throws it away

**Order:** 255 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** GitHub & CI · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 102

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 · GitHub · .github\workflows\build.yml:33-46, artefact kept seven days and never used

## What is known

A release job on a tag: clean checkout, build, record the commit in the assembly version, sign from a secret, scan with Defender on the runner, attach to the release with a checksums file. The person shipping never compiles the shipped binary. This is also the only place the signing key from entry 2 can be used safely, so the two go together MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: build.yml is still one job, and its 'Keep the exe from this build' step uploads with retention-days 7 and nothing downloads it. It is now on actions/checkout@v7 and upload-artifact@v7, so the entry's '@v4' is stale. Ship still builds the shipped exe locally: Ship.ps1:401 calls Build-Launcher.ps1, and signing runs only where the gitignored tools/signing.json exists (Build-Launcher.ps1:361-376, Sign-Artifact.ps1, Azure Artifact Signing). I measured the done condition itself. I compiled a one-line program twice with the same Framework csc Build-Launcher uses (C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe, 'version 4.8.9221.0 for C# 5'). The hashes differ: 9C31E5D4... and 3A040101..., with 20 of 3584 bytes different (timestamp and MVID). The same compiler rejects the switch that would fix this with 'CS2007: Unrecognized option: /deterministic'. So 'the same SHA-256 as a local build of the same commit' can never be met with this compiler. NEXT STEP: After the #dev agreement: add .github/workflows/release.yml on tags v*. Pin runs-on and every action to a full commit SHA. Build with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root under RUNNER_TEMP, write SHA256SUMS, and attach both to a draft release. Change Ship.ps1 around :385-420 to download that asset and check it against SHA256SUMS instead of compiling. Rewrite the done condition, because byte-identical local and runner builds are impossible here. The choices: Ship publishes only the runner's exe, verified by its checksum file; or the compiler moves to Roslyn with /deterministic /langversion:5, which changes 'built with the .NET Framework 4 csc'. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: The entry's own first step is a #dev agreement between Patrick and Djinn on where the shipped binary comes from. Two more things are needed: an Azure Artifact Signing identity usable from a GitHub runner (an outside account and a repository secret), and Patrick's choice between the two replacement done conditions, because the one written is impossible with this compiler (measured).

## Read first

- `.github\workflows\build.yml`: all 46 lines: one job on windows-latest, a parse step, a build step calling Build-Launcher.ps1, and actions/upload-artifact@v4 with retention-days 7 that nothing ever downloads
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:224-269`: the csc invocation a runner build has to reproduce, including /noconfig at :232 and the hand-listed references at :267
- `tools\Ship.ps1:253`: where the shipped exe is actually built today, on the shipping machine
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:163-171, 332-365, 390-412`: the install work CI is also running: Stop-Game and Stop-Launcher at :169-170, a Desktop shortcut at :350-365 and an Explorer restart at :396-412, which is harmless on a runner and ugly anywhere else

## What is known

Falls out of entry 115: the deploy pulls a named version rather than whatever is in a folder on one disk. Until then the scripts' error messages should say plainly that a local build tree is required and which switch overrides it, rather than failing in a way that reads as a bug CLOSED 22 SEPTEMBER, commit fe389db, as the better-message half this entry asked for. Deploy-Gamemode stopped with "server dist not found: <path>" and Deploy-Server did not check at all, so it got as far as reading files out of a folder that was not there. Both now say plainly that a local skymp build tree is required and why: Deploy-Gamemode writes the gamemode and the load order INTO that build, so a machine without one has nothing to write into, and it does not talk to the VPS at all. Both name the -Dist switch, and both say that without the fork built the deploy belongs to whoever has the build, pointing at the new Check-ShipReady.ps1 for what this machine is missing. Deploy-Server checks BEFORE it reads or sends anything, so a machine without the build stops with nothing having left it. Proved with -Dist C:\nope on both, which fails before any network call. The real fix, a deploy that pulls a named version rather than a folder on one disk, is still the other entry's.

## What is known

MEASURED 22 SEPTEMBER. gh pr list --state open returns nothing, and there are 22 remote branches besides main. git cherry against origin/main says 21 of the 22 are already on main by patch equivalence: they were squash-merged and never deleted. Only djinn/jump-sprint-probe has commits not on main, 2 of them, "The jump and sprint probe says how its hook is doing on every start". WHY THIS IS NOT JUST TIDINESS: two of the stale ones are djinn/owngame-creation-club and djinn/scan-skyrim-ccc, whose work IS on main and is confirmed in the code. ## Traps

Making a job required is a repository setting, not a file, and today branch protection on main has no required status checks at all, so a new job blocks nothing until somebody changes that. If entry 120 pins 'Launcher builds' as required and this change renames the job, every pull request stalls forever including the fix; change both in the same sitting. CI runs tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, which stops running Thornswood and game processes and writes Thornswood.lnk to the Desktop: harmless on a throwaway runner, ugly if anybody copies that step to a real machine. The launcher is C# 5 compiled by the .NET Framework 4 csc, so do not add a job that builds it with a modern SDK.

## 272. No application manifest: the window is blurry on mixed DPI and the exe declares no identity

**Order:** 272 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 117

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:231-242; the DPI is worked around by hand at tools\app\Downgrade.cs:540-552

## What is known

A twenty line manifest with per-monitor awareness, the supported Windows entries and run-as-invoker, plus one compiler switch. A blurry window is one of the first things a stranger notices and the last thing anybody reports, and the declared identity is what Windows shows in the file's properties and in the SmartScreen prompt MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The title is partly wrong. I measured a scratch copy of the shipped 1.1.92 exe (C:/Thornswood/Launcher/Thornswood.exe) and it already carries csc's default manifest: assemblyIdentity name='MyApplication.app' version='1.0.0.0', requestedExecutionLevel asInvoker, uiAccess false. It has no dpiAware and no supportedOS. So run-as-invoker is already declared, and the missing parts are per-monitor DPI and the supportedOS GUIDs. WPF on the Framework makes itself system DPI aware on its own, which matches the assumption behind the Downgrade.cs offset. The identity claim is also wrong: the file Properties dialog reads the version resource the build already generates (Build-Launcher.ps1:181-216), and SmartScreen shows the Authenticode signer (entry 14), not assemblyIdentity. There is a trap the entry misses. The build sets no TargetFrameworkAttribute (grep finds none in tools/app or Build-Launcher.ps1), and on the Framework, WPF's reaction to WM_DPICHANGED is governed by Switch.System.Windows.DoNotScaleForDpiChanges, whose default depends on the targeted framework. A PerMonitorV2 manifest on its own may leave the window unscaled on the second monitor rather than sharp. That has to be measured on a real mixed-DPI desktop. Downgrade.cs ClickCommandLine at 578-597 scales its offset by GetDpiForWindow over GetDpiForSystem (declared at 796-797) and still drives Steam's console, so the DPI mode change moves a synthesised click into Valve's window. NEXT STEP: Claude can do now: write tools/app/Thornswood.manifest (assemblyIdentity Thornswood.Launcher.Thornswood with a four-part version, asInvoker, supportedOS GUIDs through Windows 10/11, dpiAwareness PerMonitorV2 and legacy dpiAware true). Pass /win32manifest in the cscArgs array at Build-Launcher.ps1:240; /win32icon can stay, only /win32res conflicts. Add the AppContext handling so WPF actually rescales: set Switch.System.Windows.DoNotScaleForDpiChanges=false before the Application is created in Shell.cs, or emit a TargetFramework attribute in the generated info file. Work out whether the Downgrade.cs ratio becomes 1 under PerMonitorV2 and change it to match. Compile to a temp root and confirm the embedded manifest text with the same byte probe used here. Leave the visual check to a person. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Needs the #dev line between Patrick and Djinn, because it changes DPI behaviour for the whole launcher and for the Steam console click. After that a person has to confirm on a mixed-DPI desktop that the window is sharp and correctly sized on both monitors, and that the Downgrade click still lands in Steam's console. Nobody here starts the launcher.

- `tools/app/Downgrade.cs:532-563`: ClickCommandLine, which scales a 72 pixel offset by GetDpiForWindow divided by GetDpiForSystem, an assumption that only holds while this process is system DPI aware
- `tools/app/Shell.cs:460-475`: the window placement maths against SystemParameters.WorkArea, the other thing a DPI mode change moves

## Traps

Do not use (Get-Item ...).VersionInfo as the proof: the version resource is generated from assembly attributes at Build-Launcher.ps1:188-216, so /win32manifest cannot displace it and that test cannot fail. PerMonitorV2 moves this process into unvirtualised coordinates, which is exactly what Downgrade.cs's 72 pixel offset assumes it is not, so getting the manifest right and the offset wrong types into the wrong place in somebody else's application. csc accepts one /win32manifest and it conflicts with /win32res, and this build already passes /win32icon. The declared identity is what Windows shows in the file's properties and in the SmartScreen prompt, which ties it to entry 14's signing identity.

## 276. Installed apps lists Thornswood only after the first launch, and without a size

**Order:** 276 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 121

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Register.cs:78-126 · Your PC · tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1 writes no registry entry

## What is known

The installer writes the same key at install time with the size of the payload it just moved, under the same hashed name so the launcher updates that row rather than adding a second. Somebody who installs and does not launch has a program Windows cannot see MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The first half is mostly closed already. Setup-Thornswood.ps1:608-677 opens the launcher itself at the end of a successful install (Open-Launcher). tools/Setup.bat never passes -NoOpen, and neither does Bootstrap.cs:1020-1026, so Register.Ensure writes the key seconds after install. The key is missing only when the install's own checks failed (:655-659). That window is the one that asks for a screenshot, and the install is broken at that point anyway. Setup-Thornswood.ps1 writes no Uninstall key (grep: no HKCU or Uninstall writes). Register.cs:118-122 still deliberately omits EstimatedSize. The entry's fix rests on a premise that no longer holds under the own-game-folder layout: the installer's payload is not Thornswood's footprint. I measured this machine read-only from C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt: - C (copied) lines: 7,957 files, 1,093.4 MB. - L (hard linked to Vortex's copy) lines: 22,696 files, 40,433.5 MB. - du: Launcher 5 MB, Profile 48 MB. OwnGame.cs:235-283 already adds up copyBytes when it builds the folder, and made.txt (:875) is written at that moment. So a real number is available with no walk at launch. It is roughly 1.15 GB of Thornswood's own bytes against 41 GB that Explorer would show for the Game folder. NEXT STEP: What can be done now, pending Patrick's call on which number to show: 1. tools/app/OwnGame.cs: where it writes made.txt (:875) after a build, also write copied=<copyBytes>. It already has that value at :235-240 and :311-350. 2. tools/app/Register.cs Ensure: read copied= from Profile\OwnGame\made.txt if present. Add the launcher exe size and write EstimatedSize as a DWord in KB. When the record is absent, write nothing, which keeps the 'no invented number' rule at :118-122. Update that comment to say the number comes from OwnGame's build record, not a walk. 3. Drop the installer-side key write the entry proposes. The installer opens the launcher, the launcher writes the key within seconds, and a second writer with its own copy of the FNV hash (Register.cs:40-55) is the double-row risk the entry itself warns about. 4. Compile and ship on the dev channel. After a person has launched once, read EstimatedSize with Get-ItemProperty and check there is exactly one row. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to decide what Windows should show as Thornswood's size: the copied bytes OwnGame measured, or nothing, as Register.cs:118-122 decided. He also has to confirm the installer-side key write can be dropped, since the installer already opens the launcher. The registry result is only visible after a person runs the launcher.

## Traps

Main had not done any of this: its home.html, index.html and privacy.md st

## Traps

The public markdown is editable from the site, so server-side rendering turns somebody typing into a document into somebody writing HTML on the public front page unless you sanitise. The site's hub is admin-gated and entry 79 deletes it, so do not spend effort making index.html pretty. Every response says Cache-Control: no-store today, so self-hosting is only worth it alongside real cache headers or you have swapped one round trip for another. Deploying the site is the person's job, and server.js changes ship with everything else as one complete release.

## Traps

This file is the server, so a mistake is a live outage for everybody, and only the person deploys it. ## 294. The Skyrim build number and the depot ids are compiled into the exe rather than carried in the feed

**Order:** 294 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 145

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Config.cs:77 and 206 (an expected file size); tools\app\Downgrade.cs:41-46 (three depot and manifest ids, and the newer build's size)

## What is known

The pinned build, its file signature and the manifests that produce it are data in the feed, not constants in the binary, so everyone can be moved to a new pin without shipping code. The project already applies this principle correctly elsewhere; the downgrade is the one place it did not MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The pin is still compiled in and nothing in the last 250 commits touches it. Downgrade.cs:38 AppId 489830, :48-52 the three depot/manifest pairs, :54 NewerExeBytes; Config.cs:122 ExpectedExeBytes = 37157144 and :273 the migration default (the entry's :77/:206 have moved). VersionDoc (Config.cs:461-541) has no pin fields; OnVersionDoc (Shell.cs:4333-4357) adopts serverAddress, collectionUrl, serverPort, maxOnline and collectionRevision only. Setup-Thornswood.ps1:40 (exe size) and :46-51 (depots) duplicate it, and that script still ships in the installer (Package-Thornswood.ps1:527). The premise does not hold, though: the build number lives in far more places than the entry names. Checks.cs:620 and Pages.cs:181 test skse64_1_6_1170.dll by name; Downgrade.cs:122-124, Shell.cs:1831-1832 and :1869, and Pages.cs:179 say 1.6.1170 in text; Package-Thornswood.ps1:183 packs skse64_1_6_1170.dll; Add-Bodies/Add-Characters/Add-JContainers pick the 1170/AE1170 builds. So putting the exe size and depots in the feed cannot move the pin without a launcher release. A pin move also needs a new script extender and collection revision, and CLAUDE.md already makes every change one complete release, launcher included. NEXT STEP: Now: the inventory above is the correction to this entry. If Patrick wants the plumbing anyway: (1) Config.cs VersionDoc gets optional expectedExeBytes (long), newerExeBytes (long) and depots ([{id, manifest}]), all defaulting to zero or null. (2) Shell.cs OnVersionDoc, beside the maxOnline line at :4344, adopts each value only when it is non-zero, and the existing cfg.Save writes it. (3) Downgrade.cs reads the depots and newer size from cfg and keeps the array at :48-52 as a clearly labelled fallback. (4) Publish-Update.ps1 writes the values from one record (for example a new tools/skyrim-pin.json), and Setup-Thornswood.ps1 reads the same record out of the installer stage in place of its own :40/:46-51 copy. (5) Compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root <scratch> -NoPause and grep for 8442952117333549665 and expectedExeBytes. Otherwise close the entry, and fix only the duplication between Downgrade.cs and Setup-Thornswood.ps1. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides whether the pin should be feed data at all, given that the script extender dll name and the launcher's text are compiled in and a pin move is always a full release. If yes, he also decides which single record holds the pin.

Record the collection revision the build was made against and compare it against what Vortex has installed, which Vortex writes into its own profile data. Both now read one constant, Checks.MostPluginsWithoutCollection, which is still 40, so nothing behaves differently. The doc comment above CollectionProblem had two summaries stacked on one method. One of them still argued for the old po3_StartOnSave.dll sentinel and left out "ahead". It is now one summary that says what the method returns today and why a plugin count alone is not enough. A new harness, tools/test-collection-threshold.js, reads both comparisons out of the C#, runs them against every count from 0 to 200, and holds the doc comment to that shape. **Order:** 298 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 149

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\OwnGame.cs:147-150, which refuses because hard links only work inside one volume

## What is known

Ask where to install on the volume it needs, during setup, before anything is written. Failing that, offer to move, or fall back to copies with the disk cost stated. Plenty of people keep games on a second drive, and today they meet a refusal rather than a choice MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: OwnGame.cs:147-149 still returns the flat 'has to be installed on the same drive' sentence. Since 20-21 Sep this blocks more than a feature: OwnGameRequired (ShellOwnGame.cs:158 onward) refuses Play outright, with a MessageBox, whenever WhyNot names a reason. So somebody with Skyrim on D: and Thornswood on C: cannot play at all. Place() (OwnGame.cs:785-791) already falls back to File.Copy when CreateHardLink fails, so the copy path exists mechanically. The installer (tools/setup/Bootstrap.cs:108 defaults to C:\Thornswood; BuildDrives :146-192) offers every fixed drive with no hint which one Skyrim is on, and its intro text at :411 still describes the old shape ('puts Thornswood into the Skyrim you already have on Steam... does not make a second copy'). The entry's trap that djinn/own-game-folder is not on main is out of date: 56af203 (1.1.75) and 5dcc6b5 put it on main, the branch no longer exists, and CLAUDE.md says so. Measured here: C:\Thornswood\Game is 41 GB apparent and its Data folder 26 GB, roughly what a copy fallback would cost. NEXT STEP: Doable now, inside the settled design: (1) Bootstrap.cs finds Skyrim's Steam library (the same libraryfolders.vdf walk as Steam.SkyrimPath, Steam.cs:107-130), preselects that drive, and says on screen when a different drive is picked that Thornswood has to share Skyrim's drive. Rewrite the stale text at :411 while there. (2) OwnGame.cs:147-149 names the exact way out: reinstall Thornswood to <Skyrim drive>\Thornswood, or move the Skyrim library to <Thornswood drive> in Steam's Storage settings. Compile the launcher and the setup stub. Left for #dev: whether the launcher may fall back to copies (about 26 to 41 GB, never silently) or move an install itself. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn in #dev: a copy fallback or a launcher-driven move both change the hard-link design. The installer steering and the clearer refusal need no decision.

## 301. (done) DONE: The chat overlay watches only <head>, and voice reads the launcher's files off the game's thread

**Order:** 301 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 158

Everyone's PC · tools\ts-ui\thornswood-bridge.js:458-474, 479-491, 277-283; tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-voice.js:119-135, 509-514, 527-530

## What is known

Scope the observer to the part of the document it cares about, budget the per-frame work, use styling to hide rather than removing and reinserting, and never do synchronous disk writes on the render thread. This is the code between the person and every frame of the game DONE 24 September, pull request #294, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: The chat overlay no longer watches the whole page. thornswood-bridge.js used to watch the whole document (subtree on) and, on every change anywhere in the page, ran six whole-page queries and pulled the tick boxes, dice and resize corner out from under React. Now it watches only the direct children of <head> and puts its own stylesheet back if the sheet is ever removed. That sheet already hid those elements with display:none !important, so they are now hidden instead of removed. In the voice plugin, the per-frame status and port handlers no longer call readFileSync. Each one starts an fs.readFile and uses the last result it brought back. If no background read ever comes back within 5 s, the plugin goes back to the old synchronous reads and logs that once. A new harness, tools/test-chat-overlay-cost.js, proves all of this and shows every line of chat still reaches the screen. MEASURED: tools/test-chat-overlay-cost.js ran against the old bridge and plugin (restored from HEAD for the run): 36 pass, 14 fail. Old numbers: 25 party-strip redraws (5 s of thornswood-party.js's 200 ms interval) ran 150 querySelectorAll and woke the observer 25 times. One chat line ran 12 queries. The voice plugin made 5 synchronous reads inside frames in the first second and 55 over the whole run. With the new code all 50 checks pass: 0 queries, 0 observer wake-ups, 0 synchronous reads in frames. The harness also shows the last 50 lines on screen in order, from the game side and through thornswood-chat.js's socket, and a line typed before chat.js loaded still goes out. Read from the fork: NodeInstance::Tick (skyrim-platform/src/platform_se/skyrim_platform/NodeInstance.cpp:200-207) runs uv_run(uv_default_loop(), UV_RUN_NOWAIT) on every update, and the Node env is built on uv_default_loop() (lines 113-136), so async fs callbacks should arrive. skymp5-client uses its own TimersService instead of libuv timers, so async is unproven in play. That is why the fallback exists. The front's webpack.config.ts uses style-loader with its defaults, and none of the chat's display rules in the front's scss is !important. Code: tools/ts-ui/thornswood-bridge.js:451-486 (keepSheet and the observer on <head>). tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-voice.js:139-213 (readChannelAsync, refreshChannel, channelText). The status handler is at :618-627, the port handler at :653-665. STILL TO DO BY A PERSON: For Patrick: put this on the dev channel and have a person judge frame time in play; nothing here measures a frame. In the same session, check that the dice pouch, the tick boxes and the resize corner stay hidden, that the voice indicator still shows the launcher's status, and that thornswood-voice.log does not say "never came back". That line means async reads do not work in this build and the plugin went back to the old synchronous reads. Two parts of the entry's plan were not done. requestAnimationFrame coalescing was skipped: with the observer on <head> nothing is left to coalesce per change, and rAF can stop while the browser is not being drawn. The synchronous push-to-talk writes (writePtt, writeMuted) were left alone as the entry said: an async "0" could land before the "1" and leave the microphone open. The entry's title claim about writes on every key press was wrong, as triage found. Deploy is the dev Ship below. It is a plugin and a page file with no gamemode change, so no gamemode deploy is needed.

That setting is AutoUpdateBehavior 1 in steamapps\appmanifest_489830.acf. The launcher writes nothing unless the person presses Yes and Steam is closed. The write changes only that value's bytes, goes through a temp file and File.Replace, and leaves a read

## Traps

AutoUpdateBehavior 1 is a strong mitigation, not a lock: Steam still updates on a launch from Steam, which is the exact thing the existing log line already asks people not to do. The acf is Valve's KeyValues format, tab delimited, not JSON and not INI, so a regex replacement that normalises whitespace can leave Steam unable to parse it. Never rewrite the file while Steam is running, and re-check the value only after Steam has been closed and reopened. C# 5 only. Downgrade.cs is shared with entries 160 and 159, so split the work.

## 305. The Nexus collection carries the plugin order from revision 5, and what is left is proving a clean install matches the server

**Order:** 305 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 38

## Where it lives

Nexus collection ombo2a revision 5 · collection.json pluginRules, 51 rules over 52 full plugins · %APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\userlist.yaml · revisions 2 to 4 carried no rules at all

## What is known

Re-upload the collection with its load order included, which Vortex supports and which costs minutes. Or ship only the own-folder shape, which makes the reference list authoritative everywhere. Today a first-time person installs, presses Play, is refused, and presses Fix DONE IN REVISION 5, 22 SEPTEMBER. The order is pinned as LOOT after rules in Vortex's userlist, one chain over the 52 full plugins from Water for ENB.esm to Playable Rieklings.esp, and revision 5's collection.json carries them: 51 plugin rules where revisions 2 to 4 had none. It is the order this machine deployed from revision 5, and the server takes the same list through Deploy-Gamemode -Vortex -NewOrder in entry 46, so both come from one source. THE MCM HELPER STEP IS ALREADY TRUE: revision 5 installs MCM Helper 1.6.2, and its MCMHelper.esp carries the light flag (header flags 0x200), checked in Vortex's copy and in the game folder. DOES LOOT STILL MOVE THINGS: not the chained plugins. LOOT treats an after rule as a hard constraint, so a sort can put other plugins between them but cannot reorder them. Light plugins and anything outside the chain can still move, and the server does not count those by position. What can still break it is somebody dragging plugins by hand, which the install instructions now tell people not to do. LEFT: the proof this entry asked for, a clean profile install compared line for line with the reference list. It can only be done after the release in entry 46, because until then the reference list on this machine is revision 4's. The 97 plugins, one listed twice and 48 of 55 were never checked and no longer matter. MEASURED ON THE MACHINE, 22 SEPTEMBER, after revision 5 published the order. LOOT treats the collection's "load after" rules as hard constraints and puts them ahead of its own masterlist. All 52 full plugins are chained one after another, so autosort cannot swap any two of them, and after a Sort Now all 52 landed in exactly the server's order. That is the fix working. THREE LIMITS, and the second one is maintenance nobody will remember without this line. ONE, light plugins are not chained. LOOT can still move an esl around, and that is fine, because the server's position check skips light plugins entirely. TWO, A PLUGIN ADDED LATER IS NOT PINNED UNTIL SOMEBODY GIVES IT A RULE. The chain covers what was in the collection when the rules were written and nothing after it. Every future plugin needs one rule putting it after the current last one in the chain, which as of revision 5 is Playable Rieklings.esp. Forget that and the new plugin floats, which is the same load order mismatch this entry exists to stop, arriving one revision later with nobody connecting the two. THREE, a conflicting masterlist rule stops LOOT rather than winning. If a future masterlist update ever contradicts one of these rules, LOOT reports a cycle and refuses to sort. The order stays where it is and the person gets an error, which is the safe way for it to fail. AND IT IS STILL DEFEATABLE TWO WAYS. The collection install dialog has a "Skip plugin rules" switch, and anybody who turns it on gets no order at all; the launcher's Fix button is the fallback for them. And dragging plugins by hand in Vortex still breaks it, because nothing about this stops a person reordering the list themselves. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #217. WHAT CHANGED: Added tools/Check-CollectionRules.ps1, a read-only check that compares the plugin rules in the Nexus collection with a plugin list. It reads the newest collection revision Vortex has installed, one plugins.txt (Profile\Default\plugins.txt unless -List names another) and the plugin headers in one Data folder. It says NO and exits 1 in four cases: a full plugin that no rule names (the entry's "a plugin added later floats" trap, and it says which rule the next upload needs), a rule the list breaks, two neighbouring full plugins that no chain of rules keeps in order, and a full plugin that a rule names but the list does not enable. Light plugins and the five base masters are left out, the same as the server's position check leaves them out. With no collection in Vortex it says SKIP and exits 0. tools/test-collection-rules.ps1 proves all of this with its own test files and runs the real script as a child process. MEASURED: Measured on this machine against revision 5 (collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z\collection.json: 51 rules naming 52 plugins). HELD, exit 0, for three lists: - the dev server's list: the 22:46 dev pack's profile\plugins.txt. Its SHA256 (A3FFEB2C...) is the same as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Skyrim Special Edition\plugins.txt. - that live plugins.txt itself. - Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt. All three: 94 enabled, 52 full, 42 light, 52 of 52 named, 51 pairs held. NOT HELD, exit 1, for the reference C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt (written 23 Sep 22:39): - "Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary.esp (line 34) must load after Thornswood-Content.esp (line 95)". - "Playable Rieklings.esp (line 93) then Thornswood-Content.esp (line 95): the rules put them the other way round". This confirms the triage's finding: diff shows Thornswood-Content.esp at line 31 in the live list and line 95 in the reference. The Profile\Default\plugins.txt.rev4.bak list: 5 plugins that revision 5 dropped are reported as floating, and 2 plugins the rules name are missing from it. Where the logic is in the new script: - Check-CollectionRules.ps1:108 picks the revision through Get-CollectionRevision. - :110-112 is the SKIP path. - :224, :238, :248 and :287 are the four findings. - :252 is Test-Reaches, which follows chains of rules only through plugins the list enables. Both files are pure ASCII with no control bytes. WHAT IS LEFT: The code is complete. The entry stays open for Patrick. Its doneWhen needs him to install the current collection revision into a clean Vortex profile (his Nexus account, in Vortex). He then runs `.\tools\Check-CollectionRules.ps1 -List <the plugins.txt that install wrote>` and Compare-Object on that file against the server's order (the dev pack list, or the live manifest read over HTTP). Not done here, and each is his decision: - The check is not wired into Ship, Deploy-Gamemode or Check-ShipReady. Putting it there would change a release gate. - The reference Profile\Default\plugins.txt on the shipping machine is out of the chain today. Its cause is entry 275 (Install-ThornswoodContent.ps1:15 anchors on a plugin that is in none of the lists). - Every future plugin still needs a rule after Playable Rieklings.esp in the next Nexus upload. This check now says so when one is missing.

## 306. Seven copies of the list on your machine, written by five tools, and nothing compares any two at Ship time

**Order:** 306 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 39

Your PC · Profile\Default, Profile\OwnGame, Profile\LocalAppData, Vortex's own, _dist\server, and tools\Ship.ps1 which never mentions the manifest

## What is known

The shipping step derives the server list from the reference it is about to pack, using the header logic Deploy-Gamemode already has, and refuses when it does not equal the live manifest, naming the first position that differs. Ten lines. Today they agree because the steps happened to be run in the right order on one machine RE-READ 22 SEPTEMBER, and most of this is already built, in Publish-Update rather than in Ship. Publish-Update.ps1:251 dot-sources LoadOrder.ps1, fetches the live manifest, and Get-ReferenceInServerOrder DIES when the server does not answer, so a pack can no longer be built against an unverified order. It puts the reference list into the server's order before zipping, so position is enforced by construction rather than compared. At :1256-1290 it derives the game order with Get-LoadOrderGame and names any full plugin the list enables that the server does not have, with the two commands to put it right. SO THE REMAINING GAP IS SMALL AND WORTH STATING EXACTLY: that check is set membership, not position, and the reordering makes position true rather than proving it. The Get-LoadOrderGame call there passes an empty ccc list, which is correct for a reference list (the shipping machine's own Creation Club files are not what testers have, and the launcher does the per-machine check), but it is worth a comment saying so before somebody reads it as an omission and adds it. Ship.ps1 itself still never mentions the manifest, so the Select-String in this row's commands still returns nothing. Whether the gate belongs in Ship as well is now a judgement rather than a defect. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #218. WHAT CHANGED: This does step 1 of the triage plan and nothing more. The new tools/test-load-order.ps1 dot-sources tools/LoadOrder.ps1 and runs it with stub light and Data checks, so it needs no game folder, no Data and no server. It checks the Publish-Update path end to end: a stale list is found at the exact first position that differs, and after Get-LoadOrderReordered it agrees at every position. It also checks the edge cases: an extra full plugin found by position, a plugin enabled twice, a missing or switched-off plugin, light plugins keeping their lines, case and spacing, Skyrim.ccc, the manifest JSON, the manifest URL and port, and that the file round trip keeps its byte order mark and newlines. It also compiles tools/app/LoadOrder.cs and checks that the launcher and the publisher give the same answers. That makes the LoadOrder.ps1 header line "held to identical output by a test" true for the first time. No change to LoadOrder.ps1, because the harness found no bug in it. MEASURED: Harness: 127 passed, 0 failed under pwsh 7.6.6 and under Windows PowerShell 5.1. 47 of those checks compare the launcher with the publisher. To show the harness catches real breakage, I ran it against 11 deliberately broken copies (scratch script mutants.ps1, run with -LoadOrderPath / -LauncherPath). Every one exited 1. The breakages were: light plugins moved, case-sensitive compare, ccc after the list, a duplicate accepted, slots unsorted, BOM read as text, a missing plugin skipped, resources served on the game port, the Data check dropped, and in LoadOrder.cs light plugins moved and a case-sensitive compare. The first version of the harness let 3 of them through. I tightened it until none got through. Real data on this machine, read only: C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt has Thornswood-Content.esp on line 31 of 95. Profile\Default\plugins.txt (written 2026-09-23 22:39) has it on line 95 of 95, and Profile\LocalAppData\Plugins.txt on line 96 of 96. The built server's order in C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\build\dist\server\server-settings.json (written 23 Sep 11:37, 57 plugins) has it at index 23. I only read the loadOrder field from that file. Against that order, Default and LocalAppData first differ at index 23: the list has Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary.esp where the server has Thornswood-Content.esp. Get-LoadOrderReordered moves 34 lines, the first being Thornswood-Content.esp, and after that the mismatch is -1. OwnGame already matches. **Order:** 307 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 163

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:113-136, 151-154, 173; the same omission in tools\Align-LoadOrder.ps1 and tools\app\Verify.cs

## What is known

Read the master bit as well as the light bit, stable-sort the flagged entries to the front, and print anything named but not found. Latent today because no plugin in the list carries that flag, and silent the day one does, which is the worst kind of bug to leave in a thing that decides form ids CLOSED 22 SEPTEMBER, commit 4fb7432, and the fix is NOT the blanket sort this entry asked for, because that would have re-keyed the world. Read-PluginHeader now reads bit 0x1 beside 0x200 and returns Master as well as Light, treating an .esm as master by extension the way it already treats an .esl as light. WHY NOT A BLANKET SORT: since 7b2634d the deploy keeps the order the server already runs, because the world keys every changed form on the position in that list. Hoisting a master that is already in that list would re-key every saved chest, door and body after it, which is the one move nothing can undo. So the sort runs ONLY where the order is decided fresh: no prior server list, or -NewOrder, -MinimalLoadOrder, -FullLoadOrder. Where the server's order is kept it is left alone, and a NEWLY ADDED master-flagged plugin now STOPS the deploy and says why, because the game loads it at the front whatever the list says and it cannot go on the end of an order a world is already keyed to. The way out is named: take it out of the collection, or wipe and rebuild with -NewOrder. AND $missing IS PRINTED AT LAST. It was collected at :231 and thrown away, so a list naming a plugin nobody has said nothing at all and the server shipped an order one shorter than the one being read. MEASURED 22 September: of the 60 plugins that take a place, seven carry the flag, Skyrim.esm, Update.esm, Dawnguard.esm, HearthFires.esm, Dragonborn.esm, Water for ENB.esm and Embers XD.esm, all .esm and all already at the top. So this was latent, exactly as this entry's own traps said, and not absent. No .esp carries it today. PROVED BY DRY RUN INTO A SCRATCH DIST, never against the live server: the live-order path reports 60 in place, 0 new, 0 gone, and the fresh-order path reports "masters first: 7 master-flagged, 0 position(s) changed" and produces a list byte for byte identical to the one the server runs. The sort is a provable no-op on today's list, so this change cannot move anybody's world. tools\test-master-flag.ps1 is 15 checks that lift Read-PluginHeader and Sort-MastersFirst out of the shipped script by text, so a rename fails loudly rather than testing a copy, and one of them fails the day an .esp in the live order carries the flag.

## 312. Nothing anywhere limits how many people can connect, and the only number that looks like a limit is decoration

**Order:** 312 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 53

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · server-settings.json has no such key · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Config.cs:70 (MaxOnline = 25 is a display string), Online.cs:42, 104-105

## What is known

A hard slot count on the server, a clear refusal past it, and a number chosen from a load test rather than a guess. How many does it hold is a question a product answers before it opens. The twenty-sixth person today is told twenty-six of twenty-five are awake PART DONE 24 September, pull request #219. WHAT CHANGED: Step 2 only, scripts only. The server cap now comes from a single place: MaxOnline in the launcher's config.json, which is where Publish-Update.ps1 already reads it for the feed. A new tools/MaxOnline.ps1 (Find-LauncherRoot, Get-MaxOnline, Set-MaxPlayers) reads that key by the same rule the feed uses. Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 writes it as the engine's maxPlayers into the built server's settings, and Deploy-Server.ps1 sends those settings. Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 sets it in place on the dev box. Live reads C:\Thornswood\config.json and dev reads C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\config.json, the same two files the live and dev feeds are published from, so the feed, the Play page and the engine show one number. If there is no number, maxPlayers is left alone. If the number is above the engine's ceiling of 1000, the deploy stops before anything is written. MEASURED: The engine does cap connections, so the entry's title is wrong on that point. ScampServer.cpp:205 requires maxPlayers, Networking.cpp:157-162 hands it to RakNet as the slot count, and Networking.cpp:148 throws "Current slots limit is 1000" at startup above MAX_PLAYERS=1000 (skymp5-server/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:46). Nothing in the repo ever wrote maxPlayers: a grep of tools finds no match. On 24 Sep, C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\build\dist\server\server-settings.json had maxPlayers 100, and so did C:\Thornswood-Dev\server-settings-vps.json (16 Sep copy). MaxOnline is 25 in both C:\Thornswood\config.json and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\config.json; only that key was read. ## 313. What the unculled position broadcast costs: 369 GB an evening at two hundred people, against an 8 TB monthly cap

**Order:** 313 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 55

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206 (every peer, every 200ms) · measured at 128 bytes a row: 1.5 MB/s at fifty, 24.5 MB/s at two hundred, against a box that measured 93 Mbit/s

## What is known

Cull by distance and cell on the server, so each person is told only about people who could possibly be audible. That is the privacy fix and the bandwidth fix in one change, and it is the reason entry 6 does not try to do it: twenty-one evenings would burn the monthly cap, and the link saturates long before that PART DONE 24 September, pull request #211. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 211, "The voice service tells each person only about people they could hear, and their party". Every peer was sent the whole position snapshot five times a second: every person's coordinates, facing, cell and name, wherever they were. That is entry 282. It told anybody holding a socket where everybody in the world was standing, and it grew with the square of the room: the entry measured 1.5 MB a second at fifty people and 24.5 MB a second at two hundred, 369 GB an evening, against an 8 TB monthly cap and a box that measured 93 Mbit/s. Now each person is sent their own row, everybody in the same cell within 100 m, and their own party wherever they are. 100 m is over the furthest any client hears, the overlay's yell at 85 m, so nobody is cut off before their own falloff would have silenced them. The party is there because the party strip (ts-ui/thornswood-party.js) draws an arrow and a distance to every member anywhere in the world off this same feed, and a cull by cell and distance MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206`: snapshot() filters on staleness and nothing else, and the setInterval at :202-206 sends the whole snapshot to every peer five times a second, so every person is told every other person's coordinates, facing, cell and name
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:837-849`: the client already computes gain from cell and distance, including the different cell means no sound rule; this is the culling rule the server should be applying
- `tools\gamemode.js:616-620`: the towns table and the cell descriptors, so you know what a cell comparison actually compares

## 316. (done) DONE: whisper, local and yell carry different distances

**Order:** 316 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Djinn · **Old number:** 91

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\launcher\voice-host.html:34 and 337 · the service half is already done: tools\voice\voice-server.js relays t === "vmode" to the room and carries mode in the roster it sends a late joiner

## What is known

CAUSE FOUND 19 September, and it is not the service. voice-server.js does relay vmode now and does carry mode in the roster, so the mode reaches every listener. The launcher's page then set panner.maxDistance from it and nothing else, and WebAudio's inverse distance model never reads maxDistance; only the linear model does. So the number changed and no voice ever did. THE FIX is on branch djinn/voice-modes: the panner keeps HRTF for direction and is told to apply no distance attenuation of its own (rolloffFactor 0 makes the inverse model return 1 at every distance), and the level is worked out from the speaker's mode instead. Full volume to 1.5 m for a whisper, 4 m for local and 8 m for a yell, fading to nothing by 5, 18 and 45 m, with a yell louder and a whisper quieter at the same distance, and ramped rather than assigned so it does not click. A mode announced before its connection finished the handshake used to be dropped, leaving that person at local range until they changed mode again; it is now kept by peer and applied when the connection opens. STILL OPEN: tools\voice\public\voice.js, the standalone page the service serves at /voice for a plain browser, has no modes at all and one fixed distance for everybody. It is a second client with a different feature set, so it is a separate piece of work, but it is reachable by anybody who opens the address. LOCAL CARRIES HALF AS FAR AGAIN, 20 September, commit ecbf7a3. Asked for by Patrick after hearing the 19 September set in game: local's 2.7 and 12 metres become 1.35 and 6, about 420 Skyrim units instead of 840. Whisper and yell are untouched, so the three modes separate more sharply than they did, and the levels are left alone again because it is the distance that was wrong and not the loudness. Patrick reports the modes themselves now work and the ranges are otherwise right. SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.90, with the gamemode on both servers, the voice service reinstalled and the site republished. FIXED IN THE OVERLAY, which is the page that actually runs: the launcher page this entry was written against is gone and thornswood-voice.js inherited the defect whole. The panner is told to apply no distance attenuation at all now, rolloffFactor 0, and the level is worked out in code: full strength to the mode's own radius, then a natural 1/d falloff scaled to reach exactly nothing at its limit, with a per mode weight on top so a yell IS louder than a whisper at the same distance. Ramped rather than assigned, so it does not click. Measured off the real function: at 12m a yell is 0.94, local 0.23 and a whisper silent; whisper ends at 7m, local at 30, a yell at 85. AND THE STANDALONE PAGE TOO. tools\voice\public\voice.js, which this entry left open as a separate piece of work, had the same ignored maxDistance and now has the same shape. It still has no speaking modes, which IS still separate work, and the file says so where somebody would look. tools\test-voice-range.js is 29 checks and drives the real functions, because a number that is ignored reads exactly like working code.

## 317. (done) DONE: relay mode lets go of the socket now

**Order:** 317 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 92

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:879-895, 583-628; tools\ts-ui\thornswood-chat.js:216-284

## What is known

A handoff between two audio paths tears the old one down completely and verifiably, and a listener registered on a shared bus can be removed. Right now the call throws, the old path stays up, and nothing says so SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.90, with the gamemode on both servers, the voice service reinstalled and the site republished. IT DID NOT THROW, WHICH IS WORSE. The call was `if (n && n.leave) n.leave()` and thornswoodNet has never had a leave, so the guard was always false and the call simply never happened. A guard that is false reads exactly like a call that worked. The page went on being handed every voice message on the shared socket and rebuilt the peer connections it had just dropped. It cannot CLOSE that socket either, which is why leave was the wrong idea rather than a missing one: the socket belongs to the chat and voice is a passenger on it. So thornswoodNet learned off(), the voice page keeps its listener in a variable and removes it, and the handler ignores sdp, ice and peers while the launcher has the audio as a second net.

## Read first

- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:876-896`: enterRelay() and the comment stating what it is for: the launcher has the audio, so anything this page built has to come down or the server sees two of everybody
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:630-650`: reconcile(), which has no relay guard at all, so the next peers broadcast calls open() again and rebuilds the connections the handoff just dropped
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-chat.js:216-255`: the whole window.thornswoodNet API: say, state, on, post, peer, isUp and setName, with no leave, and on() at :249 pushing a listener that can never be removed
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-chat.js:135-155`: retry and reconnect on every close, which is why closing the socket rejoins rather than leaves

## Steps

Closing and reopening the socket rejoins: chat.js reconnects after about a second and sends a fresh join, the service hands out a new peer id and everyone else opens to it again, and that socket is chat, so a real leave takes in-game chat down and shows the customer that chat lost the server. **Order:** 320 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 95
