## 321. The command channel between the plugins and the server has no acknowledgement, and drops the oldest on overflow

**Order:** 321 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 96

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js:495-534, 408-416 · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:3333-3359, 2863-3067

## What is known

A command channel carries an authenticated sender, a message id, an acknowledgement and a bounded retry. A queue that overflows drops the newest and tells the sender, rather than silently discarding what it already accepted. Entry 7 is what happens when two servers share this channel; this is the channel itself PART DONE 24 September, pull request #212. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 212, "The acknowledged poll hands each line to dispatch(), and its test knows it". To Do entry 290, "The command channel between the plugins and the server has no acknowledgement, and drops the oldest on overflow". Every slash line and every plugin report (/face, a swing of the axe, a broken lockpick) waits in the voice service's queue for the gamemode to collect it over loopback every 1.5 seconds. Two ways that lost commands with nobody told: GET /commands emptied the queue in one splice before the gamemode read the answer, and poll() parsed it inside a catch that returned. A batch that failed to parse, or an answer lost to the two second timeout, was gone from both ends. A full queue (200) shifted the oldest off the front without a word, so a command already taken vanished to make room. The service now gives every command an id (a stamp made at start, then a counter). GET /commands?ack=1 hands out the queue without emptying it, POST /commands/ack (loopback only, like MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:405-416`: the loopback-gated GET /commands; :412 splices the whole queue out in one go, so it is emptied before the gamemode has seen anything
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:495-534`: where a slash line is queued, and the overflow rule at :520 that drops the oldest silently
- `tools\gamemode.js:3333-3359`: poll(), the other end: an http.request to 127.0.0.1 every 1500 ms, and the parse at :3343 whose catch returns and silently discards a whole batch that has already been removed from the service

## Steps

  ```

  ```
- [ ] Add a loopback-only POST /commands/ack that removes acknowledged ids, guarded by the same isLoopback test already used at :411 and :421. (claude)
- [ ] In tools\gamemode.js poll(), acknowledge only after handle() has succeeded, so the parse failure at :3343 no longer loses a batch that the service has already forgotten. (claude)

  ```
- [ ] Change the overflow rule at :520 to refuse the newest and tell the sender, rather than silently discarding what it already accepted. (claude)
- [ ] Parse both files, then run the loopback test: POST a chat line into a locally running copy, GET /commands twice and assert the second GET still returns it until an ack arrives. (claude)

This is the whose-game gate, the thing that keeps the plugins idle unless the client is pointed at this server, so five copies of it is five places for one of them to drift. One plugin loads first and publishes a small named object, which is the pattern front.js already established for everything else PART DONE 24 September, pull request #235. WHAT CHANGED: I added one new harness, tools/test-whose-game-gate.js, and changed no runtime code. It reads every .js in tools/ts-plugins, the same set Ship.ps1 sends to Data/Platform/Plugins, so a sixth plugin would be checked too. For each one it checks four things: the gate is the first statement inside the plugin's wrapper; thornswoodGame() and the comment above it match front.js once indentation is set aside; every copy gives the same, correct answer in 15 cases run against a fake file system (no settings, another server, ours with a fresh, stale or missing note, a Thornswood.ini address, a byte order mark); and the one address in `ours` is the ServerAddress default in app\Config.cs, which is where Set-Vps.ps1 reads the address it moves. It also applies Set-Vps's replacement to each plugin and runs the gate again against the new address. The file header records why the entry's one-copy plan was not done: it fails open because of load order. MEASURED: All five copies of thornswoodGame() are 34 lines, and the gate is at chargen.js:50/53, emotes.js:50/51, front.js:40/41, mark.js:32/33 and voice.js:15/16. Today they are identical. front.js differs only by two-space indentation and the spacing before the trailing comment on `let when = Number(first);`. The harness gives 57 passed, 0 failed. To prove it catches drift, I made four edits by hand and then restored them with git checkout: emotes' note window 24h to 48h, mark's `ours` set to the old box 192.135.119.166, a statement put above voice's gate, and a word changed in chargen's gate comment. With those in place it gave 42 passed, 15 failed, and each failure named the file and the first line that differs. Set-Vps.ps1:70 takes the old address from Config.cs:13 (192.135.112.23). Its walk (skipDirs, extension list, 8MB limit) reaches all five plugins. Nothing in the repo writes a ServerAddress line into Thornswood.ini, so the ini override in the gate is only there for a hand-set ini. The dev server is on the same IP (58 references to 192.135.112.23 across tools). Load order: in the fork, skyrim-platform/src/platform_se/skyrim_platform/SkyrimPlatform.cpp:335-347 GetPathsToLoad uses std::filesystem::directory_iterator. NTFS returns names in order, so chargen.js and emotes.js load before front.js. That confirms the triage finding that the entry's stub plan, which returns true when front's object is missing, fails open. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick and Djinn in #dev, because the gate is settled design and a Claude does not decide this: pick one of (a) keep the five copies, held together by this check, which is now in place; (b) delete the retired thornswood-chargen.js together with its references in Install-Emotes.ps1:33,52, Install-Thornswood.ps1:109, Revert.ps1:69-92 and Check-Chargen.ps1:182, leaving four copies; (c) one copy that stays safe whatever the load order, where a plugin that loads before front.js and finds nothing published stays idle instead of carrying on (fails closed); (d) drop the gate now that Thornswood runs from its own folder and, by Patrick's 20 Sep decision, nothing here supports another server's install. The entry's own plan (stub returns true when globalThis.Thornswood.whoseGame is absent) must not be done as written. The entry's doneWhen (settings-file read in one file only) is not met and should not be until the #dev choice is made. The To Do List entry should be updated (not done by me, per limits): record that the check exists on this branch, give the corrected line numbers, and say that the stub plan fails open. Merging needs a normal PR. There is nothing to deploy.

## 325. (done) DONE: a server change is announced in the feed people read, and nothing pushes main by accident

**Order:** 325 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 165

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Publish-Server.ps1:194-195 (the source repo rather than the releases one), 295-305 (a git push from the current branch)

## What is known

Point it at the releases folder the way Set-Server already does, or call the news publisher, and drop the source push entirely. It is a wrong path rather than a design question, and the effect is that people are told about launcher tweaks and never about the server changes that actually affect their evening  FIXED 23 September, pull request 173. Publish-Server wrote its News entry into the version.json in the source repo. That file is the shipped default read as a template; the feed every launcher reads is the copy in the public releases clone, which is where Set-Server.ps1 already writes. So the entry that exists to tell people about the changes nobody downloads anything for went into a file nobody reads. It writes the releases clone now, resolved exactly the way Set-Server resolves it, with the repo copy as the fallback only when there is no releases clone beside it. THE PUSH WAS THE DANGEROUS HALF: it did Push-Location into the SOURCE repo and a bare git push, which takes whatever branch that repo has checked out, and on the shipping machine that is usually main. A deploy script quietly pushing main is how the rule that main is only ever what shipped gets broken without anybody deciding to break it. It is git -C into the releases clone now, and it names the command when it fails rather than leaving a News entry sitting locally. A dev publish is unchanged: no news, no push.

## Read first

- `tools\Set-Server.ps1:38-43`: the correct pattern: the comment 'version.json is published from the public releases clone, not the source one' and the ReleaseDir guess with its .git test
- `tools\Set-Server.ps1:112-117`: `git -C $ReleaseDir add/commit/push`, the shape any push in this family must take
- `tools\Publish-Server.ps1:193-195`: `if (-not $RepoDir) { $RepoDir = Split-Path -Parent $Here }` then `$VersionFile = Join-Path $RepoDir 'version.json'`, the wrong path
- `tools\Publish-Server.ps1:295-305`: Push-Location $RepoDir, then git add, commit and push from whatever branch the source repo has checked out
- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:31`: the Releases repo row, which states where version.json per branch actually lives and names the dev worktree

## Steps

  ```
- [x] Add a `[string]$ReleaseDir` parameter to the param block of tools\Publish-Server.ps1 beside the existing $RepoDir. (claude)
- [x] Resolve $ReleaseDir the way tools\Set-Server.ps1:40-43 does, guessing the sibling Thornswood-Releases clone, but fail loudly when it has no .git rather than falling back to the source repo. (claude)
  ```powershell

  ```
- [x] Point $VersionFile at $ReleaseDir at line 195 so the news entry lands in the feed people actually read. (claude)
- [x] Delete the push block at 295-305 entirely and let Set-Server.ps1 or the news publisher own the commit and push; if a push has to stay, write it as `git -C $ReleaseDir` so it can never act on the source repo's checked-out branch. (claude)
- [x] Make the resolution channel aware, because the dev channel has its own releases worktree (Thornswood-Releases-dev) and a dev publish must not write main's feed. (claude)

## Traps

The `git push` at line 304 is the dangerous part: main is what ships and is never pushed over, and a push from whatever branch the source repo happens to have checked out is exactly how that rule gets broken by accident, so remove it even if the rest waits. The repo-root version.json is not dead, it is the shipped default read as a template, so stop writing news into it rather than deleting it. Publishing news for a server change is the whole point of the script, so do not remove the news step while fixing the path.

Your own character's stagger already goes out: sync/animation.ts:258 forwards any event not in ignoredAnims (:296-304, which does not include staggerStart). The receiving machine applies it at animation.ts:180 with Debug.sendAnimationEvent on the remote actor, and DeathService's hook then blanks it. So stagger crosses the wire and is dropped on arrival. animation.ts:172-176 and :306-317 already hold the pattern needed to let a network-applied event through (the allowedAnims set used for attacks). Killmoves are paired animations between two actors whose owners are different machines, and death is server-owned, so they are a design problem, not a relay problem. NEXT STEP: Stagger only, as a prepared change. In the fork, add an allow set in animation.ts that marks formId:staggerStart just before Debug.sendAnimationEvent. Make deathService.ts hookDisableStagger let that one through and still blank a stagger the local game raises on someone else's actor. Build the client, record it with New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1 (tools/client-build.json changes), then Sync-Client.ps1 -Check and a dev Ship. No gamemode change is needed. Killmoves: write the analysis and a design note for #dev (who starts the pair, how the victim's machine and the server agree on death) and build nothing yet. known.md:22 changes in the same release if stagger lands. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A two-person playtest on dev: one staggers the other and both say what they saw. Killmoves need a design agreed between Patrick and Djinn in #dev before any code, since they touch server-owned death.

Hair colour travels on its own: in the fork, sync/appearance.ts:38-45 reads base.getHairColor().getColor() into an integer hairColor, appearance.ts:138 applies it with TESModPlatform.setNpcHairColor, and the server serialises and compares it (skymp5-server Appearance.h:50, 63, 75). So a hair colour that reaches the NPC's hair colour form round-trips as RGB, independent of tints. Nothing here can show whether RaceMenu's hair colour picker writes that form or an overlay SkyMP does not carry. Appearance is only taken while the race menu is open in the hall. One open ticket per person with an ephemeral refusal linking the open one, a cooldown, and the Member role required. Every mainstream ticket bot defaults to this. The refusal is ephemeral and either links the ticket they already have open or says how many minutes are left. Staff are exempt through is_staff. The open ticket is kept in open-tickets.json beside bot.py, which is gitignored. If the check itself fails, the person is let through. That confirms the branch's choice not to require Member on the ticket panel. Git wrote the merge commit with its default message, so I reworded it to the repo's style with the required trailer. The branch is not on origin, so no pushed commit was rewritten. No fix commit was needed. HEAD is detached. ## 345. (done) DONE: the small sweep, and one of them turned out not to be a defect

**Order:** 345 · **Wave:** 8 Nice to have · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 159

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC and VPS · tools\gamemode.js:122-129, 1806, 3257; tools\ts-ui\thornswood-chat.js:117-129; tools\launcher\voice-host.html:98-102; tools\voice\voice-server.js:159, 242-251, 444-450

## What is known

None of these will hurt anybody on their own. Together they are the difference between code that reads as finished and code that reads as still being worked on, and they cost an afternoon once somebody is already in the file for one of the larger entries SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.90, with the gamemode on both servers, the voice service reinstalled and the site republished. SIX OF THEM DONE. The chat handler no longer tests msg.t === "chat" inside a branch that could not be reached any other way. A websocket close frame is answered with a close frame, 0x88 with a two byte body of 1000, which RFC 6455 5.5.1 asks for and which this used to skip, leaving a well behaved client waiting for a reply until its own timeout. An oversized request body gets a 413 before the socket is destroyed, in both places that do it: destroying with no status is indistinguishable from the service being down, so a client one byte over would retry for ever against a service that is fine. /health carries uptime and a start time, because everything else in that payload looks identical whether the process just restarted or has been wedged for an hour. The voice page's wait for the chat page gives up after two minutes and says so instead of polling twice a second for the rest of the session. The restart drop box is resolved against the dataDir in server-settings.json rather than against whatever directory the server started in. AND ONE THAT IS NOT A DEFECT, which is why it is written down rather than done. The list asks to pick one of notify() or say() rather than sending both. Read across the file, that pairing is the pattern in FOURTEEN places and it is deliberate: notify is Skyrim's corner message and needs no browser, say is the chat and can be scrolled back to. Changing one would make that one the odd one out. tools\test-sweep.js pins the pattern instead, so anybody who later decides one channel is enough can see how many places disagree with them. WORTH KEEPING: that harness passed here and failed on the GitHub runner, because it matched across a line break and the runner checks out CRLF. Every other harness in the folder strips carriage returns on the way in and none of them said why; this one now does.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:100-160`: the log, notify and say helpers, because three of the cleanups are about which of them gets called and what happens when one fails; notify() swallows the Papyrus failure at 122-128
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:140-260`: the hand-rolled WebSocket frame loop and readBody, the two places where the protocol is implemented by hand: line 159 ignores everything but opcode 0x1, and readBody at 242-251 destroys the request without a response
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-chat.js:115-125`: the clearest dead branch: `if (msg.t !== 'chat') { fanout(msg); return; }` immediately followed by `if (msg.t === 'chat') {`, which is always true
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:444-450`: the /health route reports peers, tracked, waitingChoices and queuedCommands but no version and no uptime, so a watchdog cannot tell a restart from a hang
- `tools\launcher\voice-host.html:98-102`: ws.onclose reconnects on a flat 2000 ms timer with no backoff

## Steps

- [x] Delete the redundant `if (msg.t === 'chat')` wrapper at thornswood-chat.js:119 and de-indent its body; that is the easiest first commit. (claude)

## Traps

gamemode.js is over three thousand lines of concatenated programs with no version, no lint and no tests, so a change here has no safety net; keep each edit surgical and near the code it touches. voice-server.js implements WebSocket framing by hand, so getting the close-frame response wrong breaks every connected client at once. The client-side files ship to every machine, so a chat.js change goes out with the launcher and the server, not on its own. Do not fold this entry into a larger refactor; its whole value is that it is an afternoon's sweep.

## What is known

Then a pack can never carry it again whichever machine ships  FIXED 23 September, pull request 170. Ship-Rules had Data\OldModReborn\cache and \logs in the RUNTIME list. ## 359. Most scripts never fire, mods and vanilla alike, so anything scripted is decoration until the server implements it

**Order:** 359 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 178

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · every script event except the timer one is blocked; records still work, scripted behaviour does not

## What is known

Unblocking events is a server change with real risk, so the practical version is to decide per event which ones the server can safely allow and let the rest stay blocked. In the meantime the collection should not contain mods that only work through the blocked ones, which is what entries 168, 166 and 23 are THIS IS THE ANSWER TO the report that a lot of the mods in our list are just straight up not present in the game, from Patrick on 20 September. It is not the load order: all 102 plugins load, and the 42 that look missing are light plugins the load order file cannot see, measured under entry 168. They are loaded and doing nothing, which from a chair is indistinguishable from not being installed. This entry is why. Worth saying plainly to anybody who reports it, because the obvious next move is to go digging through the collection and there is nothing wrong there to find. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #237. WHAT CHANGED: Added tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py, a read-only audit. It reads every VMAD in the load order and every .pex script, loose and in the archives. It then sorts each plugin by what the fork's event blocker (FridaHooks.cpp:43-72) leaves alive: works, partial, a timer only a blocked event starts, dead, fragments only, no events, or records only. It also lists which blocked events the most plugins wait on, which is the data the per-event decision needs. The event names come from the game's own native scripts, not from a hand-typed list. tools/bsa.py had to be fixed for this: it could not read any compressed archive Skyrim Special Edition makes, because those use LZ4 and not zlib, and it read every archive whole. It now decodes LZ4 in plain Python and memory-maps archives. tools/test-papyrus-events.js proves both, with 57 checks. MEASURED: On C:\Thornswood\Game\Data, 99 plugins: - 15,204 scripts parsed, 0 unreadable. Each one parses to exactly the end of its file (the check is at tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:294). - 147 event names, from Form, ObjectReference, Quest, ReferenceAlias, ActiveMagicEffect, the PO3 event scripts, MCM Helper, one mod's own MCM script, and OnInit. No script anywhere declares OnInit. - Plugins by result: 1 works (SkyUI_SE), 24 partial, 23 dead, 6 with a timer only a blocked event starts (Odin, Gourmet, MoreCraftableEquipment, Solitude Arena, ZIA, Triumvirate), 2 fragments only, 3 no events, 40 records only. - Blocked events by how many plugins wait on them: OnInit 37 plugins / 189 scripts, OnLoad 25, OnActivate 24 / 803 scripts, OnDeath 20, OnCellLoad 19. - VMADs: a scan of every subrecord of every record finds 26,937, the same number as reading only the first two subrecords (tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:406-418). - bsa.py: the archive data starts 04 22 4D 18, the LZ4 frame magic, after the 4-byte length. The old zlib path failed on 10 of the 25 archives that carry scripts, and on 23 of the 47 archives under 200 MB. Where the old code could read an archive (24 of them), the new code returns identical bytes. load_strings returns identical tables for Skyrim.esm (30,301 strings), Dawnguard.esm (3,662) and Dragonborn.esm (5,282). Looking for the scripts folder across all 63 archives took 80.4 s before and 1.8 s now (tools/bsa.py:53, 145, 183). - Caprica-built .pex files (QuickLootIE) carry an object size field in the billions, so the parser no longer trusts that field (tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:248). - A full audit takes about 27 s with the disk cache warm and peaks at 289 MB of memory. - Output is the same under Python 3.9 and 3.12 (-W error). - Build-DoorTable.py --check still runs on the new bsa.py: 851 of 852 buildings named, from 6 string tables. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick and Djinn (a #dev decision, because the client runtime is settled design): which events, if any, the blocker should let through. The audit's list of blocked events and its JSON (--json) are the input for that. Narrowing the blocker afterwards is a change to FridaHooks.cpp in the fork, then a client rebuild, New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1, Sync-Client.ps1 and a dev Ship, followed by a check in the game. For Patrick (the Nexus collection): take out the mods the audit calls dead, once he has read the list. In particular IcePenguinWorldMap, Immersive Weapons, Cathedral Weathers, BetterContainerControls, atlas map markers, YokuWeapons and Playable Rieklings. Worth checking in the game before anyone trusts the premise: does TrueHUD's or Precision's MCM page appear at all? Their config scripts register through OnConfigManagerReady, a mod event the audit counts as blocked. If the page appears, mod events are getting through, and the audit overcounts dead mods. For the To Do List (this run could not edit it): 1. Entry 323's text points at the deleted Patch-Client.ps1. It should point at FridaHooks.cpp and at this tool, which is the triage's own correction. 2. known.md:30-36 lists five mods, but four of them (SunHelm Survival, SunHelm Diseases, Respawn, Tavern Games) are in neither plugins.txt nor Data. The fifth, Immersive Armors (Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp), comes out dead. That table is stale. 3. Thornswood-Content.esp gives the furniture record ThornswoodExecutionerChoppingBlock the script KzlChop, and that script is nowhere in Data. 4. The triage asked to check the audit against SunHelm coming out timer-driven. That cannot be done, because SunHelm is not installed.

## 361. (done) DONE: Merge origin/main into patrick/todo-325-mine-buildings again

**Order:** 361 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Old number:** 205

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · builds on entry 208 and the existing cooldown and manual machinery

## What is known

Nobody owns a mine. Higher tier seams are reached through a custom quest from a smith who asks for ore, and the seam holds more than the quest asks, so the work pays in coin and in ore at once. The cooldown is what makes it a wait rather than a grind, and stampCooldown already does that per person per seam. Record the no-ownership decision somewhere public so it is not relitigated DONE 24 September, pull request #303, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: I merged origin/main into the branch twice, both times without conflicts, and fixed the reviewer's one major problem. The branch adds only tools/Measure-MineBuildings.py, tools/mine-buildings.json and tools/test-mine-buildings.js, and main has not touched any of them. The first merge took main up to #288. While I was working, #289 to #298 landed (all but #293), so I merged a second time. Both merge commits were reworded locally to carry the trailers; the branch has never been pushed. The fix: the script used to count every outdoor cell in every worldspace as open ground. Now each worldspace is one place in the road map. Only Tamriel and Solstheim are open ground by default, set by a new --open flag; Solstheim is on it because the way there is a boat. That leaves three kinds of worldspace: - One whose every road in goes through a single building is written under a new `worlds` key, with that building, and its veins are counted as behindABuilding. - One with a road in that no single building sits on, like Blackreach, counts as open ground. - One that no door road reaches at all also counts as open ground, and each is named in reachedByNoDoor. A room reached only from one of these is measured from it, not written off as having no door. This rule is my addition. The stopped fix attempt did not have it: it marked such worlds as sealed and wrote every closed worldspace into `worlds`, so the counts did not add up. I kept what that attempt got right: worldspace names and editor ids, place(), and --open. I regenerated tools/mine-buildings.json. The harness now has a made-up vale reached only through a hall with a cave inside it, a reach with two lifts in, a far world no door reaches with a den inside it, and a Solstheim. ## 362. An economy with a bottom: NPCs start with gold and only have what people have spent

**Order:** 362 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 207

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · the server already owns inventory and container contents, so it can own a purse

## What is known

Each trader starts with a purse and buys and sells against it, so coin moves between people rather than appearing. Specific goods per trader rather than a universal shop. This is the single thing that makes crafting, mining and the professions worth doing, and it is also the thing that makes entry 225's trade ships possible. It needs entry 157 first, because an economy with a floor is only as good as the server's refusal to let anybody create items PART DONE 24 September, pull request #296. WHAT CHANGED: I added one read-only harness, tools/test-one-mint.js. It checks that coin enters the world in exactly one place, purse() in the spoils block (forty gold, once per character), and that everything else only moves gold or takes it away. It runs the real purse, takeGold and trade code against a fake mp, and it still refuses a second purse after a simulated restart. It lists every function that writes a pack with the reason each one cannot make a coin, parses every descriptor in the gamemode, pins every addItem caller to a table in the file, and reads tools/recipes.json for any recipe that makes gold. There is no gamemode change and no trader build, as the task limited it. MEASURED: Measured on 24 Sep against HEAD c13ada9. Writers: 13 functions write a pack, 14 writes in all (WRITERS list in tools/test-one-mint.js). Only spoils/purse and property/takeGold name gold. Descriptors: 27,778 in the gamemode and none is Gold001 (base 0xF in Skyrim.esm). Gold is written by number only in five places: gamemode.js:4298, 15314, 16356, 23077 and 23113. addItem: all 16 calls take their descriptor out of a table. Recipes: 4,529 in tools/recipes.json and none makes gold; 21 (Immersive Armors and Immersive Weapons) take gold as an input. Papyrus: the gamemode has no 'AddItem' Papyrus call. The entry's own check, Select-String 'f:Skyrim\.esm', matches 1,099 descriptors on 228 lines (frost salts 3ad5f among them) and none of them is gold, so its "four line numbers" were never gold lines. Proof that the harness catches a mint: it fails on gamemode.js from c87da23^ (class kits gave gold as "f:Skyrim.esm": 26 fails) and from 4dc2ccf^ (no purse: 14 fails). It also fails on six changed copies of today's file: a purse kept in a Map (fails the restart check), a new function writing gold into a pack, "f:Skyrim.esm" in ITEMS, moveById not taking the pile away, addItem(mp.getDescFromId(15)), and takeGold(-fee). Found and measured in a scratch run: moveById(A, A, 40 gold) turns 100 into 140, and trade.begin(A, A) returns '' and opens a trade. Two things block it today: the /trade command refuses yourself ("That is you.", gamemode.js:18991), and okB can never be set on a trade with one person on both sides, so swap() is never reached. The harness checks both. takeGold (gamemode.js:15814) does not refuse a negative amount; its only caller, gamemode.js:15847-15848, passes JOB_FEE or NOTICE_FEE (30 and 20), which the harness pins. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick with Djinn, before any code: the trader design in #dev (which NPCs trade, what each sells, starting purses, prices, and how a person buys, which has to be a Thornswood panel because the barter menu cannot be driven). Then for a Claude: a trader purse stored as a property on the trader, one function that moves coin and never creates it, per-trader stock keyed by base descriptor, and the trader count in the load banner. That code will change the WRITERS and ADD_FROM lists in tools/test-one-mint.js, which is the intended gate. To Do List corrections (not made; this run may not edit the list): the entry's readFirst is stale. CHARGEN.classes no longer carries 75/100/200/400 purses; the purse is PURSE=40 in the spoils block at gamemode.js:16597. The done-when check 'f:Skyrim\.esm' matches no gold at all; replace it with `node tools\test-one-mint.js`. New findings to record: trade.begin does not refuse a === b and moveById(a, a) doubles the pile it moves (safe today only because of the two guards above), and takeGold accepts a negative amount. Each is a one-line guard in gamemode.js if Patrick wants them closed.

## Where it lives

## What is known

Three needs, tracked per character on the same property that already holds the chargen state and the skill tiers, ticked on the server rather than by a client timer. Temperature needs the worldspace and the weather, which the server can see; hunger and thirst are counters with food and drink as the input, and the server already sees inventory. Diseases were not asked for. Do it after entry 214's economy, so food is something somebody sells you rather than something you conjure SHIPPED 23 SEPTEMBER as launcher 1.1.89, with a gamemode deploy to the live and dev servers. Built exactly as this entry described: one property per character, ticked on the server, no client timer, the server writing values it already owned. ONE THING THIS ENTRY HAD WRONG, and it cost a whole evening. It says temperature needs the worldspace and the weather, "which the server can see". The server cannot see either. Whether it is snowing on you, whether you are swimming and whether there is a fire in front of you are facts about the machine drawing the world, and the server holds a position and a cell descriptor and can answer none of them. The client reports them over the chat socket and the server does the rest, which is the same split the chopping block already used.

Pay coin to pin up work, warnings, rumours or a reward for a name, and guards can tear them down. This is the one on the roadmap that most directly makes people give each other things to do, which is the whole point of a roleplay server, and it is also the feature the front page is currently advertising DONE 24 September, pull request #238, reviewed by a second pass that tried to break it and found nothing blocking. WHAT CHANGED: Deleted tools/Add-NoticeBoards.ps1, the old installer for the Missives mod, which is no longer used. Added /unpin <n> to the property block in tools/gamemode.js. A person standing at a board can take down their own notice or their own job that nobody has taken yet. They cannot take down anyone else's. A job someone has taken stays up until the taker hands it back with /dropjob, and the fee is not refunded because it has already gone to the hold's box. Notices that come down stay in the list marked down, so /board and /take skip them and the numbers people read on the board still point at the same notices. takedown(hold, at, byWhom) is the part that stores a takedown. It checks nothing about who is asking, and it is exported on g.__thornswoodProperty so guards (entries 209/208) can use it later with their own rule. MEASURED: The new harness tools/test-unpin.js has 42 checks and all pass. It covers the entry's done-when with nobody in the world. A notice is posted through the real post() and takeGold(). The pack drops from 200 to 180, the 20 gold goes to the hold's funds, a second boot reads the register off disk with loadPart, and /board shows the notice again. It fails on main's gamemode.js with 6 failures (no unpin, no takedown, no routing). It also fails, with 12 failures, on main's board() and take() with only the new unpin added: the board shows notices that were taken down, a taken-down number can still be taken, and the count of older notices is wrong (2 instead of 1 in the 12-notice case). So those two functions had to change. Checked Missives myself: it is not in C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt or loadorder.txt (both dated Sep 23 22:39), and not among the 204 entries in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data. Nothing in tools calls Add-NoticeBoards.ps1. Only WORKING-NOTES.md mentions it, as history. The changes are in gamemode.js: board() at about :15634-15667, take() at :15701, takedown/unpin at :15776-15843, routing at :15870, the export at :15986, the chat hand-off at :17347, WORDS at :17662 and PLAYER_WORDS at :17713. WHAT TO BUILD: a race field on the recipe rows, written by Build-RecipeTable.ps1 from the output’s name and keywords the same way the owner is, and one check in mp.onCraft beside the half and rank ones. The gate is built and the hard part turned out to be deciding what it covers rather than writing it. WHO SOMEBODY IS: tools\Build-RaceTable.js sweeps every RACE record in the order into tools\races.json and installs the thin version into gamemode.js, and raceOf() resolves the appearance’s raceId against it once per load order. 258 records, 22 playable. WHICH RACES COUNT: the playable flag is read off the record itself, at an offset MEASURED by testing every four byte offset in DATA against ten races everybody knows are playable and five everybody knows are not. It is offset 32, bit 0. That came from Patrick reading a first list with Falmer, Dremora and Draugr in it: "they are not playable races so they can be by anuone only playable races should be race locked". WHAT LOCKS, AND THIS IS THE DECISION: a set named for a people is that people’s dress and locks; a tier of metal is what any smith with the perk hammers out and stays open. Patrick raised it himself: "somtimes things are called bosmer, orsimer, altmer, dunmer", then "That’s the exact reason I said it because of Bosmer armour", then "Which we should have in our mods", then "Also I believe we have Nordic armour somewhere". Asked directly what should happen to the 70 Nord named recipes he chose the cultural sets alone: NORD MAIL LOCKS AND NORDIC CARVED DOES NOT, though both say Nord, because Nordic Carved is the quicksilver tier between Elven and Glass and taking a smithing tier off everybody born wrong is not what this was for. Bosmer, Dunmer, Orsimer, Telvanni, Skaal, Nord Mail, Redguard Knight, Alik’r, Yokudan and Colovian lock. Thalmor and Forsworn are deliberately left open: the Thalmor take Bosmer as readily as Altmer, and the Forsworn are a tribe at war with the Reach rather than a people. Einherjar, Barbarian, Warchief, Stormlord and Viking are Immersive Armors flavour names and nobody is born into them. A MISSING OR UNREADABLE RACE REFUSES NOTHING, on purpose: somebody who never finished creation is already having a bad time without a craft gate on top. Nothing broke, because the editor id is what everything compares against, but the name is only there so a person can answer "why did this count as a riekling" and it was not doing that one job. Fixed by reading the 0x80 bit off each plugin’s own TES4 header.

The race is on the APPEARANCE, which is empty for a character who never finished creation, so a missing race must not refuse everything: no race reads as no gate. ## 383. Crafted a helmet twice and got one

**Order:** 383 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, medium · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js mp.onCraft · the inventory sync in the fork

## What is known

PATRICK, 23 September, in the world: "Made a helmet twice only got one". Two crafts, one item. The shape to suspect first is the same one behind the naked arrivals: the client makes the thing and puts it in its own pack, the server is told afterwards, and an inventory write that crosses the two loses one of them. WHAT TO MEASURE: whether onCraft fired twice in the server log, whether the pack held two before the next sync, and whether the second craft consumed its materials. Those three answers separate "the craft was refused", "the item was made and then overwritten" and "the client never sent the second one". MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Found in the log already on this machine, logs/dev/server.log (pulled 23 Sep 22:28). Lines 2303-2305: at 20:46:05 'User 1 tries to craft 0x38019f67 on workbench 0xc430a', then 'Recipe not found' with 13 reported inputs, including gold (baseId 15) x1 and x46, iron ingot 0x5ace4 x1+x12+x3 and 0x1be1a. The gamemode logged 'worked 38019f67 with no recipe ... tempering or the like. Allowed' (gamemode.js:9652 recipelessCraft, :9694-9697). Then '[error] Source inventory doesn't have enough 0x1be1a (1 is required while 0 present)'. So the craft was dropped server-side and the next inventory sync took the helmet back. Lines 2307-2309, 20:46:09: a phantom 'craft 0x5ace4 from 0x38019f67 x1' (the sync putting the ingots back and removing the helmet, misread as a craft) failed the same way. Lines 2312-2316, 20:46:22: the retry matched RecipeArmorRieklingHelmet3Alt (Playable Rieklings, index 56) and 'crafted -0x5ace4 x3 +0x38019f67 x1'. So two crafts, one helmet, which is what Patrick reported. The cause is in the fork. skymp5-client/src/services/services/craftService.ts builds each craft's inputs from every item that left the pack while the character was at that furniture (furnitureStreak), keyed per furniture and only cleared when a craft finishes. So the removals from the deploy respawn at 20:44 (entry 351: 'it was while looking in the forge'; log 20:44:52 'login ff000003 put 2 worn thing(s) back on') were still in that list when he crafted. CraftService.cpp RecipeItemsMatch requires GetItemCount == entry.count exactly (16 ingots reported vs 3 wanted), so FindRecipe failed. CraftEvent::OnFireSuccess removes the client's list and throws atomically (Inventory.cpp:106-147) when one entry is missing. NEXT STEP: Server side in the fork, C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp on thornswood/engine-changes, as a THORNSWOOD PATCH in skymp5-server/cpp/server_guest_lib/CraftService.cpp. When the exact match finds nothing and the output is a plugin form (below 0xff000000), try again with a looser rule: a recipe matches if every one of its inputs is covered by (reported inputs that the server's own inventory actually holds), at the same bench keyword, with conditions met. Then UseCraftRecipe as normal, so only the recipe's own inputs are removed and the server never adds anything the client did not make. Filtering by what the server holds is what keeps the phantom out: at 20:46:09 the server did not hold the helmet, so 'ingot from helmet' matches nothing. Log a line whenever the loose match was used. Add cases to unit/CraftTest.cpp: a polluted list with extra stale entries crafts the recipe and removes only 3 ingots, and a reported input the server does not hold matches nothing. Build with tools\Build-Server.ps1, record with New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1, then Publish-Server -Channel dev. The client-side streak cleanup is optional and separate, because its timing cannot be observed from here. WORKED 24 September, and the cause is not what the entry first thought. See the new entry about the client craft streak: the list of inputs was polluted after a respawn, so no recipe matched. A server side resend was built, tested and reviewed, and it makes no visible difference because the client defers its own inventory correction while the crafting menu is open; it is kept unpushed on the fork branch thornswood/craft-resync as a record. Merged instead: pull request 221, which stops the gamemode log calling such a craft tempering. And the investigation turned up a real gap, now its own fix: a craft that matched no recipe skipped the whole craft gate.

## Done when

Two crafts of the same thing leave two of it in the pack, and the log shows both.

## Traps

Do not fix this by having the server add the item: the client already added it, and adding a second is how one craft becomes two of everything for anybody who notices.

MEASURED: the plugin is listed in Profile/OwnGame/files.txt on both builds, which is the launcher's record of what Vortex deployed, and Publish-Update excludes every file in that record by path. So this plugin reaches people only through the Nexus collection, never in a pack. And the launcher compares every plugin's name and size with the server's and refuses Play on any difference, so putting the new plugin on a server before the collection carries it would lock out everybody who has the old one. Pull request 200 made /mold keep conjuring a mold until the blank mold's recipe record is actually loaded, so nothing is broken in the meantime: the key chain works the old way until the plugin arrives, and switches to the forged blank by itself the day it does. Pull request 198 already lets a smith cut a key to their own door with no mold at all.

## Done when

Thornswood Content on Nexus carries the 384-record plugin, a collection revision carries that, and the dev server has it through Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 -LoadOrder, after which a smith can forge a blank Key Mold and a Key at a forge.

## Traps

Do not run Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 -LoadOrder, Deploy-Server.ps1, or anything else that sends plugins to a server before the collection revision is out: the size check refuses Play to every tester whose copy is older. The dev server running the new gamemode with the old plugin is fine and expected; that is what pull request 200 is for.
